AP runs the spend-management platform — card program administration, bill-pay execution, policy authoring, and reconciliation to GL. Same owner as EXPENSE and AP-AUTO; this domain is the modern unification of those two AP-owned workflows.
Vendor master alignment, sourcing input to spend categories, policy coordination on indirect-procurement card spend.
Multi-currency cards, FX hedging on cross-border spend, card credit-limit allocation, cash positioning against bill-pay runs.
BizOps is the function that actually buys NCDB tools at the org level (consolidating Airtable, Notion, Coda subscriptions) and sets the citizen-developer governance policy.
Marketing ops is the heaviest NCDB user base — campaign trackers, asset libraries, content calendars all live in Airtable/Notion. Citizen-developer contributor, not enterprise owner.
People-ops teams use NCDB to track recruiting pipelines, onboarding checklists, employee directories — often before adopting a formal HRIS.
Sales-ops uses NCDB for territory planning, deal-review trackers, and pricing approvals when the CRM is too rigid.
Data team consumes NCDB data via API/ETL into the warehouse; rarely owns NCDB deployment. Tracks sprawl for data-governance reasons.
BizOps / PMO is the cross-functional owner of work-management tooling at the org level: vendor selection, license consolidation, integration with CRM / HRIS / ITSM.
Product teams that don't run on Jira (or that augment Jira with roadmap-and-launch coordination) use Asana/Monday/ClickUp for cross-functional launch projects.
Marketing campaign management, brand projects, and content calendars are major Asana/Monday/Wrike use cases. Marketing Ops often drives vendor selection.
Implementation/onboarding teams run customer projects in WORK-MGMT; the kickoff-from-closed-won handoff lands here.
Sales leadership consumes project-status views for at-risk-account intervention and deal-related delivery commitments. Not a buyer.
Process Office / Operational Excellence / Transformation function. Owns the BPA tool, the process repository, and the capability map.
Enterprise architecture function co-authors process models for IT-process alignment; bridges to APM.
SOX / ISO 9001 / ISO 27001 process documentation lives in BPA; compliance team co-authors and audits.
Transformation programs and operating-model decisions consume capability maps and value-stream analyses.

records.business_function_domain_label: Business Intelligence / Metrics Layer / Headless BI

records.business_function_domain_label: Data Engineering / Metrics Layer / Headless BI

records.business_function_domain_label: AI and Machine Learning / Metrics Layer / Headless BI

records.business_function_domain_label: Research and Development / Knowledge Graph Platform

entity.description: What an organization can do, expressed as nouns (Lead Management, Automated Invoice Matching, Workforce Scheduling, Predictive Maintenance). Capabilities are the strategic-architecture bridge between business functions (who needs them) and solutions (what software delivers them). Hierarchical to support standard capability maps (Customer Management contains Lead Management, Account Management, Opportunity Management). Capabilities are independent of which solution delivers them; a capability exists in the catalog whether the organization is mature in it or not, and the solution-capabilities junction records who can satisfy it.

Branded member self-service for balance, history, redemption, tier status, referrals.
Provision, change, suspend, resume, cancel subscriptions with proration and effective-dated changes.
Generate invoices on subscription terms (monthly, annual, anniversary) with consolidated billing.
Ingest usage events, rate against pricing tables, output billable usage; metered/consumption pricing.
Gateway integration, retry logic on declines, automated dunning emails, involuntary-churn recovery.
Recognize revenue across performance obligations and contract modifications; bridge to GL.
Real-time tax calculation on invoices, often delegated to a specialized tax engine, including jurisdiction- and product-specific rules.
MRR/ARR, churn, expansion, cohort LTV, retention curves; CFO-grade SaaS-metric reporting.
Translate sold subscriptions into product/feature entitlements consumed by app gating and provisioning.
Product catalog, taxonomy, attributes, variants, search/sort, category curation, badging.
Cart persistence, multi-step/express checkout, guest checkout, multi-currency/payment-method support.
Themable storefront frameworks (headless and templated) with mobile-first responsive design.
Order placement, validation, inventory reservation, promised-delivery calc; hand-off to OMS/ERP for fulfillment.
Coupons, BOGO, automatic promotions, cart-level discounts, qualifier rules engine.
Faceted search, autocomplete, synonyms, AI-personalized ranking and recommendations.
Account hierarchies, contract pricing, quote-to-order, requisition lists, role-based purchasing.
API-first commerce backend decoupled from presentation, enabling composable storefronts on any front-end framework.

Single, reconciled view of a customer across transactional, marketing, and operational systems. Combines CRM account/contact records, CDP behavioral profile, and MDM golden-record stewardship into one queryable surface.

Declarative approval-chain definition (sequential / parallel / conditional), approval routing rules, escalation policies, delegation, and audit trail. The shape is identical across contract approval (CLM), quote discount approval (CPQ), purchase requisition approval (S2P), offer approval (HCM), HR case approval (HRSD), change approval (ITSM), and invoice approval (AP-AUTO). Cross-cutting platform suites reuse one engine across all of these.

Demand-driven shift assignment, route optimization, skill matching, and dispatch for frontline workers. Same engine serves hourly workforce scheduling (WFM), field-service dispatch (FSM), shop-floor crew assignment (MFG-OPS), and store labor scheduling (RET-STORE).

Issuance, activation, freezing, and termination of physical and virtual corporate cards. Includes single-use, vendor-locked, and budget-bound virtual cards; per-cardholder limits; and integration with BIN-sponsor banks for the underlying card program.

Network-side rule evaluation on each card authorization request — MCC, vendor, amount, time-of-day, geography, and per-card budget — with ms-latency decline of out-of-policy transactions before settlement.
Employee-initiated reimbursement request without an underlying corporate-card transaction — receipt upload, policy check, approval, and ACH payout. Distinct from card-driven expense lines.

Ingest vendor invoices (PDF / email / portal) for direct payment via ACH, wire, card, or check, with approval routing, bank-detail enrichment, and reconciliation to GL — without requiring PO match or sourcing workflow.

Proactive employee request for spend authorization before any transaction — virtual card issuance, raised card limit, vendor bill, or reimbursement budget. Approval becomes the enforceable commitment used at card-auth or bill-pay time.
Multi-currency cards and bill pay with bank-grade FX rates, optional currency hedging, treasury netting across entities, and local-currency disbursement to reduce cross-border fees.
Aggregated spend dashboards by department / vendor / merchant / cost-center; trend and variance reporting; ML anomaly detection for unusual spend patterns; vendor consolidation insights.

records.capability_name: Flexible Schema and Rich Field Types
records.description: User-defined tables and fields without DBA involvement; rich field types including attachment, single/multi-select, status, person, date, currency, rating, formula, lookup, and rollup. Schema evolves at runtime through the UI; downstream views and automations adapt without code changes.

First-class relationships between tables (one-to-many, many-to-many, self-referential), with linked-record fields that surface related records inline, two-way navigation, and junction-table modeling for many-to-many without manual SQL.

Switchable presentation of the same underlying records as grid, gallery, kanban (by status/category), calendar (by date field), timeline/Gantt, and form views. Each view filters, sorts, groups, and hides fields independently; views are shareable per-user or per-role.

Spreadsheet-style derived columns with arithmetic, string, date, and conditional functions; cross-table rollups that aggregate child records; lookup fields that surface fields from linked records. The expressiveness gap with full code is where vendors differentiate.

Public or authenticated forms that write directly into a table, with conditional logic, prefilled URL parameters, file uploads, and survey-style branching. The primary intake surface for non-database users contributing structured data.

Live or scheduled bidirectional synchronization between a base/table and external systems of record (CRM, issue trackers, relational databases, spreadsheets, payment platforms). Updates flow both directions with conflict handling, so the no-code database becomes a working surface over canonical data rather than a copy.

Task creation with owner, due date, priority, status, subtasks, attachments, and comments; bulk operations; recurring tasks; my-work / inbox views per user. The atomic primitive on which everything else builds.

Linked predecessor/successor relationships between tasks (finish-to-start, start-to-start, etc.) with automatic schedule recalculation, critical-path highlighting, and Gantt/timeline visualization. Distinguishes serious project execution from to-do-list tools.

Per-person workload calculated from assigned tasks weighted by effort estimates, over-allocation flags, capacity-vs-demand heatmaps across teams, and reassignment workflows. The buyer-facing view that justifies adding seats.

Hierarchical goals/OKRs with measurable key results, weighted progress rollup from child tasks/projects, owner accountability views, and quarterly cadence reporting. The strategy-to-execution link that pushes WORK-MGMT into VP/exec rooms.

Trigger-action automations on tasks and items (status change, due date, assignment, form submission) with conditional branches, multi-step actions, time-based delays, and external integrations. The vendor differentiator that moves teams off email-and-spreadsheet workflows.

Configurable dashboards combining widgets across multiple projects/boards: task counts by status, burndown, velocity, workload, custom-field rollups, and embedded reports. The artifact a PM presents weekly to leadership.

Drag-and-drop and model-driven authoring of UI, data model, and business logic, generating a deployable application without hand-coded scaffolding. Spans visual page composers, data-modeling canvases, and visual logic flows.

Vendor-operated runtime for compiled or interpreted low-code apps, including auto-scaling, multi-tenant hosting, version pinning per environment, logging, and observability. Distinguishes LCAP from build-and-deploy-yourself frameworks.

Library of certified connectors to enterprise systems (ERP, CRM, relational databases, productivity suites, REST/SOAP APIs) with authentication handling, schema introspection, and bidirectional read/write. Reduces the integration tax that kills custom development.
Long-running process orchestration with human tasks, approvals, escalations, parallel/sequential branches, SLA tracking, and case-management primitives. Where LCAP overlaps with BPM/iBPMS.

Dev/test/prod environments, promotion pipelines, versioning, rollback, dependency management, branch/merge of model artifacts, and CI/CD integration. The governance layer that makes LCAP enterprise-credible vs spreadsheet-replacement tools.

Natural-language app generation, AI-suggested data models, UI scaffolding from prompts, code/expression completion, and AI-assisted refactoring inside the visual builder. The 2024+ feature line every LCAP vendor is racing to ship.
Authoring of executable and non-executable BPMN 2.0 process diagrams with full notation (pools, lanes, sub-processes, events, gateways), versioning, and validation against the BPMN spec.
Central repository for process models with check-in/check-out, version graphs, lifecycle states (draft/review/published/retired), role-based review workflows, and approval gates.
Discrete-event / Monte Carlo simulation of process models with cost, time, and resource variables; bottleneck identification; scenario comparison.
End-to-end value stream maps with lead/process time, value-add ratio, and waste categorization; SIPOC and customer-journey overlays.
Web-portal generation from the repository, audience-specific (role-filtered) process portals, and embedded help / click-through navigation for end users.

Hierarchical capability maps with heatmaps for maturity, investment, strategic-fit, and ownership; explicit linkage to applications, processes, and value streams. Cross-cutting across both APM and BPA tooling.

Pre-loaded reference content from APQC PCF (cross-industry + industry variants), TOGAF, ArchiMate, eTOM, SCOR, with import/sync and the ability to extend with org-specific custom processes. Cross-cutting: shipped by both BPA tools and EA tools.

Canonical registry of metric definitions (numerator, denominator, filters, dimensions) authored once and reused everywhere. Includes versioning, certification status, ownership, and lineage from physical sources up to logical metrics consumed by BI tools and AI agents.

Logical model of entities, dimensions, hierarchies, and relationships decoupled from physical tables. Supports star/snowflake schemas, conformed dimensions across fact tables, slowly-changing-dimension handling, and graph-style entity relationships.

Approval workflows for metric definition changes, deprecation policies, impact analysis on downstream consumers, certified vs. draft labeling, and metric-level data-contract enforcement between producers and consumers.

Single semantic model querying multiple physical sources (cloud data warehouses, relational databases, object storage, REST APIs) through one query interface. Push-down optimization to each backend, federated join planning, and per-source credential handling.

Intelligent aggregate caching, materialized-view selection, query rewriting against cached aggregates, and automatic cache invalidation when underlying data or models change. The acceleration tier that lets pure-play metric layers compete with native warehouse compute on latency.

Exposing the semantic layer through multiple protocols simultaneously: SQL (for BI tools), REST/GraphQL (for apps), MDX (for Excel and legacy BI), JDBC/ODBC (for enterprise integration). One model, many consumption surfaces.

LLM tool-use over the metric registry: natural-language-to-metric translation with deterministic grounding, agent function-calling against certified metrics, RAG retrieval that joins narrative context with quantitative metrics. The 2024+ wedge that headless-BI vendors are racing to ship.

Visual and code-based authoring of OWL/RDF ontologies (or labeled property graph schemas), namespace and prefix management, change control with versioning, SHACL constraint authoring, and ontology-quality reporting. The 'modeling studio' tier of a KGP.

OWL-RL / OWL-EL / OWL-DL reasoning engines, RDFS entailment, rule-based inference (SWRL or vendor-specific), materialized vs. on-query inference modes. Distinguishes KGP from plain graph storage: the system infers triples not explicitly asserted.
SPARQL 1.1 endpoint with query optimization, SPARQL federation across multiple remote endpoints via SERVICE clauses, named-graph access control, and full-text search integration over literals.

Query relational, document, and API sources as if they were native RDF graphs, without ETL into the triplestore. R2RML / RML mapping, on-query SPARQL-to-SQL translation, and federated querying that mixes virtual and materialized graphs in one query.

Hybrid vector+symbolic search joining graph embeddings with structured graph queries, LLM tool-use over the graph (entity lookup, neighborhood traversal, reasoning), and ontology-grounded RAG that constrains LLM outputs to typed entities and relationships.

Native triplestore (RDF) or labeled-property-graph storage tier with high-scale persistence, transaction support, replication, and backup. Distinct from KG features bolted onto a relational DB: the storage engine is purpose-built for graph workloads.
Inline and at-rest classification of data by sensitivity level; lexicon, statistical, and ML-driven inference.
Rules engine for detecting policy violations and applying actions (block, quarantine, redact, mask, watermark, alert).
Inspection of outbound email and collaboration-platform messages and attachments for sensitive content.
Agent-based monitoring of local file access, USB/removable media, printing, clipboard, screen capture.

Annual reconciliation of common-area-maintenance expenses across tenants, gross-up to occupancy, exclusion of capital items, true-up billing, and audit support.
Visualize building stacking plans by floor and suite, track vacant/leased/expiring space, and identify combinable suites for prospective tenants.
Lease and sale comparables sourced from public records, broker submissions, and third-party proprietary market data; rent-PSF benchmarking by submarket.
Tenant-portal for COIs, service requests, billing inquiries, and lease-document access; tenant-satisfaction surveys; lease-renewal pipeline.
CPI-indexed, fixed-percent, stepped, and market-reset escalation schedules; percentage-rent on retail tenants; calculation against breakpoints and overages.

Productive-time vs idle vs deadhead analytics, right-sizing recommendations, cost-per-mile and cost-per-hour benchmarking against industry baselines.
DOT registration, IFTA fuel-tax reporting, IRP apportioned registration, CSA scoring, IFTA jurisdiction-mile reporting, and audit-evidence retention.
Continuous vehicle-location tracking via OBD/AOBRD/embedded telematics, breadcrumb trail storage, and live-map visualization with playback.

Automatic-on-board recording of driving time per FMCSA Part 395 rules, HOS-rule conformance (11-hour driving, 14-hour duty, 70/8 cycles), driver vehicle-inspection-report (DVIR) capture, and roadside-inspection-mode output.
Telemetry-derived event detection (harsh braking, hard acceleration, cornering, speeding, fatigue), composite safety scoring, and per-driver coaching playlists.
Forward-facing and driver-facing video capture, AI-based incident detection (distracted driving, collision, near-miss), automatic clip upload on trigger, and incident review workflow.
Polygon and route-based geofence definition, entry/exit/dwell alerts, after-hours-use detection, and route-deviation alerting.
Engine fault-code (DTC) ingestion via OBD-II/J1939, vehicle-health scoring, real-time fault alerting, and historical fault trending per vehicle.
PM-schedule definition per vehicle class with triggers on mileage, engine hours, calendar time, or DTC codes; auto-generation of work orders ahead of due dates; deferred-maintenance tracking.

Work-order intake (from inspection, telematics trigger, or driver report), task-line composition with labor estimates, in-shop vs out-of-shop routing, completion sign-off, and post-repair quality check.
Parts master with cross-reference to vehicle make/model/year, on-hand stock and reorder thresholds per location, parts-consumption against work orders, and supplier integration for parts ordering.
Mechanic-skill profile and certification tracking, shop-bay scheduling, technician-time capture by work order, productivity (wrench-time) analytics.
OEM-warranty coverage tracking per VIN, eligible-claim identification on repair events, recall notification ingestion from NHTSA, and recall-completion tracking across fleet.
Pre-trip and post-trip driver vehicle inspection report (DVIR) capture via mobile, defect routing to maintenance work orders, mandated retention and audit-ready reporting.
Matter intake, lifecycle, party tracking (clients, opposing parties, co-counsel, courts), key-date and statute-of-limitations alerting, matter-status reporting.
Timekeeper time-entry capture with ABA UTBMS task/expense codes, hourly-vs-flat-vs-contingency-vs-AFA billing models, prebill review, e-bill submission (LEDES 1998B/2000).
Separated trust-account ledgering per client and matter, three-way reconciliation (bank statement vs ledger vs client-balance), state-specific retention rules, transfer-to-operating-on-earned.
Graph-search of new matters against existing client/party/adversary relationships, conflict-waiver tracking, ethics-wall management for shielded matter teams.
Matter-scoped document storage with version control, e-signature integration, document automation/assembly from templates, document-numbering compliance.
Online intake forms with conflict-check trigger, engagement-letter drafting from templates, retainer-payment collection, intake-to-matter conversion workflow.
Animal-patient master (species, breed, age, weight, sex, microchip), examination SOAP notes, vaccination history, problem list, chronic-condition tracking.
Appointment booking with species/exam-type fit, multi-pet household batching, online booking integration, no-show / waitlist management.
Services + product + lab + drug invoicing with per-item taxability, in-clinic POS for retail (food, supplies), client payment plans, third-party payer and pet-insurance integration.

records.capability_name: Veterinary Drug Inventory and Controlled-Substance Ledger
records.description: Drug inventory with lot tracking, controlled-substance Schedule II–V ledger reconciliation, e-prescribing (where DEA-certified), automated reorder thresholds.
Bi-directional integration with reference veterinary labs and in-house analyzers, structured results into patient record, trending across visits.
Preventive-care reminders (vaccines, dental, geriatric exams) by species/breed/age, multi-channel outreach (SMS, email, postcard), reminder-effectiveness analytics.
Per-engagement workflow templates (1040, 1120, 1065, audit, bookkeeping), task assignment, sign-off checkpoints, partner-review routing.

records.capability_name: Accounting Client Portal and Document Exchange
records.description: Secure portal for client document upload (W-2, 1099, K-1, bank statements), e-signature on tax forms (8879), client-task-list tracking.
Timekeeper time-entry per engagement, value-billing vs hourly options, WIP and AR reporting, fee-quote-to-invoice workflow.
Engagement-letter templates per service line, proposal generation, e-signature with retainer-payment collection, recurring annual re-engagement workflow.
Tax-calendar-driven recurring deadlines (federal, state, local) per engagement type, extension-form generation, deadline-vs-capacity dashboards.
Client-folder document storage with IRS / state preparer retention rules, prior-year carryforward, document-classification by year and form type.

Central agency job (engagement) record with traffic state, brief linkage, deliverable rollup, assigned teams, deadlines, and status routing. The system-of-record for the agency's active book of business — distinct from PSA's project record by retainer linkage, creative-brief origination, and media-plan attachment.

Recurring retainer agreements with monthly fee, allocated hours/scope, and live burn-down against time entries and media costs. Surfaces over-burn alerts, replenishment triggers, and end-of-period roll-forward / true-up. Distinct from subscription billing — retainer accounting tracks consumed work against a committed scope envelope, not invoiced units.

records.capability_name: Media Plan and Insertion Order Management
records.description: Per-campaign media plans broken down by outlet, daypart, audience, and budget; conversion of approved plans into insertion orders (IOs) to media outlets with negotiated rates, commission terms, and make-good provisions. Includes IO reconciliation against media-outlet invoices and post-campaign performance reporting.

Pre-engagement client estimates priced from rate cards, expected effort, and media/production cost lines with markup; conversion of approved estimates into agency jobs with locked billing terms; change-order workflow for scope creep with explicit client approval.

Configurable markup rules per cost type (labor, media, third-party production, freelance) per client agreement. Includes commission gross-up (e.g., 17.65% on net media to yield 15% commission), markup ladders by client tier, and pass-through vs. marked-up cost designations on invoices.

Live per-job and per-client margin rollups combining time costs (hours × loaded employee rate), media costs, third-party production, and overhead allocation against billable revenue. Surfaces under-water jobs, top-client margin, and discipline-level profitability for staffing and pricing decisions.

Cross-cutting capability: multi-stakeholder review and annotation of creative deliverables (images, video, copy, layouts) with version history, approval routing, mark-up tools, and audit trail. Spans agency management, work management, and DAM markets.
GIS-based farm-field boundary definition, sub-field zone mapping (soil-type, yield, productivity), and integration with satellite / aerial imagery layers for visual operations planning.
Seasonal crop-plan authoring (what to plant where), multi-year rotation modeling, cover-crop scheduling, and budget projection per field.
Per-pass record-keeping for planting events (seed variety, rate, date) and chemical / fertilizer applications (product, rate, weather conditions, applicator, restricted-use justification).
Track seed, fertilizer, chemical, and fuel inventory across farm bins / sheds; reconcile against application records and purchase invoices for spend analysis.
Field-by-field and zone-by-zone yield capture from combine telemetry, scale tickets, and grain-handling records; reconcile against pre-harvest forecasts.

Author site-specific application prescriptions for seed, fertilizer, and chemicals based on soil-test data, historical yield maps, and satellite imagery zones; export to machinery in ISOBUS / shapefile format.
Ingest and normalize telemetry from tractors, combines, sprayers, and implements via CAN-bus, ISOBUS, and OEM machinery-telematics APIs.
Multi-season yield comparison, profitability-per-zone analysis, return-on-input modeling, and identification of underperforming zones or fields.
Record FSMA-204-defined critical tracking events (growing, receiving, transformation, creation, shipping) on covered foods through the supply chain.
Generate FDA-electronically-sortable KDE reports for foods on the FSMA-204 Food Traceability List; respond to FDA traceback requests within 24 hours.

Centralized vault for supplier certifications (GFSI, organic, kosher, halal), insurance certificates, allergen statements, and country-of-origin attestations; OCR-based expiry tracking and renewal workflow.
Initiate, track, and report on product recalls: identify affected lots from lot-genealogy, notify downstream consignees, manage hold-and-segregate, file FDA Reportable Food Registry submissions.
Forward and backward lot-genealogy traversal: from raw material lots through transformation events to finished SKUs and downstream consignees; visualize as a graph.
Verify and surface origin claims (country, farm, fishery, sustainability certification) to downstream stakeholders; blockchain anchoring for tamper-evident provenance attestation.
Per-animal record of birth, calving events, lactation cycles, dry-off, breeding history, and culling decisions; serves as the herd-level system of record.
Integrate with milking parlors (conventional / rotary) and automatic milking systems to capture per-cow milk yield, milking duration, conductivity, and parlor-side alerts.

Track somatic cell count (SCC), bacterial counts, butterfat / protein components, antibiotic residue, and bulk-tank quality records per shipment; trigger drug-residue and mastitis-management workflows.

Track reproductive cycles, breeding events (natural service, AI, embryo transfer), pregnancy checks, and heat-detection signals (rumination collars, pedometers); compute reproductive efficiency metrics (days open, conception rate).
Formulate per-group total mixed rations (TMR), track feed inventory and shrink, integrate with feed-mixer load cells, and compute income-over-feed-cost (IOFC) per cow group.

Track health events (mastitis, lameness, metabolic disorders), veterinary treatments, withdrawal periods, and herd-level disease trends; integrate with rumination / activity sensors for early-warning escalation.

Author and maintain Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) plans: hazard analysis, CCP identification, critical limits, monitoring procedures, corrective actions, verification, and recordkeeping per Codex Alimentarius / FSMA requirements.
Real-time or shift-frequency CCP monitoring (cook temperature, cold chain, metal detection, etc.) with deviation escalation, hold-and-test workflow, and corrective-action tracking.

Prepare for GFSI-benchmarked certification audits (SQF, BRC-GS, FSSC 22000, IFS) with self-assessment checklists, evidence libraries, score forecasting, and corrective-action plans against prior findings.
Manage allergen-control program: allergen mapping per product line, changeover validation (ATP swabbing, allergen-specific tests), labeling control, and supplier allergen attestations.
Sampling-plan management for pathogen environmental monitoring (Listeria, Salmonella, EHEC): sample-site scheduling, result entry, trend analytics by zone (Zone 1-4), corrective-action workflow.
Score and segment ingredient and packaging suppliers by safety risk: country-of-origin, food-fraud vulnerability (VACCP), historical non-conformance, certification scope, and audit results.
Manage CSA (community-supported agriculture) memberships: season setup, share types (vegetable, fruit, flower, meat), tiered share sizes, member onboarding, and roster management.
Per-member share customization: swap-week selection (pick this not that), pause / vacation weeks, dietary substitutions (allergen-free, vegan), proration of partial weeks, and family-share splitting.
Optimize multi-stop delivery routes for DTC orders using routing engines; account for delivery windows, vehicle capacity, return depots, and cold-chain duration constraints.

On-site point-of-sale for farmers-market stalls: SKU-level pricing, scale integration for by-weight produce, cash / card / EBT-SNAP tender, end-of-day reconciliation per market day, multi-market roll-up.
Cash-and-carry POS for on-farm farmstands and pick-your-own operations: variable inventory (weight, count), product-mix decisions by harvest availability, and farmstand cash-drawer reconciliation.

Customer-facing portal: share previews ('this week's box'), recipe suggestions, pickup reminders, account history, gift-share purchases, and member-to-member share donation / referral.
Translate field-level harvest forecasts (lbs of tomatoes ready by week, lambs ready by month) into available shares / SKUs; surface scarcity-driven dynamic pricing and reserve-list waitlists.

Stage-based pipeline (sourcing, screening, diligence, IC, term sheet, closed) with deal-team collaboration, notes, and documents.
Lightweight CRM-side view of portfolio companies for deal-team awareness, distinct from full portfolio monitoring.
Fundraising-side CRM for LP outreach, meetings, and capital-commitment pipeline.
Path computation across the firm's relationship graph to identify the strongest warm-intro path to a target person.
Shared investment memos, IC documents, and deal-team commentary tied to specific opportunities.
Capital-call notice generation, LP payment tracking, and call schedule management across funds.
European/American/hybrid waterfall calculations with catchup, clawback, and hurdle-rate handling.
LP subscription document collection, KYC/AML checks, and accreditation verification.
Partner capital account statements per LP with contributions, distributions, gains/losses, and fees.
GP books for the fund vehicle with multi-currency support and GAAP/IFRS partnership-accounting compliance.
Document and trail packaging for annual fund audits.
Secure portal for LPs to access statements, capital-call notices, distribution notices, and fund documents.
Structured collection of portfolio-company KPIs via portal upload, email parsing, or accounting connectors.
Fair-value marks per ASC 820 with methodology-tagged audit trail across reporting cycles.
Time-weighted IRR/MOIC/TVPI/DPI computation across multi-vintage funds with PME benchmarking.
Aggregate performance and concentration dashboards across portfolio holdings.
Quarterly LP-facing performance reports with fund and individual position metrics.
Portfolio-company ESG and diversity metric collection for LP disclosure and SFDR compliance.
Authoritative record of equity holders, classes, and historical transactions for the issuing company.
Pool size tracking, available headroom, and reservation workflows for board-approved equity grants.
IRS 409A fair-market-value determination per methodology (income, market, asset, OPM backsolve).
RSU and option grant issuance with board approval, grant acceptance, and vesting-schedule administration.
Scenario modeling for exit proceeds distribution with multiple preferred-class participation rights, liquidation preferences, and conversion economics.
Stock-based compensation expense recognition per ASC 718 using Black-Scholes or lattice models, with forfeiture and modification accounting.
Employee-facing portal for grant acceptance, vesting visibility, exercise workflows, and tax-document access.
Tender offers, employee liquidity programs, and shareholder-initiated secondary transfers with board-approval workflow.
End-to-end fund-vehicle setup: entity formation, EIN application, banking onboarding, templated LPA. Unique to bundled emerging-manager platforms; not present in modular FUND-ADMIN.
Simplified KYC/AML and subscription document workflow for small LP bases (typically <50 LPs).
Simplified capital-call workflow for single-fund, single-class structures without European-tier catchup complexity.
Single-deal special-purpose-vehicle creation, templated docs, and ongoing admin. Dominant vehicle below ~$25M deal size.
Basic shareholder ledger and grant tracking for the GP entity and portfolio cap-table awareness; not the full ASC 718 / 409A / exit-waterfall machinery of standalone CAP-TABLE.
Simplified LP-facing portal for statements and notices, scoped to single-fund structures.

Pre-employment background, identity, and reference checks: criminal history, employment verification, education verification, drug screening, credit checks where lawful. FCRA / EU GDPR adverse-action workflows. Today linked to ATS only; cross-cutting candidate (also relevant in FSM contractor onboarding, PRM/TPRM partner screening) once those domains run Phase B.
Detect SaaS applications in use across the org via SSO logs, expense data, browser plugins, network traffic, and contract feeds.
Identify unsanctioned SaaS usage outside the official catalog; triage and promote candidates to sanctioned status or block.
Track per-user and per-feature engagement across the SaaS portfolio; identify dormant licenses, low-adoption apps, and engagement trends.
Right-size license tiers; reclaim idle licenses; downgrade where usage permits; flag over-provisioning before renewal.
Automated provisioning and deprovisioning workflows tied to SSO, HR joiner-mover-leaver events, and role changes.
Track renewal calendar across the SaaS portfolio; coordinate with procurement and legal; negotiate terms and quantity adjustments before auto-renewal.
Centralize vendor contacts, contracts, SLAs, and historical engagement across the SaaS portfolio.
Authoring of plan templates, stages, task libraries, and audience targeting (role, location, employment type) for new-hire onboarding programs.
Fan-out of templated provisioning tasks to ITSM (hardware), IGA (access), IWMS (workspace), and LMS (compliance training), with status reconciliation.
Intake, validation, and storage of new-hire forms (I-9, W-4, NDA, direct-deposit, tax forms), often with e-signature.
Pre-boarding communications, day-one nudges, cohort kick-offs, and multi-channel welcome cadences.
Buddy or mentor pairing for new hires, intro meeting scheduling, and ongoing check-in cadence.
30/60/90-day milestones, manager nudges, completion signals, and reporting on time-to-productivity.

Treating the same hardware model, software title, or SaaS app consistently across HAM, SAM, SMP, and FINOPS feeds. Depends on normalized reference-data libraries that map raw discovery strings to canonical product, version, and edition records.

Management of contracts that span multiple asset types: a single agreement covering hardware leases, software licenses, SaaS bundles, and cloud commitments. Avoids the per-sub-domain split where HAM, SAM, and SMP each carry their own contract record.
Single event stream across asset types tracking acquisition, assignment, transfer, and retirement. Acts as the cross-asset audit trail and feeds downstream reporting.
Portfolio-level cost reporting combining HAM depreciation, SAM amortization, SMP subscription, and FINOPS cloud spend into a single TCO view per business unit, application, or service.

Matching a hardware device to its installed software, to the SaaS subscription the user holds, to the cloud user account, to the FINOPS cost line. Relies on strong reference-data layers to bridge identifiers across asset types.
Real-time on-hand, reserved, and available-to-promise quantities across warehouses, stores, hubs, and 3PL locations from a single consolidated view.
Per-unit or per-batch lot and serial-number assignment, with downstream traceability for recall, expiry, and quality investigations.
Item-level reorder-point and reorder-quantity rules that trigger replenishment suggestions or auto-generated purchase orders against suppliers or transfer requests against sister warehouses.
Periodic classification of SKUs by revenue contribution (ABC) and demand variability (XYZ), driving differentiated cycle-count frequency and safety-stock policy.
Scheduled and ad-hoc cycle counts with variance review, root-cause coding, and posted adjustments that update on-hand and trigger accounting entries.
Inter-warehouse transfers with in-transit tracking, expected receipt date, and discrepancy resolution on receipt.
Real-time ATP computation factoring on-hand, reserved, in-transit, and inbound POs against committed demand, exposing reliable promise dates to OMS and CRM consumers.
Define kit-of-SKUs bills and explode kits at order or production time, with finished-kit on-hand maintained against component on-hand.
Authoring and management of eBOM, mBOM, sBOM structures with where-used traversal, multi-level BOM editing, and effectivity by date / serial / lot.
Vaulting, check-in / check-out, version control, and viewable generation for CAD models across MCAD and ECAD authoring tools.
Engineering change request, order, and notice workflow (ECR / ECO / ECN) with impact analysis, approval routing, and effectivity propagation across BOMs and downstream systems.
Single source of truth for part numbers, classifications, attributes, units of measure, and lifecycle status, feeding ERP item master and MES.
Capture, decomposition, and end-to-end traceability of system, software, and hardware requirements through design, verification, and validation.
Option and variant modeling, configurator rules, and 150 percent BOM management for engineer-to-order, configure-to-order, and assemble-to-order products.
Authoring of mBOM, manufacturing routing, work instructions, and resource allocations bridging engineering release to shop-floor execution.
Substance-of-concern tracking, supplier declarations, and reporting for RoHS, REACH, conflict minerals, PFAS, and similar product-substance regulations.
Multi-year headcount, position, and skill demand modeling driven by business strategy, growth assumptions, and productivity targets.
Internal-mobility, retirement curve, attrition baseline, and gap reconciliation modeling that builds the supply side of the workforce plan.
What-if scenario modeling (growth, restructure, geography shift, skill pivot, cost optimization) with cascade analysis into HCM, EPM, and downstream cost projections.
Identify capability shortfalls between current workforce skills inventory and future-state demand, with prioritized build / buy / borrow recommendations.
External labor-market data overlay: salary medians, supply-demand index, attrition baselines, and competitive intelligence by job family and location.
Org-structure modeling, reporting-line alternatives, span-of-control optimization, and approved org designs that cascade into HCM org changes.
Loaded-comp cost projections by cost_center, job_profile, and location across the planning horizon, with handoff to EPM for the consolidated budget.
Reconciliation of workforce plans against actuals (HCM headcount, WFM time-and-attendance, ATS requisition fill rate) to drive plan refresh cycles.
Centralized registry of enterprise applications with ownership, lifecycle stage, technology fit and metadata. The portfolio's canonical record.
Multi-dimensional value scoring (Tolerate, Invest, Migrate, Eliminate) over portfolio applications to drive rationalization decisions.
Total cost of ownership tracking per application across infrastructure, licenses, support and people. Bridges to FINOPS and IT cost analytics.
Inventory of integration points between applications: APIs, file transfers, ETL jobs, event streams. Surfaces interface dependencies for impact analysis.
Tracks technology platforms (frameworks, runtimes, databases, vendor stacks) across standard, emerging, declining and retired lifecycle stages. Drives tech-stack rationalization.
Definition and cascading of multi-year and annual strategic objectives down through org levels, with owner assignment, weighting, and progress measurement.
Balanced-scorecard and strategy-house visualization linking strategic pillars to objectives, initiatives, and measures across financial, customer, process, and learning perspectives.
Cross-functional strategic initiative registers with sponsor, owner, milestones, RAID logs, status reporting, and impact attribution to strategic objectives.
Orchestration of QBR, MBR, and weekly business review cadences with agenda templates, structured commentary capture, action-item tracking, and decision logs.

Bidirectional traceability between execution work (initiatives, OKRs, projects) and strategic intent, enabling drill-down from board-level objectives to operational deliverables and rollup in the reverse direction.
Capacity, headcount, and budget allocation traced to strategic priorities. Overlaps Strategic Portfolio Management where present, the SEM lens is strategy-office-led, the SPM lens is PMO-led.

Automated discovery of infrastructure CIs (servers, network gear, virtual machines, cloud resources) via probes, agents, and cloud APIs; ingestion into the CMDB with reconciliation against existing records.
Authoring and maintenance of the CI class hierarchy, attribute definitions, and validation rules that define the shape of every CI record.
Modeling dependencies, containment, and runtime relationships between CIs to enable impact analysis and root-cause traversal.
Mapping business services to their underlying infrastructure CIs, producing dynamic application service maps used by ITSM impact analysis and AIOPS correlation.
Capturing pre-change CI baselines, comparing live configuration against captured snapshots, and flagging unauthorized deviations as drift events.
Stewardship workflows, data-quality KPIs, audit trails, and ownership assignment for every CI class so that the CMDB stays trustworthy as the system of record.
Merging CI records from multiple discovery feeds (Discovery, RMM, NPMD, DCIM, cloud APIs) into a single authoritative record without duplicates or conflicts.
Channel-based persistent messages with threading, mentions, reactions, and edit history. Distinct from ephemeral chat (CCAAS) and from knowledge artifacts (KMS).
Ad-hoc and scheduled voice/video drop-in meetings anchored to a channel or DM.
Inviting and managing external guests (partners, vendors, customers) into channels with scoped access controls.
Federated search across messages, files, and threads; configurable retention windows and legal-hold preservation.
Promoting a chat thread to a downstream work item (ITSM ticket, support session, MSP-PSA case) without losing context.
Posting files and link previews into channels, with optional handoff to ECM for governed storage.
Real-time presence, custom status, do-not-disturb, and timezone-aware availability across channels.

Template-driven contract drafting with clause-library lookup. Authoring layer that assembles new contracts from approved templates and clauses, captures party metadata, and produces the initial draft for negotiation.

Curated repository of approved clauses with version control, fallback positions, and approval workflows. The clause library is the artifact CLM-CONTRACT-AUTHORING consumes; managing it (draft / review / approve / deprecate clauses) is a distinct surface.
Track-changes negotiation workflow with counterparty exchange, version comparison, and approval routing. Distinct from authoring (creating the draft) and repository (the executed record).
ML-driven clause comparison against the approved library to flag non-standard language, missing protections, and high-risk terms during negotiation. Augments human review; does not replace it.
Executed-contract index with search, metadata management, full-text retrieval, and lifecycle tracking from signed through expired/renewed/terminated. The system of record post-signature.
Automated extraction of obligations (deliverables, SLA commitments, payment terms, renewal triggers) from executed contracts. Populates the obligations register for ongoing tracking.

Date-based renewal alerting, auto-renewal-clause detection, renewal-vs-replace decision support, and renewal execution. Distinct from amendments (in-term changes); renewals extend or replace the term.

Court date capture from electronic court records, jurisdiction-specific deadline calculation, statute-of-limitations alerting, and electronic filing (ECF) integration. Often a separate enterprise module in litigation practice.
Attribute completion, marketing copy generation, description authoring (often AI-augmented), spec-sheet ingestion, and brand-voice consistency across the merchandising catalog.

Image, video, 3D model, and document asset linking to products with rights metadata, renditions, and CDN distribution. The DAM slice that lives inside PIM in v1; can be promoted to its own domain later.
Multi-tree taxonomy management (merchandising tree, channel-specific trees, ERP category tree), attribute-group definitions, and faceted-navigation classification used by storefronts and feeds.

Per-channel feed shaping for marketplaces, search-engine product feeds, e-commerce storefronts, retailer feeds, and GDSN datapools; validation against destination schemas, syndication-job orchestration, and publish-result tracking.
Locale-specific attribute and description variants, translation workflow (machine + human), region-specific imagery overrides, and locale-aware publishing.
Supplier data-sheet ingestion (spreadsheets, GS1 GDSN feeds, supplier portals), schema mapping from supplier vocabularies to internal attributes, and supplier-data quality scoring.
Region-specific regulatory attribute management (REACH, RoHS, Prop 65, FDA, CE), compliance declaration tracking, and gating of publish on regulatory completeness.
Review-and-approve gates before publish, role-based work queues for content editors and merchandisers, and audit trail of attribute changes for regulated merchandising.
End-to-end workflow for raising, approving, and provisioning entitlement requests (joiner, mover, ad-hoc), including pre-flight SoD checks and approval routing.
Periodic recertification campaigns where reviewers (managers, application owners) attest to or revoke user entitlements. Generates audit-grade evidence for GRC.
Rule-based and ML-driven detection of toxic entitlement combinations across systems, with mitigation workflow and accepted-risk tracking.
Catalog and lifecycle of access primitives (roles, groups, permission sets, birthright bundles) used by access requests and SoD rules.
SCIM, REST, and proprietary connectors that create, modify, suspend, and delete accounts in downstream applications on receipt of an approved access request or lifecycle event.
Check-out, check-in, holds, renewals, and fines management for circulating library materials.
Authoring, importing, and maintaining bibliographic, authority, and holdings records in MARC21 or BIBFRAME, including authority control against external files.
Ordering, receiving, and invoicing of library materials from book vendors, including approval plans, firm orders, and EDI integration.
Registration, profile management, and lifecycle of library members including patron categories, privileges, and card issuance.
Public-facing search and browse experience over the library catalog and licensed resources, including faceted search, holdings display, and self-service holds.
Subscription management, check-in, claiming, and binding workflows for periodicals and other continuing resources.
License tracking, access management, usage statistics, and renewal workflows for ebook, ejournal, and database subscriptions.
Borrowing and lending of materials between libraries, including request routing, status tracking, and resource sharing consortia management.
Real-time assignment of work orders to technicians under skill, parts, SLA, geography, and travel-time constraints. Optimizer rebuilds the day's route plan on every dispatch change.
Offline-tolerant mobile experience for field technicians: route view, work-order detail, parts lookup, time and material capture, customer signature, and photo upload. Reconciles when reconnected.

records.capability_name: Field Parts and Truck Stock Management
records.description: Per-technician truck-stock tracking, parts requisition from warehouse, return processing, and just-in-time replenishment ahead of scheduled visits.
Recurring service agreement lifecycle: drafting, activation, renewal, expiry. SLA term tracking (response time, mean time to repair) and entitlement enforcement on work orders.

Asset register of customer-owned equipment the service organization installs and maintains. Tracks model, serial, install date, warranty, location, and operational status. Out-of-service and decommissioned states preserve history without losing the record.
Recurring PM schedule per installed equipment unit. Drives proactive work-order generation when service is due; surfaces overdue and skipped cycles for escalation.
Curate the skill universe, synonyms, hierarchies, and skill-to-job-role mappings.
Define role-anchored bundles of skills plus required proficiency levels, job-architecture adjacent.
Derive worker skills from resumes, job history, completed learning, and work-activity signals.
Self, manager, peer, and test-based proficiency rating against a defined scale.
Compare current workforce skill inventory against required-role profiles to surface shortages.
Org-wide views of skill density, scarcity, and distribution by team, region, or job family.
Workflows for endorsing or contesting inferred or self-claimed skills.
Posts gigs, projects, stretch roles, full-time openings; routes employees to them.
Matches mentees to mentors by skill, aspiration, and location.
AI-derived match score between a person's skill profile and a role's required skills.
Personalized recommendations of next moves for each employee.
Ranks ready-now, ready-soon, ready-later candidates for critical roles.
Generates lateral, diagonal, and vertical pathways from current role to aspiration.
Re-ranks external applicants by inferred skill fit; surfaces internal alternatives.
Org-level visualization of skill supply, demand, gaps, and risk.
Scheduling, instructor assignment, attendance capture, and virtual-classroom integration for instructor-led and virtual-instructor-led training.
Catalog of certifications and badges, certificate template management, CEU tracking, and learner credential lifecycle.
Dynamic audiences, automated training assignment rules, learner notifications, manager nudges, and overdue escalation policies.
Learner data privacy substrate: consent capture, subject access requests, and right-to-erasure processing for training data.

Structured request intake via forms that produce work_items in the target queue with field-mapping, triage rules, and conditional routing. Asana Forms, Monday Forms, ClickUp Forms, Workfront Request Queues, Smartsheet Forms.

Group related events, alerts, and signals from across the monitored estate into a single correlated incident using ML and pattern analysis, so responders see one issue instead of a flood of raw alerts.
Detect deviations from learned baselines across metrics, logs, and traces, flagging outliers and abnormal behavior that fixed thresholds would miss.
Deduplicate, suppress, and silence flapping or low-value alerts, including during planned changes, so on-call teams are paged only on signals that matter.
Infer the probable root cause of a correlated incident from topology, change, and signal evidence, so responders start from an answer rather than a blank screen.
Forecast outages, capacity exhaustion, and error storms ahead of impact by elevating predictive signals and high-confidence incident predictions into proactive workflows.
Train, retrain, and monitor the detection and prediction models behind the platform, watching for drift so the signal stays accurate as the environment changes.
Authoritative model of the physical estate: sites, rooms, rows, cabinets, racks, and rack-unit occupancy, recording what is installed, where it sits, and how much space remains.

End-to-end power path from incoming circuit through distribution units and uninterruptible supplies down to the outlet, with phase balance, redundancy, and draw against rated capacity tracked at each link.
Modeling of cooling units, thermal zones, and airflow alongside cabinet-level temperature and humidity, keeping equipment inside its operating envelope.
Continuous capture of sensor telemetry (temperature, humidity, smoke, water leak, airflow) with threshold alarming routed to the teams and systems that must act.
Forward-looking projection of power, cooling, space, and bandwidth headroom per site and zone, with what-if modeling to schedule growth and justify build-outs.
Port-by-port and cable-by-cable map of physical connectivity, including patch panels and trunk runs, feeding the configuration database and network operations.
Structured request, approval, and execution of equipment installs, decommissions, and relocations across the floor, keeping the live model in step with physical reality.

Unified ingestion of voice, chat, email, SMS, and social interactions into skills-based queues, with automatic call distribution (ACD) that matches each contact to the best-fit available agent by skill, priority, and customer tier. Includes queue prioritization, overflow, and routing-profile administration.

Visual flow runtime for interactive voice response menus, callback offers, and digital self-service that authenticate, collect intent, deflect simple requests, and hand off to a live queue when needed. Covers prompt design, DTMF and speech capture, and flow versioning.

The agent workspace that presents the connected interaction with cross-channel customer context, controls for hold, transfer, conference, and consult, after-call wrap-up, and disposition coding. Tracks agent presence and availability states that feed routing and adherence.

Capture and retention of voice recordings and transcripts (and screen capture where licensed) across interactions, with consent handling, pause/resume for sensitive data, and retention policy enforcement so recordings are available for quality, dispute, and compliance review.

Supervisor review and scoring of recorded interactions against evaluation forms, calibration across evaluators, and coaching assignment to close performance gaps. Drives agent improvement plans tied to disposition and outcome data.

Live queue and agent dashboards with service-level, abandon-rate, and occupancy metrics and threshold alerting, plus historical reporting aggregated by queue, agent, skill, and disposition for trend analysis and staffing decisions.

Tracking of agent state changes and time-in-state against expected schedules to measure adherence and auxiliary-time breaches, surfacing intraday staffing signals. Consumes forecasts and schedules mastered in the workforce-management domain rather than owning them.

Authenticated and unauthenticated assessment of endpoints, servers, network gear, cloud workloads, containers, and web apps to detect security weaknesses, producing per-asset findings matched to a vulnerability definition.
A maintained catalog of known vulnerability definitions (CVE, vendor advisories, plugin/check metadata, affected products, base severity) that incoming findings are matched against and enriched from.
Layering exploit-prediction signals, known-exploited and active-attack intelligence, asset criticality, and exposure on top of base severity to produce a ranked queue answering what to fix first.
Routing prioritized findings to the owning team as remediation work with due dates, ownership, SLAs, and patch or configuration guidance, tracked to completion.
A governed, time-boxed path to formally accept, defer, or mark as false-positive vulnerabilities the business chooses not to fix, with approver sign-off and expiry-driven re-review.
Re-scanning to confirm fixes landed, reopening regressions, and closing findings only on verified evidence so the loop is auditable end to end.
Defensible reporting on scanning cadence, mean-time-to-remediate, and exception approvals against framework obligations such as PCI-DSS, FedRAMP, and NIS2.
Scoping a vulnerability assessment or remediation campaign over an asset population for a point-in-time posture snapshot, audit window, or program milestone.
Connect and crawl heterogeneous intranet platforms (SharePoint and Viva, Staffbase, Simpplr, WordPress) as governed sources.
Discover and register pages, hubs, spaces, libraries, and forms across connected intranets into a single map.
Detect stale, broken-link, duplicate, and low-readability content for the internal audience.
Scan internal content against accessibility standards and surface owner-mapped issues.
Assign every inventory item an accountable owner and backup with a defined review cadence.
Periodic owner attestation that content is current, with flag-stale, remediate, or archive outcomes.
Drive content from live through review-due to archived per policy and content-type retention rules.
Maintain a prioritized improvement backlog that embeds Work Management for execution.
Crawl and scan source systems to discover datasets and capture technical metadata (schema, format, owner, record counts, storage location) into the catalog.
Author, review, publish, and steward business-language definitions of concepts, linking terms to physical data assets.
Capture and present end-to-end column-level lineage between data assets, with impact analysis on schema or pipeline changes.
Automatically detect and apply sensitivity tags (PII, PCI, PHI, confidential) to data assets, routed through a steward approval workflow.
Assign stewards and owners to assets and terms, track responsibility, and run escalation when stewardship gaps or issues arise.
Surface data-quality rule results and trust scores in-context on catalog assets; the quality engine itself is mastered by the Data Quality domain and consumed here.
Run the attestation workflow by which a data owner certifies an asset as fit for production use, with grant, validity period, and revocation.
Package, publish, and list governed data products with explicit contracts (schema, SLA, owner, access policy) for consumer teams.
Author data access policies and route data-access requests through policy evaluation and a single accountable approver.
Map data assets, classifications, and processing activities to statutory obligations (records of processing, retention, lineage evidence) for compliance reporting.
Centralized intake of ideas, requests, and project proposals through standardized forms, with screening and routing into the portfolio funnel.
Scoring of candidate initiatives on business value, cost, risk, and strategic alignment to prioritize what gets funded.
Grouping of funded initiatives into portfolios that roll up to corporate strategy, with rebalancing as priorities shift.
Scheduling of roadmap items across time horizons with their dependencies and contingencies in view.
Mapping and surfacing of inter-initiative and cross-roadmap dependency chains that put delivery at risk.
Tracking of realized benefits against the business case that justified each investment, including at-risk and written-off outcomes.
Committing of people, budget, and capacity to initiatives against available supply, with conflict detection.
What-if modeling of alternative investment and capacity mixes, compared side by side before a commitment is made.

Search and present air, hotel, rail, and ground options filtered and ranked by the organization's travel policy, surfacing in-policy choices and flagging out-of-policy selections at the point of booking.
Aggregate bookable travel content from GDS, NDC, and direct-supplier sources into a unified shopping surface, including ancillaries and negotiated rates.
Create, hold, modify, and cancel reservations across air, hotel, rail, and car at the reservation-record level, managing fulfillment and ticketing.
Assemble booked segments into a single trip itinerary the traveler can view and change, keeping the journey synchronized as segments are added, modified, or disrupted.
Maintain per-traveler profiles holding preferences, loyalty memberships, travel documents, and emergency contacts that personalize shopping and satisfy identity requirements.
Route proposed and booked trips for pre-trip authorization based on policy, cost thresholds, and destination risk, capturing approvals and exception justifications.
Monitor where travelers are against destination risk intelligence, raise alerts on emerging threats, and support locating and assisting travelers during disruptions and emergencies.
Track unused and partially used tickets and travel credits, and reapply them to future bookings so prepaid value is recovered rather than lost.
Building and maintaining the annual and quarterly marketing plan as a hierarchy of plan lines tied to objectives, owners, and time periods.
Top-down allocation of marketing budget across plans, plan lines, campaigns, and channels, with approval governance on each allocation.
Capturing committed and actual marketing spend and reconciling it against allocated budget at the plan-line grain to show remaining budget and variance.
A shared campaign and content calendar that lays out marketing activity across time, teams, and channels for visibility and coordination.
Plan-level performance and marketing-ROI measurement, linking results and pipeline contribution back to the plans and budgets that funded them.
Capture, investigate, and close out workplace injuries, illnesses, near-misses, and unsafe conditions, including root-cause analysis and recordability determination.
Identify workplace hazards and assess their likelihood and consequence through job hazard analyses, job safety analyses, and risk registers.
Assign, track, and verify corrective and preventive actions arising from incidents, inspections, audits, and findings.
Track environmental permits, their conditions and limits, renewals, and monitoring obligations for air, water, and waste.
Plan, schedule, and conduct safety inspections, observations, and management-system audits against standards such as ISO 45001 and ISO 14001.

records.capability_name: Chemical and Safety Data Sheet Management
records.description: Maintain the chemical inventory, hazardous-substance register, and safety data sheets, with exposure limits and hazard communication.
Manage medical surveillance, exposure records, fitness-for-duty evaluations, and occupational medical case management.
Prequalify, qualify, and monitor contractors and third parties against safety criteria tied to access and permit-to-work.
Track emissions and release records, environmental aspect and impact registers, and regulatory environmental reporting obligations.
Plan, deliver, and record EHS training, competency, and certification, mapping required training to roles and regulations.
Plan and record industrial-hygiene sampling and exposure monitoring against occupational exposure limits for chemical, noise, and other agents.

Recognize, measure, and report lessee leases under US GAAP ASC 842, including the finance-versus-operating classification, balance-sheet recognition of operating leases, and the required quantitative and qualitative disclosures.

Recognize and measure lessee leases under the IFRS 16 single lessee model, where all leases are treated like finance leases, with the low-value and short-term exemptions and the IFRS-specific disclosure schedule.

Apply the classification tests that determine accounting treatment: finance versus operating for ASC 842 lessees and the lessor buckets, capturing the classification rationale and re-testing on modification.
Compute the initial and ongoing right-of-use asset and lease liability balances, including the discount rate applied, amortization and effective-interest schedules, and the period expense.
Account for lease modifications, remeasurements, and reassessments: scope and consideration changes, discount-rate updates, index and rate true-ups, and right-of-use asset impairment.

Produce the lease-accounting footnote disclosures: weighted-average discount rate and remaining term, maturity analysis of undiscounted cash flows, lease cost by type, and the reconciliations the standards require.

Maintain the lease record system: agreements and components, leased assets, critical dates and alerts, renewals and terminations, payment terms, and the underlying lease documents that source the accounting.
Maintain a lifecycle record for each animal: identity, breed, sex, status, parentage, and history of weights, treatments, and movements.
Organize animals into mobs (groups) and manage them collectively for movements, treatments, and pasture allocation.
Record movements of mobs between paddocks, properties, and external destinations, with date, count, and reason.
Capture weigh sessions and compute average daily gain and growth curves over time for animals and mobs.
Track joining, pregnancy, calving and lambing, sires and dams, and birth weights across the breeding cycle.
Record vaccinations, treatments, and medicine administrations with batch numbers and withholding periods that gate sale and slaughter eligibility.
Allocate pasture, plan rotational grazing with rest periods, and match stocking rate to paddock carrying capacity.
Manage electronic and visual identifiers and traceable movement records to meet the national livestock-identification scheme in the operation's jurisdiction.

Plan, structure, launch, and manage paid social campaigns, ad sets, and ads across multiple ad platforms from a single control surface, keeping objectives, schedules, and placements consistent across Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, and other social ad channels.
Combinatorially generate and test creative variants from modular assets and product feeds, then weight delivery toward the best-performing combinations automatically.
Continuously redistribute spend across ad sets and campaigns on pacing and return signals, enforcing budget caps and minimizing wasted spend.
Track creative as versioned assets with named variants, approval state, and platform-specific renditions so teams can iterate, roll back, and audit creative changes.

Attribute conversions to paid social touchpoints via server-side conversion APIs and measure true incremental lift through holdout and conversion-lift testing rather than relying solely on platform-reported numbers.
Build, sync, and govern custom, lookalike, and suppression audiences across ad platforms, including audience refresh from CRM and CDP sources.
Continuous behavior-based risk scoring of insiders from multi-source activity against per-user baselines.
Detection of unusual file, email, cloud, and removable-media data movement that signals exfiltration or misuse.
Correlation of policy violations and indicators of compromise into prioritized, deduplicated insider-risk alerts.
Case-based investigation of insider threats with activity timelines, file-lineage forensics, and analyst workflows.

records.capability_name: Evidence Collection for HR and Legal
records.description: Defensible collection, preservation, and packaging of investigation evidence for HR and Legal review.

entity.description: Intra-domain lifecycle state per master `data_object` (`applied`, `screening`, `pending_approval`, `approved`, `hired`, `rejected`). Drives derivation of workflow-gate permissions and the §1 behavioral-pattern prose in per-domain fact sheets. Required for `master + required` data_objects on every new domain load (Rule #12).

computed_fields.name: data_object_lifecycle_state_label
computed_fields.description: Composed: <data_object_name>.<state_name>. Recomputed on write so renames flow through.

fields.title: Data Object
fields.description: The master data_object this state belongs to.

fields.title: State Name
fields.description: snake_case state identifier (`applied`, `screening`, `pending_approval`, `approved`, `hired`, `rejected`). Combines with `data_object_name` to form the composed label.

fields.title: State Order
fields.description: Sort order for fact-sheet rendering. Lower = earlier in lifecycle.

fields.title: Description
fields.description: What this state means (e.g. `pending_approval = offer drafted, awaiting hiring manager sign-off`).

fields.title: Is Initial
fields.description: TRUE for the entry state (typically one per data_object).

fields.title: Is Terminal
fields.description: TRUE for terminal states (no outgoing transitions).

fields.title: Requires Permission
fields.description: TRUE when transitioning into this state requires a workflow gate. Drives derivation of `<slug>:<verb>_<entity>` permissions in the fact sheet.

fields.title: Permission Verb Override
fields.description: Optional. Overrides the auto-derived verb when `requires_permission=true`. Default verb is `state_name` (`approved → approve`); override when the natural verb differs (`hired → hire_candidate`).

fields.title: Realizing Module
fields.description: A state may be realized only when a specific module is installed (e.g. `job_applications.interviewing` is only reachable if `ATS-INTERVIEWS` is deployed). States from un-deployed modules are pruned at deploy time. NULL when the state is reachable in all deployments. See plan-modules.md §7.4.

fields.title: Process
fields.description: The process whose gated transition this lifecycle state realizes (process-to-permission edge).

records.description: Pre-hire stub created during requisition or onboarding handoff; not yet a worker of record.
Worker is currently employed and appears in headcount, payroll eligibility, and directory feeds.
Employee is on approved leave (parental, medical, sabbatical); active record but suppressed from some downstream feeds.
Employment temporarily halted (investigation, disciplinary); pay and access may be paused.
Employment ended (voluntary or involuntary); final pay processed, access deprovisioned.
Contract is being authored; terms still editable by HR or hiring manager.
Locked for review; sent to legal/HR approver for sign-off.
Cleared for execution; ready to be sent to candidate/employee for signature.
Both parties have signed; contract is in force.
Contract ended (resignation, dismissal, expiry of fixed term, mutual release).
Replaced by a newer contract (promotion, role change, addendum supplanting prior terms).
Event is being prepared (effective date, reason code, new values); editable.
Locked and routed to the configured approver for the event type.
Approver has signed off; event ready to post to the employee record.
Event applied to the worker record; downstream feeds (payroll, IGA, PA) notified.

entity.description: The canonical entity-relationship graph between data objects, independent of any specific solution's implementation. Captures directed relationships like User owns Asset (1:N, composition), Customer places Order (1:N, reference), Employee works on Project (M:N, association), Customer is a Person (1:1, inheritance). Carries both cardinality (Cardinality) and structural kind (Kind) so the catalog distinguishes ownership from loose reference from peer association from subtype. Self-references are allowed (User directly manages User).

computed_fields.name: data_object_relationship_label
computed_fields.description: Composed from the source data object name, the relationship verb, and the target data object name. Recomputed on every write so renames in either parent flow through.

fields.title: From Data Object
fields.description: The source / subject side of the relationship

fields.title: To Data Object
fields.description: The target / object side of the relationship

fields.title: Owner Side
fields.description: Which side of the relationship is the PARENT (the lifecycle owner / cascade root). `source` = the row identified by `data_object_id` is the parent and cascades into the related object on delete; `target` = the related object is the parent and owns the lifecycle. Drives the architect delete-mode derivation downstream (a composition / parent edge becomes a Semantius `parent` FK with cascade; the child side is deleted with its parent). Note: `owner` here means the parent side; it is a domain-map catalog concept, not a Semantius platform primitive.

fields.title: Cardinality
fields.description: Standard ER cardinality between the two data objects

fields.title: Kind
fields.description: Structural role of the relationship, orthogonal to cardinality: `composition` (parent owns child, cascade), `reference` (loose link, no cascade), `association` (peer-to-peer M:N), `inheritance` (subtype / IS-A)

fields.title: Verb
fields.description: Parent-voice verb describing the relationship (owns, manages, places, is assigned to)

fields.title: Inverse Verb
fields.description: Reverse-direction phrasing for navigation (is owned by, reports to)

fields.title: Required
fields.description: PRESENCE-CONDITIONAL (plan-4): a mandatory FK only WHEN the target entity is installed in the deploying unit; it never forces the target to install. The always-present case is expressed by setting the target entity necessity=required (Rule #16), not by this flag. A required edge to an absent target carries no constraint (required-if-present).

entity.description: The canonical data subjects an enterprise stores records about (Customer, Employee, Product, Asset, Order, Invoice, ...). One record per canonical concept; industry-specific or solution-specific naming variations live in the aliases entity.

fields.title: Kind
fields.description: Discriminator for catalog-owned data objects (`domain_owned`, default) vs platform built-ins seeded for relationship-graph completeness (`platform_builtin`, e.g. the `users` row). Platform built-ins do not appear in domain-level analytics but participate in `data_object_relationships`.

fields.title: Entity Type
fields.description: Classification of what kind of entity this is. Drives the Rule #12 lifecycle-state audit: only operational_workflow without lifecycle states surfaces as a gap; everything else passes whether stateful or stateless. Values: operational_workflow (has business workflow, needs lifecycle states + gates), operational_record (per-X record without workflow, e.g. notes, files, acknowledgements, log entries), catalog (config / template / taxonomy referenced by other entities; may carry a publishing lifecycle), junction (N:M link, may carry a qualifier and its own lifecycle), computed (derived rollup; lifecycle implicit in source), unclassified (default; surfaces to audit until set).

fields.title: Singular Label
fields.description: Human-friendly singular form (`Job Requisition`, `Customer`). Replaces `display_label` for fact-sheet output. The legacy `display_label` column is retained transitionally (see plan-domain-fact-sheets.md § 9.1 Step 10).

fields.title: Plural Label
fields.description: Human-friendly plural form (`Job Requisitions`, `Customers`). Required going forward.

fields.title: Catalog Description
fields.description: Short reader-facing summary of this data object (1 to 2 sentences) for the catalog Entity summary surface. Plain descriptive voice (what the entity is), distinct from the analyst-facing `description`. Empty by default; fill the empty field freely, but never overwrite a non-empty value without explicit user approval (Rule #20 shape).

fields.title: Canonical Bare-Word
fields.description: TRUE when this domain holds catalog-wide canonical authority for an unprefixed noun (e.g. ATS owns `candidates`, CRM owns `customers`). Required when `data_object_name` is a bare word; without it, naming-arbitration (Rule #9) forces a domain prefix.

fields.title: Naming Authority Rationale
fields.description: Required when `is_canonical_bare_word=true`. Explains why this domain owns the unprefixed name and which adjacent domains defer to it. Surfaced in the fact sheet to prevent future collision-prone proposals.

fields.title: Has Personal Content
fields.description: Pattern flag — TRUE when this data_object holds per-user-scoped content (e.g. interview feedback, peer reviews). Drives derivation of `<slug>:view_all_<entity>` / `<slug>:manage_all_<entity>` override permissions and an `<entity>_edit_scope` business rule in the fact sheet.

fields.title: Notes
fields.description: Free-form catalog-curator notes on this data_object. Empty by default per Rule #15; populate only with explicit per-row user approval. Acceptable content when authored: (1) isolated-master justification when this master legitimately has no edges to other masters in its domain (B6 exemption); (2) self-explanatory-name justification when a master is intentionally aliased-free (B11 exemption); (3) any other catalog-quality annotation that does not fit description / minimum_embedded_shape / naming_authority_rationale. The config-shape exemption for masters with no real workflow has moved to data_objects.entity_type (Rule #12); do not record it here. Per-domain notes belong on domain_data_objects.notes, not here.
