records.notes:
### Authoring note: minimum embedded-shape contract (archived 2026-05-23)

This contract was originally stored in the (removed) `minimum_embedded_shape` column. Field-level constraints on embedded shells are now enforced by the deployer at deploy time against the canonical entity's `fields` metadata; this note is preserved as authoring intent only.

Minimum embedded-shape contract for `candidates` — every module that embedded_masters this data_object MUST include these fields in its local-master shell. Modules may extend with additional fields; they may not omit any of these.

- `id` — primary key, unique within the local shell.
- `legal_name` — GDPR-relevant subject identifier; required for adverse-action notices and offer documents.
- `email` — primary contact; required for every outbound communication (offers, scorecard requests, adverse-action).
- `phone` — fallback contact channel; required for background-check vendor handoffs.
- `primary_source_id` — FK to `recruitment_sources` (or NULL on direct applications); required for source-attribution analytics and referral-bonus eligibility.
- `consent_status` — GDPR/CCPA-relevant; required to gate processing of personal data when the canonical master is not deployed (the embedded shell otherwise has no consent surface).
- `created_at` — required to compute time-to-* metrics consistently across modules.

When the canonical master `ATS-CANDIDATE-CRM` is installed, the full required set of `candidates` is a superset of this minimum (additional fields: middle_name, address, work_authorization, source_attribution_details, …). Modules deployed without the canonical master see only the minimum.

records.catalog_description: Candidate submissions against a specific requisition, with pipeline stage, status, source, and full evaluation history.
records.notes:
### Authoring note: minimum embedded-shape contract (archived 2026-05-23)

This contract was originally stored in the (removed) `minimum_embedded_shape` column. Field-level constraints on embedded shells are now enforced by the deployer at deploy time against the canonical entity's `fields` metadata; this note is preserved as authoring intent only.

Minimum embedded-shape contract for `job_applications` — the junction record between a candidate and a requisition with the pipeline-stage lifecycle. Modules that embedded_master applications need the junction-key subset:

- `id` — primary key.
- `candidate_id` — FK to `candidates`; required (the "who" of the application).
- `requisition_id` — FK to `job_requisitions`; required (the "what" of the application).
- `current_stage` — current pipeline lifecycle state (`applied`, `screening`, `interviewing`, `offer_extended`, `hired`, `rejected`, `withdrawn`); required for any module-level workflow that branches on stage (ATS-INTERVIEWS reads this to know when an interview can be scheduled).
- `applied_at` — required for time-to-* metrics and SLA enforcement.

The canonical master `ATS-RECRUITMENT-PIPELINE` extends with source_attribution, screening_result, rejection_reason, etc. — modules deployed standalone see only the junction-key subset.

records.description: Channel a candidate came from: job board, referral, agency, sourcing campaign, career event, or inbound. Used for source-of-hire analytics and channel ROI.
records.catalog_description: Channels a candidate came from, such as job board, referral, agency, campaign, or inbound, used for source-of-hire and channel analytics.
records.notes: Config-shaped; no per-record workflow. Sources are configured once (job_board, employee_referral, agency, career_fair, social, etc.) and edited inline. The meaningful state transitions live as attribution events on candidates, not on the source record itself.

records.description: Employee-submitted candidate suggestion linked to a requisition. Tracks the referring employee, candidate, status, and any payable bonus.
records.catalog_description: Employee-submitted candidate suggestions linked to a requisition, tracking the referring employee, candidate, status, and any payable bonus.

records.description: Curated segment or pipeline of candidates kept warm for future roles (e.g. silver medallists, alumni, target-school grads, hard-to-fill skill clusters).
records.catalog_description: Curated pools of candidates kept warm for future roles, such as past finalists, alumni, and hard-to-fill skill clusters.

records.description: Scheduled assessment event between a candidate and one or more interviewers. Carries time, location/medium, panel, interview kit, and outcome.
records.catalog_description: Scheduled assessment events between a candidate and one or more interviewers, with time, location, panel, and outcome.
records.naming_authority_rationale: ATS owns 'interviews' as the canonical hiring-interview concept in business software.

records.description: Structured interviewer feedback against a defined rubric: per-competency ratings, written notes, and a hire/no-hire recommendation.
records.catalog_description: Structured interviewer feedback against a rubric: per-competency ratings, written notes, and a hire or no-hire recommendation.

records.description: Skills, cognitive, technical, or personality test result attached to an application. Often sourced from an external assessment provider and referenced here.
records.catalog_description: Skills, cognitive, technical, or personality test results attached to an application, often sourced from an external assessment provider.

records.description: Formal employment offer extended to a candidate. Carries compensation components, start date, terms, approval chain, and status (draft / approved / sent / accepted / declined / rescinded).
records.catalog_description: Formal employment offers extended to candidates, with compensation, start date, terms, approval chain, and status.
records.notes:
### Authoring note: minimum embedded-shape contract (archived 2026-05-23)

This contract was originally stored in the (removed) `minimum_embedded_shape` column. Field-level constraints on embedded shells are now enforced by the deployer at deploy time against the canonical entity's `fields` metadata; this note is preserved as authoring intent only.

Minimum embedded-shape contract for `job_offers` — modules that embedded_master offers (`ATS-BACKGROUND-CHECKS`, `ATS-PRE-EMPLOYEE-RECORD`) need the offer-state subset:

- `id` — primary key.
- `candidate_id` — FK to `candidates`; required (offer addressee).
- `application_id` — FK to `job_applications`; required (the application this offer resolves).
- `requisition_id` — FK to `job_requisitions`; required for downstream reporting (offer-acceptance-rate by requisition).
- `state` — offer lifecycle state (`draft`, `approved`, `extended`, `accepted`, `declined`, `rescinded`); modules read this to gate their own behavior (BACKGROUND-CHECKS only runs after `extended` or `accepted`; PRE-EMPLOYEE-RECORD is only created when `state = accepted`).
- `extended_at` — required to compute time-to-accept and time-to-start metrics.

The canonical master `ATS-OFFERS` extends with compensation_components, signature_url, decline_reason, etc.

records.description: External verification result for a candidate (criminal, employment history, education, credit, identity). Status and findings typically returned by an external screening provider.
records.catalog_description: External verification results for a candidate (criminal, employment, education, credit, identity), with status and findings from a screening provider.
records.naming_authority_rationale: Background Verification is the canonical screening market and the natural home of the unprefixed name: the background check is the central object every screening product centers on, so BGV holds catalog-wide naming authority for it.

records.description: Third-party recruiter or staffing firm supplying candidates. Tracks contract terms, contact, performance, and the candidates they have submitted.
records.catalog_description: Third-party recruiters and staffing firms supplying candidates, with contract terms, contacts, performance, and submitted candidates.

records.description: Career fair, on-campus event, hackathon, or meetup used as a sourcing channel. Tracks attendees, captured leads, and event ROI.
records.catalog_description: Career fairs, campus events, hackathons, and meetups used as sourcing channels, tracking attendees, captured leads, and event return.

records.description: Reusable template defining the stages, tasks, timing, and assignees that make up an onboarding journey for a class of new hire (e.g. engineering, sales, executive, hourly retail, contractor). Plans are versioned and selected based on role / location / employment type when a journey is instantiated.
records.catalog_description: Reusable templates defining the stages, tasks, timing, and assignees for onboarding a class of new hire, versioned and selected by role, location, or type.

records.description: Instance of an onboarding plan applied to a specific new hire. Materialized when offer.accepted (ATS) or employee.created (HCM) fires. Carries the bound employee_id, assigned tasks, completion state, current stage, and milestone timestamps (pre-boarding start, Day-1 reached, 30/60/90 completion).
records.catalog_description: Live onboarding journeys for a specific new hire, carrying assigned tasks, current stage, completion state, and milestone timestamps.

records.description: Phase within a plan or journey (pre-boarding, Day-1, week-1, month-1, 30/60/90 day). Defines task grouping, expected duration, and gate conditions. Stages can be sequenced or run in parallel.
records.catalog_description: Phases within an onboarding plan or journey, such as pre-boarding or 30/60/90 day, defining task grouping, duration, and gate conditions.

records.description: Discrete to-do within a journey: sign I-9, attend orientation, complete compliance training, meet buddy, receive laptop. Carries assignee (new hire / manager / IT / facilities / HR), due date, completion state, evidence, and task type (form / training / meeting / provisioning / acknowledgment). Many tasks are local; a subset triggers cross-domain handoffs into ITSM, IWMS, Payroll, LMS, IGA, or HRSD.
records.catalog_description: Discrete to-do items within an onboarding journey, each with an assignee, due date, type, and completion state, some triggering handoffs to other systems.

records.description: Pairing of a new hire with an existing employee for the onboarding period — buddy, mentor, peer-coach, or sponsor depending on the program. Carries scope (peer / cross-functional), start and end dates, and meeting cadence.
records.catalog_description: Pairings of a new hire with an existing employee for onboarding support, with scope, start and end dates, and meeting cadence.

records.description: Group of new hires onboarding together (campus intake class, training boot-camp batch, executive cohort, frontline class). Enables shared activities (group orientation, cohort meetings) and cohort-level analytics distinct from the per-journey view.
records.catalog_description: Groups of new hires onboarding together, such as a campus class or training batch, enabling shared activities and cohort-level reporting.

records.description: Email, video, push notification, or SMS sent to a new hire during the journey — pre-boarding nudges, Day-1 schedule, post-Day-1 check-ins, cohort announcements. Carries channel, template, scheduled send time, delivery state, and engagement metrics.
records.catalog_description: Email, video, push, or SMS messages sent to a new hire during onboarding, with channel, template, scheduled send time, delivery state, and engagement metrics.

records.description: Record of paperwork collected from a new hire as part of the journey: I-9, NDA, handbook acknowledgment, direct-deposit form, country-specific tax forms, country-specific work-permit evidence. Captures signature state, external e-signature envelope reference ids, and audit metadata. Distinct from the canonical document templates, which would be mastered by a Document Management domain (not yet in catalog).
records.catalog_description: Paperwork collected from a new hire during onboarding, such as tax and eligibility forms, with signature state and e-signature envelope references.

records.description: Multi-year strategic plan covering target headcount, skills, location, and cost. The SWP umbrella entity; carries planning horizon (typically 1-5 years), base assumptions (attrition rate, hire ramp, productivity factor), approval state (draft / review / approved / published / reconciled), and pointers to the scenarios and forecasts that compose it.
records.catalog_description: Multi-year strategic workforce plans covering target headcount, skills, location, and cost, with planning horizon, base assumptions, and approval state.

records.description: Period-by-period headcount targets (typically monthly or quarterly) broken down by org unit, location, function, level, and employment type. Includes opening balance, additions (hires, transfers in), reductions (attrition, RIF, transfers out), and target end-of-period count. The basis for plan-vs-actual reconciliation against HCM.
records.catalog_description: Period-by-period headcount targets broken down by org unit, location, function, level, and type, with openings, additions, and reductions.

records.description: Projected need for specific roles derived from the capacity model: which positions, when, where, at what level. Feeds the requisition pipeline — approved demand becomes an authorized requisition in ATS via the headcount.approved handoff.
records.catalog_description: Projected need for specific roles derived from the capacity model: which positions, when, where, and at what level, feeding the requisition pipeline.

records.description: Comparison of current-state skills inventory vs future-state demand by role, level, and geography. Drives build/buy/borrow strategy: which gaps to close via training (LMS), external hires (ATS), or contingent workforce. Outputs feed both SWP scenarios and LMS curriculum decisions.
records.catalog_description: Comparisons of current skills inventory against future demand by role, level, and location, guiding build, buy, or borrow decisions.

records.description: What-if models layered on top of a base workforce plan. Each scenario carries a type (growth / reduction / restructure / geography_shift / skill_pivot / cost_optimization), the perturbation parameters, and the modeled outcome on headcount, skills, and cost. RIF planning, expansion planning, M&A integration, and reorgs all sit here.
records.catalog_description: What-if models layered on a base workforce plan, each with a type, perturbation parameters, and the modeled outcome on headcount, skills, and cost.

records.description: Proposed structure changes: new positions, eliminated positions, reporting-line changes, span-of-control adjustments, layer-level redesign. Carries current vs proposed state and the migration path between them.
records.catalog_description: Proposed organization structure changes such as new or eliminated positions and reporting-line shifts, capturing current versus proposed state and the migration path.

records.description: External labor-market overlay used to validate plan assumptions: availability, prevailing salary, time-to-hire, and supply concentration by role × geography × level. Typically sourced from third-party labor-market data providers rather than generated internally; the SWP-side record is the imported/cached view used for planning.
records.catalog_description: External labor-market benchmarks used to validate workforce-plan assumptions: availability, prevailing salary, time-to-hire, and supply by role, geography, and level.

records.description: Fully-loaded cost forecast per period, by org unit / role / location / level. Inputs: headcount × comp band × loading factor (benefits, taxes, equity) × jurisdiction. The bridge to EPM — produced inside SWP from the workforce plan, then handed off to EPM where it's rolled into the consolidated budget. Without this object the SWP↔EPM boundary is fuzzy; with it, SWP masters the workforce-driven cost build and EPM masters the consolidated financial plan that consumes it.
records.catalog_description: Fully-loaded workforce cost forecasts per period by org unit, role, location, and level, built from headcount, compensation bands, and loading factors.

records.description: Canonical record of a person currently or formerly employed by the organization. Carries identity (legal name, contact, IDs), employment metadata (start date, end date, employment type, country), and pointers to position, job profile, org unit, manager, and life-event history. The most multi-mastered data object in the catalog: HCM masters the core HR slice, Payroll masters the comp/withholding slice, and IGA masters the identity/access slice. Onboarding, PA, and Talent Management consume or contribute.
records.catalog_description: Canonical records of people currently or formerly employed, carrying identity, employment metadata, and links to position, manager, and org unit.
records.naming_authority_rationale: Employee is the unambiguous canonical term across business software. Multi-master is a metadata reality (HCM system-of-record + slices held by MDM/PAYROLL/IGA + embedded_master in ATS/BEN-ADMIN/COMP-MGMT/EMP-EXP/LMS/ONBOARDING/TALENT-MGMT/WFM), not a naming problem.

records.description: Approved slot in the org — a 'chair' with role definition, cost center, reporting line, location, and FTE allocation. Distinct from job_profiles (the catalog definition) and from employees (the person filling the slot). A position can be open, filled, or eliminated. SWP designs future positions via org_designs; HCM operationalizes them once approved.
records.catalog_description: Approved org slots with role definition, cost center, reporting line, location, and FTE allocation. Each can be open, filled, or eliminated.

records.description: Canonical role definition in the job catalog: title, family, level, responsibilities, required skills and competencies, pay range, FLSA classification. Distinct from positions (which are slots referencing a profile). Many positions share a single job profile.
records.catalog_description: Canonical role definitions in the job catalog: title, family, level, responsibilities, required skills, pay range, and FLSA class. Many positions share one profile.

records.description: Node in the organizational hierarchy: division, business unit, department, team. Carries manager, cost center alignment, geographic scope, and parent/child relationships. HCM masters the operational hierarchy; EPM contributes the cost-center mapping (which would be Finance-mastered once a Finance/GL domain is loaded).
records.catalog_description: Nodes in the organizational hierarchy such as divisions, departments, and teams, with manager, cost center alignment, geographic scope, and parent-child links.
records.naming_authority_rationale: HCM is the canonical owner of org_units catalog-wide. Every flagship HCM platform (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM, BambooHR, ADP) masters the org structure (department / division / business_unit / team) as a unified hierarchical tree. The HR cluster (PAYROLL, ATS, ONBOARDING, BEN-ADMIN, LMS, TALENT-MGMT, EMP-EXP, WFM) holds embedded_master copies for standalone deployment; the IT operational cluster (ITSM, ITAM, CMDB) holds embedded_master copies for assignment routing and chargeback. The bare-word claim arbitrates the catalog-wide reference.

records.description: Contractual terms of employment: contract type (permanent, fixed-term, contractor, intern), start and end dates, governing jurisdiction, working hours, notice period, IP and non-compete clauses, references to the signed document. HCM masters; HRSD contributes when employee-relations cases reference contract terms.
records.catalog_description: Contractual terms of employment: contract type, start and end dates, jurisdiction, working hours, notice period, and references to the signed document.

records.description: Lifecycle event records for an employee: hire, promotion, transfer, leave start, leave return, comp change, termination. The audit history that drives plan-vs-actual analytics (PA consumer) and downstream system updates. HCM masters; PA derives metrics from the event stream.
records.catalog_description: Lifecycle events for an employee, such as hire, promotion, transfer, leave, comp change, and termination. The audit history of an employment.

records.description: Umbrella entity for financial planning artifacts: annual budget, rolling forecast, long-range plan (LRP). Carries planning period, version, approval state, and pointers to the line-item budgets, forecasts, and variances that compose it. Consumes workforce_cost_projections from SWP for the people-cost line.
records.catalog_description: Umbrella records for financial planning artifacts: annual budget, rolling forecast, and long-range plan, with period, version, and approval state.

records.description: Approved annual or quarterly budget by org unit, cost center, account, and period. Once approved, drives spend authorization downstream (procurement, headcount, capex). Plan-vs-actual variance is the operational output.
records.catalog_description: Approved annual or quarterly budgets by org unit, cost center, account, and period, driving downstream spend authorization.

records.description: Rolling forecast records (typically monthly or quarterly refresh): updated view of expected revenue, cost, and headcount given current actuals. Distinct from the static budget. Refreshing forecasts upstream of SWP triggers workforce plan re-alignment.
records.catalog_description: Rolling forecasts that refresh the expected revenue, cost, and headcount view given current actuals, distinct from the static budget.

records.description: What-if financial models layered on top of a base plan: revenue upside / downside cases, cost-cutting scenarios, M&A scenarios. Mirrors the structure of SWP's workforce_scenarios for the financial dimension; the two are usually linked via the cost projection.
records.catalog_description: What-if financial models layered on a base plan, such as revenue upside, downside, cost-cutting, and acquisition scenarios.

records.description: Actual-vs-plan reconciliation records: account, period, planned amount, actual amount, variance, and root-cause commentary. The operational analytic output of EPM; consumed by org leaders, FP&A, and PA (when variance touches people cost).
records.catalog_description: Actual-versus-plan reconciliations by account and period, capturing planned amount, actual amount, variance, and root-cause commentary.

records.description: Forecast of voluntary and involuntary attrition over a planning horizon, typically broken down by org unit × tenure × performance band × geography. Derived from historical patterns and predictive models; consumed by SWP to update plan assumptions (the canonical attrition.forecast_updated handoff).
records.catalog_description: Forecasts of voluntary and involuntary attrition over a planning horizon, broken down by org unit, tenure, performance band, and geography.

records.description: Calculated workforce KPIs and metrics: time-to-fill, attrition rate, retention rate, span-of-control, internal-mobility rate, training completion rate, cost-per-hire, time-to-productivity. Derived from HCM, ATS, LMS, Payroll event streams. PA is the master of the calculated KPI definitions and the materialized metric values; source systems master the underlying events.
records.catalog_description: Calculated workforce metrics such as time-to-fill, attrition, retention, and cost-per-hire, derived from HR, recruiting, learning, and payroll event streams.

records.description: Named cohort definitions used for analysis and intervention: hi-po, flight-risk, top-quartile-performer, early-career, returning-from-leave, regrettable-loss-risk. Drives Talent Mgmt programs (high_potential.identified is the canonical outbound handoff) and HR Service Delivery actions.
records.catalog_description: Named workforce cohort definitions used for analysis and intervention, such as high-potential, flight-risk, top-performer, and early-career.

records.description: Employee engagement, pulse, and sentiment survey responses. Mastered by PA (or by a specialized engagement-platform when used). Drives segment-level engagement scoring and intervention triggers.
records.catalog_description: Employee engagement, pulse, and sentiment survey responses, used to score engagement and trigger interventions.

records.description: ML / statistical model outputs deployed in PA: flight-risk scores, performance trajectory, internal-mobility likelihood. Carries the model identifier, training window, target metric, and the materialized scores per employee. Consumes employees and employment_events as features.
records.catalog_description: Outputs of machine-learning and statistical models such as flight-risk and mobility scores, with model identifier, training window, and per-employee scores.

records.description: Unplanned interruption of, or quality reduction to, a service. Carries severity, priority, category, assignee, affected CI(s), and the MTTR clock. The flagship ITSM work item. ITOM and SECOPS feed in (events become incidents, security alerts become incidents).
records.catalog_description: Unplanned service interruptions or quality reductions, with severity, priority, category, assignee, and affected components.

records.description: Planned, catalog-driven request: access, hardware, software, information. Distinct from incidents — incidents are reactive, service requests are proactive. The fulfillment for many requests crosses domains (provisioning ↔ IGA, asset assignment ↔ ITAM, HR exception ↔ HRSD).
records.catalog_description: Planned, catalog-driven requests for access, hardware, software, or information, distinct from reactive incidents.

records.description: Root-cause record for one or more incidents that recur or share a pattern. Carries known-error workaround, permanent fix candidate, and links to the change that will resolve it. Problem management is a discipline mature ITSM tools support but most orgs underuse.
records.catalog_description: Root-cause records for recurring or related incidents, with known-error workarounds and links to the fix that will resolve them.

records.description: Planned modification to a service or configuration item. Carries change type (standard, normal, emergency), risk score, CAB approval state, implementation window, and back-out plan. The boundary object between ITSM and CMDB — CIs are updated as a result of an executed change.
records.catalog_description: Planned modifications to a service or configuration item, with change type, risk score, approval state, schedule, and back-out plan.

records.description: KB content backing both self-service portals and agent-assist tooling. Lifecycle: draft → review → published → retired. Quality and freshness are the silent ITSM KPIs that drive deflection rate.
records.catalog_description: Knowledge-base articles backing self-service portals and agent-assist tools, moving through draft, review, published, and retired.
records.naming_authority_rationale: ITSM is the canonical owner of the knowledge_articles entity catalog-wide. Every flagship ITSM vendor (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, Freshservice, BMC Helix, Ivanti) mints this name verbatim. KMS, CSM, HRSD, and LSD all consume or contribute to ITSM-mastered knowledge_articles rather than re-mastering. The bare-word claim makes the catalog-wide reference unambiguous.

records.description: Definition of what can be requested: the form schema, fulfillment workflow, approval routing, SLA, and the price/charge-back rules. Each service request instance references a catalog item.
records.catalog_description: Definitions of what can be requested: the request form, fulfillment workflow, approvals, service level, and charge-back rules.

records.description: Service-level agreement record: response-time, resolution-time, and availability targets per priority / category / customer tier. SLAs attach to incidents, service requests, and changes; breach metrics roll up to operational KPIs.
records.catalog_description: Service-level agreements setting response, resolution, and availability targets by priority, category, or customer tier.
records.notes: Config-shaped master with no workflow. Authored once at SLA setup, edited inline when terms renegotiate; no per-state permissions needed. Breach signals fire on metrics, not on a state machine of the SLA record itself. Rule #12 config-shape exemption.

records.description: Lease, maintenance, support, or warranty contract governing an asset or pool of assets. Distinct from contract templates / signature artifacts (CLM-mastered): this is the ITAM-side index of contracts attached to physical or software assets. ITAM contributes the asset-pool linkage; CLM masters the contract document itself.
records.catalog_description: Lease, maintenance, support, or warranty contracts governing an asset or pool of assets, indexed on the asset side.

records.description: Cross-cutting lifecycle audit log applicable to hardware, software, and SaaS assets: procurement, deployment, transfer, retirement, disposal. ITSM (incident-driven failure events), HCM (employee termination → recall), and Onboarding (provisioning) all contribute events.
records.catalog_description: Cross-cutting lifecycle log for hardware, software, and SaaS assets: procurement, deployment, transfer, retirement, and disposal.

records.description: Physical IT asset: laptop, desktop, server, mobile, network gear, peripheral. Carries serial number, MAC/asset tag, current user / location / room, lifecycle state, depreciation schedule, and procurement reference. The HAM master; CMDB models the same physical thing as a CI for the operational/topology view.
records.catalog_description: Physical IT assets such as laptops, servers, network gear, and peripherals, with serial number, asset tag, current user or location, and lifecycle state.

records.description: Canonical software product in the catalog (e.g. a creative suite, productivity suite, CAD application, IDE). Carries vendor, edition, family, version range. Distinct from installations (which reference a title) and from licenses (which entitle a count of users to a title).
records.catalog_description: Canonical software products in the catalog, with vendor, edition, family, and version range, separate from installations and licenses.

records.description: License entitlement: vendor, title, purchased count, license model (per-user, per-device, concurrent, site, subscription), term, renewal date, governing contract. The legal right-to-use, distinct from actual installations.
records.catalog_description: License entitlements granting the right to use a software title, with vendor, purchased count, license model, term, and renewal date.

records.description: Discovered install of a software title on a specific device or for a specific user. The operational fact, distinct from the licensing right. Discovery feeds; VULN-MGMT reads to scope vulnerability scans.
records.catalog_description: Discovered installs of a software title on a specific device or for a specific user, the operational fact distinct from the licensing right.

records.description: Audit / true-up record: entitled count, installed count, the resulting gap, true-up cost, and audit-defense evidence. Triggered by vendor audit or proactive internal review. The artifact that justifies a SAM tool's ROI.
records.catalog_description: License audit and true-up records comparing entitled to installed counts, with the resulting gap, true-up cost, and supporting evidence.

records.description: Canonical SaaS app in the portfolio (collaboration, CRM, productivity, design, work-management tools). Carries vendor, category, criticality tier, sanctioned/shadow flag, and links to the active subscription. Distinct from SAM's software_titles which are typically installed (or hybrid). The flagship SMP entity.
records.catalog_description: SaaS applications in the company portfolio, with vendor, category, criticality, owner, and whether each is sanctioned or shadow IT.

records.description: The contractual instance for a SaaS app: plan / tier, seat count, MRR or ARR, billing cadence, renewal date, primary owner. One app may have multiple subscriptions (BU, region, M&A-inherited free tier). Linked to a contract (CLM) and a PO (S2P).
records.catalog_description: Contractual subscriptions for SaaS apps: plan tier, seat count, recurring cost, billing cadence, renewal date, and owner.

records.description: SMP's view of a user-to-app license seat: who holds a seat at which tier, cost-per-seat, utilization signal, last active. Drives reclamation and rightsizing. Correlates with an iga_user_entitlement record (the governance view of the same access fact); the two routinely diverge.
records.catalog_description: User-to-app license seat assignments, showing who holds a seat at which tier, its cost, utilization, and last activity, to drive reclamation.

records.description: Per-app per-user activity metrics: logins, time-in-app, feature usage, last-active date. The basis for license right-sizing, renewal-tier decisions, and shadow-IT vs sanctioned-app analysis.
records.catalog_description: Per-user activity for each SaaS app: logins, time in app, feature usage, and last-active date, used to right-size licenses.

records.description: SaaS app discovered in use but not officially sanctioned. Found via expense data (corporate card SaaS charges), SSO logs (unsanctioned login), browser extensions, network traffic, or signup-with-corporate-email detection. The thing finance, security, IT, and SMP all want to see but historically nobody owns end-to-end.
records.catalog_description: SaaS apps found in use but not officially sanctioned, discovered through expense data, sign-on logs, browser, or network signals.

records.description: Canonical contract record: counterparty / supplier, contract type (MSA, SOW, NDA, DPA, subscription, lease), effective and expiry dates, total value, governing law, status (draft, in-negotiation, signed, active, expired, terminated). The most multi-mastered SaaS-related object — CLM owns the document, S2P and SMP contribute context.
records.catalog_description: Contracts with counterparties or suppliers, covering type, value, key dates, governing law, and lifecycle from draft to terminated.

records.description: Specific performance, payment, delivery, reporting, or compliance commitment extracted from a contract — each with its own owner, due date, and status. Post-signature obligation tracking is where contracts deliver (or fail to deliver) value.
records.catalog_description: Specific commitments extracted from a contract, such as performance, payment, delivery, or reporting, each with an owner and due date.

records.description: Reusable clause library: preferred and fallback language for indemnification, IP, termination, SLA, payment terms, data-protection, AI-use, audit rights. Drives consistency in authoring and accelerates negotiation.
records.catalog_description: Reusable clause library with preferred and fallback language for terms like indemnification, IP, termination, and payment.

records.description: Pre-approved drafts (NDA, MSA, DPA, SOW, order form) assembled from the clause library, used to author new contracts. Carries versioning, approval state, and risk-tier classification.
records.catalog_description: Pre-approved contract templates such as NDAs, MSAs, and SOWs, assembled from the clause library to author new contracts.

records.description: E-signature envelope: signing audit trail, IP addresses, external e-signature provider envelope and document reference IDs, and the signed PDF artifact. Distinct from contracts, one contract may have many signature events (counterpart, amendment, renewal).
records.catalog_description: E-signature envelopes with signing audit trail, IP addresses, provider references, and the signed document, one contract may have many.

records.description: RFx process record: RFI, RFQ, RFP, or reverse auction. Carries scope, supplier list, scorecard / weighting, responses, and the awarded supplier. The pre-contract stage that produces a sourcing decision feeding CLM.
records.catalog_description: Competitive bidding processes (RFI, RFQ, RFP, or reverse auction), tracking scope, suppliers, scorecards, responses, and the awarded supplier.

records.description: Internal demand for a purchase: what's needed, who's requesting, justification, budget reference, approval state. The origination point of a procurement workflow; SMP-triggered shadow-IT sanctioning lands here.
records.catalog_description: Internal requests to buy something, capturing what is needed, the requester, justification, budget reference, and approval state.

records.description: Issued PO to a supplier: line items, agreed prices, delivery terms, payment terms, ship-to / bill-to. Authorizes the supplier to deliver. PO creation is a primary trigger for downstream system updates — ITAM gets the asset reference, SMP gets the SaaS subscription anchor.
records.catalog_description: Orders issued to a supplier authorizing delivery, with line items, agreed prices, delivery terms, payment terms, and ship-to and bill-to details.

records.description: Confirmation that ordered goods or services were received as expected: receipt date, quantity received, condition. The basis for 3-way matching against PO + invoice that AP runs before payment.
records.catalog_description: Confirmations that ordered goods or services were received as expected, recording receipt date, quantity, and condition, used in invoice matching before payment.

records.description: Supplier-issued invoice for goods or services delivered. AP runs 3-way match (PO + receipt + invoice) before approving for payment. Multi-domain consumption: EXPENSE consumes when a corporate card path overlaps, FINOPS consumes the cloud-invoice slice for cost allocation.
records.catalog_description: Supplier-issued invoices for delivered goods or services, matched against purchase order and receipt before approval for payment.

records.description: Canonical record of an IT thing under management: server, container, application, business service, network device, database, cloud resource. The flagship CMDB entity, referenced by changes, incidents, problems, and topology. Multi-feed: DISCOVERY auto-populates, HAM provides the physical-asset overlay for hardware CIs, SAM/SMP overlay for software/SaaS CIs.
records.catalog_description: Canonical records of IT things under management: servers, containers, applications, services, network devices, databases, and cloud resources.

records.description: Edges in the CI graph: depends-on, runs-on, contains, member-of, hosted-by, communicates-with. The topology that makes service mapping, impact analysis, and event correlation possible.
records.catalog_description: Edges in the configuration-item graph such as depends-on, runs-on, and hosted-by, the topology behind service mapping and impact analysis.
records.notes: Config-shaped graph edges (CI dependencies). Discovered or hand-curated, then maintained inline. No workflow gates. No per-state permissions needed (Rule #12 config-shape exemption).

records.description: The CI type hierarchy (Computer → Linux Server → Web Server, Application → Microservice → REST API) defining schema, inherited attributes, and class-level monitoring/discovery policies. The schema-of-schemas for the CMDB.
records.catalog_description: Configuration-item types in a hierarchy, defining schema, inherited attributes, and class-level monitoring and discovery policies.
records.notes: Config-shaped CI class schema (attributes, validation rules). Authored by data stewards, edited inline. No workflow gates. No per-state permissions needed (Rule #12 config-shape exemption).

records.description: Business-service-to-CI mapping: which CIs underlie a named business service. The bridge between technical topology (CMDB / DISCOVERY) and business impact (used by ITSM, SECOPS, OBS).
records.catalog_description: Mappings of named business services to the configuration items that underlie them, linking technical topology to business impact.
records.notes: Auto-refreshed topology projection. Generated by discovery, edited by service owners. Updates emit service_map.updated but no per-state permission boundary. No workflow gates (Rule #12 config-shape exemption).

records.description: Captured configuration state at a point in time, used for drift detection, approved-state validation, and audit evidence. Triggers an unauthorized-change incident when current state diverges.
records.catalog_description: Captured configuration states at a point in time, used for drift detection, approved-state validation, and audit evidence.
records.notes: Immutable snapshot reference; captured once, then read-only for drift compare. No workflow gates. No per-state permissions needed (Rule #12 config-shape exemption).

records.description: A discovery job execution: scope (subnet, cloud account, k8s cluster, AD forest), credentials used, start/end timestamps, candidates emitted, errors encountered.
records.catalog_description: Records of a discovery job run, covering scope, credentials used, start and end times, candidates emitted, and errors encountered.

records.description: Pre-CMDB candidate emitted by a scan, awaiting normalization and reconciliation into a configuration_item. The buffer between raw scan output and the curated CMDB; some candidates never promote (transient, duplicate, scope-excluded).
records.catalog_description: Candidate devices emitted by a scan, awaiting normalization and reconciliation into a configuration item before joining the CMDB.

records.description: Connector / probe / credential definition for a discovery integration: hypervisor, public-cloud account, Kubernetes cluster, directory service, SNMP credential. The configuration that drives scans.
records.catalog_description: Connector, probe, and credential definitions for discovery integrations such as hypervisors, cloud accounts, clusters, and directory services.

records.description: Raw event from a monitored system — state change, threshold crossing, status update, log signal. The firehose, volume-heavy and noisy. AIOPS consumes the full stream for correlation; alerts are the human-relevant subset.
records.catalog_description: Raw events from monitored systems: state changes, threshold crossings, status updates, and log signals consumed for correlation.

records.description: Filtered, human-relevant subset of events that crossed a threshold, matched a pattern, or were enriched with priority and routing. Alerts are what gets paged or ticketed; events are what feeds the correlation engine.
records.catalog_description: Filtered, human-relevant events that crossed a threshold or matched a pattern, enriched with priority and routing, ready to be paged or ticketed.

records.description: What to monitor, at what frequency, with what thresholds, for which CIs. Often auto-bound to CIs by class via DISCOVERY — a new web-server CI inherits the web-server monitoring policy by default.
records.catalog_description: Monitoring policies defining what to monitor, at what frequency and thresholds, for which configuration items, often auto-bound by class.

records.description: Resource utilization snapshots (CPU, memory, disk, throughput, IOPS) at fixed intervals for capacity planning, trend analysis, and FinOps cost allocation. The infra-side counterpart to OBS metric_series.
records.catalog_description: Periodic resource utilization snapshots such as CPU, memory, disk, and throughput, used for capacity planning, trend analysis, and cost allocation.

records.description: Time-series metric streams from instrumented applications — counters, gauges, histograms, summaries. The dev-instrumentation counterpart to ITOM's capacity_records, typically higher-cardinality and tied to release versions.
records.catalog_description: Time-series metric streams from instrumented applications: counters, gauges, histograms, and summaries tied to release versions.

records.description: Application log stream entries, structured and unstructured. Indexed for search; correlated with metrics and traces for root-cause analysis.
records.catalog_description: Application log stream entries, structured and unstructured, indexed for search and correlated with metrics and traces for root-cause analysis.

records.description: End-to-end request traces across microservices — parent-child spans, service identification, latency attribution. The fundamental observability artifact for diagnosing latency and dependency issues in service meshes.
records.catalog_description: End-to-end request traces across microservices, with parent-child spans, service identification, and latency attribution for diagnosing issues.

records.description: Service-level objective definitions and breach state: target (e.g. 99.9% requests under 300ms over 28 days), error budget remaining, burn rate, last breach. Drives the slo.breached handoff that creates incidents.
records.catalog_description: Service-level objective definitions and their breach state, with targets, remaining error budget, burn rate, and last breach.

records.description: Aggregated exception records: unique exception fingerprint, first/last seen, occurrence count, affected releases, environments, owners, status (unresolved/resolved/ignored).
records.catalog_description: Aggregated exception records grouped by fingerprint, with first and last seen, occurrence count, affected releases, owners, and status.

records.description: Clustered group of events and alerts identified as a single underlying incident — the noise-reduction artifact. A storm of 200 alerts collapses to one correlation with a candidate root-cause CI and the suggested incident.
records.catalog_description: Clustered groups of events and alerts identified as a single underlying incident, with a candidate root cause for noise reduction.

records.description: Detected deviation from learned normal behavior: KPI excursion outside seasonality bands, novel error pattern, traffic shape change. Feeds correlation and predictive_signals.
records.catalog_description: Detected deviations from learned normal behavior, such as KPI excursions, novel error patterns, or traffic shape changes.

records.description: RCA record — ML-suggested or human-confirmed. Links candidate root-cause CIs to the correlated event cluster and the resulting incident. Seeds ITSM problem records via the root_cause.identified handoff.
records.catalog_description: Root cause analysis records, suggested or human-confirmed, linking candidate causes to the correlated event cluster and resulting incident.

records.description: Proactive forecast emitted before symptoms surface: predicted capacity exhaustion, predicted failure of a CI based on degradation pattern, predicted SLO breach within the burn-rate window.
records.catalog_description: Proactive forecasts emitted before symptoms surface, such as predicted capacity exhaustion, component failure, or an upcoming service-level breach.

records.description: Canonical record of a customer — account (B2B) or end-customer (B2C). Carries identity, segmentation, lifecycle stage, account hierarchy, and pointers to opportunities, cases, subscriptions, and unified profile. The flagship customer-facing entity and the catalog's most multi-mastered row: CRM masters the sales view, CSM the service view, SUB-MGMT the financial view, CDP the unified resolved profile. The structural twin of `employees` on the customer side.
records.catalog_description: Canonical records of customers, whether business accounts or end consumers, carrying identity, segmentation, lifecycle stage, and account hierarchy.
records.naming_authority_rationale: Customer is the unambiguous canonical term across business software. Multi-master is a metadata reality (federated across CRM-sales / CDP-marketing / CSM-success / MDM-golden-record / SUB-MGMT-subscription views), not a naming problem; future master-data promotion to a shared module is an orthogonal deployer concern.

records.description: Person at a customer account (B2B) or contact-level record (B2C-relevant). Carries title, email, decision-maker flag, preferred channel, opt-in state. MA contributes engagement data; SALES-ENG contributes cadence touchpoints.
records.catalog_description: People at customer or prospect organizations, carrying title, contact details, decision-maker flag, preferred channel, and opt-in state.

records.description: Pre-qualification prospect record — source, score, status (new/working/qualified/disqualified/converted), assigned rep, conversion target (which contact + account it would become). MQL handoff from MA lands here.
records.catalog_description: Prospects captured before qualification, tracking source, score, status, assigned rep, and the contact and account they would convert into.

records.description: Active sales deal — stage, amount, close date, probability, products/SKUs, competitor, decision criteria. Drives CPQ quote generation and closed-won triggers downstream subscription activation.
records.catalog_description: Active sales deals, tracking stage, amount, close date, probability, products, competitor, and decision criteria.

records.description: Sales-process taxonomy: stage definitions, exit criteria, default probability, allowed-next-stage transitions. The configuration object behind the opportunity pipeline.
records.catalog_description: Sales-process stage definitions with exit criteria, default probability, and allowed transitions, the configuration behind the opportunity pipeline.

records.description: Logged touchpoint between sales and a contact/opportunity — call, email, meeting, demo, content view. SALES-ENG sub-domain may co-master if its data_objects load expands later (cadence sequences, call recordings).
records.catalog_description: Logged touchpoints between sales and a contact or opportunity: calls, emails, meetings, demos, and content views.

records.description: Customer-facing support ticket — the flagship CSM entity. Distinct from ITSM `incidents` (internal IT) and `service_requests` (catalog-driven internal requests). Carries severity, channel, queue, SLA clock, customer + contact references, CSAT linkage. SUB-MGMT-driven dunning failures and CSM-detected churn risk both surface as cases.
records.catalog_description: Customer-facing support tickets, carrying severity, channel, queue, SLA clock, and references to the customer, contact, and satisfaction survey.

records.description: What support a customer can use — service tier (Silver/Gold/Platinum), monthly support hours, supported channels (email/chat/phone), named contacts, included services, SLA response targets. Activated from the SUB-MGMT subscription.activated handoff.
records.catalog_description: Records of what support a customer can use, covering service tier, monthly hours, supported channels, named contacts, and SLA response targets.

records.description: Customer satisfaction, NPS, or CES survey response tied to a case, interaction, or relationship-level survey. Drives retention scoring and feeds churn-risk signals back to SUB-MGMT and account-health into CRM.
records.catalog_description: Customer satisfaction, NPS, and effort survey responses tied to a case, interaction, or relationship-level survey.

records.description: Customer's recurring revenue contract — plan, term, MRR/ARR, billing cadence, seat count, lifecycle (trial / active / paused / canceled / churned). **Seller-side view**; distinct from `saas_subscriptions` (SMP, buyer-side view of what we consume from vendors).
records.catalog_description: Customers' recurring revenue contracts, covering plan, term, MRR or ARR, billing cadence, seat count, and lifecycle from trial to churned.

records.description: Seller-issued invoice — line items, tax, payment terms, due date, status (draft/sent/paid/overdue/written-off). **AR side**; distinct from S2P `invoices` (AP-side, supplier-issued).
records.catalog_description: Seller-issued invoices billed to customers, with line items, tax, payment terms, due date, and status from draft to paid or written off.

records.description: Metered-billing inputs — events / consumption units / overage credits feeding usage-based pricing tiers. Stream from product instrumentation (or B2C-COMM events) into SUB-MGMT for cycle aggregation.
records.catalog_description: Metered usage inputs (events, consumption units, overage credits) that feed usage-based pricing and billing aggregation.

records.description: ASC 606 / IFRS 15 deferred-revenue schedules: performance obligations, allocation across obligations, recognition timeline, recognized vs deferred amounts. The bridge between SUB-MGMT and Finance/GL.
records.catalog_description: Deferred-revenue schedules under ASC 606 and IFRS 15, with performance obligations, allocations, recognition timeline, and recognized versus deferred amounts.

records.description: Payment failure / retry / collection / past-due-warning records driving the involuntary-churn workflow. Surfaces as customer cases when CSM intervention is required; escalates to write-off if collection fails.
records.catalog_description: Payment failures, retries, and past-due warnings that drive the involuntary-churn and collections workflow.

records.description: Unified event stream — every customer interaction across web, mobile, email, in-product, sales-engagement, support. The firehose CDP is built around: typically millions of events per day per active customer base. Multi-feed from MA (campaign events), B2C-COMM (storefront), CRM (sales activities), CSM (support interactions), product instrumentation. The customer-side counterpart to ITOM's `events`.
records.catalog_description: Unified stream of every customer interaction across web, mobile, email, in-product, sales, and support channels.

records.description: Identity-resolution edges: email ↔ device ↔ cookie ↔ login ↔ phone. The graph that turns anonymous interactions into resolved customers. Built up over time from event signals; quality drives every downstream activation. IGA contributes employee-as-customer overlap for B2C-employer scenarios.
records.catalog_description: Identity-resolution edges linking email, device, cookie, login, and phone, turning anonymous interactions into resolved customers.

records.description: Defined segments / cohorts (high-value-active, 90-day-churn-risk, holiday-shoppers, post-purchase-anchor). Computed from events + attributes; activated outbound to MA for campaign targeting, to B2C-COMM for personalized storefront, to SALES-ENG for outreach prioritization.
records.catalog_description: Defined customer cohorts (high-value-active, churn-risk, holiday-shoppers) computed from events and attributes, activated for targeting and outreach.

records.description: Derived / calculated attributes attached to the resolved profile: LTV, RFM score, propensity-to-buy, churn-likelihood, preferred-channel, lifecycle stage. The materialized scoring layer of the unified profile; downstream segments and personalization rules read from here.
records.catalog_description: Derived attributes attached to a resolved customer profile, such as lifetime value, RFM score, propensity to buy, churn likelihood, and lifecycle stage.

records.description: Observed multi-channel journey progression — the inbound view of how a customer moved through touchpoints over time. Distinct from MA `nurture_journeys` (orchestrated outbound sequences): customer_journeys are descriptive (what happened), nurture_journeys are prescriptive (what we'll do).
records.catalog_description: Observed multi-channel journeys showing how a customer moved through touchpoints over time.

records.description: Marketing campaign definitions — email blast, drip sequence, multi-channel, paid social tie-in, webinar series, ABM play. Carries target audience (segments), schedule, content variants, attribution settings, performance KPIs.
records.catalog_description: Marketing campaign definitions across email, multi-channel, and account-based plays, with target audience, schedule, content variants, and KPIs.

records.description: Email templates and sent instances at marketing scale: list-driven, volume-heavy, branded. Carries open/click/bounce/unsubscribe metrics, deliverability state, sender-reputation impact. Distinct from SALES-ENG `sales_emails` (1-1, rep-driven).
records.catalog_description: Email templates and sent instances at marketing scale, with open, click, bounce, and unsubscribe metrics and deliverability state.

records.description: Scoring records per lead/contact — explicit signals (form-fill, demo-request, content-download) + implicit signals (behavior, fit/firmographic match). The mechanism behind the MQL handoff to CRM; thresholds and decay rules drive routing.
records.catalog_description: Scores per lead or contact combining explicit signals (form fills, demo requests) and implicit fit signals, driving qualified-lead routing.

records.description: Multi-touch outbound nurture flows — branching paths, wait conditions, exit criteria, content trees. The orchestrated counterpart to CDP `customer_journeys`; MA defines, CDP observes resulting behavior.
records.catalog_description: Multi-touch outbound nurture flows, with branching paths, wait conditions, exit criteria, and content trees.

records.description: Lead-capture form definitions: fields, mapping to leads/contacts, hidden field rules, conditional logic, post-submit routing (lead score boost, nurture enroll, sales-rep notification).
records.catalog_description: Lead-capture form definitions, with fields, mapping to leads and contacts, conditional logic, and post-submit routing.

records.description: Multi-step outreach sequence: touchpoint definitions (call, email, social, video, voicemail-drop), timing, branching rules based on engagement. The core entity of sales-engagement platforms; enrollment can be manual (rep choice) or automated (CDP intent signal, CRM opportunity stage).
records.catalog_description: Multi-step outreach sequences defining touchpoints, timing, and branching rules, used to enroll and engage prospects systematically.

records.description: Recorded sales call: audio/video, transcript, participants, talk-track / topic / sentiment metadata. Conversation-intelligence tooling attaches this to deals and feeds conversation_intelligence_records downstream.
records.catalog_description: Recorded sales calls with audio or video, transcript, participants, and topic and sentiment metadata, attached to deals for review.

records.description: Individual sales emails sent (1-1, not blasts) — open/reply/click tracking, thread context, sentiment. Distinct from MA `marketing_emails` (volume-scale, list-driven, brand-template-bound).
records.catalog_description: Individual one-to-one sales emails sent to prospects, with open, reply, and click tracking and thread context.

records.description: AI-extracted insights from calls, emails, and meetings: competitor mentions, pricing discussions, sentiment shifts, commitments made, action items, risk signals. Feeds opportunity stage signals back to CRM and deal-coaching recommendations to managers.
records.catalog_description: AI-extracted insights from calls, emails, and meetings, including competitor mentions, sentiment shifts, commitments, and risk signals.

records.description: Authored social-channel post (draft, scheduled, or published) with per-channel variants, media assets, copy, lifecycle state, and approval history. The unit of work in publishing tools.
records.catalog_description: Authored social posts (draft, scheduled, or published) with per-channel variants, media, copy, lifecycle state, and approval history.

records.description: Brand-owned connected account on a specific social network with credentials, permissions, and channel-specific metadata. Covers major short-form, long-form, video, image-sharing, professional, and discussion-forum networks.
records.catalog_description: Brand-owned connected accounts on specific social networks, with credentials, permissions, and channel-specific metadata.

records.description: Inbound conversation in the unified inbox: comment, direct message, mention-reply, or review on a brand-owned account. The unit of engagement. Distinct from social_mentions (off-channel listening artifacts).
records.catalog_description: Inbound conversations in the unified inbox: comments, direct messages, mention-replies, and reviews on brand-owned accounts.

records.description: Brand or keyword mention detected by social listening across networks, news, blogs, forums, and review sites — typically off-channel and from non-followers. Distinct from social_messages (on-channel inbox).
records.catalog_description: Brand or keyword mentions detected across networks, news, blogs, forums, and review sites, typically from non-followers off-channel.

records.description: Saved monitoring query/topic (keywords, hashtags, competitors, geographies, sentiment filters) that drives the listening pipeline. Configuration data with a long lifecycle.
records.catalog_description: Saved monitoring queries defined by keywords, hashtags, competitors, geographies, and sentiment filters that drive social listening.

records.description: Creator/influencer profile managed in influencer-marketing tools: audience metrics, content history, contracts, payments, and campaign attribution. Distinct from contacts (which represent customer/prospect individuals).
records.catalog_description: Creator and influencer profiles, with audience metrics, content history, contracts, payments, and campaign attribution.
records.naming_authority_rationale: Social media management owns 'influencers' as the canonical creator-relationship concept. No competing meaning in business software.

records.description: Schema definition for a class of content entries: fields, references, validation, and locale settings. CMS-specific configuration; renames or removals couple tightly to downstream frontend code. Industry synonyms include Models, Schemas, and Content Types depending on the headless CMS in use.
records.catalog_description: Schema definitions for a class of content entries, specifying fields, references, validation, and locale settings.

records.description: Individual structured content record conforming to a content_type, served via the CMS delivery API to any channel. The thing a headless CMS exists to manage. Industry synonyms include Entries, Documents, and Stories depending on the headless CMS in use.
records.catalog_description: Individual structured content records conforming to a content type, served through a delivery API to any channel.

records.description: A scheduled batch of content changes published together, used to coordinate go-lives across many entries (campaign launch, product update). Industry synonyms include Releases, Launch, and Scheduled Releases depending on the headless CMS in use.
records.catalog_description: Scheduled batches of content changes published together to coordinate go-lives across many entries.

records.description: Workflow definition for editorial review and publishing: named states (draft / in_review / approved / published), transitions, and role-based step ownership. Distinct from ECM document workflows (different content shape and lifecycle).
records.catalog_description: Definitions of editorial review and publishing workflows: named states, transitions, and which role owns each step.

records.description: Configured locale available within a CMS account or environment, including fallback chain, default locale flag, and translation status conventions. Drives field-level localization on content entries.
records.catalog_description: Locales configured within a content environment, including fallback chain and default flag, driving field-level localization.

records.description: Isolated working copy of a CMS's content: dev, staging, or production environment; dataset, branch, or space. Used to test content-type changes and content migrations safely before promoting.
records.catalog_description: Isolated working copies of content such as dev, staging, or production, used to test content changes safely before promoting.

records.description: Image, video, audio, document, or design file with metadata, rights, taxonomy, and delivery URLs. The DAM master; HCMSs contribute content-bound assets uploaded inline to entries and consume DAM-hosted assets by URL reference. PIM and B2C-COMM also reference product imagery via DAM.
records.catalog_description: Images, videos, audio, documents, and design files with metadata, rights, taxonomy, and delivery URLs.

records.description: A single payroll cycle execution, scoped to pay group, country, and pay period. Drives gross-to-net calculation across the eligible employee population and produces pay_slips, payroll_journal_entries, and tax_filings. The atomic unit of payroll operations.
records.catalog_description: Payroll cycle executions scoped to a pay group, country, and period, driving gross-to-net calculation and producing pay slips, journal entries, and tax filings.

records.description: Per-employee per-cycle gross-to-net statement: earnings, pre/post-tax deductions, employer contributions, tax withholdings, net pay, YTD totals. Called Pay Stub (US), Payslip (UK/AU/IE), Bulletin de Paie (FR), Lohnzettel (DE), Holerite (BR). Worker-portal accessible; legally retained per jurisdiction.
records.catalog_description: Per-employee per-cycle gross-to-net pay statements, showing earnings, deductions, contributions, withholdings, net pay, and year-to-date totals.

records.description: Configurable definition of an earning type (regular, overtime, bonus, commission, severance, retro-pay) with tax treatment, GL mapping, accumulator rules, and country localization. Foundation of the payroll calculation engine.
records.catalog_description: Definitions of pay types such as regular, overtime, bonus, and severance, with tax treatment and accounting rules. Foundation of the payroll calculation engine.

records.description: Configurable definition of a deduction (pre-tax 401k, post-tax Roth, medical premium, HSA, garnishment, union dues) with priority, ceiling, and GL mapping. Drives net-pay arithmetic and benefits-payroll integration.
records.catalog_description: Configurable definitions of pay deductions such as retirement, medical premiums, garnishments, and union dues, with priority, ceiling, and ledger mapping.

records.description: Federal, state, provincial, or local taxing jurisdiction with rate tables, deposit schedules, and reporting forms. Includes US IRS/state/locals, UK HMRC, German Finanzamt, French URSSAF, Australian ATO.
records.catalog_description: Taxing jurisdictions (federal, state, provincial, or local) with their rate tables, deposit schedules, and reporting forms.

records.description: Periodic statutory submission to a tax authority (US 941/W-2, UK FPS/EPS, German DEUEV/Lohnsteueranmeldung, French DSN, Australian STP). Includes payment and reporting; failure carries penalties.
records.catalog_description: Periodic statutory submissions to a tax authority, covering payment and reporting, where failure carries penalties.

records.description: Court-ordered or agency-issued instruction to withhold from an employee's wages (child support, tax levy, bankruptcy, student loan, creditor). Carries priority, ceiling, remit-to instructions, and lifecycle (active, released, exhausted).
records.catalog_description: Court-ordered or agency-issued instructions to withhold from an employee's wages, carrying priority, ceiling, remit-to details, and lifecycle status.

records.description: GL posting produced by a pay_run, decomposed by cost_center / department / earning_code / deduction_code into debit and credit lines. The payroll-to-finance handoff payload.
records.catalog_description: General-ledger postings produced by a pay run, broken down into debit and credit lines by cost center, department, and pay code.

records.description: Configurable employer-sponsored benefit offering: medical, dental, vision, life, disability, 401(k), HSA/FSA, voluntary. Carries eligibility rules, contribution structure, plan year, carrier and coverage tiers.
records.catalog_description: Employer-sponsored benefit offerings such as medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and retirement, with eligibility rules, contributions, and coverage tiers.

records.description: Per-employee per-plan elected coverage record with effective dates, covered dependents, contribution amounts, and beneficiary designations. The source of truth for deduction calculation in payroll.
records.catalog_description: Per-employee, per-plan elected coverage with effective dates, covered dependents, contributions, and beneficiaries. The basis for payroll deductions.

records.description: Person covered under an employee's benefit plan (spouse, domestic partner, child, disabled adult). Carries relationship, DOB, SSN, dependent-eligibility documents.
records.catalog_description: People covered under an employee's benefit plan, such as a spouse, partner, or child, with relationship, birth date, and eligibility documents.

records.description: Qualifying event (marriage, birth, adoption, divorce, dependent loss-of-coverage, employment change) that opens a mid-year enrollment window. Triggers benefit_enrollments changes outside open enrollment.
records.catalog_description: Qualifying life events such as marriage, birth, adoption, or coverage loss that open a mid-year benefits enrollment window.

records.description: Annual employer-defined window during which employees may elect or change benefit_plans for the next plan year. Drives mass campaign communications, decision-support tooling, and a synchronous load on the carrier_feeds layer at close.
records.catalog_description: Annual windows during which employees may elect or change benefit plans for the next plan year, driving enrollment communications and carrier updates.

records.description: Insurance provider, 401(k) recordkeeper, or COBRA administrator that fulfills a benefit_plan. Drives the carrier_feeds integration.
records.catalog_description: Insurance providers, retirement recordkeepers, and benefit administrators that fulfill a benefit plan and receive enrollment feeds.

records.description: Outbound integration to a benefit_carrier (EDI 834 enrollment, 820 remittance, custom API, file_drop). Mostly weekly batch; failures cause coverage discrepancies between HR system of record and carrier of record.
records.catalog_description: Outbound integrations that send enrollment and remittance data to a benefit carrier, typically as weekly batches whose failures cause coverage discrepancies.

records.description: Total-rewards package definition per role, level, location: base structure, bonus target, equity guideline, allowances. Distinct from sales-incentive plans (those live in Sales Performance Management).
records.catalog_description: Total-rewards package definitions per role, level, and location, covering base, bonus target, equity, and allowances.

records.description: Pay-range structure by grade and geographic zone with minimum, midpoint, maximum, and benchmarking source. Drives offer guidance, merit eligibility, and pay-equity gap analysis.
records.catalog_description: Pay ranges by grade and geographic zone, with minimum, midpoint, maximum, and benchmark source, guiding offers and pay-equity analysis.

records.description: Periodic compensation review cycle (annual, semi-annual, focal): budget pool, eligibility, calibration step, approval chain, effective date. The recurring operating model of comp management.
records.catalog_description: Periodic compensation review cycles, with budget pool, eligibility, calibration step, approval chain, and effective date.

records.description: Per-employee per-cycle proposed merit increase, bonus, and equity refresh from manager, with calibration adjustments and final approval. Approved values become the pay-rate change posted to payroll.
records.catalog_description: Per-employee proposed merit increases, bonuses, and equity refreshes for a cycle, with calibration adjustments and final approval.

records.description: Personalized total-rewards letter delivered to a worker showing the value of base, bonus, equity, benefits, and perks. Generated on hire, merit cycle close, and annually.
records.catalog_description: Personalized total-rewards statements showing a worker the value of their base, bonus, equity, benefits, and perks.

records.description: RSU, option, or PSU award tied to a vesting schedule. Carries grant date, type, share count, strike (if option), vesting cadence, performance metrics, and forfeiture rules. Integrates with external equity-administration platforms.
records.catalog_description: Equity awards such as restricted stock units, options, and performance units, with grant terms, vesting schedule, and forfeiture rules.

records.description: Imported market salary data for a job-level-geography combination, sourced from an external compensation-survey provider. Drives salary_bands maintenance.
records.catalog_description: Imported market salary data for a job-level and geography combination, sourced from external compensation surveys.

records.description: Published shift schedule for a department / location / week, derived from labor-demand forecasts and worker-availability constraints. The product of a scheduling-optimization run.
records.catalog_description: Published shift schedules for a department, location, and week, derived from labor-demand forecasts and worker-availability constraints.

records.description: A scheduled work block assigned to a worker: start, end, position, location, break plan, premium pay flags. The atomic scheduling unit.
records.catalog_description: Scheduled work blocks assigned to a worker, with start, end, position, location, break plan, and premium pay flags.

records.description: Recorded clock-in / clock-out / break event from a time-collection device, mobile app, or manual entry. Approved time entries are the WFM↔PAYROLL handoff payload.
records.catalog_description: Clock-in, clock-out, and break events from a device, app, or manual entry; approved entries feed payroll.

records.description: Worker-initiated request for time away: PTO, sick, parental, bereavement, jury duty, FMLA. Carries policy, eligibility check, approval chain, and accrual deduction. Called Leave Request (UK), Vacation Request (US), PTO Request.
records.catalog_description: Worker requests for time away (vacation, sick, parental, bereavement, jury duty), carrying eligibility, approval chain, and accrual deduction.

records.description: Per-worker per-leave-type running balance: accrued, taken, scheduled, available. Calculated against time_off_policies and reset per accrual cycle.
records.catalog_description: Per-worker running balances for a leave type: accrued, taken, scheduled, and available, reset each accrual cycle.

records.description: Accrual / entitlement rule definition for a leave type: by country, role, tenure tier, with caps, carry-over, and conversion rules. Country-specific by statute (US PTO, UK statutory leave, German Urlaub, French Congés Payés).
records.catalog_description: Accrual and entitlement rules for a leave type by country, role, and tenure, with caps, carry-over, and conversion rules.

records.description: Recorded meal and rest-break event evidencing compliance with labor-law break requirements (US state mandates, EU Working Time Directive). Carries waiver attestation where applicable.
records.catalog_description: Recorded meal and rest-break events evidencing compliance with labor-law break requirements, with waiver attestation where applicable.

records.description: Atomic learning unit: e-learning module, video, live session, blended program, external content. Carries content reference, duration, format, language, prerequisites, certification award.
records.catalog_description: Learning units such as e-learning modules, videos, live sessions, or blended programs, with format, duration, and prerequisites.
records.naming_authority_rationale: LMS owns 'courses' as the canonical training-course concept. No competing meaning in business software.
records.notes: Pattern flags audit (2026-05-23): no personal content (course is the asset, not a learner record), no submit lock (drafts can be edited until publish), no single approver (publish workflow is typically multi-stage SME + L&D review). All three flags correctly false.

records.description: Curated sequence of courses targeting a role, skill, or certification. Drives ordered enrollment and progress tracking across multiple courses.
records.catalog_description: Curated sequences of courses targeting a role, skill, or certification, driving ordered enrollment and progress tracking.

records.description: Per-learner per-course state record: assigned date, due date, attempts, status (not_started, in_progress, completed, expired), score. The operational unit of learning tracking.
records.catalog_description: Per-learner per-course records tracking assigned and due dates, attempts, status, and score.

records.description: Granular completion event for a course or activity, often xAPI / SCORM / cmi5 statement: actor, verb, object, result, timestamp. Feeds skill_profiles and certifications.
records.catalog_description: Granular completion events for a course or activity (actor, verb, object, result, timestamp) feeding skill profiles and certifications.

records.description: Issued credential against a worker (internal certification, vendor cert, regulatory cert) with issue date, expiry, issuing body, and renewal rules. Drives recertification campaigns.
records.catalog_description: Credentials issued to a worker (internal, vendor, or regulatory), with issue date, expiry, issuing body, and renewal rules. Drives recertification campaigns.

records.description: Per-worker collection of skills with self-assessed and validated proficiency levels, derived from completed courses, certifications, performance signals, and inferred peer-comparison. The central artifact of HCM-side skills-cloud and talent-intelligence offerings.
records.catalog_description: Per-worker collections of skills with self-assessed and validated proficiency, derived from courses, certifications, and performance signals.

records.description: Mandatory training assignment tied to a regulation, role, location, or hire-event (anti-harassment, AML, GDPR, OSHA, HIPAA). Carries due date, escalation policy, audit log.
records.catalog_description: Mandatory training assignments tied to a regulation, role, location, or hire event, with due dates and escalation policy.

records.description: Per-cycle per-worker review artifact: self-assessment, manager assessment, ratings, narrative, calibration outcome. Drives merit_recommendations and succession_plans.
records.catalog_description: Per-cycle per-worker review records holding self and manager assessments, ratings, narrative, and calibration outcome.

records.description: Individual goal or OKR with owner, period, metric, weight, status, alignment to organizational objectives. Reviewed within performance_reviews cycles.
