records.description: Per-employee portal account in the equity-administration product. Embedded_masters equity_grants for portal visibility.
records.catalog_description: Per-employee portal accounts in the equity-administration system, giving each employee visibility into their equity grants.

records.description: Shareholder-initiated sale of existing equity: tender offer, employee liquidity program, or direct transfer. Board-approval workflow.
records.catalog_description: Shareholder-initiated sales of existing equity: tender offers, employee liquidity programs, or direct transfers, with board approval.

records.description: End-to-end fund-vehicle setup record: entity formation filings, EIN application, banking onboarding, templated LPA. Unique to emerging-manager bundled platforms.
records.catalog_description: End-to-end fund-vehicle setup records, covering entity formation filings, tax-ID application, banking onboarding, and partnership agreement.

records.description: Special Purpose Vehicle — single-deal investment vehicle (LLC-typed) with limited LP base. Dominant vehicle below ~$25M deal size.
records.catalog_description: Single-deal investment vehicles with a limited investor base, the common structure for smaller deals.

records.description: Investor commitment to an SPV: simpler than fund-level lp_subscriptions; typically smaller LP base, single capital call at close.
records.catalog_description: Investor commitments to a special purpose vehicle, typically a small investor base with a single capital call at close.

records.description: Inventory-scoped item record: SKU, unit of measure, lot/serial-controlled flag, ABC/XYZ class, default cost method (FIFO, LIFO, weighted-average), weight, and dimensions. INV-MGMT-mastered for standalone deployments; embedded-masters `commerce_products` when B2C-COMM is canonical.
records.catalog_description: Inventory items with SKU, unit of measure, lot or serial control, ABC class, default cost method, and physical dimensions.
records.notes: Config-shape master. SKU is created and edited inline through admin UI. No per-state permissions needed beyond create/edit/delete; lifecycle states are not modeled per Rule #12 config-shape exemption.

records.description: INV-MGMT's finer-grain location catalog: warehouse, store, bin, zone, or hub. Defers to OMS `inventory_locations` (canonical) when present; deployable standalone otherwise.
records.catalog_description: Fine-grained stock locations: warehouse, store, bin, zone, or hub used to track where inventory sits.
records.notes: Config-shape master. Locations are authored once and edited rarely; no workflow.

records.description: Per-item by per-location quantity record: on_hand, reserved, in_transit, available_for_allocation. Real-time maintained by stock_movements; not directly edited.
records.catalog_description: Per-item, per-location quantity records (on hand, reserved, in transit, available), maintained automatically from stock movements.
records.notes: Derived state, not workflow. Maintained by `inv_stock_movements` posting; no lifecycle states modeled.

records.description: Append-only event ledger of inventory transactions: receipt, issue, transfer-in, transfer-out, adjustment-positive, adjustment-negative. Underlies stock_balances; posted movements are immutable.
records.catalog_description: Append-only ledger of inventory transactions (receipts, issues, transfers, adjustments). Posted movements are immutable and drive stock balances.
records.notes: Submit-lock applies: a posted movement is immutable; reversal is a new compensating movement, not an edit.

records.description: Inter-location transfer header with lines: source location, destination location, requested-by user, status (requested, approved, in_transit, received, discrepancy, reconciled), expected arrival date.
records.catalog_description: Inter-location transfers of stock, with source, destination, requester, expected arrival, and status from requested to reconciled.

records.description: Scheduled or ad-hoc inventory count session: location, item-filter scope (ABC class, last-counted-before, all), assigned counter, status (scheduled, counting, variance_review, posted), per-line variances.
records.catalog_description: Scheduled or ad-hoc inventory count sessions, with location, item scope, assigned counter, status, and per-line variances.
records.notes: Single-approver pattern: variance review is gated by a designated approver who signs off on the adjustment before posting.

records.description: INV-MGMT-scoped lot or batch identifier: lot_code, item, supplier, manufacture_date, expiry_date, originating receipt. Distinct from FDS `traceability_lots` (FSMA-204 food-traceability scope).
records.catalog_description: Lot or batch identifiers for inventory, with item, supplier, manufacture and expiry dates, and originating receipt.

records.description: Individually-tracked unit with a unique serial: item, current location, current status (in_stock, reserved, issued, returned, scrapped), warranty_start.
records.catalog_description: Individually tracked units identified by a unique serial number, with item, current location, status, and warranty start.

records.description: Item by location replenishment policy: reorder_point, reorder_quantity, safety_stock, lead_time_days, preferred_supplier, auto_generate_po flag.
records.catalog_description: Per-item, per-location replenishment policies: reorder point and quantity, safety stock, lead time, and preferred supplier.
records.notes: Config-shape master. Authored by inventory planners; no workflow gates.

records.description: Bill-of-kit for sellable bundles: parent item, list of component items with quantities, assembly_required flag (vs. explode-at-order).
records.catalog_description: Bills of kit for sellable bundles: the parent item plus component items with quantities and an assembly-required flag.
records.notes: Config-shape master. Kit BOMs are authored by merchandisers; no workflow.

records.catalog_description: Physical or organizational locations referenced across the system, used to place and group other records.
records.naming_authority_rationale: IWMS is the canonical owner of the abstract locations entity (named site / office / branch / facility where business activity happens). REAL-EST contributes the property-backed location records when commercial real estate is managed; HCM holds an embedded_master copy as employee work-location; the operational cluster (ITSM, ITAM, CMDB, FSM, ATS, ONBOARDING) embedded_masters for standalone deployment. The locations layer sits above physical real-estate (property_spaces) and below operational specifics (inventory_locations, pickup_locations).

records.description: The engineering item master: every distinct part number, assembly, or purchased component the engineering organization recognizes. Anchors revisions, BOMs, CAD files, and the downstream item-master feed to ERP and MES.
records.catalog_description: Distinct parts, assemblies, and components the organization recognizes, anchoring revisions, BOMs, and CAD files.

records.description: Revision records on an engineering part (rev A, B, C). Each released revision is a frozen snapshot of the part's attributes, BOM, and CAD references; engineering change orders are the only mechanism that mints a new released revision.
records.catalog_description: Released revisions of an engineering part, each a frozen snapshot of attributes, BOM, and CAD references minted only by a change order.

records.description: Engineering Change Order (ECO) master. Captures the proposed change, impact analysis (where-used traversal), CAB approval routing, effective date, and the set of affected parts / BOMs / drawings. Frozen on submission; only the CAB can override after that.
records.catalog_description: Engineering change orders capturing a proposed change, impact analysis, approval routing, effective date, and the affected parts, BOMs, and drawings.

records.description: Parent-child line items in the engineering BOM. Each row represents one child part under a parent assembly, with quantity, reference designator (for PCB / mechanical), effectivity (from-revision / from-date / from-serial), and find number. ECOs add, remove, or alter these lines.
records.catalog_description: Parent-child line items in an engineering bill of materials, each linking one child part under a parent assembly with quantity and effectivity.

records.description: CAD file metadata records (parts and assemblies). The vault stores the source CAD file (mechanical part and assembly files, electronic schematic and PCB files); this is the database record that tracks owner, check-in/out state, revision, viewable, and which engineering_revision it backs.
records.catalog_description: Metadata records for CAD parts and assemblies, tracking owner, check-in and check-out state, revision, and the file they reference.
records.naming_authority_rationale: PLM is the catalog-wide canonical owner of CAD-related concepts. Every flagship PLM vendor (Teamcenter, Windchill, ENOVIA, Aras, Autodesk Vault, Propel) mints this name verbatim against the same vault concept. No other domain in the catalog has a competing claim on CAD modeling artifacts; ITSM/CMDB/ITAM track physical/virtual configuration items, not CAD source files.

records.description: 2D drawing records derived from CAD models, with their own revision, approval, and title-block metadata. Drawings often have a release cycle distinct from the 3D model they reference, especially in regulated industries where the drawing IS the controlled artifact.
records.catalog_description: Two-dimensional drawings derived from CAD models, with their own revision, approval, and title-block metadata and a separate release cycle.
records.naming_authority_rationale: PLM is the catalog-wide canonical owner of CAD-related concepts. Drawings have a separate lifecycle from the 3D models they reference, so they warrant their own master. Same vendor unanimity as cad_models.

records.description: Manufacturing BOM (mBOM). The eBOM restructured for manufacturing assembly order, with phantom-part rollups, kitting, and process-specific decompositions. The mBOM feeds the MES / production planning system.
records.catalog_description: Manufacturing bills of materials restructured for assembly order, with phantom-part rollups, kitting, and process-specific decompositions.

records.description: Routing master: ordered sequence of operations required to produce a part, with work center, setup time, run time, and resource allocations. Drives MES work-instruction generation and ERP standard-cost calculations.
records.catalog_description: Routings defining the ordered sequence of operations to produce a part, with work center, setup time, run time, and resource allocations.

records.description: Resolved configurations of a configurable product: a specific combination of option-and-variant selections that the configurator engine has validated against the 150% BOM and configuration rules. Each variant is a sellable / buildable configuration with its own price, lead time, and resolved BOM.
records.catalog_description: Resolved product configurations, each a validated combination of option selections that is sellable or buildable, with its own price, lead time, and bill of materials.

records.description: Per part × substance × regulation declaration that asserts whether a controlled substance is present in the part, at what concentration, and whether it falls under a regulatory exemption. Aggregates from supplier declarations and propagates up the BOM via roll-up.
records.catalog_description: Declarations stating whether a controlled substance is present in a part, at what concentration, and whether a regulatory exemption applies.

records.description: Reference catalog of substances controlled by product-substance regulations (RoHS Restricted Substances list, REACH SVHC list, REACH Annex XVII, conflict minerals 3TG, PFAS lists by jurisdiction). Each substance row carries CAS number, regulation pointers, threshold concentrations, and exemption references.
records.catalog_description: Reference catalog of substances controlled by product regulations, with CAS number, regulation pointers, threshold concentrations, and exemptions.

records.description: System, software, and hardware requirements with parent-child decomposition (system → subsystem → component requirements). Carries verification method (test / inspection / analysis / demonstration), allocated subsystem, and traceability links to test cases (via the existing requirements_to_test_traceability junction).
records.catalog_description: System, software, and hardware requirements with parent-child decomposition, verification method, allocated subsystem, and links to test cases.

records.description: Balanced-scorecard and strategy-house visualizations linking strategic pillars to objectives, initiatives, and measures across financial, customer, process, and learning perspectives. Configured once per planning horizon; rarely changes structure.
records.catalog_description: Strategy-map visualizations linking strategic pillars to objectives, initiatives, and measures across financial, customer, process, and learning views.
records.notes: Config-shaped; no workflow. Authored once per planning cycle, edited inline; no per-state permissions needed.

records.description: QBR, MBR, and WBR operating-cadence meeting records. Carries agenda, participants, structured commentary against initiatives and KRs, action items, and outcome summary. Once closed, the record is locked as the audit trail of the cadence.
records.catalog_description: Operating-cadence meeting records (quarterly, monthly, weekly) with agenda, participants, commentary, and action items, locked as an audit trail once closed.

records.description: Decisions captured during operating reviews or strategy off-sites: changes to objective priorities, resource reallocation, initiative go/no-go, scope adjustments. Single decision-maker per record; once decided, the record is locked except by explicit revert.
records.catalog_description: Decisions captured during operating reviews and strategy off-sites, such as priority changes, reallocation, and initiative go or no-go.

records.description: The merchandising-master record for a sellable SKU as PIM models it: a hub of attributes, descriptions, variants, categorizations, translations, digital assets, and channel-specific overrides. Distinct from B2C-COMM commerce_products (storefront runtime view) and PLM engineering_parts (engineering record). Authoritative for marketing / catalog content; consumed by commerce, inventory, CPQ, and marketplaces.
records.catalog_description: Merchandising master records for sellable products, hubs of attributes, descriptions, variants, categories, translations, and assets consumed across channels.
records.notes: Workflow-bearing master. Submit-lock applies once submitted for review until approved or rejected.

records.description: Definition of a single attribute available to PIM products: data type, validation rules, attribute group, locale-awareness, and channel-specific overrides. Distinct from runtime attribute values on a product instance.
records.catalog_description: Definitions of product attributes available to products, with data type, validation rules, attribute group, locale awareness, and channel overrides.
records.notes: Config-shaped master. Authored by merchandising admin; record_status is the only workflow signal. Edits flow through the standard CRUD lifecycle without per-state permissions.

records.description: Specific size / color / locale / pack-size variant of a parent PIM product. Each variant has its own SKU, can have its own publish state, and inherits attribute defaults from the parent.
records.catalog_description: Specific size, color, or pack-size variants of a parent product, each with its own SKU and publish state, inheriting attribute defaults from the parent.
records.notes: Lifecycle inherits from parent pim_products in most vendors, but variant-level publish state is supported.

records.description: Hierarchical taxonomy node used to classify PIM products. Multiple parallel taxonomies coexist (merchandising tree, channel-specific trees, ERP category tree); each one's tree lives in this table with a parent_category_id self-reference.
records.catalog_description: Hierarchical taxonomy nodes used to classify products, supporting multiple parallel category trees through a parent self-reference.
records.notes: Config-shaped master. Taxonomy edits flow through record_status; no per-state workflow needed.

records.description: Locale-keyed string variant of an attribute or description on a PIM product or attribute. Drives multi-language publishing; can be machine-generated, human-translated, or a hybrid pipeline.
records.catalog_description: Locale-keyed translations of a product attribute or description, driving multi-language publishing through machine, human, or hybrid pipelines.
records.notes: Lightweight workflow: pending -> in_translation -> review -> approved. Translation memory and machine-translation suggestions feed in_translation.

records.description: Image, video, 3D model, or document asset tied to one or more PIM products. Carries rights metadata, renditions / derivatives, and CDN-delivery URLs. The DAM slice that lives inside PIM in v1; can be split out to a DAM domain when warranted.
records.catalog_description: Image, video, 3D model, and document assets tied to products, with rights metadata, renditions, and delivery URLs.
records.notes: Workflow: uploaded -> pending_approval -> approved -> published -> retired. Approval is one-or-many depending on rights review.

records.description: Definition of an outbound publishing channel: marketplace seller portals, merchant feeds, storefront platforms, retailer feeds, GDSN datapools, or a custom partner endpoint. Holds destination-schema mapping rules, credentials, and per-channel attribute overrides.
records.catalog_description: Definitions of outbound publishing channels such as marketplaces and merchant feeds, holding destination mappings, credentials, and per-channel overrides.
records.notes: Config-shaped master. Channel configuration; provisioned at deployment, edited rarely.

records.description: A single publish run of a product (or batch) to a syndication channel. Carries queue position, run status, per-record validation results, and rejection reasons from the destination.
records.catalog_description: Publish runs that send a product or batch to a syndication channel, with queue position, status, validation results, and rejection reasons.
records.notes: System-driven workflow: queued -> running -> partial_success / succeeded / failed. No human approval gates; admins re-queue from failed.

records.description: Customer-owned equipment that the service organization installs and maintains. Carries identity (manufacturer, model, serial), placement (customer_site), and lifecycle state (active, out_of_service, decommissioned). The asset register that work orders are performed against and service contracts cover.
records.catalog_description: Customer-owned equipment that the service organization installs and maintains, with identity, placement, and lifecycle state, covered by work orders and contracts.

records.description: Recurring preventive-maintenance plan attached to an installed_equipment unit. Defines cadence, due date, grace window, and overdue escalation. Drives proactive work-order generation when the next service is due.
records.catalog_description: Recurring preventive-maintenance plans for installed equipment, defining cadence, due date, grace window, and overdue escalation.

records.description: Physical service location belonging to a customer. One customer can have many sites (commercial chains, multi-property landlords, residential customers with multiple properties). Distinct from CRM accounts (the commercial relationship) and from internal locations (the service organization's own facilities).
records.catalog_description: Physical service locations belonging to a customer, where one customer can have many sites across properties or chains.

records.description: Medium-neutral catalog description of an intellectual work or expression, encoded in MARC21 or BIBFRAME. Covers books, ebooks, periodicals, serials, audio recordings, video, maps, manuscripts, datasets, and any other library material regardless of format.
records.catalog_description: Catalog descriptions of intellectual works across all formats, from books and periodicals to audio, video, maps, and datasets, encoded in library standards.
records.naming_authority_rationale: Library Management is the canonical owner of bibliographic records catalog-wide. The term is the universal library-science name for the catalog entry, used by every ILS and LSP vendor regardless of the medium described.

records.description: Physical or digital copy of a work held by the library. One bibliographic record may have many items, each with its own barcode, location, status, and circulation history.
records.catalog_description: Physical or digital copies of a work held by the library, each with its own barcode, location, status, and circulation history.

records.description: Controlled-vocabulary record for a name, subject, organization, or uniform title used as a heading in bibliographic records, supporting consistent retrieval and disambiguation.
records.catalog_description: Controlled-vocabulary records for names, subjects, organizations, or titles used as headings, supporting consistent retrieval and disambiguation.

records.description: Summary of which copies of a bibliographic record exist at a given location, including coverage statements for serials and shelf-location information.
records.catalog_description: Summaries of which copies of a title exist at a given location, including serial coverage statements and shelf-location information.

records.description: Circulation transaction recording the loan of a library item to a patron, including due date, renewal history, and return status.
records.catalog_description: Circulation transactions recording the loan of an item to a patron, with due date, renewal history, and return status.

records.description: Patron request to reserve a bibliographic record or specific item for later pickup, including position in queue, pickup location, and trap status.
records.catalog_description: Patron requests to reserve a title or specific item for later pickup, with queue position, pickup location, and trap status.

records.description: Monetary charge against a patron account for overdue, lost, or damaged library items, including assessment, payment, and waiver workflow.
records.catalog_description: Charges against a patron account for overdue, lost, or damaged items, with assessment, payment, and waiver workflow.

records.description: Configuration rule defining loan period, renewal limits, fine accrual, and hold behavior for a combination of item type and patron category.
records.catalog_description: Rules defining loan period, renewal limits, fine accrual, and hold behavior for each combination of item type and patron category.

records.description: Registered library member with borrowing privileges, contact information, patron category, and account history. Distinct from platform users; a patron may or may not have a linked user account for self-service.
records.catalog_description: Registered library members with borrowing privileges, contact information, patron category, and account history.

records.description: Classification of patrons (e.g. student, faculty, staff, public, juvenile) that drives circulation policy and access entitlement.
records.catalog_description: Classifications of patrons (student, faculty, staff, public, juvenile) that drive circulation policy and access entitlement.

records.description: Order for library materials from a book vendor, including line items, fund allocations, EDI exchange status, and receiving workflow.
records.catalog_description: Orders for library materials from a book vendor, with line items, fund allocations, EDI exchange status, and receiving workflow.

records.description: Book or serials vendor relationship managed by the library, including account credentials, EDI settings, claiming defaults, and contact information.
records.catalog_description: Book or serials vendor relationships managed by the library, with account credentials, EDI settings, claiming defaults, and contacts.

records.description: Active subscription to a periodical or other continuing resource, including issue prediction, check-in records, claim history, and renewal schedule.
records.catalog_description: Active subscriptions to periodicals or continuing resources, with issue prediction, check-in records, claim history, and renewal schedule.

records.description: License agreement for an electronic resource (database, ebook collection, ejournal package), including authorized users, concurrent-user limits, ILL permissions, and renewal terms.
records.catalog_description: License agreements for electronic resources (databases, ebooks, ejournals), with authorized users, concurrent-user limits, and renewal terms.

records.description: Patron-owned saved query or reading list in the discovery layer, optionally configured to send alerts when new matching items are added to the catalog.
records.catalog_description: Patron-owned saved queries or reading lists, optionally configured to alert when new matching items are added to the catalog.

records.description: Patron-initiated request to borrow material from another library, including routing across sharing partners, shipping status, and fulfillment workflow.
records.catalog_description: Patron requests to borrow material from another library, with routing across sharing partners, shipping status, and fulfillment workflow.
records.naming_authority_rationale: Library Management is the canonical owner of interlibrary loan requests. The phrase 'interlibrary loan' is unambiguously library-domain with no plausible competing claim from any other catalog domain.

records.description: Partner library or consortium member with which this library participates in resource sharing, including agreement terms, default lending policies, and contact endpoints.
records.catalog_description: Partner libraries or consortium members for resource sharing, with agreement terms, default lending policies, and contact endpoints.

records.description: Versioned ontology of skill nodes, synonyms, parent-child relationships.
records.catalog_description: Versioned ontologies of skill nodes, with synonyms and parent-child relationships.

records.description: Individual skill node belonging to a taxonomy version; the row referenced by every profile entry, competency-model entry, and inference run.
records.catalog_description: Individual skill nodes within a taxonomy version, referenced by every profile entry, competency model, and inference run.
records.naming_authority_rationale: SKILLS-MGMT is the canonical authority for the bare-word skill ontology in the catalog. Every domain that references individual skill atoms (TALENT-MGMT, LMS, ATS, TLNT-INTEL) defers to this row. No other domain has a competing claim on the bare noun.

records.description: Discrete proficiency-rating event against a skill, with rater, method (self, manager, peer, test), score, and timestamp.
records.catalog_description: Proficiency-rating events against a skill, recording the rater, method (self, manager, peer, or test), score, and date.

records.description: Peer or manager validation of a claimed or inferred skill on a profile; one-shot social signal distinct from a formal assessment.
records.catalog_description: Peer or manager validations of a claimed skill on a profile: a quick social signal, distinct from a formal assessment.

records.description: Role-anchored bundle of required skills plus target proficiency levels, used for gap analysis and internal matching.
records.catalog_description: Role-anchored bundles of required skills and target proficiency levels, used for gap analysis and internal matching.

records.description: Audit record of a passive skill-inference batch on skill profiles: model version, input signals (learning, performance, work activity), outputs, timestamp.
records.catalog_description: Audit records of automated skill-inference batches, capturing model version, input signals, outputs, and timestamp.

records.description: Internal postings covering full-time roles, gigs, projects, stretch assignments, and mentorships.
records.catalog_description: Internal opportunity postings covering full-time roles, gigs, projects, stretch assignments, and mentorships.

records.description: Employee expression of interest in an internal opportunity, with status workflow (submitted, reviewed, accepted, rejected, withdrawn).
records.catalog_description: Employee expressions of interest in an internal opportunity, tracking status from submitted through accepted, rejected, or withdrawn.

records.description: AI-generated next-move suggestions for an employee, with rationale and freshness.
records.catalog_description: AI-generated next-move suggestions for an employee, with rationale and freshness.

records.description: Computed match between a person and a role or opportunity, with score, model version, drivers.
records.catalog_description: Computed match scores between a person and a role or opportunity, with score, model version, and drivers.

records.description: AI-projected route from a current role toward an aspiration, with required skills (distinct from employee-authored career_aspirations).
records.catalog_description: Projected routes from a worker's current role toward an aspiration, with the skills required, distinct from employee-authored aspirations.

records.description: Matched mentor-mentee relationship with goals, cadence, and status.
records.catalog_description: Matched mentor and mentee relationships, with goals, meeting cadence, and status.

records.description: Audit record of a matching or scoring batch: model version, inputs (skill profiles, opportunities, roles), outputs (fit scores, recommendations), timestamp.
records.catalog_description: Audit records of a matching or scoring batch, capturing model version, inputs, outputs such as fit scores and recommendations, and timestamp.

records.description: Single recruiter-to-candidate touchpoint (email, InMail, call, SMS, event invite). Carries channel, direction, timestamp, status, and content reference.
records.catalog_description: Single recruiter-to-candidate touchpoints across channels such as email, call, or SMS, with direction, timestamp, status, and content reference.

records.description: Multi-touch automated outreach sequence targeting talent-pool segments. Carries cadence, step templates, audience filter, and lifecycle state.
records.catalog_description: Multi-touch automated outreach sequences targeting talent-pool segments, with cadence, step templates, audience filter, and lifecycle state.

records.description: Junction between candidates and recruitment_events recording registration, check-in, attendance, and conversion outcome.
records.catalog_description: Links between candidates and recruiting events, recording registration, check-in, attendance, and conversion outcome.

records.description: Free-text recruiter note attached to a candidate, application, or pool, time-stamped and authored by a user.
records.catalog_description: Free-text recruiter notes attached to a candidate, application, or talent pool, time-stamped and authored by a user.

records.description: Per-candidate opt-in record for GDPR / CCPA / data retention. Carries consent type, jurisdiction, granted timestamp, withdrawal timestamp, retention window.
records.catalog_description: Per-candidate opt-in records for privacy and data retention, with consent type, jurisdiction, and granted and withdrawal timestamps.

records.description: Junction between candidates and talent_pools. Carries added timestamp, source, status_in_pool (cold/warm/hot), match score, and last_engagement timestamp.
records.catalog_description: Links between candidates and talent pools, carrying added date, source, status in the pool, match score, and last engagement.

records.description: Rule-based pool definition (boolean filter over candidates) that materializes membership automatically. Examples: 'Senior PMs in NYC with FinTech experience', 'Engineering alumni who left in the last 2 years'.
records.catalog_description: Rule-based pool definitions over candidates that automatically populate membership from a saved filter.

records.description: Persisted recruiter boolean query over the candidate database. Carries filter expression, last_run timestamp, alert preferences.
records.catalog_description: Saved recruiter searches over the candidate database, with the filter expression, last-run time, and alert preferences.

records.description: Bounty rule defining the payout amount and conditions for a successful referral (e.g. $5000 paid 90 days after hire start, scaled by role level).
records.catalog_description: Bounty rules defining the payout amount and conditions for a successful referral, such as a fixed sum paid after the new hire's start.

records.description: Individual payout instance triggered when a referred candidate is hired and meets tenure conditions. Lifecycle: pending -> approved -> paid (-> clawed_back).
records.catalog_description: Individual referral payouts triggered when a referred candidate is hired and meets tenure conditions, moving from pending to approved to paid.

records.description: Time-bounded promotion offering bonus referral rewards (e.g. 'double bonus for engineering Q3 2026', 'spot-bonus for hard-to-fill roles'). Scopes a referral_rewards override.
records.catalog_description: Time-bounded promotions offering bonus referral rewards, scoping an override to the standard referral payout rules.

records.description: Configured bundle of check types (county criminal + national + MVR + drug screen + employment verification + education verification) that can be ordered as one unit. Catalog-shaped: defines what a 'standard package' looks like for a role tier.
records.catalog_description: Configured bundles of check types that can be ordered as one unit, defining what a standard package looks like for a role tier.

records.description: Individual sub-check result inside a background_checks order (e.g. county_criminal, ssn_trace, employment_verification, drug_screen). Each component has its own status, result, and provider source.
records.catalog_description: Individual sub-check results inside a background check order (county criminal, SSN trace, employment verification, drug screen), each with its own status and source.

records.description: Pre-check legally required disclosure form presented to the candidate before any consumer report is requested. Carries the disclosure text version, candidate acknowledgment signature, timestamp, and jurisdiction-specific addenda (CA, NY, etc.).
records.catalog_description: Legally required disclosure forms shown to a candidate before a consumer report is requested, with text version, signature, and timestamp.

records.description: Human review decision on a completed background_check (Clear / Engaged / Decisional / Declined). Carries adjudicator, decision rationale, individualized assessment notes per EEOC guidance.
records.catalog_description: Human review decisions on a completed background check (clear, engaged, decisional, declined), with rationale and individualized assessment notes.

records.description: FCRA-mandated notice issued when a background_check result is used to decline a candidate. Two-step process: pre-adverse notice + waiting period + post-adverse final notice. Carries notice type, sent timestamp, copy_of_report enclosure, dispute window expiry.
records.catalog_description: FCRA-mandated notices issued when a background check is used to decline a candidate, covering the pre-adverse and post-adverse two-step process and dispute window.

records.description: Candidate-initiated dispute of a background_check component result under FCRA rights. Carries disputed component, candidate statement, provider re-investigation result, resolution.
records.catalog_description: Candidate-initiated disputes of a background check result under FCRA, with the disputed component, candidate statement, re-investigation result, and resolution.

records.description: Configured stage in the recruiting pipeline (sourced, applied, screened, phone_screen, onsite, offer, hired). Per-requisition or per-template ordered list; defines the lifecycle of a job_application.
records.catalog_description: Configured stages in the recruiting pipeline (sourced, applied, screened, onsite, offer, hired) that define a job application's lifecycle.

records.description: Audit-trail record of an application moving between stages. Carries from_stage, to_stage, actor, timestamp, reason. Source of cycle-time, time-in-stage, and conversion-rate analytics.
records.catalog_description: Audit-trail records of an application moving between stages, with from-stage, to-stage, actor, timestamp, and reason for cycle-time analytics.

records.description: Approval step in the chain that gates opening a job_requisition (hiring manager -> finance -> exec). Each step carries approver, decision, timestamp, rationale.
records.catalog_description: Approval steps that gate opening a job requisition, each recording the approver, decision, timestamp, and rationale.

records.description: Syndication of a job_posting to an external board (LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor, internal mobility portal). Carries board name, post timestamp, expiry, cost, applicant attribution.
records.catalog_description: Syndications of a job posting to external boards, with board name, post and expiry times, cost, and applicant attribution.

records.description: Custom screening question attached to a job_posting or template (knockout questions, qualifying questions). Carries question text, type (boolean/single-select/free-text), required, knockout rule.
records.catalog_description: Custom screening questions attached to a job posting or template, including knockout and qualifying questions with their answer type and rules.

records.description: Candidate-supplied answer to an application_screening_question on a specific job_application. Drives auto-disqualify on knockout rules.
records.catalog_description: Candidate answers to screening questions on a specific job application, used to auto-disqualify on knockout rules.

records.description: Voluntary self-identification submitted by an applicant for EEO-1 / OFCCP / VEVRAA reporting (gender, race/ethnicity, veteran status, disability). Required compliance artifact for US employers >100 employees; stored separately from candidates record per regulation.
records.catalog_description: Voluntary self-identification submitted by applicants for equal-employment reporting, stored separately from candidate records per regulation.

records.description: Reusable interview template per role / stage. Bundles assigned questions, target competencies, recommended scorecard, expected duration. Greenhouse's core authoring unit.
records.catalog_description: Reusable interview templates per role and stage, bundling questions, target competencies, recommended scorecard, and expected duration.

records.description: Composition of interviewers assigned to a specific interview, including their role on the panel (lead, technical, behavioral, debrief moderator) and weighting on the consolidated scorecard.
records.catalog_description: Interviewers assigned to a specific interview, with each person's role on the panel and weight on the consolidated scorecard.

records.description: Library item for assessments (coding challenge, work sample, take-home, skills test). Carries title, vendor, time limit, scoring rubric. Materializes into candidate_assessments when assigned.
records.catalog_description: Reusable assessment definitions such as coding challenges, work samples, and skills tests, with time limit and scoring rubric, assigned to candidates.

records.description: Question bank entry tied to competencies. Carries question text, type (behavioral / technical / situational), competency tags, suggested follow-ups, rubric.
records.catalog_description: Reusable interview questions tied to competencies, with question type, suggested follow-ups, and scoring rubric.

records.description: Bookable time window an interviewer has marked available. Drives self-serve scheduling (Goodtime / Modern Hire / Calendly for Recruiting). Carries interviewer, start, end, allowed interview types.
records.catalog_description: Bookable time windows an interviewer has marked available, with allowed interview types, driving self-serve scheduling.

records.description: Versioned snapshot of a job_offer during negotiation (initial -> counter -> revised -> accepted). Each version carries the structured terms (base, bonus, equity, start_date) and the author of the change.
records.catalog_description: Versioned snapshots of a job offer during negotiation, each holding the structured terms and the author of the change, from initial through accepted.

records.description: Approval step in the offer-approval chain (HRBP -> Comp -> Finance -> Exec). Triggered when an offer exceeds band, includes non-standard equity, or matches other escalation rules.
records.catalog_description: Approval steps in the offer-approval chain, triggered when an offer exceeds band, includes non-standard equity, or matches other escalation rules.

records.description: Generated PDF artifact of the offer terms, distinct from the structured offer record. Versioned in lockstep with offer_versions. Carries template_id, render timestamp, e-sign envelope link.
records.catalog_description: Generated PDF letters of the offer terms, versioned alongside the structured offer and linked to the e-signature envelope.

records.description: FCRA-mandated notice sent to a candidate before a final adverse-action decision based on a consumer report. Carries a copy of the report and Summary of Rights, and opens a waiting period (typically 5 business days) during which the candidate may dispute findings before the final adverse-action notice issues.
records.catalog_description: FCRA-mandated notices sent to a candidate before a final adverse-action decision, including the report and rights summary and opening a dispute waiting period.

records.description: OFCCP-mandated log of every Internet Applicant against a requisition, capturing demographic data, expressed interest, basic qualifications, and disposition. Federal contractors must retain for OFCCP audit; the record is independent of EEO voluntary self-id.
records.catalog_description: OFCCP-mandated logs of every internet applicant against a requisition, capturing demographics, expressed interest, qualifications, and disposition for audit.

records.description: Typed reason-for-non-selection on a job application. Drives OFCCP applicant-flow reporting and internal hiring analytics; distinct from `application_stage_transitions` which logs the stage change but not the categorized business reason.
records.catalog_description: Categorized reasons a job application was not selected, driving OFCCP applicant-flow reporting and internal hiring analytics.

records.description: GDPR Articles 15-22 (and analogous CPRA/PIPEDA) request from a candidate exercising access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, or objection rights against personal data the ATS holds. Tracks request type, intake channel, due date, fulfillment, and verification.
records.catalog_description: Privacy rights requests from candidates exercising access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, or objection, with intake, due date, and fulfillment.

records.description: Candidate acknowledgment of receipt of the FCRA Summary of Consumer Rights at consent time, prior to a background check. Required by 15 U.S.C. §1681g(c). Captured separately from the consent itself so the disclosure copy and acknowledgment timestamp persist for audit.
records.catalog_description: Candidate acknowledgments of receiving the summary of consumer rights at consent time, captured separately so the copy and timestamp persist for audit.

records.description: Voluntary candidate disclosure of protected-class membership (race, ethnicity, gender, veteran status, disability status) per EEOC and OFCCP self-id requirements. Distinct from `eeo_responses` which captures the survey response: this row captures the offer/decline-to-answer decision and audit metadata.
records.catalog_description: Voluntary candidate disclosures of protected-class membership per EEOC and OFCCP requirements, recording the offer or decline-to-answer decision and audit metadata.

records.description: Federal-contractor audit log of every applicant-flow event (requisition open, application receipt, disposition, hire) carrying the actor, timestamp, and OFCCP-relevant fields needed to reconstruct compliance decisions during an audit. Immutable append-only.
records.catalog_description: Immutable, append-only audit logs of every applicant-flow event for federal contractors, carrying the actor, timestamp, and compliance-relevant fields.

records.description: Per-requisition role-scoped staffing junction: assigns specific users to recruiter, hiring manager, coordinator, interviewer, and reviewer roles on a single requisition. Captures team composition without requiring global RBAC for transient interview-panel membership.
records.catalog_description: Assignments of specific users to recruiter, hiring manager, coordinator, interviewer, and reviewer roles on a single requisition.

records.description: Campaign container that bundles assignments by audience and due-date: annual code-of-conduct cycle, harassment refresh, security awareness wave.
records.catalog_description: Campaigns that bundle compliance training assignments by audience and due date, such as an annual code-of-conduct cycle.

records.description: Measurable result attached to an okr_objective. The unit of scoring on OKR programs — vendors universally model KR as first-class (Asana, Monday, ClickUp, Workfront).
records.catalog_description: Measurable results attached to an objective, the unit of scoring that tracks progress toward the goal.

records.description: Periodic status update on an okr_objective or key_result during the active cycle. Cadence-of-record (weekly/bi-weekly) for OKR programs. May discuss individual performance — flagged as personal content.
records.catalog_description: Periodic status updates on an objective or key result during the active cycle, the cadence of record for OKR programs.

records.description: Typed dependency between two work_items: predecessor/successor with type (FS finish-to-start, SS start-to-start, FF finish-to-finish, SF start-to-finish). Backs the WORK-DEPS-SCHED capability. Modeled by Asana, Monday, ClickUp, Workfront, Smartsheet.
records.catalog_description: Typed dependencies between two work items, linking predecessor and successor with finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish, or start-to-finish type.

records.description: Zero-duration gate within a work_project marking a meaningful transition. Distinct from a regular work_item by gate semantics (passed/missed). Asana, Monday, ClickUp, Workfront, Smartsheet all model.
records.catalog_description: Zero-duration gates within a project marking a meaningful transition, distinguished from regular items by passed or missed semantics.

records.description: Single approval gate on a work_item or work_project, performed by a designated approver. Belongs to a work_approval_chain. Per-step states: pending / approved / rejected / expired.
records.catalog_description: Single approval gates on a work item or project, performed by a designated approver, with states pending, approved, rejected, or expired.

records.description: Ordered or parallel set of work_approval_steps gating a work_item or work_project transition. Backs the APPROVAL-WORKFLOW capability (cross-cutting; this is the WORK-MGMT realization).
records.catalog_description: Ordered or parallel sets of approval steps that gate a work item or project transition.

records.catalog_description: Per-user, per-period sums of allocated effort across work items, compared against a capacity ceiling.

records.description: User-defined field attached to a work_project or workspace, typed (text, number, date, select, etc.). Applies to all work_items in scope. Monday columns / Asana custom fields / ClickUp custom fields / Workfront / Smartsheet column types.
records.catalog_description: User-defined fields attached to a project or workspace, typed as text, number, date, select, and more, applying to all items in scope.

records.description: Per-work_item value for a work_custom_field. Junction-style master: tuple (work_item, work_custom_field, value). Monday column_values, Asana custom_field_values, Smartsheet cells.
records.catalog_description: Per-work-item values for a custom field, one value per item and field.

records.description: Container within a work_project that groups work_items for board/list views. Asana sections / Monday groups / ClickUp statuses-as-columns / Workfront statuses / Smartsheet parent rows.
records.catalog_description: Containers within a project that group work items for board and list views.

records.catalog_description: Reusable project blueprints with seeded sections, items, custom fields, and automations.

records.catalog_description: Reusable work-item blueprints with seeded assignee role, due-date offset, subtasks, and custom field defaults.

records.catalog_description: Free-form labels attached to work items for cross-cutting categorization such as priority, theme, or status.

records.catalog_description: Files or external links attached to a work item.

records.description: Structured intake form definition: schema (fields, validation), target project, routing rules. Asana Forms, Monday Forms, ClickUp Forms, Workfront Request Queues, Smartsheet Forms.
records.catalog_description: Structured intake form definitions, with field schema, validation, target project, and routing rules.

records.catalog_description: Submitted instances of an intake form, carrying field values, submitter, and timestamp, and converting to a work item via routing rules.

records.description: Typed role assignment of a user to a SaaS application (business owner, IT owner, finance owner, security owner). Not a flat FK on saas_applications because one app may have multiple typed owners; modeled by Productiv and LeanIX as a first-class junction.
records.catalog_description: Typed owner assignments linking a user to a SaaS app as its business, IT, finance, or security owner.

records.description: Discovered or configured connection between SMP and a SaaS application's APIs (SSO source, SCIM source, finance source, usage source). records.catalog_description: Configured connections between the SaaS management platform and an app's APIs for sign-on, provisioning, finance, and usage data.

records.description: Curated, published listing of a sanctioned SaaS application that employees can browse and request access to. Carries description, owner, request route, SSO availability, approval workflow. records.catalog_description: Published listings of sanctioned SaaS apps that employees can browse and request, with description, owner, request route, and approval flow.

records.description: System-raised anomaly on the SaaS portfolio: shadow-IT signup detected, license-overage projected, renewal window opening, integration token expiring, vendor-risk score change. records.catalog_description: System-raised alerts on the SaaS portfolio: shadow-IT signups, projected license overages, opening renewals, or vendor-risk changes.

records.description: Portfolio-rationalization stage of a SaaS application (Evaluate, Pilot, Sanctioned, Sunset, Retired). records.catalog_description: Portfolio-rationalization stages of a SaaS app such as evaluate, pilot, sanctioned, sunset, and retired.

records.catalog_description: System-generated proposals to right-size or consolidate SaaS spend, with estimated savings, rationale, type, and status.

records.catalog_description: Executed reclamation actions against a license seat (revoke, downgrade, or reassign), with the savings realized.

records.catalog_description: Per-renewal-cycle envelopes covering timeline, owner, vendor proposals received, fallback notes, and decisions taken.

records.catalog_description: SaaS vendor risk scorecards covering attestation status, data-processing review, subprocessors, breach history, and posture score.

records.description: Declarative orchestration: trigger + steps (provision in SaaS app, send notification, file offboarding action, request approval, escalate). records.catalog_description: Declarative automation workflows with a trigger and steps such as provisioning, notifying, offboarding, or requesting approval.

records.description: Subjects of a background check order: the person being screened, their contact and consent details, and the identifiers searches resolve against. The order is placed for a screening candidate.
Criminal-history searches run as components of an order across county, state, federal, and national sources, each returning records to review or a clear result.
Verifications of a candidate's past employers, titles, and dates against the employment history they declared, run as a component of an order.
Verifications of a candidate's degrees, institutions, and graduation dates with the awarding bodies, run as a component of an order.
Driving-record pulls for roles that require driving, returning license status, violations, and endorsements for DOT/FMCSA driver qualification.
Verifications of professional licenses, certifications, and credentials with the issuing authority for roles that require them.
Searches of sanctions, debarment, and global watchlists for matches against a candidate, run as a component of an order.
Checks of healthcare exclusion lists for candidates barred from federally funded healthcare programs, run for healthcare employers.
Status-history entries tracking an order as it moves through ordered, pending, in progress, completed, and disputed states over time.
Invitations sent to a candidate to start their portion of a screening order, tracking sent, opened, and completed engagement.
Sessions in which a candidate signs in to the screening portal to give consent, supply information, and upload documents for their order.
Notifications sent to candidates and requesters at key points in a screening order, recording channel, recipient, and delivery outcome.
Configurable eligibility rule sets that map screening results to pass, fail, or review outcomes so the same standard applies to every candidate.
Written consents a candidate signs authorizing a consumer report before any screening is ordered, as FCRA requires.
EEOC Green-factor assessments weighing the nature of an offense, time elapsed, and job relevance before a record disqualifies a candidate.
Jurisdiction-aware fair-chance checks that enforce when and how criminal history may be considered under state and local ban-the-box laws.
Verifications that a candidate is who they claim to be, validating identity documents and biographic data before and during the engagement.
Ongoing subscriptions that keep a worker under post-hire monitoring so new records surface as alerts instead of waiting for the next rescreen.
Alerts raised against a monitoring subscription when a new criminal record surfaces for a monitored worker, queued for review and adjudication.
Periodic re-runs of a screening package for an existing worker to refresh clearance on a schedule the role or policy sets.
Screenings of candidates and records outside the United States, handling country-specific sources, consent, and lawful-basis requirements.
GDPR lawful-basis consent records captured from a candidate before a background screening is run on a non-US (EU/UK) data subject. Distinct from learner-training consent.
records.catalog_description: GDPR consent records for background screening of non-US candidates, capturing lawful basis, scope, and withdrawal.

records.description: External parties the organization depends on and risk-manages: the broad umbrella inventory record covering suppliers, service providers, processors, and partners, whether or not each is an invoiced supplier.
Per-service, contract-scoped relationships with a third party. Each engagement carries its own scope, data access, and risk profile, so one third party can hold several distinct engagements.
Criticality classifications such as critical, high, moderate, and low that drive re-assessment cadence and the depth of controls a third party must demonstrate.
Vendor-side respondents and relationship owners who answer questionnaires and supply evidence for a third party. Smaller programs inline these as attributes.
Business-sponsor intake requests that start the third-party lifecycle, naming the proposed third party, the service, and the sponsoring team before diligence begins.
Termination and exit due-diligence records for ending a third-party relationship: data return or destruction, access revocation, and final obligations. Not every program formalizes exit.
Flags marking an engagement as supporting a critical or important business function under operational-resilience rules, driving heightened oversight. Sector-bound.

The deep, engagement and contract-gated diligence record that decides whether it is safe to do business with a third party. Distinct from operational supplier qualification: it is keyed on the third party and scored from questionnaires and external ratings.
Reusable questionnaire templates the assessment library draws from, such as standardized security and control questionnaires issued to third parties during diligence.
Per-question answers a third party returns on an assessment, with the supporting evidence attached, linking each response to the questionnaire version used.
Batches that send a questionnaire to many third parties on a periodic re-assessment cadence and track collection to completion. Some programs assess ad hoc instead.
Evidence artifacts collected during diligence, such as audit reports, certifications, and policies, stored against the third party and its assessment.
Agreements required when a third party handles protected health information, tracking the signed instrument and its scope. Sector-bound to US healthcare.
Processor agreements required when a third party processes personal data on the organization's behalf, tracking the instrument and the processing terms. Jurisdiction-bound.

Receipt and expiry tracking for third-party control reports and certifications, such as service-organization control reports and security-standard certifications. Distinct from employee policy attestations.
Payment-card service-provider compliance tracking, recording a third party's attestation of compliance and its validity window. Sector-bound.
Records aligning third-party diligence to financial-regulator interagency guidance on managing third-party relationships. Sector-bound to regulated financial institutions.
Internal computed risk scores per third party and engagement, recalculated from assessment results and monitoring signals to drive the re-assessment cadence.

Point-in-time external security scores ingested for a third party from outside-in scanning sources, snapshotting the score, the source, and the scan date. Not every program subscribes to an external feed.

Breach, sanctions, and financial-distress events surfaced against a third party for triage, each linking the signal to the third party it concerns. Optional where a program does not ingest external signals.
Issues raised against a third party from an assessment or a monitoring signal, carrying a third-party reference and a remediation lifecycle. Distinct from the enterprise compliance-risk register.
Vendor-scoped remediation plans that resolve a third-party finding, time-boxed to the next review cycle or contract renewal, with owners and due dates tracked to closure.
Decisions to accept a third-party finding rather than remediate it, recorded with an owner, a rationale, and an expiry so accepted risk is revisited. Not every program formalizes acceptances.
Subcontractor and nth-party edges linking a third party to the providers it in turn depends on, building the supply-chain graph behind a direct relationship. Not universal.
Derived views showing where many critical engagements trace back to the same shared fourth parties, surfacing single points of failure across the supply chain.
Structured registers of information-and-communications-technology providers maintained for operational-resilience reporting. Sector-bound to regulated financial institutions.
Disclosures of the chain of subcontractors a critical provider relies on, required by operational-resilience rules to make nth-party dependencies visible. Sector-bound.
Attestations a provider gives about the security and integrity of its supply chain under supply-chain risk-management standards. Sector-bound.

The buyer-side statement of work that scopes outsourced services a firm will deliver: the deliverables, the schedule, the price basis, and the acceptance terms. The headline document the whole engagement hangs off, distinct from the underlying contract that governs it.

The active firm-level engagement that executes a statement of work: the spine milestones, deliverables, and invoices bind to, carrying the supplier, the contract reference, and the engagement-scoped scorecard. One supplier can hold several distinct engagements.

Bids and proposals a firm submits against a specific statement of work, capturing the proposed scope, approach, and price for evaluation. Optional because some buyers run a SOW off a pre-awarded master agreement without a bid round.
Amendments to an active statement of work that revise scope, schedule, deliverables, or price, tracked through approval so the SOW stays current. Optional because not every engagement amends.

Schedule-and-payment checkpoints that break a services engagement into accountable stages, each tied to deliverables and to the milestone invoice it releases. The settlement mechanic that makes outcome-based services payment work.

Concrete work products a firm produces under a statement of work, tracked from submission to acceptance against the milestone they close. Optional because some buyers settle on the milestone alone and inline deliverables as attributes.

Invoices a firm raises against an accepted milestone of a services engagement, so payment follows delivered outcomes rather than elapsed time. The settlement record for outcome-based services work, distinct from time-and-materials contingent invoices.

Formal sign-off records capturing that the buyer accepted a deliverable or milestone, who accepted it, and when, gating the milestone invoice. Optional because some buyers accept implicitly on invoice rather than recording a typed acceptance.

entity.description: Junction table connecting domains to the data objects they hold, with a mastery qualifier. Captures the observation that Customer lives in CRM (primary), Billing (secondary), and Support (secondary), the seed of the data-silo map.

computed_fields.name: domain_data_object_label
computed_fields.description: Composed from the parent domain name and the parent data object name. Recomputed on every write so renames in either parent flow through.

fields.title: Role
fields.description: The domain's role with respect to this data object. master: authoritative owner of some slice in a holistic deployment. embedded_master: point-solution local master — owns its own copy when deployed standalone; demoted to consumer at runtime when a canonical master is also deployed in the same environment. contributor: writes some fields without being authoritative. consumer: reads only. derived: produces computed projections only. Combined with the necessity column, embedded_master+required rows count toward the Signal 1 multi-master integration-burden score; embedded_master+optional rows do not.

fields.title: Necessity
fields.description: Whether the domain's relationship to this data object is load-bearing for its workflow. required: the domain cannot function in any realistic deployment without this relationship being active (e.g. OMS reads customers, ATS embedded-masters positions). optional: the domain tolerates absence — the read/write happens only in some deployment configurations or for some workflows (e.g. ATS embedded-masters cost_centers when finance isn't deployed alongside, but functions fine without). Combined with role, embedded_master+required rows count toward the Signal 1 multi-master integration-burden score; embedded_master+optional rows do not.

AGENCY-MGMT masters Agency Job: Central engagement record for an agency client — the unit of billable work.

AGENCY-MGMT masters Agency Time Entry: Time logged against an agency_job + task + deliverable by an employee or freelancer, with client-rate-card application, billable/non-billable/agency-overhead coding, and discipline tagging (strategy, design, account, production).
AGENCY-MGMT masters Retainer: Recurring fee agreement with a client — monthly amount, included scope (hours or deliverables), period, and live burn-down against logged time + costs.
AGENCY-MGMT masters Media Plan: Per-campaign media-buying plan broken down by outlet, channel, daypart, audience, flight dates, and budget allocation.

AGENCY-MGMT masters Insertion Order: Purchase order from the agency to a specific media outlet (publisher, broadcaster, platform) committing budget at negotiated rates with commission terms and make-good provisions.
AGENCY-MGMT masters Creative Brief: Initiating document for a creative job — client objective, audience, key message, mandatories, deliverable list, deadlines, and budget.
AGENCY-MGMT masters Creative Deliverable: Asset under production within an agency_job — an image, video, layout, copy doc, or campaign element with version history and proofing/approval state.
AGENCY-MGMT masters Agency Estimate: Pre-engagement client estimate priced from rate cards, expected effort, and media/production cost lines with markup.
AGENCY-MGMT consumes customers (CDP/CRM-mastered) as the agency client list — the buyer side of every agency_job, retainer, and invoice.
AGENCY-MGMT consumes employees (HCM-mastered) as the resourceable agency staff pool — assigned to jobs, logging time at loaded billing rates.
AGENCY-MGMT consumes contracts (CLM-mastered) — Master Services Agreements and signed SOWs that seed billing terms, scope, and rate cards on agency_jobs.
AGENCY-MGMT consumes won opportunities (CRM-mastered) as the trigger to spin up an agency_job and request scope finalisation.
AGENCY-MGMT consumes suppliers (S2P-mastered) — media outlets, freelancers, production houses billed against insertion_orders and job costs.

PAYROLL local-masters positions for pay-grade / FLSA classification / GL-allocation tagging when no HCM is deployed; reads from HCM when present.
PAYROLL local-masters org_units for cost-centre and legal-entity allocation of payroll journals when no HCM is deployed; reads from HCM when present.
PAYROLL local-masters cost_centers for journal-entry GL allocation when no ERP is integrated; reads from ERP-FIN when present.
PAYROLL consumes legal_entities to determine the employer-of-record, tax registration, and reporting entity per pay_run.
PAYROLL consumes benefit_dependents only when imputed-income or dependent-coverage tax treatment is in scope (US health plans, life-insurance >50k). Many deployments skip this.

ATS local-masters the new-hire pre-employee record (offer accepted, but not yet active in HCM); persists until handoff via offer.accepted. Reads from HCM for internal-mobility candidates when present.
ATS local-masters positions for requisition-to-position binding (open headcount, hiring manager, required skills); reads from HCM/SWP when integrated.
ATS local-masters job_profiles for requisition templates and competency requirements; reads from HCM when present.
ATS local-masters org_units to scope requisitions to a department/location for routing and posting; reads from HCM when present.
ATS local-masters cost_centers only for budget-tagged requisitions in deployments without finance integration; many ATS deployments skip cost_centers entirely.
ONBOARDING local-masters positions for first-day-readiness checks (workstation, manager, location) when no HCM is integrated. Reads from HCM when present.
ONBOARDING local-masters org_units to scope journeys to a department/location and assign location-specific tasks; reads from HCM when integrated.
ONBOARDING consumes hardware_assets to confirm Day-1 laptop/peripheral readiness via the ITAM lifecycle handoff.
BEN-ADMIN local-masters org_units for benefit-group assignment (different benefit eligibility by location, business unit) when no HCM is integrated.
BEN-ADMIN consumes legal_entities to scope benefit-plan offerings (different plans by employer-of-record / country).
COMP-MGMT local-masters positions for salary-band assignment, job-architecture binding, and pay-equity grouping when no HCM is integrated.
COMP-MGMT local-masters job_profiles for job-level and grade structures when deployed standalone; reads from HCM when integrated.
COMP-MGMT local-masters cost_centers for merit-budget allocation only in deployments without finance integration.
COMP-MGMT consumes the approved financial_plan to validate merit-cycle budget envelope. Many deployments run comp planning standalone with an Excel-imported budget number.
LMS local-masters the worker record for learner-profile fields (manager, department, role, hire date) when deployed standalone; reads from HCM when integrated.
LMS local-masters positions only for role-based learning-path assignment in deployments without HCM integration; many LMS deployments key off employees + department only.
LMS local-masters org_units for department-scoped course assignment, manager hierarchy, and team-level reporting when deployed standalone.
LMS local-masters job_profiles for competency-to-course mapping in skills-cloud LMS deployments; many LMS deployments skip job_profile binding.
LMS local-masters cost_centers for training-cost allocation only when finance integration exists or training-budget tracking is enabled; many deployments skip cost-centre tagging on training.
TALENT-MGMT local-masters positions for succession-planning, internal-mobility, and nine-box grouping when deployed standalone.
TALENT-MGMT local-masters org_units for manager-hierarchy roll-ups, calibration scoping, and goal-cascade trees when deployed standalone.
WFM local-masters cost_centers for labor-cost allocation when finance integration is absent (retail, restaurant, healthcare deployments often tag shifts by cost_center).
EMP-EXP local-masters the worker record for respondent identity, demographic-cohort breakdowns, and manager-hierarchy filtering when deployed standalone; reads from HCM when integrated.
EMP-EXP local-masters org_units for team-level / department-level engagement breakdowns when deployed standalone.
PA reads positions for span-of-control, vacancy-rate, and headcount analytics. Not derived — used as a dimensional source, not republished.
PA reads org_units as the analytical hierarchy for every people-KPI dashboard cut.
PA reads compensation_plans for pay-equity analytics that incorporate plan-design context. Many PA deployments skip this.
PA reads merit_recommendations to inform attrition modelling (under-promoted, under-merited workers).
PA reads course_enrollments to model learning-engagement features alongside the existing learning_records consumption.
PA reads survey_responses (anonymised) to fuse engagement signals into attrition and performance modelling. Distinct from engagement_drivers (aggregate) — this is row-level.
PA reads benefit_enrollments for total-rewards-analytics and benefits-utilisation reporting. Many PA deployments skip benefits analytics.
PA reads time_entries for productivity, overtime-burden, and burnout-risk feature engineering.

fields.title: Role
fields.description: The module's relationship to this data_object. master = the module canonically owns this data_object. embedded_master = the module ships a local-master shell (demoted to reference at deploy time if the canonical master is also installed). contributor = the module writes into a data_object mastered elsewhere. consumer = the module reads only. derived = the module materializes computed/derived data from this object.

fields.title: Necessity
fields.description: Meaningful on `consumer` / `embedded_master` rows that gracefully degrade. required = the module breaks without this data_object available. optional = the module functions fine without it (e.g. ATS-OFFERS embedded_masters salary_bands as optional — offers go out without guidance overlay). `master` rows are required by definition; this field is ignored there. See plan-modules.md §4.4.

entity.description: Junction between `domain_modules` and `tools`. Records that a deployable module requires (or optionally uses) an atomic tool. A tool is atomic and lives once in `tools`; this row only references `tool_id`, it never copies a tool. The domain's `system` skill derives its toolset by rolling these up over the domain's modules (primary + host domains); per-module Semantius coverage is computed from these rows. Replaces the retired per-module-skill `skill_tools` grain per plans/per-domain-skill-restoration.md.

computed_fields.name: key
computed_fields.description: 2-tuple natural key for the domain_module_id -> tool link: domain_module_id.tool_id. Materialized by the BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger from this computed_fields JsonLogic. Mirrors the handoff_processes.key idiom.

fields.title: Module
fields.description: The deployable module (full or starter) that requires this tool.

fields.title: Tool
fields.description: The atomic tool (canonical row in `tools`) this unit requires. Referenced, never copied.

fields.title: Requirement Level
fields.description: Whether the tool is irreducible for this unit's primary workflows (`required`) or covers a degraded / augmenting mode (`optional`). Carried verbatim from the migrated `skill_tools` rows; the coverage rollup counts only `required` tools in its denominator.

fields.title: Notes
fields.description: Empty by default. Populate only when there is something exceptional to call out about this pair. No vendor or product names (SKILL.md Rule #18).

fields.title: Record Status
fields.description: Standard workflow per SKILL.md Rule #1. Carried verbatim from the migrated `skill_tools` rows (all `new`).

fields.title: Key
fields.description: Computed 2-tuple natural key (domain_module_id.tool_id). Materialized by the BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger from entities.computed_fields. unique_value=true enforces idempotency on the pair at the database layer.

entity.description: Autonomous, independently-deployable unit between capabilities (market-analysis layer) and the live Semantius semantic models. Each module is self-contained: it owns its own data_objects, lifecycle states, edges, and tool surface, and composes with other modules at deploy time via the existing master / embedded_master demotion mechanism (no dependency tree). See plan-modules.md for the design intent.

validation_rules.message: Full modules require a domain_id (only starter modules may have NULL domain_id).

fields.title: Module Kind
fields.description: Discriminator distinguishing full modules (deployable units that master data_objects) from starter kits (first-class deployable units that embed but never master data_objects). Full modules require a domain_id; starters may have NULL domain_id and use domain_module_host_domains to declare touched domains.

fields.title: Module Code
fields.description: Natural key — stable identifier (`ATS-CANDIDATE-CRM`, `KNOWLEDGE-MGMT`). UPPER-KEBAB. Per-domain modules prefix with the parent domain code; cross-cutting modules use a bare descriptor.

fields.title: Primary Home Domain
fields.description: The standalone-product domain that is this module's primary home. Required: every module has a primary home domain. Additional installable hosts are listed in domain_module_host_domains.

fields.title: Description
fields.description: What this module does, what it masters, when it's used standalone vs alongside others.

fields.title: Industry
fields.description: Optional. Set when this module is tailored to a single industry (e.g. Real Estate, Crop Production). Leave null for cross-industry horizontal modules. Powers the per-industry section on the marketing site.

fields.title: Catalog Tagline
fields.description: One buyer-facing sentence for catalog list cards at the module grain. Workflow + value framing, not analyst voice. See Rule #20.

fields.title: Catalog Description
fields.description: 1-3 paragraph buyer-facing marketing description for the module catalog detail page. Buyer voice, not analyst voice. See Rule #20.

fields.title: Specification Requirements
fields.description: Authored build directives for the modeler/deployer: implementation requirements this deployable's promise depends on that are NOT derivable from the entity graph. Used mainly by starters/bundles that collapse a multi-entity pattern from the full module into a flat field on a surviving embedded shell. Prose intent, not a field-contract copy; the deployer honors it at spec time. Empty by default; never overwrite without explicit user approval.

records.description: The candidate-relationship backbone of an ATS, masters candidates (including the `prospect` lifecycle state), recruitment sources, agencies, and events. Structurally the same shape as standalone candidate-CRM products. Folds the AI-RECRUIT capability (resume parsing, ML matching, screening assistants) since those tools operate on `candidates` and are tightly bound to candidate workflows.
records.catalog_tagline: Build and nurture a pipeline of candidates long before a role opens.
records.catalog_description:
Capture every candidate, source, and recruiter touchpoint in one place. Run nurture campaigns, log interactions, and keep warm relationships ready so you can fill roles from people who already know you.

Consent and data-subject requests are tracked alongside each profile, so candidate privacy is handled as part of the workflow rather than bolted on.

records.description: Curated candidate groupings for nurture and pipeline-building (`talent_pools`). Embedded-masters `candidates`; deployed alone, materializes a thin candidate shell. Mirrors standalone talent-acquisition CRM products.
records.catalog_tagline: Group and segment candidates so the right shortlist is one search away.
records.catalog_description: Organize candidates into pools and segments, tag them by skill or stage, and save the searches you run most. When a requisition opens, your shortlist is already assembled instead of rebuilt from scratch.

records.description: Employee-driven candidate sourcing with referral-bonus tracking (`candidate_referrals`). Embedded-masters `candidates`. Cross-domain handoffs to PAYROLL (bonus payout) and EMP-EXP (engagement signal).
records.catalog_tagline: Turn your employees into your best sourcing channel.
