records.catalog_tagline: Show every named account a website built for them, the moment they land.
records.catalog_description: Make the website speak to each account by name. Resolve who is visiting, then serve personalized experiences, dynamic content, tailored CTAs, and account-specific landing pages, driven by personalization rules tied to firmographics and intent. Turn anonymous traffic from your target accounts into recognized, relevant visits that convert, instead of a one-size-fits-all homepage.

records.description: The technician-side field app: field-visit execution, offline sync, route-of-day, and proof-of-completion. Split out of dispatch operations to match the market shape (every flagship ships a distinct technician mobile app).
records.catalog_tagline: Give technicians an offline-ready field app: their day's route, the job, and proof it got done.
records.catalog_description: Put the work in the technician's hand. The mobile module runs the field visit from arrival to sign-off: the route of the day, the job details, parts used, and proof-of-completion, all working offline and syncing when signal returns. Technicians stop juggling paper and phone calls, and the office gets clean, timely completion data the moment the job closes. This is the truck half of field service, separate from the dispatcher's desk.

records.description: Coordinates release trains and program increments: PI planning, PI objectives, and cross-team dependency mapping and resolution, with flow and velocity analytics across the train.
records.catalog_tagline: Run PI planning and keep your release trains moving without cross-team surprises.
records.catalog_description: Plan and execute program increments with your teams. Stand up release trains, run PI planning, commit PI objectives, and map cross-team dependencies so they get resolved before they block delivery. Built-in flow and velocity analytics show how each train is progressing so release-train engineers can steer the program in real time.

records.description: Manages the portfolio-to-delivery backlog hierarchy (epics to features), agile roadmaps and release plans, lean-portfolio funding linkage, and OKR-to-delivery alignment.
records.catalog_tagline: Connect portfolio strategy to the agile backlog teams actually deliver.
records.catalog_description: Keep strategy and delivery in sync. Manage the backlog hierarchy from portfolio epics down to features, plan agile roadmaps and releases, link lean-portfolio funding to the work it pays for, and align OKRs to the delivery that achieves them. Gives delivery leaders a current, honest picture of what is planned and how it ladders up to portfolio outcomes.

records.description: Connects the delivery toolchain and models value streams: tool connections, value-stream definitions, flow-metric definitions, and the mirrored work items that flow through each stream.
records.catalog_tagline: Connect your delivery tools and map the value streams work flows through.
records.catalog_description: Lay the foundation for measuring delivery. Connect your planning, source, CI/CD, and service tools, define your value streams, and let the platform mirror the work items moving through them. Configure which flow metrics matter and how they are computed, so the rest of the platform can measure delivery against a model you control, across tools you did not build.

records.description: Computes flow metrics, surfaces bottlenecks, benchmarks DORA performance, and analyzes investment mix and delivery-to-outcome alignment over the mirrored value-stream data.
records.catalog_tagline: Measure flow, find bottlenecks, and tie delivery to business outcomes.
records.catalog_description: Turn mirrored delivery data into decisions. Measure flow velocity, time, load, efficiency, and distribution across your value streams, surface the bottlenecks slowing delivery, and benchmark performance with DORA metrics. Analyze whether effort is going to new value, defects, or debt, and tie delivery outcomes back to business investment so leaders can act on what the flow data shows.

records.description: Cross-domain starter kit for small and mid-sized IT teams. Embeds lightweight shells of the records a small IT shop manages: the helpdesk (optional), the hardware register, the SaaS application and renewal tracker, and the contract register. The renewal/contract spine (asset_contracts + saas_subscriptions) is required; hardware, SaaS apps, helpdesk, and on-prem licenses are optional. domain_id NULL; hosts ITSM, HAM, SMP, ITAM, SAM. Replaces the helpdesk-plus-spreadsheets reality; budget stays in the general ledger.
records.catalog_tagline: Run your whole IT shop from one place: tickets, devices, SaaS renewals, and contracts, without the spreadsheets.
records.catalog_description: One place to manage IT for a small team. Track the hardware you own and who has it, every SaaS app and when its subscription renews, and the contracts behind them, so nothing slips through a spreadsheet and no renewal catches you off guard. Add a lightweight helpdesk for tickets and requests if you do not already run one, or keep the one you have. Start with the renewal and contract essentials and turn on the device, SaaS, and helpdesk pieces as you need them. Built for IT teams that have outgrown spreadsheets but do not need a full enterprise IT suite.
records.specification_requirements:
Cost fields on the embedded shells. For the standalone renewal-and-cost view to resolve, two embedded masters each need a flat cost figure plus a currency code:

- `asset_contracts`: a flat `renewal_cost` (or `annual_value`) numeric field.
- `saas_subscriptions`: a flat `annual_spend` (or MRR/ARR) numeric field.

Coexistence: these flat fields are a standalone-only denormalization. They are not needed when the full asset-management and SaaS-management modules are already installed (those carry cost on their own spend entities); when such a full module is added later, the flat field must be deduplicated and reconciled against the canonical source so cost is not double-counted.

records.description: Single-domain starter kit for a small IT team that wants a lightweight service desk without the full ITSM suite or any asset estate. Embeds lightweight shells of ITSM's own records: incidents and service requests (the required helpdesk core), plus an optional request catalog, knowledge base, and SLA clocks. Problem, change, release, and event handling stay in the full itsm-* modules you turn on when you outgrow the desk; assets are out of scope (IT-OPS-STARTER and HAM). The embedded shells demote to the canonical itsm-* masters when those modules install alongside. The narrow, single-domain complement to IT-OPS-STARTER.
records.catalog_tagline: Stand up a lightweight IT help desk in a day: log tickets, take requests, and answer the same questions once.
records.catalog_description: A simple service desk for a small IT team. Log incidents when something breaks, take service requests from a catalog or by free text, and move each ticket from new to resolved to closed without a heavyweight tool. Turn on a knowledge base so common answers get written once and reused, a request catalog so people ask for the right things, and SLA clocks so nothing sits too long, each when you are ready. Start with just tickets and grow into the rest as your team and your process mature. Built for IT teams that want ticketing and self-service without standing up a full enterprise service-management suite.

records.description: Supplier master data, onboarding, registration, and qualification. The intake and master-record spine of supplier management.
records.catalog_tagline: Onboard, qualify, and maintain every supplier on one trusted master record.
records.catalog_description: Run supplier onboarding from invitation through registration, document collection, and approval. Qualify new suppliers against your standards before they go active, and keep the supplier master, contacts, and documents current as the relationship evolves. One clean record per supplier that procurement, finance, and compliance all work from.

records.description: Supplier performance scorecards, KPIs, reviews, and corrective actions. Measures and improves supplier delivery, quality, and service.
records.catalog_tagline: Score supplier performance and drive improvement where it slips.
records.catalog_description: Measure suppliers against delivery, quality, responsiveness, and savings targets, and roll the results into weighted scorecards your category managers and finance teams share. Spot underperformers early, open corrective actions, and track them to closure so supplier performance improves cycle over cycle.

records.description: Supplier risk assessment, certifications, sanctions and compliance screening, and ESG. Operational, qualification-gated supplier risk, distinct from deep third-party due diligence (TPRM).
records.catalog_tagline: Assess supplier risk and prove compliance before and after you sign.
records.catalog_description: Score each supplier for financial, operational, cyber, and ESG risk, and keep certifications and insurance current with automatic expiry alerts. Screen suppliers for sanctions and compliance gaps, escalate elevated risk to governance and procurement, and keep a defensible record of every check behind each supplier decision.

records.description: The screening order itself, the candidate subject, the orderable package catalog, the concrete component searches (criminal, employment, education, MVR, drug, watchlist, healthcare exclusion), order status history, and candidate-facing invitation and portal engagement. The point-in-time transaction every screening product sells first.
records.catalog_tagline: Order a background check, build the package, and run every search from one screen.
records.catalog_description: Order an employment background check, choose a package, and let it expand into the concrete searches it needs: criminal records, employment and education verification, driving records, drug and health screening, and global watchlist checks. Invite the candidate to a portal to give consent and fill in what only they can supply, then track every component to completion with a clear status on the order. One order, one subject, every search in one place.

records.description: The screening decision and the FCRA/EEOC paperwork chain: adjudication against the eligibility matrix, FCRA disclosures, candidate authorizations, pre-adverse and adverse action notices, summary-of-rights acknowledgements, disputes, individualized assessments, and ban-the-box assessments. Regulation-driven entities that must exist even where a vendor hides them in the order UI.
records.catalog_tagline: Decide each result against your matrix and walk the FCRA adverse-action chain by the book.
records.catalog_description: Adjudicate every screening result against a configurable eligibility matrix so the same rule applies to every candidate. When a result is disqualifying, walk the full compliance chain: deliver the disclosure and summary of rights, capture the candidate authorization, send the pre-adverse notice with the report copy, honor the waiting period, and issue the adverse-action notice, with disputes and EEOC individualized assessments handled in line. Keep a defensible, auditable record behind every screening decision.

records.description: The post-hire and standalone-identity surface: continuous monitoring subscriptions, the criminal-records monitoring alert stream, periodic rescreenings, identity verification, right-to-work / I-9 / E-Verify, international screening, and GDPR consent for non-US data subjects. Every flagship sells this as a separately-priced product distinct from the pre-hire order.
records.catalog_tagline: Keep cleared workers cleared with continuous monitoring, rescreening, and identity checks.
records.catalog_description: Stop treating the background check as a one-time event. Subscribe workers to continuous monitoring and get an alert the moment a new criminal record surfaces, schedule periodic rescreenings for sensitive roles, and verify identity and right to work up front and over time. Handle international screening and the consent and lawful-basis records non-US data subjects require, so a clearance keeps its meaning long after the hire.

records.description: Register the broad third party, scope the per-service engagement, capture the vendor-side contacts, and classify criticality before any diligence begins. The intake spine: business-sponsor requests in, the third-party master and its tier out, plus offboarding and exit due diligence.
records.catalog_tagline: Register every third party, scope the engagement, and tier it before diligence starts.
records.catalog_description: Bring every external party you depend on into one inventory, not just the suppliers you invoice. Take in a business sponsor's request, register the third party and the specific service engagement, capture who to contact on the vendor side, and classify how critical the relationship is so the right depth of diligence kicks in. Flag the engagements that are critical or important to the business, and run a clean exit when a relationship ends. One trusted record per third party that procurement, security, and risk all work from.

records.description: The deep, engagement and contract-gated diligence that distinguishes third-party risk from operational supplier qualification: questionnaires, document collection, certification and attestation checks, regulatory agreements, and the pre-contract go or no-go.
records.catalog_tagline: Run the questionnaires, collect the evidence, and decide go or no-go before you sign.
records.catalog_description: Send each third party the diligence its tier demands and grade what comes back. Build assessments from a library of security questionnaires, collect every answer and its supporting evidence, and gather the certifications, audit reports, and attestations that prove the controls are real. Track the regulatory agreements a relationship requires, run periodic re-assessment campaigns, and reach a clear, defensible go or no-go before the contract is signed. The deep diligence that decides whether it is safe to do business.

records.description: Post-contract watching: recompute the internal risk rating per third party and engagement, ingest external security ratings, and triage breach, sanctions, and financial signals to drive the re-assessment cadence.
records.catalog_tagline: Keep watching after you sign, with ratings, signals, and a live risk score.
records.catalog_description: Stop treating diligence as a one-time gate. Recompute each third party's risk rating on a cadence set by its tier, pull in external security ratings as they change, and triage breach, sanctions, and financial-distress signals as they surface. When a third party drifts into higher risk, the score moves and the right reviewers see it in time to act, so a clearance keeps its meaning long after the contract goes live.

records.description: Turn findings raised from assessment and monitoring into tracked, time-boxed remediation that closes before renewal, and record risk acceptances with an expiry when a finding will not be fixed. Consumes audit findings handed off from the audit domain.
records.catalog_tagline: Turn findings into tracked remediation that closes before the next renewal.
records.catalog_description: Raise an issue the moment an assessment or a monitoring signal surfaces a problem, and drive it to closure. Open vendor-scoped remediation plans time-boxed to the next review cycle or contract renewal, assign owners, and track them to done. When a finding will not be fixed, record a risk acceptance with a clear owner and an expiry date so nothing stays accepted forever. A defensible trail of every issue raised against a third party and how it was resolved.

records.description: Visibility beyond the direct third party: subcontractor and fourth-party edges, concentration risk across shared providers, and the regulatory registers and subcontracting-chain disclosures that resilience frameworks require.
records.catalog_tagline: See past the direct vendor into the subcontractors and concentration risk behind it.
records.catalog_description: Your risk does not stop at the companies you contract with directly. Map the subcontractors and fourth parties your providers depend on, spot where many of your critical services trace back to the same handful of providers, and maintain the registers and subcontracting-chain disclosures that operational-resilience rules require. Add supply-chain attestations where standards demand them, so you can answer for the whole chain, not just the first link.

records.description: The pre-delivery surface: author the statement of work, take in services proposals, stand up the engagement against the supplier and the contract, and amend scope through change orders. Masters the SOW, the engagement, the proposal, and the change order; consumes the supplier, the contract, and rate cards from their owning domains.
records.catalog_tagline: Author the SOW, take in proposals, and stand up the engagement before the work begins.
records.catalog_description: Turn an awarded services deal into a working engagement. Author the statement of work that scopes what the firm will deliver, take in the proposals or bids attached to it, and stand up the engagement against the supplier and the signed contract. When the work shifts, raise a change order and keep the SOW current instead of letting scope drift. The services firm stays your supplier and the SOW stays your contract; this module is where you shape the engagement they hang off of.

records.description: The delivery and settlement surface: break the engagement into milestones and deliverables, track each to acceptance, and settle on what was delivered through milestone-based invoices. Masters the milestone, the deliverable, the milestone invoice, and the acceptance record.
records.catalog_tagline: Track milestones and deliverables to acceptance, then pay on what was actually delivered.
records.catalog_description: Run the delivery half of a services engagement. Break the statement of work into milestones and the deliverables that close them, then track each one to formal acceptance so payment follows delivered outcomes, not elapsed time. Raise milestone-based invoices against accepted work and keep a clear, auditable record of who accepted what and when. Outcome-based settlement that ties every payment back to a milestone the buyer signed off.

records.description: The core booking engine: products, departures, rate options, bookings, participants, add-ons, promo codes, gift cards, payments, refunds, customers, manifests, notifications, reviews, and reports. Deployable standalone for simple operators; embeds guide/resource assignments and waiver status when those modules are present.
records.catalog_tagline: Take and manage bookings online and at the counter, with real-time availability, payments, gift cards, and guest messaging.
records.catalog_description: The heart of your booking operation. Publish products and departures, show live availability, and capture bookings from your website, the phone, or a walk-up counter. Collect payments, sell gift cards, apply promo codes, and process refunds and cancellations. Keep a roster for every departure, message guests automatically, and see how the business is performing. Works on its own for simple operators and pairs with scheduling and waivers when you need them.

records.description: Schedules the people and equipment behind each departure: bookable resources, guide assignments, equipment rentals, lodging units, and trip itineraries. The adventure and multi-day differentiator; separable so general day-tour operators can run the core without it.
records.catalog_tagline: Assign guides, equipment, vehicles, and lodging to every trip, and prevent double-booking your resources.
records.catalog_description: Schedule the people and gear behind each departure. Track guide availability and certifications, auto-assign or hand-pick guides for each trip, and confirm them by text. Manage rentable equipment, vehicles, and rooms as bookable resources so you never double-book a raft, a van, or a bunk. Built for multi-day and guided-adventure operators who sell an experience, not just a seat.

records.description: Distributes products and availability to online travel agencies and reseller marketplaces, manages reseller partners and commission agreements, and syncs channel bookings back to the operator calendar. records.catalog_description: Reach more customers by selling through online travel agencies and reseller partners. Push your products and live availability out to the channels you choose, manage reseller agreements and commission rates, and pull channel bookings back into one calendar so availability stays accurate everywhere. Run it only when you want to grow beyond direct bookings.

entity.description: Junction table binding regulations to the domains they apply to, with an applicability qualifier. Captures the reuse pattern: one HIPAA regulation row binds to many healthcare-touching domains (EHR, Claims Management, Patient Portal); one Payroll domain binds to many country-localization regulations (Payroll-DE, Payroll-FR, Payroll-US). Applicability separates strict requirements (HIPAA on EHR is mandatory) from softer guidance (HIPAA on a CRM is conditional on whether PHI flows through it).

records.description: Front-line sales leader who inspects pipeline by deal risk, runs forecast roll-ups, and coaches reps on recorded calls.
RevOps analyst who tunes deal-scoring and forecasting models, monitors forecast accuracy, and curates activity-attribution rules.
Quota-carrying rep whose activities are auto-captured, who submits a periodic forecast, and who acts on deal warnings and coaching.
Enablement coach who reviews recorded calls against the playbook and runs structured coaching sessions.
Owns the requisition-to-offer pipeline for assigned reqs: sources, screens, schedules, drafts and sends offers, drives candidates to hire.
Builds and works talent pools and the candidate CRM; generates qualified pipeline ahead of open reqs.
Owns interview logistics and offer / pre-employee paperwork; schedules panels and keeps the process moving.
Accountable for the recruiting function's output: approves reqs and offers, owns pipeline health and vendor relationships.
The role owning the open position. Cross-functional (sits in the hiring department, not Recruiting): defines the req, interviews, decides the hire, approves the offer.
Owns hiring-compliance surfaces: background-check adjudication, FCRA / adverse-action, EEO / OFCCP, and candidate data-subject requests.
PMO / BizOps lead who owns cross-team programs, triages intake, and rolls up OKR progress from work items.
Individual contributor who executes assigned work items, posts updates, and submits cross-team requests through intake.
Marketing operator who runs campaign projects with creative review and routes creative requests through intake queues.
Cross-functional objective owner who commits and scores OKRs and links key results to executing work items.

IT Operations persona that runs day-to-day SaaS administration: discovering and triaging applications, managing integrations and owners, optimizing license usage and reclamation, and operating automation workflows and self-service requests.

Procurement persona that owns the commercial SaaS lifecycle: renewal pipeline, vendor negotiations, spend allocation, and vendor risk attestation, with read access to discovery and usage data that informs renewal decisions.

IT Asset Management persona that governs the SaaS portfolio end to end across discovery, optimization, renewal, and automation; the cross-module owner accountable for portfolio cost, compliance, and lifecycle.
Owns the end-to-end contingent-workforce program: requisition intake, supplier distribution, rate-card governance, and the time-to-invoice flow. Spans worker sourcing and time-and-invoicing.
Governs the staffing-supplier panel and the rate cards: onboards and activates suppliers, approves rate cards by role and region, and monitors supplier performance against billed invoices.
Coordinates day-to-day contingent-labor operations: shepherds worker assignments and tenure tracking in sourcing, and chases timesheet approvals and invoice matching in time-and-invoicing.

Owns day-to-day operation of the learning platform: maintains the course catalog, manages enrollments and learning paths, configures automation and audiences, and administers credentials and continuing education.
Authors and versions courses, lessons, content assets, and assessments; publishes new training and retires outdated material across self-paced and instructor-led delivery.
Delivers instructor-led and virtual instructor-led sessions: runs scheduled offerings, records attendance, grades assessments, and supports learners through completion and certification.

Runs regulatory and policy training programs end to end: schedules compliance campaigns, tracks assignment completion, assembles training evidence, manages recertification, and produces regulator filings.
Cross-functional people leader who assigns and nudges direct reports through required and developmental learning, monitors completion and certification status, and follows up on overdue training.

Owns client engagements end to end: scopes the project, structures tasks and milestones, requests staffing, and drives delivery to completion. Accountable for on-time, on-scope delivery and for the project's billing readiness.

Owns the staffing and capacity workflow: matches skilled people to project demand, plans and commits resource allocations, confirms and releases assignments, and watches utilization and skill gaps across the billable workforce.

The billable practitioner who executes assigned project tasks and logs time and expenses against the engagements they work. Drives tasks to completion and submits clean actuals for approval and billing.

Owns project billing and revenue: manages budgets and rate cards, invoices reached milestones and approved time, and recognizes project revenue. Accountable for accurate, auditable project financials feeding the general ledger.

Accountable for the contract lifecycle end to end: owns the repository, signs off on approvals and executions, drives obligation tracking and renewals, and keeps authoring and negotiation moving across the team.
Runs the day-to-day contract workflow: assembles drafts from approved templates, shepherds signature envelopes, tracks obligations to closure, and processes renewals ahead of expiry.
Reviews and approves contract language, clause and template content, and redlines counterparty terms during negotiation. The legal gate on what the organization is willing to sign.
Bridges sourcing and contracting: turns awarded sourcing outcomes into draft agreements, consults on supplier terms during negotiation, and reads the repository for active supplier commitments.

Runs product operations: keeps roadmap and backlog hygiene, instruments and reports adoption and quality metrics, and coordinates release and beta logistics across teams.
Leads delivery of prioritized product work: takes accepted features through in-delivery and release, reports shipped and rolled-back states, and feeds feasibility input back into discovery.
Owns the marketing automation platform: configures campaigns, journeys, lead scoring, and forms, and keeps the program running across modules.
Plans and runs marketing campaigns and nurture journeys end to end, from authoring through launch and follow-up.
Frontline HR service agent: picks up employee cases from the portal queue, triages and classifies them, works them to resolution, and attaches knowledge. Reopens closed cases when something changes.

Accountable for HR service delivery output: owns the case queue, SLAs, routing rules, and the approval gate. Oversees workload, aging, and escalations across the case workflow and the employee portal.
Owns the HR knowledge base: curates and publishes articles, organizes them by case category, and promotes resolved cases into reusable knowledge to deflect future requests.
Owns the intranet governance program across all connected sources: sets policy, oversees recertification, and is accountable for content currency and accountability coverage.
Accountable owner for specific pieces of intranet content; responds to recertification attestations and remediates or archives stale content.
Connects and maintains intranet sources, runs crawls and scans, and keeps the inventory and connectors healthy.
Day-to-day governance operator: authors and publishes glossary terms, proposes and approves data classifications, manages stewardship assignments, and certifies assets within a data domain.
Accountable owner of a set of data assets and data products: grants and revokes certifications, signs off access policies, and is accountable for the asset's fitness for production use.
Operates the catalog platform itself: configures and runs metadata crawlers, manages lineage capture, maintains data domains, and curates the data-product marketplace surface.
Cross-functional governance authority spanning Data Engineering and GRC: sets classification and access policy, signs off enterprise data policies, and owns regulatory mapping of the data estate.
Analyst or data-product consumer who discovers assets in the catalog, reads glossary and lineage to build trust, and requests access to governed data products through policy.
Builds and publishes the product catalog, runs the storefront, and launches coupons and promotions. Reads order activity to see what is selling and adjust merchandising.
Runs the order-to-cash flow end to end: captures carts, completes checkouts and payments, creates orders, and drives them through fulfillment and shipping. Cross-functional operations persona.
Picks, packs, and ships paid orders and manages shipments and returns. Reads order detail to fulfill against the right line items.
Owns the enterprise process architecture: maintains capability maps, governs the process model repository, and aligns value streams to strategy.
Models and analyzes business processes and value streams, runs simulations, and prepares models for review and publication.
Accountable for one or more published business processes: approves publication, sponsors reengineering, and owns process outcomes. Cross-functional persona.

Owns the corporate travel program: sets and maintains travel policy, configures the approval workflow, monitors program spend and supplier performance, and is accountable for duty-of-care readiness across the organization.
Books and manages travel on behalf of one or more travelers: shops policy-aware fares, holds and tickets reservations, builds and amends itineraries, and reapplies unused-ticket credits.

Cross-functional self-service traveler: self-books within policy, maintains their own traveler profile, submits pre-trip approval requests, views and changes their own itinerary, and acknowledges duty-of-care alerts affecting them.
Owns the end-to-end marketing planning and budget process: builds and approves plans, sets budgets, oversees allocation and spend-to-plan reconciliation, and reports plan-level performance.
Authors marketing plans and plan lines, maintains the marketing calendar, and works with budget owners to align plan lines to allocated budget.

Cross-functional owner of marketing budget governance: approves budgets and allocations, monitors spend against plan, and reconciles committed and actual spend. Often sits in or partners with Finance.

Owns the site safety program: incident investigation, hazard and risk assessment, corrective actions, inspections, and required training. Accountable for closing incidents and verifying corrective actions.
Plans and runs exposure monitoring and industrial-hygiene sampling, manages occupational-health surveillance, and governs the chemical inventory and safety data sheets.
Owns environmental permits, conditions, and limits, emissions and release records, and ISO 14001 conformance; accountable for permit renewals and environmental reporting.
Cross-functional site leader accountable for the whole EHS program at an establishment, spanning safety, occupational health, environmental compliance, and audit readiness.
Prepares lease accounting: classifies leases, maintains right-of-use and liability schedules, records modifications and remeasurements, and generates the journal entries for the general ledger.
Maintains the lease record system: agreements and documents, critical dates and alerts, renewals and terminations, and the payment terms that feed lease accounting.
Owns lease-accounting policy and the close: approves classifications and modifications, reviews and files disclosures, and signs off on the lease subledger for financial reporting.
Runs the whole grazing operation: oversees herd performance, grazing plans, sales, and compliance across all properties and mobs.
Manages the animals and mobs day to day: records, weights, breeding, treatments, and movements in the yard and paddock.
Plans and executes pasture rotations: allocates paddocks, sets rest periods, and matches stocking rate to carrying capacity, moving mobs accordingly.
Owns the paid social estate: campaign strategy, budget allocation across platforms, and overall performance against targets. Accountable for spend and results.
Operates day-to-day optimization: bid and budget tuning, audience iteration, pacing, and responding to threshold breaches across ad sets.
Owns ad creative: concepts and variants, dynamic creative optimization rules, and the creative approval workflow that feeds live campaigns.
Triages insider-risk alerts, tunes detection indicators, and drives day-to-day monitoring of user risk across the workforce.
Investigates escalated insider-risk cases end to end: builds the activity timeline, performs file-lineage forensics, collects evidence, and packages it for HR and Legal.
Owns the insider risk program: approves case dispositions, governs HR/Legal escalation, and oversees exit-risk monitoring policy.

Designs and deploys executable process definitions and decision tables, owns versioning and breaking-change governance, and decides the orchestration topology across the engine and the case and decision layer.
Runs the live engine: monitors running instances, triages and resolves incidents, suspends or terminates stuck instances, and keeps throughput healthy across the execution and case modules.
Works the human side of orchestrated processes: claims and completes human tasks, advances case files with ad-hoc activities and milestones, and escalates when work stalls.
Configures channels, audiences, checklist templates, and learning modules, and authors and schedules company-wide frontline broadcasts and recognition programs.

Store, plant, or field manager who cascades broadcasts to their team, assigns and verifies tasks, approves shift swaps, and recognizes workers. Cross-functional: reports into store or plant operations, not internal comms.

Deskless worker who reads and acknowledges broadcasts, completes and submits tasks and checklists, requests and claims shift swaps, finishes microlearning, and sends and receives recognition from a mobile or shared device.

Owns the employee advocacy program end to end: enrolls advocates, sets topics and goals, runs campaigns, oversees gamification and rewards, and reports reach and pipeline impact to marketing leadership.
Sources, writes, and approves shareable content and suggested share copy, organizes it into topic streams, and keeps the advocate feed and newsletters fresh and on-brand.
An enrolled employee who reshares curated content to their personal social networks, earns points and recognition, and represents the employer brand to their own audience.
Runs the short-term rental operation end to end: listings, bookings, guest experience, turnovers, and owner reporting.
Owns listing distribution and nightly pricing: channel connections, rate plans, and dynamic-pricing rules.
Handles guest communication and bookings and coordinates turnovers so each guest has a smooth stay.
Schedules and verifies housekeeping and turnover work against the booking calendar.
Produces owner statements and payouts and handles lodging-tax filing and permit compliance.
Runs the marina end to end: oversees slip inventory and assignment, reservations, the boatyard, billing, and the fuel dock.
Assigns slips, handles transient arrivals and departures, and keeps the dock and assignment board current.
Handles reservations, boater and vessel records, document collection, and front-desk billing inquiries.
Runs the boatyard: estimates and work orders, haul-out and launch scheduling, and pump-out logging.
Owns contracts, recurring and metered billing, invoicing, and fuel and store reconciliation.
Owns the operator's booking operation: configures products, departures, and rates, oversees bookings, refunds, guide scheduling, and waiver compliance, and manages distribution.
Front-line staff who take and amend bookings over the phone, at the counter, and online, collect payments, and ensure each guest has signed a waiver.
Field staff assigned to departures: confirm availability, review the manifest and participant requirements, check out equipment, and run the trip.
Manages reseller and online-travel-agency relationships, maps products to channels, sets commission terms, and keeps channel availability in sync with the operator calendar.

entity.description: System-type domains (CRM, ITSM, HRIS, MDM, ATS, ERP, CMS, ...). Self-referential to support a sub-domain hierarchy (ITSM contains Incident Management, Problem Management, Change Management).

fields.title: USA Market Size (USD M)
fields.description: Estimated annual USA enterprise software TAM for this domain in USD millions. Ballpark from public market research (Gartner/IDC/Forrester class), ±30% precision.

fields.title: Source Year
fields.description: Calendar year the market-size estimate refers to.

fields.title: Code
fields.description: Short acronym or abbreviation (CRM, ITSM, CMDB) for compact display

fields.title: Icon Name
fields.description: Lucide icon name that visually identifies the domain (e.g. shield, database, users).

fields.title: Catalog Tagline
fields.description: One buyer-facing sentence for catalog list cards. Workflow + value framing, not analyst voice. See Rule #20.

fields.title: Catalog Description
fields.description: 1-3 paragraph buyer-facing marketing description for catalog detail page. Buyer voice, not analyst voice. See Rule #20.

fields.title: Industry
fields.description: Optional. Set when this domain is specific to a single industry (e.g. Banking Operations, Insurance Claims). Leave null for cross-industry horizontal domains.

fields.title: Certification Required
fields.description: TRUE when solutions in this domain typically require formal certification or regulator approval to enter or operate in the market — e.g. FedRAMP for US federal, FDA clearance for medical devices, banking-regulator approval for core banking. Use to filter constraint-bound domains.

fields.title: Catalog Release
fields.description: Release date for this domain in the web site catalog. Empty if not scheduled.

fields.title: Min Org Size
fields.description: Smallest organisation-size tier at which this domain becomes a real budget concern (i.e. dedicated tooling is purchased, even at starter level). Values: 10 xs <50 / 20 s <500 / 30 m <2500 / 40 l <10000 / 50 xl 10000+.

fields.title: Cost Band
fields.description: Typical annual subscription tier for an enterprise deployment. $ <$50K, $$ $50K-$250K, $$$ $250K-$1M, $$$$ $1M-$5M, $$$$$ $5M+.

fields.title: Notes
fields.description: Free-text reviewer notes, change log, postponed-decision parking. Append dated entries rather than overwriting.

fields.title: Domain Kind
fields.description: Nature of the domain row. established_market = owns its own masters and has at least one primary-coverage vendor. emerging_market = owns its own masters but only partial vendor coverage. bundle = owns no masters; it embeds / consumes from other domains' markets (a deployable starter promoted to a domain row). Filters and audit floors branch on this: bundle rows are exempt from the market-shape floors (capabilities, masters, function-owner, solutions) and from the market-research metadata floor.

records.description: Workflows for managing IT requests, incidents, problems, changes, and knowledge in support of internal business users.
records.catalog_tagline: Run a responsive IT service desk that resolves incidents, fulfills requests, and ships changes without breaking the business.
records.catalog_description:
IT Service Management gives your service desk one place to capture, route, and resolve everything your workforce throws at it: outages, password resets, new-laptop requests, recurring problems, and risky changes. Tickets follow a clear lifecycle from intake to closure, with priority routing, approvals, and SLA timers built in, so nothing slips and the right person always owns the next step.

The suite spans incident, request, problem, change, knowledge, and service-level management, plus an agent workspace that pulls the full picture together. Self-service portals and a curated knowledge base deflect routine work, while problem and change workflows keep the underlying environment stable. The result is faster resolution, fewer repeat issues, and a measurable service experience your users and auditors can both trust.
records.business_logic: Ticket classification, deduplication, and priority routing benefit from ML, but the underlying workflow remains state-machine driven.

records.description: Monitoring, event management, and operational control of IT infrastructure and services.
records.catalog_tagline: Watch every server, network, and service in one place, catch problems before users feel them, and keep capacity ahead of demand.
records.catalog_description:
Bring monitoring, event management, and capacity planning together so your operations team works from one live picture of the infrastructure. Collect signals from across the estate, turn raw events into meaningful alerts with the policies you control, and cut through the noise so the team chases what actually matters instead of every blip. When something breaks, the alert is already correlated to the affected service and routed to the people who can fix it.

The same operational data keeps you ahead of growth. Track utilization over time, see where headroom is running out, and forecast when you will need more before a resource is exhausted. Automate the routine recovery steps and scheduled work that used to page someone at 3 a.m., so the team spends its time on the problems that need judgment, not on the ones a runbook can handle. The payoff is fewer outages, faster recovery, and infrastructure spend that tracks real need.
records.business_logic: Event management, capacity calculations, and topology-aware impact analysis, engine-led; service-mapping master data is the smaller part.

records.description: Umbrella domain covering hardware, software, cloud-cost, and enterprise-asset management.
records.catalog_tagline: Know every asset you own, what it costs, and where it is in its life, across hardware, software, SaaS, and cloud.
records.catalog_description: Manage your entire technology estate from one place. Track every asset from purchase through deployment, transfer, and retirement, and keep a single record of the contracts, leases, warranties, and support agreements that govern them. Reconcile the inconsistent ways each feed names the same hardware and software so your inventory is clean and trustworthy. Roll the whole portfolio up into total-cost-of-ownership and position reporting that finance, procurement, and IT can all act on, so you renew on time, cut waste, and prove what you have when audit or compliance asks.
records.business_logic: Normalization tables (the same hardware/software model expressed inconsistently across feeds) are the small irreducible kernel — they require maintained reference data, not a runtime engine.

records.description: Authoritative record of configuration items and their relationships, underpinning ITSM and ITOM.
records.catalog_tagline: Keep one trusted record of every server, application, database, and the connections between them, so changes and incidents can be reasoned about in minutes.
records.catalog_description:
Build a single, authoritative picture of your IT estate. Bring infrastructure, applications, and the dependencies that tie them together into one place, organize it with a class model you control, and keep it current as the environment changes. When something breaks or a change is proposed, you can see exactly what it touches and what depends on it before you act.

The same trusted graph powers the work around it: map components up into the business services they support, capture point-in-time baselines to catch unauthorized drift, and give every record an owner who keeps it accurate. The result is faster, safer change, quicker incident diagnosis, and an estate you can stand behind at audit time.

records.description: Automated identification of IT infrastructure and the mapping of components into business services.
records.catalog_tagline: See every device, cloud resource, and service before you can manage it.
records.catalog_description: Discovery scans your networks, cloud accounts, and directories to find the IT you actually run, then fingerprints each asset and maps how components connect into the business services they support. It turns blind spots into a normalized, reconciled inventory that feeds your CMDB, asset management, and operations tools, so teams stop guessing what exists and start acting on a trusted source of truth.
records.business_logic: Scanning, fingerprinting, and credentialed inspection across networks, cloud APIs, and agents (code-dominant collection plane).

records.description: Machine-learning-driven event correlation, anomaly detection, and noise reduction for IT operations.
records.catalog_tagline: Cut through alert noise and turn a flood of IT signals into a short list of correlated, root-caused issues your teams can act on before users feel the impact.
records.catalog_description:
An AIOps platform sits across the high-volume telemetry your IT estate produces every second, metrics, logs, traces, events, and alerts, and uses machine learning and statistical analysis to find the few patterns that matter. Instead of paging on every threshold breach, it groups related signals into a single correlated incident, filters out duplicate and flapping alerts, and surfaces the probable root cause so responders start from an answer rather than a blank screen.

Operations and engineering teams use it to detect anomalies against learned baselines, suppress noise during planned changes, and receive early warning of predicted outages and capacity problems while there is still time to act. Correlated incidents and high-confidence predictions flow straight into incident and problem workflows, and suppression decisions flow back to the monitoring layer, so the whole operational loop stays in sync.

Behind the scenes, detection and prediction models are continuously retrained and watched for drift, keeping the signal accurate as the environment changes. The result is fewer pages, faster mean time to resolution, and a clearer picture of service health, so on-call teams spend their time fixing problems instead of triaging alerts.
records.business_logic: Event correlation, deduplication, anomaly detection, and root-cause analysis: ML and statistical algorithms across high-volume telemetry.

records.description: Unified metrics, logs, and traces for distributed systems, primarily targeting engineering teams.
records.catalog_tagline: See what every service in production is doing, and know the moment it stops behaving.
records.catalog_description:
Bring metrics, logs, and traces together so you can answer what is happening across your distributed systems without jumping between tools. Watch live dashboards, drill from a slow request into the exact trace, and search raw logs to find the root cause.

Set service level objectives, track error budgets as they burn, and group recurring errors so the right engineer is paged before customers notice. When something breaks, the signals that fired the alert are already in front of you, with a clean handoff to your incident and ticketing workflows.
records.business_logic: Telemetry collection pipeline, trace analysis, log indexing at scale, metrics TSDB, and exemplar correlation — high-cardinality data infrastructure.

records.description: Authoring, execution, and tracking of manual and automated software tests.
records.catalog_tagline: Plan, run, and track every test so releases ship with confidence.
records.catalog_description: Give your QA and engineering teams one home for the whole testing effort. Author reusable test cases with clear steps and expected results, organize them into suites, and scope each release with a test plan that sets entry and exit criteria. Run manual and automated tests against the environments you target, capture pass, fail, blocked, and skipped outcomes with full logs, and turn failures into tracked defects that flow straight to the developers who own them. Tie every test back to the requirements it verifies so you always know your coverage, see release readiness at a glance, and stop shipping the surprises that erode customer trust.
records.business_logic: Test runner orchestration (queuing, parallelisation, retry) is engine-like, but the test-management application itself is pure CRUD over cases, runs, and defects.

records.description: Top-down planning of investments, demand, resources, and agile delivery across portfolios.
records.catalog_tagline: Plan where the organization invests next, balance demand against capacity, and track the value every initiative actually delivers.
records.catalog_description:
Strategic Portfolio Management is where leadership decides which initiatives to fund, how to sequence them, and who works on them. Demand requests arrive, get scored on business value and risk, and the strongest candidates become funded initiatives grouped into portfolios that roll up to corporate strategy.

Resource and capacity planning is the engine: every initiative competes for the same people, budget, and time, so allocations are committed against capacity, what-if scenarios are modeled before a commitment is made, and roadmap items are scheduled with their dependencies and contingencies in view.

After the plan is set, the work is to keep it honest. Benefits are tracked against the case that justified each investment, portfolios are rebalanced when priorities shift, and dependency chains surface the blockers that put delivery at risk. The result is a single, defensible view of what the business is doing, why, and whether it is paying off.
records.business_logic: Resource allocation, capacity what-if, and roadmap scenario modeling are the non-trivial engines; the rest is demand, project, and outcome records.

records.description: Inventory and rationalization of the enterprise application landscape, including business capabilities, technology fit, and lifecycle.
records.catalog_tagline: See every application you run, score what it is worth, and decide what to keep, fix, or retire.
records.catalog_description:
Build one trustworthy inventory of the applications, interfaces, and technology platforms your organization depends on, with the business capabilities each one supports. Track every application through its full life from planned to retired, and keep owners, costs, and technical details in one place.

Once the landscape is mapped, score each application on cost, business value, and technical fit so you can rank the portfolio and act with confidence. Spot redundant or aging applications, plan migrations and retirements, and give leadership a clear, defensible view of where to invest and where to cut.
records.business_logic: TIME (tolerate/invest/migrate/eliminate) scoring rules over portfolio attributes — a small declarative layer.

records.description: Detection, response, and remediation of security incidents, vulnerabilities, and threats.
records.catalog_tagline: See the threat, run the response, and close the loop before it becomes a breach.
records.catalog_description: Bring every security signal into one place so your team can triage alerts, investigate incidents, and coordinate the response from detection through containment and recovery. Correlate activity across your tools, keep a defensible record of what happened and what you did about it, and hit the regulator notification clock when an incident crosses the reporting line. Turn a flood of noise into prioritized cases your analysts can actually work, and shorten the time from first signal to fully contained.
records.business_logic: Detection rules, correlation, ML-based anomaly detection, and high-volume log analytics — the SIEM/EDR core.

records.description: Playbook-driven automation of security operations workflows across alerts and case management.
records.catalog_tagline: Turn your security team's repetitive response steps into automated playbooks so every alert gets handled fast, consistently, and with a full audit trail.
records.catalog_description:
Give your security operations center a way to respond to alerts at machine speed instead of by hand. Build playbooks that capture how your analysts actually work, enrich an indicator, check it against threat intelligence, isolate a host, disable an account, open a case, and let the platform run those steps automatically the moment a qualifying alert arrives. The repetitive triage that used to consume an analyst's day runs in seconds, and the steps that genuinely need human judgment are the only ones that reach the queue.

Connect the tools you already own so a single response can reach across the stack. Playbooks call out to endpoint, network, identity, email, and ticketing systems through reusable connectors, gather the evidence, take the containment action, and write everything back to a security case so the incident has one timeline from first signal to closure. Analysts work the case, assign tasks, escalate when criteria are met, and track every action against the clock.

Measure and improve the whole response. Every run is recorded, so you can see how often a playbook fires, where it succeeds or fails, and how long containment takes, then tighten mean time to respond release after release. The same record gives leadership and auditors defensible proof that incidents were handled, escalated, and disclosed on time.
records.business_logic: Playbook DSL runtime that executes orchestrated steps across security tools — the engine IS the product, even if individual steps are declarative.

records.description: Identification, prioritization, and remediation of security vulnerabilities across endpoints, cloud, and applications.
records.catalog_tagline: Find every weakness across your estate, fix the ones an attacker would actually use first, and prove it stayed fixed.
records.catalog_description:
Run a closed loop that turns a sprawling, noisy list of security weaknesses into a short list of fixes the right team actually completes. Discover what you own first, from endpoints, servers, and network gear to cloud workloads, containers, web apps, and source code, then scan it continuously so new exposures surface within hours instead of at the next quarterly review. Each scan produces findings tied to a specific asset and a specific vulnerability, deduplicated and tracked through their own lifecycle so a weakness opened today is the same record you confirm, remediate, and verify weeks later.

Not every finding deserves the same urgency, so layer risk on top of raw severity. Combine base severity scores with exploit-prediction signals, known-exploited and actively-attacked intelligence, asset criticality, and exposure to produce a ranked queue that answers the only question that matters at scale: what do we fix this week. Route the winners to the team that owns the fix as remediation work with due dates and ownership, and give the business a governed path to formally accept and time-box the risks it chooses not to fix yet.

Close the loop and keep it auditable. Re-scan to confirm fixes actually landed, reopen anything that regresses, and watch mean-time-to-remediate trend down by asset group, business unit, and severity. Hand auditors defensible evidence that scanning cadence, remediation timelines, and exception approvals meet the obligations that frameworks such as PCI-DSS, FedRAMP, and NIS2 expect, so vulnerability work stops being a spreadsheet fire drill and becomes a measured, repeatable control.
records.business_logic: Vulnerability scanning engines (network, host, web, container, code), CVE matching, and risk scoring: the algorithmic surface is the product.

records.description: Collection, curation, and operationalisation of indicators and adversary intelligence.
records.catalog_tagline: Pull threat indicators and adversary intelligence from open and commercial feeds, curate them, then push the high-confidence signals straight into your detection stack.
records.catalog_description:
Bring every threat indicator your team relies on into one curated catalog. Pull hashes, IP addresses, domains, URLs, and exploited CVEs from open feeds, commercial intelligence providers, and information-sharing communities, then normalize them across STIX, TAXII, and the formats each source uses, deduplicate the overlap, and score what is left by confidence and by how relevant it is to your environment. Track the actors, campaigns, and malware families behind the indicators, map the techniques they use to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and write finished-intelligence reports your analysts, responders, and leadership can act on.

Turn that catalog into protection. Push high-confidence indicators directly into your SIEM, endpoint tooling, firewalls, and DNS controls for blocking and detection, and record a sighting every time your own telemetry matches a known indicator so you see who is being targeted and where. Manage priority intelligence requirements so collection stays focused on what leadership actually cares about, retract false positives quickly, and share back to the community in formats that respect Traffic Light Protocol handling.

Keep the program defensible. Show coverage against the requirements you set, evidence how indicators flowed from feed to block, and connect threat intelligence to the incidents, vulnerabilities, and risks it informs across the rest of your security operations.
records.business_logic: Indicator correlation, enrichment pipelines, and adversary attribution: analytic substrate beneath a curation workflow.

records.description: Integrated risk management spanning policy, controls, risk assessment, and compliance evidence.
records.catalog_tagline: Run risk, compliance, policy, and audit on one connected register so nothing falls through the cracks.
records.catalog_description: Bring enterprise risk, controls, policies, regulatory obligations, attestations, and audit issues into a single governed workspace. Identify and score risks, map them to the controls that mitigate them, test those controls on a schedule, and capture the evidence that proves it. Publish policies, drive attestation campaigns, track obligations against frameworks like SOX, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and NIST CSF, and open remediation plans the moment a control fails. Teams get a defensible, always-current view of their compliance posture and a clean audit trail instead of scattered spreadsheets and last-minute scrambles.
records.business_logic: Risk aggregation (Monte Carlo, qualitative-to-quantitative mapping) and control-effectiveness scoring; control libraries and assessments are CRUD.

records.description: Planning, fieldwork, evidence, and issue tracking for internal and external audits.
records.catalog_tagline: Plan, execute, and report internal audits from a risk-based plan through fieldwork, findings, and tracked remediation.
records.catalog_description:
Run your internal audit function end to end. Build a risk-based annual plan, scope engagements, and assign teams, then carry out fieldwork with work papers and control tests that capture evidence as you go. When you raise a finding, route it for management response, agree on recommendations, and track follow-up actions to closure so nothing slips.

Produce review-ready reports for leadership and the audit committee, and keep a defensible trail of who tested what, when, and with what result. Sign-offs, locked work papers, and a clear status on every open issue give you confidence that the audit cycle is under control and that remediation is actually getting done.

records.description: Business impact analysis, continuity planning, and exercise execution for resilience.
records.catalog_tagline: Know what would hurt most if it stopped, plan the recovery, and prove the plan works before you need it.
records.catalog_description:
Build an organization that keeps running when something goes wrong. Start with a business impact analysis that maps each critical service to the processes, applications, people, and suppliers it depends on, then set the recovery time and recovery point targets that say how fast each one has to come back and how much data you can afford to lose. Turn those targets into continuity and disaster recovery plans with named owners, recovery strategies, and step-by-step runbooks, so the response is written down and approved instead of improvised under pressure.

Keep the plans honest. Schedule tabletop, walkthrough, and full-interruption exercises, capture the gaps and action items each one surfaces, and feed the findings back into the plans so they get stronger with every test. When a real disruption hits, activate the right plan, stand up the response team, work the call tree and mass-notification roster, log every decision and outbound message, and stand down cleanly with an after-action record that improves the next response.

Give leadership and auditors a defensible answer on resilience. Track plan currency and exercise coverage, evidence the controls that frameworks such as ISO 22301, DORA, and NIS2 expect, and connect continuity to the risks and compliance findings raised elsewhere so a critical risk automatically refreshes the continuity exposure it threatens.
records.business_logic: Dependency mapping between business services, applications, and infrastructure is the modest algorithmic layer; the rest is plans, BIAs, and exercise records.

records.description: Mapping of important business services to people, processes, technology, and third parties, with tolerance setting.
records.catalog_tagline: Map the services your customers depend on, set the limits you can never breach, and prove you can stay inside them when something breaks.
records.catalog_description:
Run your business through the lens of the services that matter most to customers and to the market, not the systems that happen to support them. Identify your important business services, then map each one down to the people, processes, applications, data, and third parties it relies on, so you can see exactly what a single failure would take out and where the hidden single points of failure are.

For every important service, set an impact tolerance: the maximum disruption you are willing to accept before customers or the wider market are harmed. Test those limits against severe but plausible scenarios, from a key supplier going dark to a cyber outage or a data-center loss, and record whether each service stayed inside tolerance or breached it. Turn every breach and near miss into tracked remediation with owners and due dates, so the gaps close instead of resurfacing in the next test.

Give boards and regulators a clear, evidenced view of how resilient the organization really is. Maintain the self-assessment and reporting that rules such as DORA and NIS2 expect, link operational-resilience incidents back to the services and tolerances they threatened, and keep the dependency map current as the business changes, so resilience is a living posture you can defend rather than a document that ages on a shelf.
records.business_logic: Mapping algorithms that propagate impact across the important-business-service graph; minor compared to the workflow surface.

records.description: Onboarding, due diligence, and ongoing risk monitoring of vendors and third parties.
records.catalog_tagline: Know who you do business with, prove they are safe before you sign, and catch the risks that surface after the contract goes live.
records.catalog_description:
Third-Party Risk Management runs the full lifecycle of vetting and watching the vendors, suppliers, and service providers your organization depends on. Onboard a new third party, classify it by how critical it is and how much data or access it touches, then run the due diligence the tier demands: security questionnaires, document collection, certification checks, and a clear go or no-go before the contract is signed.

After onboarding, keep watching. Re-assess on a cadence set by the vendor's tier, ingest external security-rating and breach signals, and turn findings into tracked remediation that closes before the next review cycle or contract renewal. Escalate the third parties that drift into higher risk so the right reviewers in procurement, security, and compliance see them in time.

Built to give risk, procurement, and security teams one defensible record of every third party, the evidence behind each decision, and the open issues that still need to close. Maps to the frameworks regulated organizations answer to, including DORA's requirements for an information register of ICT providers and visibility into the subcontracting chain.
records.business_logic: Risk scoring rules over questionnaire responses; typically rule-driven and expressible in a declarative engine.

records.description: Data subject rights, consent, processing inventory, and privacy assessments.
records.catalog_tagline: Handle data-subject requests, capture consent, and keep your processing inventory audit-ready.
records.catalog_description: Run the privacy operations that keep you compliant with GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, and the privacy laws that follow them. Intake and fulfill data-subject access, correction, and deletion requests through a tracked pipeline that fans out to every source system and meets the statutory response clock. Capture and prove consent against the specific purpose it was given for, and honor withdrawals across the systems that rely on it. Maintain a living record of processing activities so you always know what personal data you hold, where it lives, who it is shared with, and on what legal basis. Author privacy and data-protection impact assessments, route them for sign-off, and log breaches with the notification timing regulators expect, so an audit or a regulator inquiry becomes a report you can pull rather than a fire drill.
records.business_logic: Data-inventory discovery (scanning sources to map personal data) is the irreducible kernel; the workflow side (DSR, consent) is declarative.

records.description: Environmental, social, and governance data collection, disclosure, and reporting.
records.catalog_tagline: Measure your footprint, hit your targets, and report with confidence.
records.catalog_description: Turn raw operational data into a defensible sustainability record. Pull in activity data and utility readings, apply the right emission factors, and calculate Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions down to the facility. Set reduction and net-zero targets, track them against live metrics, and run the initiatives that close the gap. When reporting season arrives, prepare disclosures to each framework you answer to, from CSRD and ISSB to GHG Protocol, keep the audit trail your assurance provider needs, and score the suppliers that drive your value-chain footprint. One place to manage the numbers, the commitments, and the evidence behind every claim you publish.
records.business_logic: Emissions calculation engine (Scope 1/2/3, conversion factors, allocation rules), regulated and irreducible; the data-collection side is workflow.

records.description: Employee case management, knowledge, journeys, and document management for the HR function.
records.catalog_tagline: Give employees one place to ask HR questions, get answers, and track every request to resolution.
records.catalog_description:
Run employee HR support as a single service experience. Employees raise questions and requests from a self-service portal, find answers in a curated knowledge base, and watch their case move from intake to resolution without chasing anyone.

Behind the scenes, incoming cases are triaged and routed to the right HR specialist, escalated across payroll, benefits, access, and other teams when needed, and resolved against documented service levels. Approvals, assignments, and reopen handling are built into the workflow so nothing slips between stages.

As cases resolve, the knowledge base grows from real questions, deflecting future requests and freeing HR teams to focus on the cases that genuinely need a human.

records.description: Workplace booking, space optimization, real-estate management, and visitor handling.
records.catalog_tagline: Book the desk, reserve the room, and prove the space is working.
records.catalog_description: Run the hybrid workplace end to end: a single registry of sites, buildings, and floors that every booking flow rides on, self-service desk and meeting-room reservations with check-in and no-show recapture, a facilities service desk for workplace tickets, and occupancy analytics that turn badge and booking signals into space-utilization reporting. The payoff is a workplace employees can navigate without friction and a real-estate footprint leaders can right-size with evidence instead of guesswork.
records.business_logic: Space-optimization algorithms (occupancy planning, stack diagrams, scenario modeling) for real-estate teams; the rest is reservations and workflow.

records.description: Pre-registration, check-in, badging, and tracking of physical-site visitors.
records.catalog_tagline: Pre-register every visitor, check them in fast at the door, and keep a defensible record of who was on-site, when, and why.
records.catalog_description:
Invite visitors before they arrive and let them fill in their details, accept the agreements your site requires, and get screened ahead of time, so check-in at the front desk is a tap rather than a clipboard. When they walk in, verify them, print or push a badge scoped to where they are allowed to go, and notify their host automatically. Every step is timestamped, so the people watching the lobby always know who is in the building.

The same flow keeps you compliant and ready for an emergency. Non-disclosure acknowledgments and watchlist screening run as part of the visit instead of as a separate chore, host responsibility is recorded against each guest, and a live on-site roster is one click away when the alarm sounds. Sealed audit logs give security, facilities, and compliance teams a single trustworthy trail of every arrival and departure.

records.description: Intake, matter management, and operational workflows for the in-house legal function.
records.catalog_tagline: Run the in-house legal department as a service: take in requests, triage them into matters, and move legal work to close.
records.catalog_description:
Legal Service Delivery gives the in-house legal team a single front door for the rest of the business. Employees and business units submit requests for advice, review, or representation through an intake portal; the legal team triages each request, decides whether to open a matter, route it to outside counsel, or answer it directly, and then tracks the work through to resolution. Matters carry their parties, key dates, budgets, and assigned counsel in one place, so nothing falls through the cracks and the team can see how much legal work is in flight at any moment.

Around the matter sit the operational workflows that legal teams live in every day: issuing and releasing legal holds, orchestrating ediscovery collection and production, recording legal advice with its privilege classification, engaging and managing outside counsel, and responding to inquiries from regulators within deadline. Court-bound matters get a docket that tracks filings, hearings, and trial dates against the calendar.

The value is faster, more consistent legal service with far less email and spreadsheet tracking. Leaders get visibility into demand, workload, cycle time, and outside-counsel spend, while the business gets a predictable place to ask for legal help and a clear answer on where each request stands.

records.description: Authoring, negotiation, execution, and post-signature management of contracts.
records.catalog_tagline: Draft, negotiate, sign, and track every contract from first draft through renewal in one place.
records.catalog_description:
Manage the entire life of a contract without losing the thread. Author new agreements from a library of pre-approved clauses and templates, route them through legal and business review, and capture redlines as counterparties negotiate. When terms are settled, send for electronic signature and store the executed document in a searchable repository.

After signing, the work continues: track the obligations each contract creates, get ahead of due dates and renewals, and know the moment a commitment is satisfied, breached, or waived. Every contract stays current, every deadline stays visible, and the organization always knows what it has agreed to.
records.business_logic: Clause-comparison and risk-detection ML during negotiation; the rest is repository, redlining workflow, and approvals.

records.description: End-to-end procurement workflows from sourcing through purchase order to payment.
records.catalog_tagline: Run procurement end to end: source suppliers, raise requisitions, issue purchase orders, receive goods, and match invoices in one connected workflow.
records.catalog_description:
Source-to-Pay is the operational backbone of corporate buying. It tracks the requisition, the purchase order, the goods receipt, and the supplier invoice as one connected chain of records, with approvals, three-way matching, and savings tracking layered on top. Buyers raise requisitions and route them through approval, sourcing managers run RFx events and award contracts, receivers post goods receipts against open orders, and accounts-payable specialists match invoices to orders and receipts before payment is released.

The value is control and speed across the whole buying motion: every dollar of spend is requested, approved, and reconciled against a negotiated price, exceptions are routed instead of stalling the line, and spend categories drive the routing so direct, indirect, services, and tail spend each follow the right path. Teams get a single audit trail from first sourcing event to final payment, fewer maverick purchases, and measurable savings captured at line-item granularity.
records.business_logic: Tax/compliance determination, savings calculation, and contract-price compliance; the rest is requisition, PO, and invoice workflow.

records.description: Supplier onboarding, master data, performance, and relationship management.
records.catalog_tagline: Onboard new suppliers, qualify them against your standards, and monitor performance and risk on one supplier record.
records.catalog_description:
Run supplier onboarding from invite through KYC, banking, tax, and sanctions checks. Capture insurance, ISO, and SOC certifications with automatic expiry alerts so renewals never lapse.

Score supplier performance against delivery, quality, and SLA targets. Roll KPIs into tiered scorecards your category managers and finance teams share.

Assess supplier risk on financial, ESG, cyber, and operational axes. Escalate elevated scores to governance and procurement for re-qualification or replacement.
records.business_logic: Supplier scorecard math (KPI roll-ups, weighted ratings), a calc layer over CRUD records.

records.description: Invoice capture, matching, approval, and payment execution for accounts payable.
records.catalog_tagline: Capture invoices, match them to POs and receipts, and pay suppliers on time without the spreadsheet shuffle.
records.catalog_description: Accounts Payable Automation takes the manual grind out of paying suppliers. Invoices arrive by email, PDF, or supplier portal and are captured and read automatically, then matched line by line against the purchase order and goods receipt so clean invoices flow straight through and only real exceptions reach a human. Approvals route to the right people on policy, duplicate and fraud checks run before any money moves, and approved bills are grouped into scheduled payment runs across ACH, wire, check, and other methods. The result is faster cycle times, fewer late-payment penalties, captured early-payment discounts, and a clean audit trail your controllers and auditors can trust.
records.business_logic: OCR/IDP for invoice capture, three-way match against PO and receipt, duplicate detection, and fraud rules — algorithm-heavy at the front of the workflow.

records.description: Case management, omnichannel engagement, and self-service for external customer support.
records.catalog_tagline: Capture every customer issue, triage it across channels, and resolve it fast against the support level the customer is owed.
records.catalog_description:
Customer Service Management turns inbound questions, complaints, and incidents into tracked cases your team can route, prioritize, and close. Capture cases from email, chat, phone, and social in one queue, then let triage and AI-assisted classification put each one in front of the right agent with the right context.

Resolve faster with a knowledge surface that suggests answers as agents work and lets them publish proven fixes back for self-service. Bind every case to the entitlements and service levels the customer has paid for, so response and resolution clocks reflect real contractual commitments and breaches are visible before they happen.

Close the loop with satisfaction capture on every interaction, feeding retention and health signals back to the teams that own the relationship.
records.business_logic: Skills-based routing and next-best-action recommendations are the only non-CRUD layer; both are increasingly handled by ML models invoked from declarative rules.

records.description: Dispatch, scheduling, mobile work order, and parts management for on-site service technicians.
records.catalog_tagline: Schedule, dispatch, and complete on-site service work while keeping equipment, contracts, and customer commitments in sync.
records.catalog_description: Field service management runs the full loop from a service request to a closed visit. Dispatchers match the right technician, parts, and time slot to each job; technicians work the route, capture what happened on site, and close out the work order. The installed-equipment record, preventive-maintenance schedules, and service contracts stay current so the next visit starts with full context.
