Brand and creative assets are referenced from the asset repository rather than stored here; generic task and project work is referenced from the work-management layer; campaign execution is referenced from the marketing-execution layer. Sits upstream of execution and downstream of corporate finance.
records.catalog_tagline: Plan your marketing, allocate the budget, and reconcile every dollar of spend back to the plan.
records.catalog_description: Build the annual and quarterly marketing plan as a hierarchy of plan lines, then allocate budget top-down across plans, campaigns, and channels. Track committed and actual spend against every plan line so you always know what is left to spend and where it went. Lay the whole program out on a shared marketing calendar, route budget allocations and spend through approval, and measure plan-level performance and marketing ROI. Connects to your work-management tasks, your asset library, and your campaign-execution tools without duplicating them.
records.business_logic: Budget allocation rollups across the plan-line hierarchy, plan-to-actual spend reconciliation (committed vs actual vs plan), forecast and scenario math on remaining budget, and approval-chain governance on budget allocations and spend.

records.description: Operational system-of-record for workplace safety (incidents, hazards, risk assessments, corrective actions), occupational health and industrial hygiene, audits and inspections, and environmental compliance (permits, emissions, chemical and safety data sheets). Satisfies OSHA, EU-OSHA, ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 obligations at the establishment level. Operationally upstream of corporate sustainability disclosure (supplies incident and environmental data) and a peer to food-safety management (same safety-management-system archetype, occupational and environmental rather than food-specific).
records.catalog_tagline: Keep your people safe and your sites compliant: log incidents, control hazards, run inspections, and stay ahead of OSHA and environmental rules.
records.catalog_description: Capture every injury, near-miss, and hazard the moment it happens, then drive each one to a closed corrective action. Run job hazard analyses and risk assessments, schedule and complete inspections and audits, and track the training and contractor qualifications that keep your sites compliant. Manage chemicals and safety data sheets, monitor industrial-hygiene exposures and occupational-health records, and keep environmental permits, emissions, and OSHA logs audit-ready. One place to prove your safety and environmental programs are working, from the shop floor to the regulator.
records.business_logic: Incident-investigation workflows, OSHA recordability determination, serious-injury-and-fatality and leading-indicator analytics, exposure-limit and sampling calculations against occupational exposure limits, corrective-action escalation, and permit-condition and emission-limit monitoring go beyond the JsonLogic-declarable slice.

records.description: Lessee lease accounting and administration: bringing every operating and finance lease onto the balance sheet under ASC 842 and IFRS 16. Covers right-of-use asset and lease liability recognition, lease classification (finance vs operating under ASC 842; single lessee model under IFRS 16), amortization and liability schedules, modification and remeasurement accounting, journal-entry generation into the general ledger, and quantitative and qualitative disclosure reporting, with an administration layer for lease records, critical dates, and documents. Distinct from the real-estate and workplace view (which treats leases as occupancy records, not an audited subledger) and from commercial real-estate operations (landlord-side CAM, escalations, and the leasing pipeline). The accounting kernel is a certification-grade financial-compliance surface owned by the office of the controller.
records.catalog_tagline: Audit-ready ASC 842 and IFRS 16 lease accounting from contract to disclosure.
records.catalog_description: Put every lease on the balance sheet with the right right-of-use asset, lease liability, and amortization schedule, then generate the journal entries, disclosures, and audit trail your external auditors will accept. Classify finance versus operating leases under ASC 842 or run the single lessee model under IFRS 16, handle modifications and remeasurements without rebuilding spreadsheets, and track critical dates and lease documents in one place. Built for the controller's team to stay compliant and close on time across the whole lease portfolio.
records.business_logic: Amortization and lease-liability schedule generation (effective-interest unwinding, straight-line operating-lease cost plug), lease classification tests (ASC 842 five criteria; IFRS 16 single lessee model), modification and remeasurement re-calculation (discount-rate reassessment, index and rate true-ups, scope changes), impairment of right-of-use assets, and parallel ASC 842 / IFRS 16 schedule computation where both bases are reported. The disclosure maturity analysis and weighted-average rate and term rollups are computed, not declarative.

records.description: Records, plans, and tracks beef, sheep, and mixed grazing-livestock operations: individual-animal records, mob (group) management, mob movements between paddocks and properties, weight gains with average-daily-gain tracking, breeding and calving records, treatment and medicine records with withholding periods, pasture allocation and rotational grazing planning, and the electronic-identifier traceability layer (EID / RFID ear tags, national identification scheme device numbers). Buyer is the small-to-mid grazing operation, station, ranch, or family farm. Distinct from Dairy Herd Management (milking, lactation, milk quality) and from the crop / whole-farm Farm Management Information System, though it shares the paddock and whole-farm substrate with the latter.
records.catalog_tagline: Run your herd and your pastures from one place: animals, mobs, movements, weights, breeding, treatments, and grazing plans.
records.catalog_description: Track every animal and every mob from birth or purchase through to sale, with weights and average daily gains, breeding and calving records, and treatment and medicine logs that keep your withholding periods straight. Move mobs between paddocks and properties, allocate pasture, and plan rotations against your stocking rate and carrying capacity. Capture electronic ear-tag reads in the yard and keep your traceability records audit-ready for the identification scheme in your region. Built for the grazier, station, or family farm that wants real records without the weight of a full enterprise system.
records.business_logic: Beyond CRUD and state-based workflow: average-daily-gain and growth-curve computation from weight series, stocking-rate-versus-carrying-capacity grazing optimization, rest-period and rotation scheduling driven by pasture cover and rainfall, and withholding-period date arithmetic that gates sale and slaughter eligibility after a treatment.

records.description: Cross-channel paid social ad campaign orchestration, dynamic creative optimization, ad-set budget reallocation, audience management, and social attribution / incrementality measurement across the Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Snapchat, and Pinterest ad platforms. Distinct from SMM (organic social publishing, scheduling, engagement, and listening), from MA (email / SMS lifecycle journeys), and from broader programmatic ad-tech / DSPs. Sits at the paid surface of social: it spends ad budget against social ad accounts, versions and optimizes creative, and ties spend to conversions, where SMM stops at organic reach. Flagship vendors are paid-social pure-plays (Smartly.io, Madgicx, Strike Social, Adsmurai) plus omnichannel performance leaders (Skai).
records.catalog_tagline: Run paid social across Meta, TikTok, and LinkedIn from one place: orchestrate campaigns, optimize creative, and reallocate budget to what converts.
records.catalog_description: Manage every paid social campaign across the major ad platforms without living in five ad managers. Structure campaigns, ad sets, and ads against your social ad accounts, build and sync audiences, and push spend where the returns are. Version your creative, let dynamic creative optimization test the combinations, and promote the winners automatically. Watch pacing and performance in real time, reallocate ad-set budgets on a ROAS and pacing signal, and tie spend back to conversions with attribution and incrementality testing so you know what actually drove revenue, not just what the platform reported.
records.business_logic: Bid and budget optimization across ad sets, dynamic creative optimization (combinatorial generation and performance-weighted selection of creative variants), auto budget reallocation between ad sets on a pacing and ROAS signal, multi-touch attribution and incrementality / conversion-lift modeling, and pacing / anomaly detection on live spend. These are algorithmic decision loops over external ad-platform telemetry rather than declarative CRUD plus state workflow, which is why the JsonLogic-expressible share is moderate.

records.description: Detects, investigates, and mitigates risk posed by trusted insiders (employees, contractors, partners). Scores user behavior for risk, correlates anomalous data movement and policy-violation signals into prioritized alerts, runs insider-threat investigations with file-lineage forensics and evidence collection, and monitors departing-employee exit risk. Consumes data-egress signals from Data Loss Prevention, sensitive-data context from Data Security Posture Management, and employment status from Human Capital Management; hands high-risk cases to HR and Legal. Distinct from DLP (which enforces content egress at the perimeter) and DSPM (which secures data at rest): insider risk is the human-centric case-and-investigation discipline that fuses those signals around the person.
records.catalog_tagline: See, investigate, and contain insider risk before trusted users cause a breach.
records.catalog_description: Spot the people-shaped risks your perimeter tools miss. Score every user's behavior, surface anomalous data movement and risky activity as prioritized alerts, and turn the noise into a clear case queue. Investigate with file-lineage forensics and a full activity timeline, collect defensible evidence for HR and Legal, and keep a close watch on departing employees during their highest-risk window. Pull in egress signals, sensitive-data context, and employment status automatically, so analysts spend their time on real threats instead of stitching data together.
records.business_logic: Behavior-based risk scoring models over multi-source activity (endpoint, email, file, cloud, identity), anomaly detection against per-user baselines, indicator-of-compromise correlation, and file-lineage reconstruction. These ML and correlation engines sit beyond the JsonLogic-declarable CRUD and state-workflow slice.

records.description: Durable execution and runtime orchestration of long-running business processes: an engine that deploys executable process definitions (BPMN and code-first), runs each as a stateful, fault-tolerant process instance with automatic retries, timers, signals, and compensation, drives human-task inboxes and case handling, and evaluates decision tables (DMN) at runtime. The market spans developer-centric durable-execution engines (Camunda, Temporal, Orkes Conductor, Flowable) and the orchestration runtimes inside Business Orchestration and Automation Technology suites. Distinct from Low-Code Application Platform (LCAP, which builds and deploys apps), Business Process Architecture (BPA, which models and publishes process blueprints), Robotic Process Automation (RPA, which drives UIs), and Process Mining (PROC-MIN, which analyzes the event logs this engine emits). This is the successor runtime category to the retired intelligent business process management suite market.
records.catalog_tagline: Run your long-running business processes as durable, auditable workflows that never lose their place.
records.catalog_description: Turn a process model into a running engine. Deploy each process definition, then launch instances that survive restarts, retry failed steps automatically, wait on timers and external events, and pick up exactly where they left off. Route the human steps to the right people's inboxes, manage flexible cases that do not follow a fixed path, and evaluate your decision tables in real time so the rules live in one place. Every step is recorded, so you always know which instances are running, stuck, or done, and you can prove what happened and when.
records.business_logic: Durable state-machine execution: a persistent process-instance engine that advances tokens through BPMN gateways, handles timers, message and signal correlation, parallel and compensating branches, retry and backoff on failed jobs, and at-least-once job dispatch to distributed task workers. Plus a DMN decision engine evaluating hit policies over decision tables at runtime. These are general-purpose execution semantics that go well beyond declarative CRUD.

records.description: Mobile-first operations platform for non-desk workers who have no corporate email or workstation: broadcast messaging and acknowledgment, task and checklist execution, shift-swap conversations, microlearning, and recognition delivered through a single branded app, kiosk, or shared device. Bought by store, plant, and field operations rather than internal communications or HR. Consumes the workforce's employees from HCM and shifts from Workforce Management, and hands work back to those systems. Distinct from Employee Communications and Intranet (office-comms publishing platform, internal-comms buyer), Workforce Management (owns the shift record and swap approval), Retail Store Operations (retail-only task execution), and Employee Experience and Engagement (survey listening, not broadcast or recognition).
records.catalog_tagline: Reach, task, and recognize your frontline workforce from one mobile app, no corporate email required.
records.catalog_description: Connect every deskless worker on the floor through a branded mobile app, kiosk, or shared device. Broadcast targeted announcements and confirm who has read them, push tasks and checklists that workers complete and submit from their phones, and let teams swap shifts, finish bite-size training, and recognize each other in the same place. Built for store, plant, warehouse, and field staff who never had a work email, with handoff back to scheduling and store operations.
records.business_logic: Audience targeting and supervisor-cascade routing to workers without unique work email; mandatory-read acknowledgment tracking; multilingual content delivery under union and works-council content rules; offline-tolerant task submission sync from shared and personal devices.

records.description: Software market for curating brand content and broadcasting it to employees, who reshare it to their own personal social networks to extend organic reach, strengthen employer brand, and drive social selling. Tracks each employee share, gamifies participation with points and leaderboards, scores advocate influence, generates internal newsletters of shareable content, and attributes resulting clicks, reach, and pipeline back to revenue. Distinct from Social Media Management (brand-owned channels and external influencer programs), Employee Communications and Intranet (internal-only news and announcements), Frontline / Deskless Worker Communication (internal deskless comms), and Employee Experience and Engagement (engagement and pulse surveys). The advocate is an employee resharing externally, not a brand channel and not an internal audience.
records.catalog_tagline: Turn your employees into your most trusted social channel: curate content, make sharing one click, and measure the reach and pipeline it drives.
records.catalog_description: Give your team a steady stream of approved, on-brand content and let them share it to their own LinkedIn, X, and Facebook networks in a single click, with ready-to-post copy they can personalize. Reward participation with points, badges, and leaderboards, surface your top advocates, and send each person a tailored newsletter of what is worth sharing this week. See exactly what every share earned in clicks, reach, and earned media value, and connect that activity to the pipeline and revenue it influenced. Built for marketing and communications teams who want authentic employee reach without chasing people for screenshots.
records.business_logic: Advocate influence scoring and reach / earned-media-value computation over per-share engagement; share-to-pipeline attribution modeling; gamification point and leaderboard ranking engines; AI content recommendation and personalized share-copy generation for each advocate.

records.description: Software market for managing short-term and vacation rental properties: listing setup and distribution across booking channels and online travel agencies, reservation and guest management, dynamic nightly pricing, housekeeping and turnover coordination, and owner trust accounting. Distinct from long-term residential property management (lease-and-tenant shaped) and from hotel property management systems; serves individual hosts, professional short-term rental managers, and hospitality operators.
records.catalog_tagline: Distribute listings across every booking channel, manage reservations and guests, automate pricing and turnovers, and account for each owner, in one short-term rental platform.
records.catalog_description: Run a short-term and vacation rental business end to end. Publish and sync listings across the major booking channels from a single calendar, capture reservations and message guests in a unified inbox, and let dynamic pricing set the right nightly rate. Coordinate cleaning and turnovers between checkouts, collect payments, and keep guests and owners informed automatically. Owner trust accounting produces commission-based statements and payouts, with optional lodging-tax remittance and local permit tracking for regulated markets.
records.business_logic: Dynamic nightly pricing (demand, seasonality, lead-time, and competitor-set rules), availability-calendar reconciliation across channels to prevent double-booking, channel-specific rate and fee mapping (cleaning fees, channel commissions, taxes), owner-statement commission math (management percentage and pass-through expense allocation), and occupancy/lodging-tax calculation and remittance per jurisdiction.

records.description: Software market for operating marinas, boatyards, and dry-stack facilities: slip, berth, mooring, and rack inventory and assignment; transient, seasonal, and waitlisted reservations; recurring slip contracts with metered electric and water billing; boater and vessel records; boatyard service, haul-out, and launch scheduling; and fuel-dock and ship-store point of sale. Serves marina operators, yacht clubs, municipal harbors, and dry-stack storage businesses. Distinct from long-term residential property management and from hotel property management systems.
records.catalog_tagline: Run your marina end to end: assign slips and storage, take reservations, bill boaters and meter utilities, schedule the boatyard, and sell fuel, all in one place.
records.catalog_description: Operate a marina, boatyard, or dry-stack facility from a single system. Lay out your docks, slips, moorings, and racks, then assign each vessel by fit and keep an accurate availability calendar across transient, seasonal, and waitlisted demand. Take reservations and transient bookings, manage boater and vessel records with insurance and registration on file, and bill on recurring contracts with metered electric and water charges. Schedule haul-outs, launches, and boatyard work orders, run the fuel dock and ship store, and keep owners and boaters informed automatically.
records.business_logic: Slip-fit assignment matching vessel length, beam, and draft to berth dimensions and utilities; availability-calendar reconciliation across transient, seasonal, and waitlist demand to prevent double-booking of slips, moorings, and racks; metered-utility billing math turning electric and water sub-meter reads into invoice lines; seasonal, transient, and long-term rate and proration rules; fuel-dock inventory and pump reconciliation; and dry-stack launch scheduling against forklift and rack capacity.

records.description: Software market for product marketing: competitive intelligence and battlecards, go-to-market launch planning and coordination, messaging and positioning craft, and sales-enablement content. Bought by the Product Marketing lead, distinct from sales planning (GTM-PLAN) and product management (PROD-MGMT). Anchors the launch-orchestration and competitive-enablement surfaces no sales-planning or roadmap vendor masters.
records.catalog_tagline: Run every product launch, win every competitive deal, and arm sales with the right message and content.
records.catalog_description: Bring product marketing into one place: track competitors and ship battlecards your sellers actually use, plan and coordinate launches from kickoff to GA, craft the messaging and positioning that the whole company aligns on, and produce the sales-enablement content that closes deals. Run win/loss programs to learn why you win, and see which content and messaging move the needle. Stop scattering launches and competitive intel across docs and decks, and give the business one source of truth for how the product goes to market.
records.business_logic: Competitive-intel relevance scoring and source de-duplication over ingested intel feeds; sales-enablement content engagement analytics and recommendation ranking; win/loss theme extraction and sentiment from interview transcripts; launch-readiness rollup scoring across cross-functional checklists.

records.description: Downstream account-based engagement platform: contact- and account-level intent capture, anonymous-to-account identity resolution, engagement scoring, multichannel orchestration, account-based advertising, and 1:1 web personalization. Ingests ICPs and target account lists authored in Go-to-Market Planning and runs engagement against them. Bought by Marketing Operations; distinct from the planning shell (GTM-PLAN) and from campaign automation (MA).
records.catalog_tagline: Know which accounts are in-market, then engage them across ads, web, and orchestration before competitors do.
records.catalog_description: Turn your target account list into pipeline. Capture intent signals and resolve anonymous web traffic to real accounts, score engagement so you know who is heating up, and orchestrate multichannel plays across advertising, web, and outreach. Run account-based ad campaigns and personalize the website for named accounts, all governed by consent. Ingest the ICP and target lists your planning team authored and engage against them, so marketing spend lands on the accounts that matter.
records.business_logic: Predictive and third-party intent scoring, anonymous-visitor to account identity resolution, account/contact engagement scoring models, programmatic ad bidding and audience activation, and AI-driven web personalization variant selection.

records.description: Software market for scaling agile delivery across many teams, programs, and portfolios: program-increment and release-train coordination, epic-to-feature backlog hierarchy, cross-team dependency management, agile roadmaps, OKR-to-delivery alignment, and flow analytics. Bought by the engineering and agile-transformation office (release-train engineers, VP Engineering, the agile PMO). Distinct from SPM (top-down CIO/EPMO investment planning), from generic work management (not framework-aware), and from the value-stream delivery toolchain (which builds and ships code rather than planning it).
records.catalog_tagline: Plan and coordinate agile delivery across every team, program, and portfolio in one place.
records.catalog_description: Bring scaled-agile delivery under one roof. Model the full delivery hierarchy from portfolio epics down to features, stories, sprints, and release trains, and plan each program increment with your teams. Map and resolve cross-team dependencies before they block delivery, keep agile roadmaps and release plans current, and connect OKRs to the work that achieves them. Live flow and velocity analytics show where delivery is on track and where it is stuck, so release-train engineers and delivery leaders can steer in real time. Built for organizations running multiple teams or trains that need coordinated, framework-aware planning rather than a generic task board.
records.business_logic: Beyond declarable CRUD: cross-team dependency-health computation, velocity and flow rollups across the release-train and program-increment hierarchy, what-if PI planning, and OKR-to-delivery alignment scoring.

records.description: Software market for measuring end-to-end software delivery flow across a heterogeneous toolchain the platform does not own: value-stream mapping, flow metrics (velocity, time, load, efficiency, distribution), bottleneck and constraint detection, DORA benchmarking, and software-delivery-to-business-outcome alignment. A tool-agnostic overlay that integrates the delivery toolchain to measure it rather than producing its artifacts. Distinct from the value-stream delivery toolchain (which builds and ships software) by measuring across tools it does not own, and from SPM (top-down investment planning) by observing actual flow bottom-up after work happens.
records.catalog_tagline: See how work really flows across your whole delivery toolchain, and where it gets stuck.
records.catalog_description: Get one honest view of software delivery across every tool your teams already use. Connect your planning, source, CI/CD, and service tools, map your value streams, and let the platform mirror the work items flowing through them. Measure flow velocity, time, load, efficiency, and distribution, surface the bottlenecks slowing delivery, and benchmark delivery performance with DORA metrics. Tie delivery outcomes back to business investment so leaders can see whether effort is going to new value, defects, or debt. Built as a tool-agnostic layer for organizations running a mixed toolchain that no single delivery platform can measure end to end.
records.business_logic: Almost entirely derive-and-measure over mirrored upstream work items: flow-metric computation across the value stream, bottleneck and constraint detection, DORA rollups, and feature-vs-defect-vs-debt investment-mix analysis. The genuine declarable CRUD is limited to value-stream definitions, tool-connection configuration, and metric thresholds.

records.domain_name: Real Estate Agent (solo / small firm bundle)
records.description: Solo-agent and small-firm persona bundle. Single-install deployable for individual real estate agents covering lead capture and contact relationships (CRM-LEAD-MGT, CRM-ACCT-MGT), listing creation and MLS syndication, tour scheduling, transaction execution, disclosure handling (RE-BROK-AGENT-OPS), and contract reference (CLM-REPOSITORY). One module to install; larger brokerages deploy the underlying full modules and skip the starter.
records.catalog_tagline: A working surface for the real-estate agent.
records.catalog_description: Bring contacts, listings, and the documents behind each deal into one agent-facing workspace. Move leads forward, keep listing and transaction paperwork organized, and stay on top of every active deal from a single view that travels with the agent across the systems they already use.

records.description: Small-shop persona bundle for HVAC service businesses (5-30 technicians). Single-install deployable covering customer accounts and contacts (CRM), service dispatch and field execution (FSM-DISPATCH-OPS), installed equipment register and PM cadence (FSM-INSTALLED-BASE), recurring maintenance agreements (FSM-SERVICE-CONTRACTS), quote-to-invoice (CPQ + SUB-MGMT), and parts inventory (HAM). Larger organizations deploy the full modules and skip the starter.
records.catalog_tagline: A ready-to-run home-services starter that takes an HVAC job from customer call to scheduled visit and invoice.
records.catalog_description: This starter packages the field-service essentials a heating and cooling service business needs on day one. It bundles the customer and contact record, the installed equipment at each site, work orders and field visits, service contracts, and the quote-to-invoice path so a small team can book a call, schedule a technician, complete the job, and bill it without stitching tools together. It is a fast on-ramp to field service for trades operators who want the core workflow working immediately and can grow into the full modules later.

records.description: Cross-domain starter kit for small and mid-sized IT teams. Embeds lightweight shells of the records a small IT shop manages: the helpdesk (optional), the hardware register, the SaaS application and renewal tracker, and the contract register. The renewal/contract spine (asset_contracts + saas_subscriptions) is required; hardware, SaaS apps, helpdesk, and on-prem licenses are optional. domain_id NULL; hosts ITSM, HAM, SMP, ITAM, SAM. Replaces the helpdesk-plus-spreadsheets reality; budget stays in the general ledger.
records.catalog_tagline: Run your whole IT shop from one place: tickets, devices, SaaS renewals, and contracts, without the spreadsheets.
records.catalog_description: One place to manage IT for a small team. Track the hardware you own and who has it, every SaaS app and when its subscription renews, and the contracts behind them, so nothing slips through a spreadsheet and no renewal catches you off guard. Add a lightweight helpdesk for tickets and requests if you do not already run one, or keep the one you have. Start with the renewal and contract essentials and turn on the device, SaaS, and helpdesk pieces as you need them. Built for IT teams that have outgrown spreadsheets but do not need a full enterprise IT suite.

records.description: Employment background verification / pre-employment screening as a standalone market: order screening packages, run criminal, employment, education, identity, driving, drug, and watchlist components, adjudicate against an eligibility matrix, run the FCRA/EEOC adverse-action and compliance chain, and keep workers cleared post-hire with continuous monitoring, rescreening, identity, and right-to-work verification. Distinct from the recruiting-embedded screening step that an applicant-tracking module local-masters.
records.catalog_tagline: Order, track, and adjudicate employment background checks with the FCRA adverse-action chain built in.
records.catalog_description: Run employment background checks end to end. Build screening packages from criminal, employment, education, identity, driving, and drug components, then invite candidates to a portal to give consent and complete their checks. Adjudicate results against a configurable eligibility matrix, and when a result is disqualifying, walk the full pre-adverse and adverse action chain with disclosures, authorizations, summary-of-rights acknowledgements, and dispute handling. Keep workers cleared after hire with continuous monitoring, rescreening, identity verification, and right-to-work checks.
records.business_logic: Adjudication rules engine that evaluates screening results against a configurable eligibility matrix; orchestration of third-party data-source retrieval and result aggregation across criminal, employment, education, and identity sources; continuous-monitoring alert generation against post-hire data feeds.

records.description: Buyer-side procurement of outsourced services from a firm under a statement of work: author the SOW, intake proposals, run the engagement, track milestones and deliverables, accept the work, and settle milestone-based invoices. The unit is the engagement and its deliverables from a firm, not an individual contractor as in contingent workforce. References the services firm as a supplier mastered elsewhere, the SOW or master agreement as a contract document mastered in contract lifecycle management, and rate cards where the work is rate-priced; masters the SOW engagement cluster itself.
records.catalog_tagline: Buy outsourced services under a statement of work (SOW), then track milestones to acceptance and payment.
records.catalog_description: Procure outsourced services from a firm under a statement of work, not headcount you manage day to day. Author the SOW, take in proposals, and stand up the engagement, then break the work into milestones and deliverables and track each one to acceptance. Settle on what was delivered with milestone-based invoices, handle change orders when scope shifts, and keep a clear record of who accepted what and when. The services firm stays your supplier and the SOW stays your contract; this is where you run the engagement in between.
records.business_logic: Deliverable and milestone acceptance scoring, services-bid evaluation and supplier matching, and change-order impact assessment sit beyond the declarable CRUD and state-workflow slice.

records.description: Software market for operator-side reservation and operations management of tours, activities, attractions, rentals, and guided adventure trips. Covers real-time availability and capacity, online and counter booking, resource and guide scheduling, digital liability waivers, integrated payments, gift cards and refunds, customer communications and reviews, and optional distribution to online travel agencies. Distinct from Corporate Travel Management (the corporate buyer side of trip sourcing) and from Short-Term and Vacation Rental Management (lodging inventory): this domain owns the sale and delivery of a scheduled, capacity-limited experience and the people and equipment that fulfill it.
records.catalog_tagline: Sell, schedule, and run your tours and activities: take bookings, manage availability and guides, collect waivers, and get paid, all in one place.
records.catalog_description: Run your entire tour or activity business from one system. Publish your trips and experiences, show real-time availability online, and let customers book and pay from your website or at the counter. Prevent overbookings, assign guides and equipment to each departure, and collect signed liability waivers before guests arrive. Process payments, issue gift cards, and handle refunds and cancellations without juggling separate tools. Built for day-tour operators, attractions, rental shops, and guided-adventure outfitters alike, with optional distribution to online travel agencies when you want to reach more customers.
records.business_logic: Real-time availability and capacity allocation across shared resources, overbooking prevention, seasonal and dynamic rate rules, guide and equipment assignment against availability, and channel-availability synchronization go beyond plain CRUD plus state workflows.

entity.description: Junction between `handoffs` and `processes`. Links a directional event-driven handoff to the APQC PCF activity (or custom process) it realizes. Populated by discovery (`discovery_query.ts` substring matcher fan-out) with `record_status='new'`; promoted to `approved` by user review per SKILL.md Rule #1. Sub-clusters trigger-event-prefix buckets in Phase D discovery and connects handoffs across different prefixes that share a process. See plan-handoff-processes.md.

computed_fields.name: key
computed_fields.description: 2-tuple natural key for the handoff -> process link: handoff_id.process_id. Materialized by the BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger from this computed_fields JsonLogic. Mirrors the handoffs.key idiom.

fields.title: Handoff
fields.description: The handoff edge being linked to a process activity.

fields.title: Process
fields.description: The process activity (APQC PCF row or custom) that this handoff realizes.

fields.title: Role
fields.description: How the handoff relates to the process. Starts with one value `implements` (this handoff IS the activity). Add more values only when discovery proposes rows that clearly do not fit, per plan-handoff-processes.md §3.

fields.title: Proposal Source
fields.description: Provenance of the proposed tag. human_curated = user explicitly authored the row by typing `add tag X for handoff Y` (highest authority; rare). agent_curated = AI agent (Phase B authoring or b1 audit fix-loop) proposed with full domain context (high confidence; the agent had context but did not bypass review). discovery_override = Discover Pass 2 resolved via curated PCF_OVERRIDES entry (medium confidence; override is hand-curated, application is automated). discovery_substring = Discover Pass 2 resolved via substring fallback (lowest confidence; machine guess). Catalog quality is measured by record_status=approved, NOT by proposal_source.

fields.title: Notes
fields.description: Empty by default. Populate only when there is something exceptional, custom, or special to call out about this pair (e.g. a hand-curated override that overrides a wrong substring match, or a note explaining why an approver kept a borderline match).

fields.title: Record Status
fields.description: Standard workflow per SKILL.md Rule #1. Discovery-proposed rows land as `new`; user review flips them to `approved` or `rejected`. Both approved and rejected rows are sticky on subsequent discovery reruns (existence-of-`key` skip).

fields.title: Key
fields.description: Computed 2-tuple natural key (handoff_id.process_id). Materialized by the BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger from entities.computed_fields. unique_value=true enforces idempotency on the pair at the database layer.

entity.description: Directional event-driven handoffs between two `domain_modules`, sharing a data object. The handoff lives between modules; whether the two modules happen to belong to the same domain or to different ones is a derived property a downstream consumer filters on, not part of the entity's identity. `source_domain_module_id` / `target_domain_module_id` carry the module attribution; `source_domain_id` / `target_domain_id` are the denormalized domain rollup (derivable from the module FKs and kept on the row for backfill-era rows where the module FKs are still NULL). `friction_level` distinguishes expensive async wiring (`medium` / `high`) from cheap in-process lifecycle walks (`low`). Signal 2 of the platform-vs-silos analysis is one such derived filter, applied at the query layer as `source_domain_id != target_domain_id` (see plan-handoffs.md Phase D). Authoring rule: new rows MUST populate both module FK columns unless the counterparty domain has not yet been modularized; legacy rows from pre-modularization carry only the domain FKs and are backfilled per the per-domain audit B10b.

computed_fields.name: key
computed_fields.description: 6-tuple natural key for the handoff edge, concatenated with '.' separators. Uses the platform `concat` operator (SQL CONCAT semantics): null values become empty string.

fields.title: Source Domain
fields.description: The domain that emits the trigger event.

fields.title: Target Domain
fields.description: The domain that receives the event and creates / mutates state in response.

fields.title: Data Object
fields.description: The data object that flows or is created as a result of the handoff.

fields.title: Integration Pattern
fields.description: How the handoff is implemented today across the silo boundary.

fields.title: Friction Level
fields.description: Proxy for the cost of maintaining this handoff today. High friction is where integrated-platform value is greatest.

fields.title: Description
fields.description: What actually happens at the handoff: payload, downstream consequences, known failure modes.

fields.title: Trigger Event
fields.description: Controlled-vocabulary FK to trigger_events. Replaces the legacy free-text `trigger_event` column (which is kept as a safety net until end-of-program review). One event row can be referenced by many handoff rows (one event, many subscribers).

fields.title: Source Module
fields.description: Handoffs really live between modules; the source-domain rollup stays as today during backfill. NULL until the source domain is modularized.

fields.title: Target Module
fields.description: Handoffs really live between modules; the target-domain rollup stays as today during backfill. NULL until the target domain is modularized.

fields.title: Key
fields.description: Computed 6-tuple natural key for the handoff edge: source_domain_id.target_domain_id.source_domain_module_id.target_domain_module_id.trigger_event_id.data_object_id, joined with `.` separators. Materialized by a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger from the entity computed_fields JsonLogic, which uses the platform concat operator (SQL CONCAT semantics: NULL becomes empty string). Marked unique_value=true; the partial unique index enforces idempotency on the 6-tuple at the database layer.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Employee Onboarding : job_offer.accepted
records.description: Candidate accepts offer in ATS; ATS publishes the offer-accepted event with offer details, position, hiring manager, location, start date. Onboarding instantiates a journey by selecting a plan based on role + location + employment type, materializes the task list, and notifies the new hire to begin pre-boarding. Failure modes: late offer-detail changes after journey instantiation (start date pushed, role re-leveled) require either journey re-materialization or manual reconciliation.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Employee Onboarding : employee.created
records.description: HCM creates the canonical employee record (typically on or near Day-1, or earlier for pre-boarding access). Onboarding binds the journey to the new employee_id so task ownership and reminders route to the right user portal. Lower friction when ATS and HCM are the same vendor; higher when they're separate.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → IT Service Management : task.it_provisioning_required
records.description: Onboarding emits the IT-provisioning task for a new hire (laptop, peripherals, baseline software access). ITSM creates the corresponding service request(s); ITSM masters the fulfillment work item. Failure modes: late role / location changes invalidate the original SR catalog selection; manual rework is common.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Identity Governance and Administration : task.access_provisioning_required
records.description: Onboarding flags the access-provisioning task for a new hire. IGA orchestrates the role/entitlement assignment via birthright-access policies and triggers provisioning to downstream systems. High friction because role-to-entitlement mappings are commonly maintained manually per business unit and drift quickly.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Workplace and Space Management : task.workplace_setup_required
records.description: Onboarding flags physical-workplace tasks: badge issuance, desk allocation, parking, building access, ergonomic kit. IWMS systems are rarely event-driven; in practice the handoff is a ticket or an email to Facilities. High friction is the norm.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Payroll Management : journey.day_one_reached
records.description: Day-1 milestone on the journey activates the new hire in Payroll. Direct-deposit, tax-withholding, and country-specific forms collected during the journey feed into Payroll's master record. Batch-sync because most payroll cycles run nightly; mid-cycle hires often require manual catch-up.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Learning Management : task.compliance_training_required
records.description: Compliance training items (security awareness, anti-harassment, HIPAA, country-specific code-of-conduct, role-specific certifications) trigger LMS enrollments. LMS masters the enrollment record and completion certificate; Onboarding consumes the completion event to close out its task. Friction sits in keeping the training catalog mapped to roles/jurisdictions.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → HR Service Delivery : task.escalation_required
records.description: When an onboarding task is blocked, overdue, or contested (missing document, declined accommodation, pre-boarding question), an HR case is opened in HRSD. HRSD masters the case lifecycle; the case-resolution event flows back to unblock the task. Friction comes from inconsistent case-routing taxonomies between Onboarding and HRSD.

records.handoff_label: Enterprise Performance Management → Strategic Workforce Planning : financial_budget.cycle_started
records.description: Annual (or rolling) budget cycle in EPM triggers refresh of workforce plans aligned to the new budget envelope. SWP planners rebuild scenarios under updated cost ceilings. High friction because EPM and SWP rarely share a common plan structure (org-unit dimensions, time grain, account hierarchies all differ), forcing manual reconciliation and re-modeling.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Strategic Workforce Planning : headcount.actuals_updated
records.description: Actual headcount changes (hires, terminations, transfers, leaves) from HCM flow to SWP for plan-vs-actual reconciliation. Usually nightly batch; some orgs run weekly. Friction sits in normalizing HCM's org structure to the planning structure SWP uses.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Strategic Workforce Planning : requisition.filled
records.description: Filled requisitions from ATS decrement open demand in SWP's position forecasts and update plan-vs-actual fill metrics (time-to-fill, fill rate by role/geo). Lower friction than headcount.actuals_updated from HCM because the requisition→forecast mapping is more direct.

records.handoff_label: People Analytics → Strategic Workforce Planning : attrition.forecast_updated
records.description: People Analytics produces an attrition forecast (typically per org unit × tenure × performance band). SWP consumes the forecast to update plan assumptions on natural reduction, refining demand for backfill hires. Friction is medium — the forecast is well-defined but pushing it back into SWP scenarios requires manual planner judgment.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Workforce Planning → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : headcount.approved
records.description: Approved headcount in SWP authorizes requisition creation in ATS. THIS IS THE CO-MASTER BRIDGE: SWP masters the intent slice (approved position, budget, time window) and ATS masters the execution slice (pipeline, candidates, interviews, offer). High friction because SWP's plan structure (org × geo × level × time) rarely matches ATS's requisition template structure (job code × location × hiring manager × pay range), requiring mapping rules that drift as either side evolves.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Workforce Planning → Human Capital Management : hcm_position.approved_for_creation
records.description: Org-design changes (new positions, restructures, eliminated positions, reporting-line changes) trigger position-master updates in HCM. HCM masters positions operationally; SWP designs them strategically. High friction during restructures and M&A — large bulk creations and deletions overwhelm HCM's per-position approval workflows.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Workforce Planning → Enterprise Performance Management : cost_projection.approved
records.description: Approved workforce cost projection (fully-loaded comp expense by period × org × geo × level) is the SWP output that EPM rolls into the consolidated budget. Without this handoff EPM's people-cost line is disconnected from the workforce plan. Friction is medium because the mapping is well-understood but account hierarchies and loading-factor definitions drift between the two domains and require periodic re-alignment.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Human Capital Management : candidate.hired
records.description: Candidate-to-employee conversion: hired candidate from ATS triggers employee-record creation in HCM. Field mapping (candidate → employee) is rarely perfect; missing fields (legal name spelling, work-eligibility detail, tax IDs) get collected in the Onboarding journey and back-filled into HCM.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Payroll Management : employee.created
records.description: New employee in HCM triggers comp profile activation in Payroll: gross-to-net rules selected by jurisdiction, deductions initialised, bank account and tax setup collected via Onboarding flow. Same trigger event as the HCM → Onboarding handoff; both subscribe to the employee.created event.
records.notes:
target_domain_module_id left NULL: tie: 4 modules at role embedded_master.

Tie-break: PAYROLL-RUN is the primary entry point: a new worker enters the next pay cycle. Tax-compliance, earnings-deductions, and pay-statements consume the worker downstream of RUN, not directly off `employee.created`.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Identity Governance and Administration : employee.created
records.description: New employee in HCM triggers directory account creation and birthright-role assignment in IGA. High friction because role-to-entitlement mappings drift per business unit, and IGA frequently needs additional context (cost center, manager, location) that arrives later in the journey. Same trigger event as the HCM → Onboarding and HCM → Payroll handoffs.
records.notes: target_domain_module_id NULL until IGA is modularized (Phase-M gap on target domain; SKILL.md authoring rule).

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : employee.terminated
records.description: Employee termination in HCM optionally triggers backfill requisition consideration in ATS. Low friction when SWP-driven; some orgs auto-open a backfill req on regrettable losses, others route through SWP for approval first.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → People Analytics : employment_event.recorded
records.description: HCM publishes employment events (hire, promotion, transfer, leave, termination) onto a stream that PA consumes to refresh KPIs (tenure, time-in-level, mobility rate, attrition). Low friction because PA tools tend to be designed around this exact ingestion pattern.
records.notes: Tie-break: PA-WORKFORCE-METRICS is the primary raw-event sink. PA-PREDICTIVE-MODELS consumes downstream derived features rather than ingesting `employment_event.recorded` directly.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Talent Management : employee.created
records.description: New employee triggers talent-profile initialisation in Talent Management: career aspirations, mobility preferences, skills profile stubs. Same employee.created trigger as Onboarding / Payroll / IGA handoffs.
records.notes: Tie-break: TALENT-PERFORMANCE-MGMT is the entry point on hire: a new perf record is created at onboarding. SUCCESSION-CAREER and CONTINUOUS-FEEDBACK consume the worker reference but are not the receiving end of `employee.created`.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → People Analytics : requisition.filled
records.description: Filled requisition events flow from ATS to PA for time-to-fill, source-of-hire, and offer-acceptance-rate KPI refresh. Same event drives the ATS → SWP handoff that updates demand forecasts.

records.handoff_label: Payroll Management → People Analytics : pay_cycle.closed
records.description: Closed pay cycle from Payroll lands a snapshot in PA for compensation analytics: total comp by org / level / geo, gender pay-gap analysis, comp velocity. Batch because pay cycles are inherently periodic.

records.handoff_label: People Analytics → Talent Management : high_potential.identified
records.description: PA's predictive-model output identifies employees in the hi-po segment; this triggers their enrollment in Talent Management programs (succession slate, accelerated development, mentor assignment). Friction sits in keeping the hi-po definition consistent with the program criteria.
records.notes: trigger_event publishes workforce_segments (master in PA-WORKFORCE-METRICS)

records.handoff_label: Enterprise Performance Management → Strategic Workforce Planning : financial_forecast.refreshed
records.description: Rolling forecast refresh in EPM (typically monthly or quarterly) triggers SWP to re-evaluate plan assumptions and scenarios. Distinct from the annual budget.cycle_started trigger — this is the in-cycle refresh signal, finer-grained and lower friction.

records.handoff_label: IT Operations Management → IT Service Management : monitoring_event.alert_triggered
records.description: Monitoring/alerting events from ITOM auto-create incidents in ITSM when severity and correlation rules match. High friction in practice — alert storms create incident floods, correlation rules drift, and dedupe logic between systems is rarely good enough. The classic 'NOC-floods-the-helpdesk' problem.

records.handoff_label: HR Service Delivery → IT Service Management : case.it_assistance_required
records.description: HR case that needs IT action (lost laptop replacement, app access for a new role, account lockout) routes a service request into ITSM. Friction sits in the case-to-SR field mapping and status synchronization back to HRSD.

records.handoff_label: IT Service Management → Configuration Management Database : service_change.completed
records.description: Completed change in ITSM updates the affected CIs in CMDB (software version, configuration state, relationship topology). Friction is medium — most ITSM/CMDB pairs are same-vendor and reasonably integrated; cross-vendor combos drift.

records.handoff_label: IT Service Management → IT Asset Management : service_incident.asset_failure
records.description: Incident resolved by replacing or retiring an asset generates a lifecycle event in ITAM. Friction sits in the asset-id resolution (incidents are filed against users or symptoms, asset IDs come later).

records.handoff_label: Discovery and Service Mapping → Hardware Asset Management : device.discovered
records.description: Auto-discovered devices (laptops, network gear, servers) flow to HAM as new hardware_assets candidates. Low friction when the discovery and HAM tool are same-vendor; medium when separate. Manual reconciliation needed for devices behind NAT or off-network.

records.handoff_label: Discovery and Service Mapping → Software Asset Management : software.discovered
records.description: Auto-discovered software installs flow to SAM as software_installations records. Drives the install-vs-entitled reconciliation that justifies SAM's existence.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → IT Asset Management : employee.terminated
records.description: Employee termination triggers asset-recall events: assigned laptops, mobile devices, badges, software licenses must be reclaimed. High friction — recall rates rarely hit 100%, and the cost of unrecovered SaaS seats / laptops shows up in financial leakage reports.

records.handoff_label: Software Asset Management → IT Service Management : license.expiry_warning
records.description: Upcoming license expiry creates a renewal-action service request in ITSM. Low friction because the trigger is calendar-based and well-defined; routing to the right owner is the only nuance.

records.handoff_label: Software Asset Management → Vulnerability Management : software_install.detected
records.description: New software install detected by SAM feeds VULN-MGMT's scan scope — the install set defines what needs to be assessed for known CVEs.

records.handoff_label: Software Asset Management → IT Service Management : license_audit.required
records.description: Vendor-initiated audit or proactive internal review triggers an audit workflow service request. Friction sits in evidence collection across SAM + CLM + S2P data.

records.handoff_label: Expense Management → SaaS Management Platforms : card.saas_charge_detected
records.description: Corporate-card SaaS charge detected by the expense system surfaces a candidate shadow-IT app in SMP. High friction: finance sees the charge, IT/SMP sees (or doesn't see) the app — reconciling vendor-name-on-card with app-name-in-portfolio is messy and is one of the highest-value SMP-to-EXPENSE integrations.

records.handoff_label: SaaS Management Platforms → Source-to-Pay : shadow_app.requires_sanctioning
records.description: Shadow-IT app that passes the threshold for sanctioning (recurring use, multiple users, business-critical) triggers a procurement requisition in S2P to formalize the relationship.

records.handoff_label: Source-to-Pay → Contract Lifecycle Management : sourcing.contract_drafted
records.description: Sourcing decision in S2P hands off to CLM to author the contract. Friction sits in clause selection, redline coordination with the counterparty, and the legal-review loop with LSD.

records.handoff_label: Contract Lifecycle Management → Source-to-Pay : legal_contract.signed
records.description: Signed contract in CLM triggers PO creation in S2P. Low friction when the CLM and S2P stack are integrated under a single suite, higher when separate.

records.handoff_label: Source-to-Pay → SaaS Management Platforms : po.saas_subscription_created
records.description: PO for a SaaS subscription creates the corresponding subscription record in SMP. Friction sits in matching the PO line items to a known SaaS app in the SMP catalog; new vendors require manual creation.

records.handoff_label: SaaS Management Platforms → Contract Lifecycle Management : renewal.30_day_warning
records.description: SMP's renewal-watch surfaces a 30-day expiry warning to CLM so the contract document workflow (amendment, renegotiation) can start in time.

records.handoff_label: SaaS Management Platforms → Source-to-Pay : seat_demand.exceeded
records.description: When SaaS usage forecasts predict seat-count overrun before renewal, SMP triggers a mid-term expansion requisition in S2P to add seats proactively (avoiding emergency procurement at over-pricing).

records.handoff_label: Contract Lifecycle Management → SaaS Management Platforms : legal_contract.renewed
records.description: Renewed SaaS contract in CLM updates the corresponding subscription in SMP with new term, new seat count, new pricing.

records.handoff_label: Discovery and Service Mapping → SaaS Management Platforms : sso_login.unsanctioned_app
records.description: SSO logs reveal a login to a SaaS app that's not in the sanctioned catalog — flagged as shadow IT. Complements the EXPENSE-side detection: SSO catches apps that use corporate SSO but aren't tracked; expense catches credit-card paid apps that don't.

records.handoff_label: Discovery and Service Mapping → Configuration Management Database : ci.discovered
records.description: Discovered devices reconcile against the existing CMDB and either match (update existing CI), promote (create new CI), or queue for manual review (ambiguous match). Low friction when DISCOVERY and CMDB are same-vendor; medium otherwise.
records.notes: source NULL until DISCOVERY is modularized

records.handoff_label: Discovery and Service Mapping → Configuration Management Database : relationship.discovered
records.description: Discovered relationships (network flows, dependencies, k8s service-mesh edges) feed the CI relationship graph. Friction is medium — relationship discovery is noisier than device discovery, and pruning false-positive edges requires class-aware rules.
records.notes: source NULL until DISCOVERY is modularized

records.handoff_label: Discovery and Service Mapping → IT Operations Management : monitoring_policy.coverage_requested
records.description: New CI from DISCOVERY auto-binds to a class-default monitoring policy in ITOM. Friction sits in the class-to-policy mapping, which drifts as policies evolve.

records.handoff_label: Configuration Management Database → IT Service Management : ci.unauthorized_change_detected
records.description: Configuration drift against a CI baseline (or change without a CAB-approved change record) creates a compliance / security incident in ITSM. Friction is medium — false positives from legitimate-but-unrecorded operational tweaks are common.

records.handoff_label: IT Operations Management → AIOps : events.burst_detected
records.description: Bursts of related events in the ITOM stream are pushed to AIOPS for correlation; AIOPS emits a correlation back. The primary data path for the IT-ops noise-reduction pipeline.

records.handoff_label: Observability → IT Operations Management : monitoring_alert.threshold_breached
records.description: OBS-side alerts (from metric thresholds, log patterns, trace anomalies) are mirrored into the ITOM event/alert stream so AIOPS and ITSM see them in the unified pipeline. Modern stacks make this near-trivial.

records.handoff_label: Observability → IT Service Management : slo.breached
records.description: SLO breach (error budget exhausted, burn-rate spike) creates an incident in ITSM. High friction in practice, the routing from an OBS-side SLO-breach event to a correctly assigned ITSM incident is rarely turnkey, especially when the SLO-owning team and the incident-handling team differ.

records.handoff_label: Observability → AIOps : anomaly_candidate.detected
records.description: OBS-detected anomalies (metric-shape deviations, latency-distribution shifts) feed AIOPS correlation as candidate inputs.

records.handoff_label: AIOps → IT Service Management : correlation.identified
records.description: A correlated alert cluster surfaces as ONE incident in ITSM instead of N. The defining noise-reduction promise of AIOps — and the hardest integration to land cleanly, because suppressing the underlying alerts requires bidirectional state with ITOM, and ITSM needs to expose the correlated-events bundle as evidence on the incident.

records.handoff_label: AIOps → IT Service Management : root_cause.identified
records.description: Confirmed RCA seeds an ITSM problem record (the long-lived root-cause artifact) and links it to the incident(s) that triggered it. Friction sits in the human-in-the-loop confirmation step — most AIOps RCAs need analyst sign-off before they reach problem-management.

records.handoff_label: AIOps → IT Operations Management : monitoring_event.suppression_applied
records.description: AIOPS-learned noise-suppression rules feed back to ITOM to prune events at the source, reducing pipeline cost. Low friction because the feedback is rule-based and well-bounded.

records.handoff_label: Marketing Automation → Customer Relationship Management : crm_lead.qualified
records.description: MA-driven scoring crosses the MQL threshold; the lead routes to CRM with a recommended owner. Friction comes from definition drift — what counts as MQL, who owns routing, what happens to disqualified leads — and from the lead-to-contact-to-opportunity conversion chain inside CRM.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Configure-Price-Quote : crm_opportunity.requires_quote
records.description: Opportunity reaches the proposal stage; CPQ generates a configured quote (product mix, discount structure, term). Friction sits in product-catalog sync between CRM and CPQ and in approval workflows for non-standard pricing.

records.handoff_label: Configure-Price-Quote → Contract Lifecycle Management : quote.accepted
records.description: Accepted quote hands off to CLM for contract authoring — pulls in clause language, populates the agreed terms, routes for signature.

records.handoff_label: Contract Lifecycle Management → Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management : legal_contract.signed
records.description: Signed contract creates the customer subscription in SUB-MGMT: plan, term, MRR/ARR, billing cadence, seat count, start date. The 'order-to-active' moment.

records.handoff_label: Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management → Customer Relationship Management : subscription.activated
records.description: Subscription activation marks the account as an active customer in CRM, updates ARR rollups, and unlocks customer-success workflows. Low friction when same-vendor stack; medium when CRM and billing are separate.

records.handoff_label: Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management → Customer Service Management : subscription.activated
records.description: Subscription activation creates the matching customer_entitlements record in CSM: tier mapped to support level, named contacts seeded, SLA targets bound. Friction sits in mapping subscription plan SKUs to support tiers, which is rarely 1:1.

records.handoff_label: Digital Commerce → Customer Relationship Management : customer.signed_up
records.description: Storefront signup creates the canonical customer record in CRM. Low friction in B2C-native integrated stacks; medium in stitched-together stacks.

records.handoff_label: Digital Commerce → Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management : order.subscription_purchase
records.description: Storefront order containing a subscription SKU creates the customer_subscription in SUB-MGMT, bypassing the CPQ/CLM path used for B2B deals.

records.handoff_label: Customer Data Platform → Customer Relationship Management : profile.lifecycle_changed
records.description: CDP-detected lifecycle stage change (new → engaged → loyal → at-risk → churned) updates the customer record in CRM. Friction comes from CDP's lifecycle model not matching CRM's account-status taxonomy.

records.handoff_label: Marketing Automation → Customer Data Platform : marketing_campaign.engagement_recorded
records.description: Marketing engagement events (email open, click, content view, form submission) feed CDP for profile enrichment and segment recomputation.

records.handoff_label: Customer Service Management → Customer Relationship Management : case.critical_health_drop
records.description: Cluster of critical cases or sustained low CSAT triggers an account-health-drop signal back to CRM, surfacing as a churn-risk flag on the account. High friction because the threshold definition is org-specific and the CRM-side account-health field rarely has good UX for the alert.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Customer Service Management : crm_opportunity.closed_won
records.description: Closed-won opportunity in CRM triggers entitlement provisioning in CSM ahead of (or in parallel to) subscription activation in SUB-MGMT. Important for fast onboarding of high-touch customers.

records.handoff_label: Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management → Customer Service Management : payment.failed
records.description: Payment failure opens a customer-success case in CSM for proactive intervention — distinct from automated dunning emails, this is the human-touch path for higher-value accounts.

records.handoff_label: Customer Service Management → Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management : case.churn_risk_detected
records.description: CSM-side churn-risk detection (case patterns, low CSAT, low product usage) feeds back to SUB-MGMT to influence dunning treatment, retention offers, and renewal forecasting. High friction because the churn-risk model rarely lives in SUB-MGMT's data model, requiring an event-driven adapter.

records.handoff_label: Marketing Automation → Customer Data Platform : marketing_campaign.event_recorded
records.description: Campaign delivery, open, click, bounce, and unsubscribe events flow from MA to CDP for unified event-stream aggregation. Low friction because event-stream ingestion is exactly what CDP tools are built for.

records.handoff_label: Digital Commerce → Customer Data Platform : storefront.interaction
records.description: Storefront events (page view, product view, add-to-cart, checkout, return, search) flow from commerce to CDP for behavioral profile enrichment and segment recomputation.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Customer Data Platform : crm_opportunity.stage_changed
records.description: Opportunity-stage transitions and sales-activity events flow from CRM to CDP. Friction sits in the identity match — CRM contacts must reconcile to CDP-resolved customer profiles, which is not always 1:1.

records.handoff_label: Customer Service Management → Customer Data Platform : case.created
records.description: Case lifecycle events (created, escalated, resolved, CSAT received) flow from CSM to CDP so the unified profile reflects support interactions. Friction is medium — case identifiers need to resolve to the CDP profile, and case context (severity, root cause) needs schema mapping.

records.handoff_label: Customer Data Platform → Marketing Automation : segment.activated
records.description: CDP-defined segment activates into MA for campaign targeting. Friction sits in segment-definition portability — what CDP calls 'high-value-active' may not map cleanly to MA's list-and-criteria model, requiring sync logic.

records.handoff_label: Customer Data Platform → Sales Engagement : high_intent_signal.detected
records.description: CDP-detected high-intent signal (pricing-page revisits, integration-doc views, competitor-comparison engagement) triggers cadence enrollment in SALES-ENG so reps reach out at the right moment. High friction: the intent signal is probabilistic, the cadence enrollment rules are rep-team-specific, and the systems have very different data models. The marquee 'intent data → outreach' handoff that powers modern outbound.

records.handoff_label: Customer Data Platform → Digital Commerce : segment.activated
records.description: Segment activation drives personalized storefront experience: which products surface, which banners show, what discount tier applies. Friction is medium — real-time segment evaluation at storefront render-time is non-trivial latency-wise.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Sales Engagement : crm_opportunity.assigned
records.description: New opportunity assignment in CRM auto-enrolls the contact in the appropriate cadence in SALES-ENG. Friction sits in cadence-selection rules (which cadence for which deal type, region, segment) which drift faster than the integration code.

records.handoff_label: Sales Engagement → Customer Relationship Management : call.completed
records.description: Completed calls (and their disposition, duration, recording link) log to the CRM activity timeline. Low friction because activity-sync is a core SALES-ENG ↔ CRM integration that vendors invest in heavily.

records.handoff_label: Sales Engagement → Customer Relationship Management : deal_insight.captured
records.description: Conversation-intelligence-extracted insight (competitor mentioned, pricing objection, decision-maker identified, commitment made) updates the opportunity record in CRM — fields, custom flags, risk score. Friction comes from rep adoption of the AI-suggested fields, not the integration itself.

records.handoff_label: Marketing Automation → Customer Relationship Management : nurture.completed
records.description: Nurture journey completion (whether successful conversion or exit) updates lead status in CRM. Low friction in same-vendor all-in-one stacks; medium when MA and CRM are separate.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Marketing Automation : crm_contact.synced
records.description: Contact updates in CRM (new contact, status change, opt-in change, account ownership) sync to MA so audience lists and campaigns stay current. Batch-sync is the typical pattern — real-time would be ideal but most stacks accept hourly or daily latency here.

records.handoff_label: Social Media Management → Customer Service Management : social_message.received
records.description: Inbound social message (comment, DM, mention-reply) classified as a service issue (complaint, order question, technical problem) triggers case creation in CSM with the message payload, customer context (if resolvable), and channel metadata. Failure modes: classifier misfires flood the CSM queue with non-service items; social-handle-to-customer-record reconciliation is unreliable across networks; cases reopened in CSM rarely sync back to the originating SMM thread, fragmenting conversation history.
records.notes: Probabilistic-signal-becomes-deterministic-action pattern; aggravated by identity reconciliation across handle namespaces.

records.handoff_label: Social Media Management → Customer Service Management : social_mention.detected
records.description: Listening pipeline detects a brand/product mention with negative sentiment or high reach off-channel (Reddit thread, Twitter complaint without @mention, review-site post) and routes it to CSM for proactive outreach. Failure modes: sentiment classification false positives consume agent time; off-channel mentions rarely include a resolvable customer identity; coordination with PR/comms is manual.
records.notes: Off-channel companion to social_message.received; same probabilistic-signal shape but without an inbox conversation to reply into.

records.handoff_label: Social Media Management → Customer Relationship Management : social_lead.captured
records.description: Social interaction with explicit intent, DM asking pricing, click-through on a lead-gen form, message-ad reply, converts into a CRM-mastered lead with handle, captured form data, and source attribution. Failure modes: handle-to-existing-contact reconciliation produces duplicate leads; form-data quality from social lead-gen ads is inconsistent across networks.
records.notes: Identity-reconciliation pattern; usually well-supported by MA-to-CRM connectors but quality is uneven.

records.handoff_label: Social Media Management → Customer Data Platform : social_engagement.recorded
records.description: Social engagement events (likes, shares, comments, video-view depth, story interactions, profile visits) stream to CDP to enrich the unified customer profile with behavioral signals across channels. Failure modes: identity reconciliation across per-network handle namespaces is unreliable; many engagement events lack a resolvable user; cross-platform deduplication of the same person is hard.
records.notes: Identity-reconciliation pattern at scale; the single biggest CDP-enrichment headache in the social stack.

records.handoff_label: Social Media Management → Marketing Automation : influencer_campaign.completed
records.description: Completed influencer-marketing campaign performance (reach, engagement, conversions, earned media value, content samples) feeds back from the influencer tool to MA campaign attribution and ROI reporting. Failure modes: cross-vendor schemas don't align on attribution windows; influencer-driven conversions are hard to attribute deterministically; payout reconciliation is often manual.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack pattern, the influencer module is rarely part of the MA platform; lossy aggregation common.

records.handoff_label: Social Media Management → Marketing Automation : social_post.published
records.description: Published social post tied to a multi-channel campaign in MA emits a publish event with channel, post URL, and tracked UTM parameters so MA can attribute downstream conversions to the campaign. Failure modes: campaign-id mapping between SMM tool and MA platform is brittle; UTM consistency depends on author discipline; engagement data from the social network arrives on a different cadence than the publish event.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack pattern; weakest of the six handoffs — implementation-dependent and bypassable in single-vendor stacks.

records.handoff_label: Headless Content Management → Digital Experience Platform : content_entry.published
records.description: HCMS publishes a content entry; DXP must re-render the affected pages, invalidate its CDN cache, or trigger an ISR rebuild. Payload typically includes content_type, entry_id, locale, and changed fields. Low friction when DXP and HCMS are the same vendor's integrated stack; bespoke and medium-friction when HCMS and DXP are from different vendors.

records.handoff_label: Headless Content Management → Digital Commerce : content_entry.published
records.description: Storefront refreshes product copy, banner content, or marketing pages when CMS publishes. Common in composable-commerce stacks pairing a headless commerce engine with a headless CMS. Failure modes: stale storefront caches when the webhook silently fails; mis-localized content when the storefront's locale resolution diverges from the CMS's.

records.handoff_label: Headless Content Management → Marketing Automation : content_entry.published
records.description: Marketing-Automation campaigns reference content snippets, hero copy, and CTAs that live in the CMS, but the link between a CMS entry and a campaign template is rarely event-driven. Marketers manually copy CMS content into the MA email/SMS template; CMS-side changes after the campaign is built don't propagate. Shadow-data pattern: the campaign's content of record diverges silently from the CMS source.

records.handoff_label: Headless Content Management → Digital Experience Platform : content_release.scheduled
records.description: Scheduled CMS release triggers a build pipeline ahead of go-live time so the rendered frontend is ready when the release publishes. SSG/ISR build kickoff via webhook. Failure modes: build pipeline runs against partial release content; release time changes don't re-trigger the build.

records.handoff_label: Headless Content Management → Digital Commerce : content_release.published
records.description: Coordinated go-live of a content release and commerce changes (new collection launch, pricing campaign). The release event fans out to the storefront which invalidates caches and refreshes catalog-adjacent content. Friction increases when the commerce platform's content cache TTL is uncoordinated with the release window.

records.handoff_label: Headless Content Management → Digital Experience Platform : content_type.changed
records.description: Field renames, type changes, or removals on content_types break frontend renderers that are coupled to the schema. Typically handled through dev coordination (PR + deploy) rather than event-driven propagation. Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity pattern: the CMS schema and the frontend's TypeScript types must move together but live in different repos / different vendor tools.

records.handoff_label: Digital Asset Management → Headless Content Management : digital_asset.published
records.description: DAM publishes an approved asset; HCMS authors need the asset to appear in their picker for inclusion in content entries. Integration typically resolves asset URLs at content delivery time, so DAM URL rotation, taxonomy renames, or rights-revocations break already-published HCMS entries downstream. Identity-reconciliation pattern: same asset, different identifier spaces across DAM and HCMS, no canonical resolver in most stacks.

records.handoff_label: Payroll Management → Core ERP Financial Management : pay_cycle.posted
records.description: Pay run closure produces decomposed GL postings (gross wages debit by cost_center / earning_code; employer tax + benefits accrual; net pay credit to cash clearing) that flow to ERP-FIN. Canonical payroll-to-finance handoff. Failure modes: unmapped earning_codes; cost_center mid-cycle reorgs; multi-entity intercompany cost allocations.
