records.handoff_label: Payroll Management → Benefits Administration : pay_cycle.closed
records.description: Per-employee deduction totals reconciled against active benefit_enrollments to detect election drift. Discrepancies require manual carrier_feed correction and retro-pay calculation.

records.handoff_label: Payroll Management → Expense Management : expense.reimbursable
records.description: Approved expense_reports flagged for payroll reimbursement (rather than card-cleared) feed into the next pay_run as a non-taxable earning_code.

records.handoff_label: Payroll Management → People Analytics : pay_cycle.closed
records.description: Closed pay_run cohort feeds people-analytics pay-equity, total-rewards, and labor-cost analyses.

records.handoff_label: Workforce Management → Payroll Management : pay_period.closed
records.description: Approved time_entries flow to PAYROLL as the source of variable-pay hours. Failure modes: late approvals trigger retro pay; rounded vs unrounded reconciliation; multi-WFM/multi-PAYROLL stacks with worker-id misalignment.

records.handoff_label: Workforce Management → Professional Services Automation : time_entry.approved
records.description: Project-tagged time_entries feed PSA for utilization and billable-hours calculation.

records.handoff_label: Compensation Management → Payroll Management : merit_cycle.approved
records.description: Approved merit, bonus, and equity refresh values become effective-dated pay-rate changes and one-time payments in payroll. Cycle-close timing must align with pay_run boundaries; mid-cycle promotions arrive as off-cycle adjustments.
records.notes: target_domain_module_id left NULL: tie: 2 modules at role consumer.

records.handoff_label: Compensation Management → Human Capital Management : merit_cycle.approved
records.description: Cycle-close pay-rate changes post to the worker record (base salary, bonus target, equity guideline).

records.handoff_label: Compensation Management → People Analytics : merit_cycle.closed
records.description: Cycle-close dataset feeds pay-equity gap analysis and compa-ratio distribution analytics.

records.handoff_label: Benefits Administration → Payroll Management : enrollment.changed
records.description: Election change (life event or open-enrollment) triggers mid-cycle deduction adjustment in payroll. Failure modes: retro adjustments crossing pay-period boundaries; tax-treatment changes (pre-tax vs post-tax) requiring W-2 corrections.
records.notes: target_domain_module_id left NULL: tie: 2 modules at role consumer.

records.handoff_label: Benefits Administration → Core ERP Financial Management : enrollment.changed
records.description: Employer-side benefit cost accrual posts to GL as part of personnel-cost rollup.

records.handoff_label: Benefits Administration → Payroll Management : benefit_open_enrollment.closed
records.description: Open-enrollment close produces large carrier_feed batches (834 EDI) plus mass payroll deduction-code updates. Identity-reconciliation pattern: per-carrier member-id schemes diverge from HRIS employee-id; failure modes are silent coverage gaps discovered weeks later.
records.notes: Corrected 2026-05-26 audit: was wired to stale trigger 82 (open_enrollment.closed mis-pointed at benefit_carriers). Re-pointed to event 420, source module BEN-PLAN-DESIGN (71), payload benefit_enrollments (147).

records.handoff_label: Learning Management → Talent Management : learner_certification.earned
records.description: Cert / course completion updates the worker skill_profile (Skills Cloud), which feeds talent-mobility matching and succession bench analysis. Friction: cross-vendor LMS↔TALENT stacks have brittle skill-taxonomy reconciliation.

records.handoff_label: Talent Management → Compensation Management : calibration.complete
records.description: Calibrated performance ratings feed the merit_recommendation matrix at cycle planning. Failure modes: cycle-cadence mismatch (annual review vs semi-annual merit); late calibration delays merit cycle.

records.handoff_label: Employee Experience and Engagement → People Analytics : survey.cycle_closed
records.description: Cycle-close driver scores feed people-analytics cohorts for cross-cutting analyses (engagement × attrition, engagement × DEI, engagement × performance).

records.handoff_label: Employee Experience and Engagement → Human Capital Management : attrition_risk.high
records.description: Attrition-risk inference from engagement signals surfaces to managers via HCM dashboards. Probabilistic-signal → deterministic-action pattern: a risk score is not a directive; intervention is gated by manager judgment, data-privacy rules (anonymity floor), and DEI-bias concerns.
records.notes: B10b tie resolution: trigger_events.data_object_id=employees is embedded_master on both EMP-EXP modules. attrition_risk.high is derived from survey_responses + engagement_drivers analysis, so CONTINUOUS-LISTEN is the signal publisher.

records.handoff_label: Vendor Management System → Source-to-Pay : pm_work_order.invoiced
records.description: Approved contingent_timesheets × rate_cards produce contingent_invoices that flow into S2P / AP-AUTO for three-way match and payment to the staffing supplier.

records.handoff_label: Vendor Management System → Human Capital Management : worker.tenure_threshold
records.description: Contingent worker crossing co-employment-risk tenure threshold (typically 18-24 months) must be reclassified, off-boarded, or converted. Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity: VMS and HCM rarely share identity; the watch-list is built by exception report and processed manually.

records.handoff_label: HR Service Delivery → Identity Governance and Administration : case.access_required
records.description: HR cases requiring app or system access (e.g. role change, special-project access) escalate to IGA. Identity-reconciliation pattern: HR case context (employee_id, role, department) must map to IGA identity-graph keys; cross-vendor stacks lack canonical resolver.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Benefits Administration : job_offer.accepted
records.description: Offer acceptance opens the new-hire benefit-enrollment window in BEN-ADMIN, gated by the actual employee.created event from HCM.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Compensation Management : job_offer.signed
records.description: Offer signature instantiates the new-hire compensation plan (base, target bonus, equity grant, sign-on) in COMP-MGMT.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Benefits Administration : employee.terminated
records.description: Termination triggers COBRA event handling in BEN-ADMIN (US) or local statutory leaver process. Failure modes: late termination dates cause overpayment of employer premium.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Compensation Management : employee.promoted
records.description: Promotion event triggers off-cycle compensation review (eligibility, band placement, increase recommendation) in COMP-MGMT.

records.handoff_label: Core ERP Financial Management → Enterprise Performance Management : payroll_period.closed
records.description: Period close pushes actual personnel cost into EPM for variance reporting against headcount_plans and workforce_cost_projections.

records.handoff_label: Accounts Payable Automation → Core ERP Financial Management : payment_run.executed
records.description: Payment run produces cash_transactions and clearing journal_entries that post to ERP-FIN GL.

records.handoff_label: Accounts Payable Automation → Core ERP Financial Management : supplier_invoice.matched
records.description: Three-way match success posts the supplier invoice to AP subledger; exceptions queue for review.

records.handoff_label: Supplier Lifecycle Management → Source-to-Pay : supplier.approved
records.description: Supplier onboarding completion makes the supplier eligible for sourcing events and purchase orders.

records.handoff_label: Supplier Lifecycle Management → Accounts Payable Automation : supplier.bank_changed
records.description: Supplier bank-account changes carry significant fraud risk; identity-reconciliation pattern. Strong vendor-master controls and out-of-band verification gate the propagation to AP-AUTO.

records.handoff_label: Expense Management → Core Financial Management : expense_report.approved
records.description: Approved expense_reports post accrual journal_entries to ERP-FIN; reimbursement routed via AP or payroll based on policy.

records.handoff_label: Expense Management → Accounts Payable Automation : expense_report.approved
records.description: Expense reimbursement via AP rather than payroll: the approved expense_report becomes a supplier_invoice paid in the next payment_run.

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Core ERP Financial Management : revenue.recognised
records.description: Project rev-rec posts to GL via journal_entries; percentage-of-completion or milestone trigger dependent.
records.notes: target NULL until ERP-FIN declares consumer DMDO on `revenue_recognition_records`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Source-to-Pay : service_project.staffing_required
records.description: Project staff-augmentation demand triggers a contingent-worker requisition routed through S2P / VMS.
records.notes: target NULL until S2P declares consumer DMDO on `purchase_requisitions`

records.handoff_label: Core ERP Financial Management → Enterprise Performance Management : accounting_period.closed
records.description: Period close pushes actuals into EPM for variance analysis against budgets / forecasts / scenarios. Mapping between GL accounts and planning hierarchies often drifts cycle-to-cycle.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Workforce Management : employee.created
records.description: New employee provisioned in HCM becomes a schedulable resource in WFM — identity, position, base FTE. Mid-shift onboarding and badge-binding are typical edge cases.
records.notes: target_domain_module_id NULL until WFM is modularized (Phase-M gap on target domain; SKILL.md authoring rule).

records.handoff_label: Workforce Management → Human Capital Management : absence.approved
records.description: Approved absence_requests update PTO balances in HCM; tenure-based accruals and country-specific carry-over rules apply (US PTO, UK statutory, German Urlaub, French Congés Payés).

records.handoff_label: Workforce Management → Strategic Workforce Planning : actuals.posted
records.description: Period actuals from WFM feed Strategic Workforce Planning plan-vs-actual. Coding mismatches between WFM cost-centers and SWP plan units cause reconciliation pain.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Professional Services Automation : crm_opportunity.closed_won
records.description: Closed-Won deal triggers PSA project creation. High friction: deal terms in the opportunity rarely map cleanly to scope, staffing, and milestones; manual transcription is common (cross-vendor stack shape — CRM and PSA are typically different vendors).

records.handoff_label: Contract Lifecycle Management → Professional Services Automation : legal_contract.signed
records.description: Signed SOW seeds PSA project scope, billing terms, and milestone schedule. Deviations between contract terms and operational project structure require manual reconciliation.

records.handoff_label: Expense Management → Professional Services Automation : expense.approved
records.description: Project-tagged expense_reports flow to PSA for T&E billing rollup and project cost. Project-code errors and late corrections are recurring pain.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → IT Service Management : monitoring_alert.threshold_breached
records.description: RMM agent telemetry breaches a monitoring policy threshold and the alert is forwarded to ITSM to auto-create an incident with affected endpoint, telemetry snapshot, and severity. Failure modes: alert-to-ticket bridges across different vendors break on auth/throttling/schema drift; threshold rules drift between systems; duplicate-alert suppression in one tool doesn't propagate to the other; closing the incident rarely closes the originating alert.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack pattern; the canonical RMM↔ITSM friction point.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → AIOps : monitoring_alert.threshold_breached
records.description: RMM alerts stream to an AIOps correlation engine for noise reduction, multi-source event correlation, and incident clustering before any ticket is created. Failure modes: enrichment lag between alert emission and AIOps consumption; correlation accuracy depends on consistent CI identifiers across RMM/ITOM/AIOps; back-channel closure rarely flows to RMM.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → IT Service Management : patch_job.scheduled
records.description: A scheduled patch job in RMM creates a corresponding change record in ITSM for CAB approval and audit trail. Failure modes: approval delays in ITSM don't gate RMM execution; emergency patch jobs bypass change-control by design and leave the change record stale.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → IT Service Management : patch_job.completed
records.description: Patch job completion updates the corresponding ITSM change record with per-endpoint execution result and closes it. Failure modes: partial-failure handling differs between tools; rollback events may not be reflected in the change history.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → Hardware Asset Management : hardware_endpoint.discovered
records.description: RMM agent installation on a new endpoint syncs hardware specs (CPU, RAM, disk, serial, BIOS) to the HAM asset register. Failure modes: identity reconciliation across RMM agent-id, HAM asset-tag, and CMDB CI-id is unreliable; VMs and ephemeral cloud instances create churn in HAM that doesn't map to a physical lifecycle.
records.notes: Identity-reconciliation pattern; same logical device in three identifier spaces.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → Software Asset Management : software_endpoint.discovered
records.description: RMM agent reports detected installed software per endpoint to SAM for entitlement reconciliation. Failure modes: normalization (publisher/product/version) varies between RMM tool dictionaries and SAM tool dictionaries, causing reconciliation gaps; metering data (last-used, frequency) is rarely included in the RMM payload.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → Configuration Management Database : ci_endpoint.discovered
records.description: RMM contributes CI attributes (OS, installed services, network config) to the CMDB. Failure modes: CMDB receives the same logical CI from multiple discovery sources (RMM, AD, agent-less scans, cloud APIs) with conflicting attribute values; reconciliation rules are CMDB-vendor-specific and rarely fully cover RMM's payload shape.
records.notes: source NULL until RMM is modularized

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → Discovery and Service Mapping : network_device.discovered
records.description: RMM-led SNMP/agent-led network scans push discovered (often unmanaged) devices to the broader DISCOVERY inventory. Failure modes: scan-coverage overlap with dedicated discovery tools creates duplicate device records; classification (printer vs switch vs IoT) is inconsistent across sources.

records.handoff_label: Hardware Asset Management → Remote Monitoring and Management : asset.retired
records.description: A hardware asset retired/disposed in HAM should trigger RMM agent uninstall and license release to avoid orphaned agents continuing to phone home and consume seats. Failure modes: classic leaver-pattern friction — the 'going away' event reliably reaches HAM but doesn't reliably reach RMM; orphan agents accumulate; per-endpoint billing inflates.
records.notes: Leaver / cancellation recall pattern; structural friction across the IT-ops cluster.

records.handoff_label: Data and AI Platform → Business Intelligence and Analytics : semantic_metric.published
records.description: A metric defined in the platform's semantic layer is published for BI consumption. Each downstream BI tool re-imports or re-models the metric in its own semantic format; definitions drift, names collide, and the same metric name ends up disagreeing across BI tools even when both originated in the same platform metric. Identity reconciliation across systems pattern.
records.notes: Convergence is partially solved within single-vendor stacks but breaks at vendor boundaries.

records.handoff_label: Data and AI Platform → Data Catalog and Governance : data_product.published
records.description: A new data product is published on the platform: schema, owner, SLA, lineage. The enterprise data catalog needs to register it, attach glossary terms, surface stewardship workflows, and propagate lineage upstream. Lineage formats differ per platform (OpenLineage, proprietary), enterprise catalogs maintain their own model; sync is bespoke. Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity pattern.
records.notes: Open standards (OpenLineage, Iceberg metadata, Polaris) are reducing this friction but most enterprises still hand-roll the bridge.

records.handoff_label: Data and AI Platform → Conversational AI : ai_agent.deployed
records.description: An AI agent built on the platform is deployed and needs to be exposed via a conversational-AI surface (assistant copilots, CRM-embedded agents, contact-center bots, custom chatbot front-ends). The agent's tools, retrieval indexes, and guardrails sit on the platform; the channel surfaces (intent routing, conversation state, voice synthesis) sit in the conversational-AI vendor.
records.notes: Newer pattern; standards (MCP, ACP) are emerging in 2024–2025 but not yet universal.

records.handoff_label: Data and AI Platform → AIOps : pipeline_run.failed
records.description: A platform pipeline run fails or breaches its SLA. AIOps tooling needs the failure to correlate with infrastructure events, recent deployments, and downstream business impact. Today: pipelines emit Prometheus metrics or webhook events; AIOps tools ingest them but rarely have first-class understanding of pipeline semantics (lineage to consuming dashboards, SLA criticality).

records.handoff_label: Data and AI Platform → Master Data Management : golden_record.synced
records.description: Customer/supplier/product golden records mastered in the MDM hub are projected into the lakehouse as platform-side data products; conversely, the platform's analytical resolution often produces a higher-quality match than the operational MDM hub. Who's authoritative? Most enterprises end up with a bidirectional batch sync where neither side fully trusts the other. Cross-vendor stack with same logical entity pattern.
records.notes: Often the trigger for an MDM-modernization project that ends up moving golden-record mastery onto the platform itself.

records.handoff_label: Data and AI Platform → Data Quality : quality_check.failed
records.description: A platform-native quality check on a lakehouse table fails. The enterprise DQ tool needs the finding to feed its central scorecard and ticketing. Two parallel quality systems exist; reconciliation is manual or via webhooks.

records.handoff_label: Data Integration → Data and AI Platform : replication_load.completed
records.description: A managed ingestion tool completes a load and signals the platform to refresh dependent pipelines and materializations. Mature pattern with first-class event integration in most lakehouse runtimes.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Data and AI Platform : access_policy.updated
records.description: An enterprise governance tool updates an access policy (tag-based, attribute-based, lineage-derived). The platform's native RBAC layer needs to enforce it. Policy syntax differs; not every governance assertion maps to a platform-native control; bridges are bespoke and drift over time. Identity reconciliation pattern in the access-control axis.
records.notes: Standards (OpenPolicyAgent, ABAC profiles in lakehouses) reduce but don't eliminate the friction.

records.handoff_label: Remote Monitoring and Management → MSP Professional Services Automation : monitoring_alert.threshold_breached
records.description: RMM monitoring alert breaches a policy threshold and creates an MSP-PSA ticket in the affected customer's queue, with telemetry snapshot, endpoint context, and SLA-aware priority. Friction is lower than the RMM-to-ITSM equivalent in unified same-vendor MSP stacks but rises in cross-vendor MSP stacks.
records.notes: Same alert-to-ticket pattern as RMM→ITSM; native in unified vendor stacks, friction high in cross-vendor combinations.

records.handoff_label: MSP Professional Services Automation → Remote Access and Support : msp_ticket.escalated
records.description: Tier-1 ticket escalates to a remote-session need; technician launches the remote-control tool against the affected endpoint. Failure modes: ticket-to-endpoint mapping is hostname-based and breaks for shifting laptop names; session recording rarely auto-links back to the ticket.
records.notes: Parallel to ITSM→RMM ticket.escalated handoff.

records.handoff_label: MSP Professional Services Automation → Hardware Asset Management : ticket.created
records.description: New MSP ticket references a specific customer-owned asset; HAM (or the MSP's asset register equivalent) provides device metadata, warranty status, and asset history. Low-friction in unified stacks where assets are mastered inside the PSA itself.
records.notes: Most MSP PSAs include native asset registers — this handoff is internal in same-tool stacks but cross-domain when an external asset register is canonical.

records.handoff_label: Remote Access and Support → IT Service Management : support_session.completed
records.description: Completed remote session writes a session summary (duration, technician, actions taken, recording link) back to the originating ITSM incident as a work-note. Failure modes: ticket-id correlation is brittle when session was launched outside the ticket flow; recording links break when retention policy expires before the ticket closes.
records.notes: Strongest in same-vendor stacks; cross-vendor stacks rely on connector quality.

records.handoff_label: Remote Access and Support → MSP Professional Services Automation : msp_session.completed
records.description: Session duration should populate a billable time entry in MSP-PSA, but in cross-vendor MSP stacks technicians manually transcribe session minutes into the PSA. Failure modes: session minutes go unbilled, customer disputes arise over after-the-fact time entries, productivity reporting under-counts work.
records.notes: Classic time-tracking friction in cross-vendor MSP stacks; native in unified single-vendor MSP stacks.

records.handoff_label: Remote Access and Support → Governance, Risk and Compliance : session.recorded
records.description: Recorded sessions feed compliance evidence archives for PCI/HIPAA/SOX audits. Failure modes: retention-policy mismatch between RA tool and GRC archive; redaction obligations (passwords, PHI) inconsistently applied; chain-of-custody for evidence is rarely tamper-evident across systems.
records.notes: Only fires in regulated environments; GRC-domain dependency may not yet be loaded — script skips silently if target missing.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → Expense Management : card_transaction.posted
records.description: When the corporate-card platform is a different vendor from the expense-reimbursement system, settled card transactions must propagate to create expense report lines. Identifier mismatches (card_id vs employee_id), MCC remapping per chart-of-accounts, and timing drift (auth, posted, settled) routinely create duplicate or orphaned expense lines. High friction in mixed-vendor stacks; intra-platform when same vendor.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → Core ERP Financial Management : card_transaction.posted
records.description: Daily/weekly batch feeds card transactions to the GL with categorization mapping per chart-of-accounts; reconciliation against bank-feed at month-end. Mapping maintenance is the bulk of the integration work.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → Core ERP Financial Management : bill_payment.completed
records.description: Bill-pay completions create AP voucher and cash-disbursement entries in the GL; bank-feed reconciliation closes the loop. Manual touchpoints when payment fails or is reversed.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → Accounts Payable Automation : supplier_invoice.received
records.description: Large orgs frequently run SPEND-MGMT (non-PO bill pay) and AP-AUTO (PO-matched three-way-match) in parallel; the same supplier-issued invoice can arrive through either path. Duplicate-invoice detection across two systems with different identifier spaces and routing rules creates ongoing reconciliation burden. Cross-vendor stack pattern with same logical entity.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → Core ERP Financial Management : spend_request.approved
records.description: Approved pre-spend requests create commitment / encumbrance entries in the GL for budget tracking; later settled by the actual card_transaction or payment_run.

records.handoff_label: Source-to-Pay → Corporate Spend Management : vendor.added
records.description: New supplier records in S2P (with DUNS, tax IDs, bank details) must propagate to SPEND-MGMT for bill-pay payee setup. Different identifier spaces (internal vendor_id, DUNS, supplier_code) create duplicate vendor records and routing errors. Classic identity-reconciliation pattern.

records.handoff_label: Expense Management → Corporate Spend Management : expense_policy.updated
records.description: Policy changes authored in EXPENSE (per-category limits, prohibited MCCs, approver thresholds) must propagate to SPEND-MGMT real-time card-auth rules. Drift between submission-time checks and authorization-time checks leads to declined valid transactions or approved out-of-policy spend. Cross-vendor stack pattern with same logical entity.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → Enterprise Performance Management : spend_commitment.created
records.description: Committed and actual spend feeds EPM (FP&A platforms) for budget-vs-actual variance reporting at the department and cost-center level.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → Cloud Financial Operations : card_transaction.posted
records.description: Cloud-provider charges on corporate cards feed FINOPS for cost allocation across business units and projects. Bypasses the normal cloud-bill ingest path, requires merchant-side mapping to cloud account, and creates double-counting risk if both the card-side and bill-side flows are configured.

records.handoff_label: Corporate Spend Management → SaaS Management Platforms : card_transaction.posted
records.description: SaaS purchases on corporate cards reveal shadow IT to SMP — merchant categorization required to identify SaaS subscriptions vs other spend, then deduplicated against the existing SMP saas_subscription catalog. The card-side discovery path is the primary signal for off-procurement SaaS today. Shadow-data pattern.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Work Management : crm_opportunity.closed_won
records.description: Sales closes a deal in CRM; delivery / Customer Success spin up a kickoff project in their work-management tool. Custom iPaaS automations or hand-built webhooks bridge the two; payload mapping (opportunity products to project tasks, account stakeholders to project members) is bespoke per org.
records.notes: High-friction shape: cross-vendor stack with the same logical entity. Mainstream CRM platforms don't ship a canonical 'project from won opportunity' flow; every services-delivery org reinvents the bridge. Reusing existing trigger_event id 84.

records.handoff_label: Work Management → Strategic Portfolio Management : work_item.completed
records.description: Work-management platforms publish task-completion data to portfolio dashboards in SPM tools. The portfolio rollup powers strategy-to-execution dashboards and OKR progress (via okr_objectives.key_results linking down to work_items). Nightly sync is the common pattern; richer real-time integrations exist but are vendor-specific.
records.notes: Stable, bespoke integration per SPM/WORK-MGMT vendor pair. Friction medium because the dimensional mismatch (operational task → portfolio status) requires per-org mapping rules.

records.handoff_label: Work Management → IT Service Management : work_item.status_changed
records.description: Cross-functional WORK-MGMT items intersect with IT support requests: a marketing project task ('IT-provision new SaaS') needs to be linked to an ITSM request, with status mirrored both ways. Bidirectional sync is bespoke; off-the-shelf WORK-MGMT-to-ITSM connectors exist but require careful per-team configuration.
records.notes: High-friction shape: cross-vendor stack with the same logical work entity in two systems. Status-mapping mismatches between WORK-MGMT statuses and ITSM workflow states are the common breakage.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Work Management : okr_objective.created
records.description: Executive-level OKRs created in SPM (or in a slide deck, or an HCM perf system) need to cascade into team-level OKRs in the work-management tool. Almost universally manual: someone reads the corporate OKR and authors child OKRs in the WORK-MGMT goals module. The cascade gap is what dedicated OKR-platform vendors exist to close.
records.notes: High-friction shape: probabilistic-to-deterministic. Strategic OKRs are written narratively; team OKRs need to be measurable and assigned. The translation step has no canonical engine.

records.handoff_label: Work Management → Professional Services Automation : work_project.completed
records.description: Services orgs running delivery in WORK-MGMT close a project and need utilization, billable hours, and milestone-based revenue recognition to roll up into PSA. Nightly sync of project status + hours is the common pattern; richer real-time integration exists but is uncommon.
records.notes: Medium friction. Stable integration when both sides exist; the bigger issue is the small fraction of services orgs that run delivery in pure WORK-MGMT vs in an integrated PSA — most use PSA's native project module.

records.handoff_label: Business Process Architecture → Process Mining : process_model.published
records.description: BPA tool publishes a to-be process model; mining tool ingests it as the conformance baseline against event-log data. Payload: BPMN XML + variant metadata. Failure modes: schema drift between modeler and miner, missing activity-to-event mappings.

records.handoff_label: Business Process Architecture → Application Portfolio Management : capability_map.updated
records.description: Capability map changes invalidate APM application-to-capability heatmaps. Co-master friction: the same map exists on both sides with different lineage. Failure modes: out-of-sync versions, terminology drift between EA and Process Office, application bindings become stale.

records.handoff_label: Business Process Architecture → Application Portfolio Management : process_model.published
records.description: BPA tool publishes a process; EA tool maps applications that support it for TIME scoring. Payload: process metadata + linked capabilities. Failure modes: process owner mapping lags, capability bindings drift.

records.handoff_label: Process Mining → Business Process Architecture : conformance.deviation_detected
records.description: Mining tool detects significant conformance deviation against the published model; process owner is alerted to redesign. Today usually a human handoff (ticket, email, PowerPoint review). Failure modes: deviations ignored, root cause attribution unclear, redesign cycle takes months.

records.handoff_label: Business Process Architecture → Product Management : value_stream.bottleneck_identified
records.description: BPA-side value-stream analysis surfaces a delivery bottleneck; product management consumes for prioritization. Today: meetings + slides. Failure modes: priorities not adjusted, no closed loop back to the value-stream artifact.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Identity Governance and Administration : employee.terminated
records.description: Termination in HCM must immediately revoke identity access in IGA: disable account, remove group memberships, terminate app-level entitlements. Failure modes: contractor terminations not flowing (different HCM table); rehires confuse the de-provisioning idempotency; access lingers after termination is the canonical audit finding.
records.notes:
Leaver recall pattern: the going-away event is harder to catch than the arriving event because exits happen via many channels (resignation, RIF, contract end, no-show, death). HCM is the system of record but not always the first to know.

target_domain_module_id NULL until IGA is modularized (Phase-M gap on target domain; SKILL.md authoring rule).

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → IT Service Management : employee.terminated
records.description: Termination in HCM creates a fan-out of offboarding service requests in ITSM: workspace cleanup, mail-forwarding setup, equipment-return tracking, exit-interview scheduling. Failure modes: template tasks for new role types missing; tasks created against wrong assignee groups when org changed shortly before termination.
records.notes: Task fan-out pattern: a single trigger generates a workflow of per-template ITSM tickets. Each ticket is its own lifecycle but they share the termination correlation_id.

records.handoff_label: Compensation Management → Payroll Management : merit_cycle.approved
records.description: Approved merit cycle in COMP-MGMT must propagate new pay rates into PAYROLL before the next pay run. Failure modes: effective-date mismatches between COMP-MGMT planning calendar and PAYROLL pay-period calendar create retro adjustments; partial-cycle approvals (some managers signed off, some not) split the load across pay runs.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack shape: COMP-MGMT and PAYROLL frequently live in different vendors; employee identity sync is the friction.

records.handoff_label: Benefits Administration → Payroll Management : enrollment.changed
records.description: Benefit enrollment changes in BEN-ADMIN (open enrollment, life events, plan election changes) must update payroll deductions for the affected pay period. Failure modes: late-bound effective dates after pay-period close trigger retro deductions; carrier-confirmed enrollment changes lag the payroll feed.
records.notes: Same-stack low-friction pattern: BEN-ADMIN and PAYROLL typically share an HRIS suite, so the integration is native event-stream or batch with established mapping.

records.handoff_label: Core ERP Financial Management → Audit Management : journal_entry.posted
records.description: Every posted GL journal entry must flow into the audit log for forensic review and anomaly detection. Failure modes: high volume drowns the audit pipeline; backdated entries arrive after the audit-period close.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack pattern: ERP-FIN and AUDIT often live in different vendors; same logical entity (journal_entry) but different identifier spaces.

records.handoff_label: Core ERP Financial Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : journal_entry.posted
records.description: GRC consumes posted journal entries for SOX-style control testing (segregation-of-duties checks, threshold reviews, manual-journal scrutiny). Batched nightly for testing; not real-time.
records.notes: One event, many subscribers: AUDIT and GRC subscribe to the same journal_entry.posted event with different downstream effects.

records.handoff_label: Accounts Payable Automation → Core ERP Financial Management : supplier_invoice.duplicate_detected
records.description: AP-AUTO duplicate-detection routes flagged invoices to the AP controller via ERP-FIN's exception queue. Failure modes: false positives drown the queue; legitimate duplicates from supplier portals get auto-paid before the alert lands.
records.notes: Exception/alert pattern: loose coupling, no feedback loop. Controller resolves outside the source domain.

records.handoff_label: Accounts Payable Automation → Core ERP Financial Management : payment.exception
records.description: Bank rejections, account closures, ACH returns, and routing errors during a payment run land here. ERP-FIN must reverse the cash posting and re-queue the invoice; AR side may need notification if the failed payment was a customer refund.
records.notes: High-friction: payment exceptions require manual disposition; SLA-sensitive (supplier relations).

records.handoff_label: Accounts Payable Automation → Customer Service Management : payment.exception
records.description: Customer-facing refund payment failures need CSM awareness so the customer can be contacted before they discover the missing refund themselves.
records.notes: One event, many subscribers: ERP-FIN takes the accounting action; CSM takes the customer-comm action.

records.handoff_label: Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management → Customer Service Management : dunning.escalation
records.description: Dunning sequence escalation (retry count, days-overdue, severity tier) triggers CSM retention or collections handoff. Failure modes: CSM doesn't know when to stop dunning a strategic-customer for relationship reasons; collections double-contacts after CSM intervention.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack: SUB-MGMT and CSM often distinct platforms; loose coupling causes contact-cadence collisions.

records.handoff_label: Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management → Customer Service Management : subscription.renewal_required
records.description: Subscriptions entering the renewal window (90 days from term-end by default) must surface in CSM for the renewal motion. Failure modes: auto-renew customers slip through CSM's view; multi-product subscriptions have staggered terms.
records.notes: Calendar-driven; same-stack low-friction if SUB-MGMT and CSM share a vendor.

records.handoff_label: Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management → Customer Relationship Management : subscription.downgraded
records.description: Downgrades are churn-risk signals: lower tier, fewer seats, removed modules. CRM needs the opportunity record reopened for expansion replan; CSM needs to run retention motion.
records.notes: Going-away pattern: downgrades are harder to catch than upgrades because they arrive via many channels (in-app, support ticket, contractual amendment).

records.handoff_label: Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management → Core ERP Financial Management : revenue.recognised
records.description: SUB-MGMT computes revenue recognition under ASC 606 (or equivalent) and feeds resulting GL entries to ERP-FIN. Failure modes: rev-rec timing differences between SUB-MGMT and ERP-FIN close calendars; deferred-revenue reclassifications create suspense entries.
records.notes: Period/cycle-close pattern: tight timing coupling around month-end.

records.handoff_label: Cloud Financial Operations → Source-to-Pay : cloud_spend.threshold_breached
records.description: Cloud-provider spend has exceeded a configured threshold (per-account, per-service, monthly). Procurement needs to engage for commitment-discount conversations; finance leadership needs visibility for forecast adjustment.
records.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic pattern: spike detection is heuristic, action is binding (commit dollars).

records.handoff_label: Enterprise Performance Management → Audit Management : financial_forecast.refreshed
records.description: Refreshed forecast feeds into the audit trail for forecast-accuracy review and as input to management-review documentation. Failure modes: forecast versions proliferate (top-down, bottom-up, scenario variants); audit needs the single authoritative version.
records.notes: Multiple-version pattern: forecast.refreshed fires for every scenario refresh; audit needs filter by official version flag.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Sales Engagement : crm_lead.scored_above_threshold
records.description: A lead's predictive score has crossed the qualified-handoff threshold; SALES-ENG picks up for cadence enrollment. Failure modes: noisy scoring causes cadence whiplash; threshold tuned per segment but not surfaced.
records.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic shape: scoring is heuristic, action is binding (enroll in cadence).

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Revenue Intelligence : crm_opportunity.closed_lost
records.description: Closed-lost opportunities feed REV-INTEL for win-loss analysis. Failure modes: rep-entered loss reasons are free-text and inconsistent; lost-then-revived deals double-count.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack: REV-INTEL is often a distinct platform; identifier reconciliation is messy.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Sales Performance Management : crm_opportunity.created
records.description: New opportunities feed pipeline quota tracking in SALES-PERF. Failure modes: rep-attribution edge cases (transfers, team deals).
records.notes: Same-stack low-friction if SALES-PERF lives inside the CRM.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Sales Performance Management : account.tier_changed
records.description: Account tier changes trigger territory or quota realignment. Failure modes: mid-quarter changes invalidate existing assignments; commission impact is retroactive.
records.notes: Period-coupling shape: tier changes are felt at quota recalculation boundaries.

records.handoff_label: Configure-Price-Quote → Customer Relationship Management : quote.expired
records.description: Expired quotes need rep follow-up to re-engage or re-quote. Failure modes: silent expiry; reps unaware until customer escalates.
records.notes: Calendar-driven low-friction.

records.handoff_label: Sales Engagement → Customer Relationship Management : sales_cadence.completed
records.description: Completed cadences signal an opportunity stage check. Failure modes: cadence completion without engagement should mark for nurture, not advance.
records.notes: Tight loop: SALES-ENG → CRM are typically same-vendor.

records.handoff_label: Sales Engagement → Customer Relationship Management : meeting.no_show
records.description: Missed meetings flag opportunity stage-back or extra cadence iteration. Failure modes: false no-shows from calendar timezone errors; rep-side reschedules not captured.
records.notes: Engagement-data quality issue.

records.handoff_label: Revenue Intelligence → Customer Relationship Management : deal_risk.escalated
records.description: Revenue intelligence flags a high-risk opportunity; CRM surfaces it to the rep. Failure modes: too many alerts dilute attention; AI risk scores not explainable.
records.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic shape: REV-INTEL inference, CRM intervention.

records.handoff_label: Revenue Intelligence → Sales Performance Management : pipeline_health.degraded
records.description: Pipeline health metrics dropping below threshold prompt sales leadership pipeline-build motion. Failure modes: lagging indicators trigger after the quarter is already lost.
records.notes: Leadership-layer signal: REV-INTEL upward to SALES-PERF leadership.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Account Planning → Customer Service Management : account_health.declined
records.description: Strategic account planning flags declining health; CSM engages for retention. Failure modes: health score components disagree (usage, sentiment, billing) — CSM unclear what to address.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack: ACCT-PLAN often a separate planning tool from CSM operations.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Account Planning → Sales Engagement : whitespace.identified
records.description: Whitespace (cross-sell / upsell) feeds SALES-ENG for prospecting. Failure modes: account-team toes; whitespace not synchronized with existing CSM relationships.
records.notes: Probabilistic identification meets coordinated outreach.

records.handoff_label: Partner Relationship Management → Customer Relationship Management : co_sell.opportunity_created
records.description: Joint opportunities flow from PRM into CRM with split-credit metadata. Failure modes: commission split rules need re-evaluation per deal; partner identity drift.
records.notes: Identity reconciliation: partner_id and account_owner_id are separate identifier spaces.

records.handoff_label: Partner Relationship Management → Customer Relationship Management : partner_referral.qualified
records.description: Partner-sourced referrals flow into CRM lead-routing. Failure modes: dedup against existing prospects; partner-attribution edge cases.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack: PRM platform distinct from CRM in most stacks.

records.handoff_label: Supplier Lifecycle Management → Core ERP Financial Management : supplier.onboarded
records.description: Newly-onboarded supplier triggers vendor-master creation in ERP-FIN: AP setup, payment-method record, tax-form repository. Failure modes: supplier-identity duplication when the same legal entity appears under different names; bank-detail validation delays.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack: SUP-LIFE is often a separate platform from ERP-FIN.

records.handoff_label: Supplier Lifecycle Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : supplier.risk_elevated
records.description: Risk-score elevation triggers GRC engagement: enhanced due diligence, mitigation plan, exit strategy if warranted. Failure modes: false-positive risk signals from third-party data; rep-attribution edge cases.
records.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic: risk scoring is heuristic, GRC engagement is binding.

records.handoff_label: Contract Lifecycle Management → Source-to-Pay : legal_contract.expired
records.description: Expired contracts trigger procurement renewal-decision workflow. Failure modes: auto-renewal clauses missed; silent expiry of long-tail contracts.
records.notes: Calendar-driven; common late-binding issue.

records.handoff_label: Contract Lifecycle Management → Accounts Payable Automation : legal_contract.amended
records.description: Contract amendments propagate to AP-AUTO: updated payment terms, discount schedule, GL coding. Failure modes: retroactive amendments require recalculating already-paid invoices.
records.notes: Period-coupling shape: amendments often have effective dates in past periods.

records.handoff_label: Electronic Signature → Contract Lifecycle Management : envelope.completed
records.description: Completed e-signature envelopes flow into CLM as authoritative signature_records. Failure modes: identity-of-signer verification gaps; multi-party-signing edge cases.
records.notes: Cross-platform pattern: the ESIGN vendor integrates with CLM via webhook or batch sync. envelopes is ESIGN-side, signature_records is CLM-side; this handoff carries the envelope and CLM constructs the matching signature_record.

records.handoff_label: Metrics Layer / Headless BI → Business Intelligence and Analytics : metric.certified
records.description: When a metric definition is certified in the metrics layer, BI tools that consume via SQL/REST need to refresh their cached schema and dashboard definitions. Mainstream BI tools all integrate via vendor-specific connectors, the protocol exists, but per-tool drift in semantic interpretation is the friction source.
records.notes: Medium friction. The newer metrics-layer / BI integrations are stable; the broken state is when BI tools also author local metrics that diverge from the central definitions.

records.handoff_label: Metrics Layer / Headless BI → Data and AI Platform : metric.certified
records.description: AI agents on data-AI platforms ground LLM responses in metric definitions via tool-use APIs. When a metric is certified, the agent's tool catalog needs to update.
records.notes: Medium friction. The 2024+ wedge for metrics-layer vendors: deterministic AI grounding requires fresh definitions and clean lineage. Vendor-specific connectors dominate, each metrics-layer vendor exposes its own LLM-facing API.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Metrics Layer / Headless BI : metric.deprecated
records.description: When a data asset is deprecated in the catalog, downstream metrics that reference it should be flagged or auto-deprecated. Almost universally manual today: catalog tools surface the deprecation, but a human has to walk the metric registry to identify and deprecate dependents.
records.notes: High-friction shape: lineage staleness. The catalog-side knows the asset is deprecated; the metric-side may not pick it up for weeks. The gap exists because lineage tools are immature at metric-to-asset granularity.

records.handoff_label: Knowledge Graph Platform → Data and AI Platform : ontology.published
records.description: Published ontology updates trigger AI agents that use the graph for grounded reasoning to refresh their tool / schema cache. Agent frameworks and vendor-specific agent runtimes consume KG schemas via SPARQL or REST.
records.notes: Medium friction. The integration protocols exist; the friction is keeping agent schemas in sync with rapidly-iterating ontologies during AI-app development.

records.handoff_label: Master Data Management → Knowledge Graph Platform : kg_entity.linked
records.description: MDM golden records are the authoritative source for master entities (Customer, Product, Supplier). KGP ingests them and links to ontology classes, but the data models differ: MDM is record-centric and survivorship-driven, KGP is relationship-centric and reasoning-driven. Bidirectional sync is bespoke.
records.notes: High-friction shape: cross-vendor stack with the same logical entity. The 'is the MDM Customer the same as the KGP Person entity?' reconciliation problem is the canonical failure mode.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Knowledge Graph Platform : ontology.published
records.description: Data Catalog and Governance platforms maintain business glossaries that semantically overlap with KGP ontologies. When a glossary term is added/changed, KGP ontology should reflect (and vice-versa). Almost universally manual; very few tools bridge the two models automatically.
records.notes: High-friction shape: probabilistic glossary terms to deterministic ontology concepts. Some tools bridge both sides natively; others rely on manual stewardship.

records.handoff_label: Customer Service Management → Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management : health_score.declined
records.description: Declining customer health score flags renewal risk; SUB-MGMT may need to adjust dunning lenience or surface for retention. Failure modes: multiple health-score variants disagree.
records.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic shape.

records.handoff_label: Contact Center as a Service → Customer Service Management : call.escalated
records.description: Escalated calls trigger CSM case re-assignment to a specialist or supervisor. Failure modes: original agent's context lost in handoff.
records.notes: Tight loop; same-vendor typical.

records.handoff_label: Contact Center as a Service → Customer Service Management : sentiment.negative
records.description: Real-time negative sentiment triggers CSM triage for outreach. Failure modes: AI sentiment scoring is unreliable; false positives drown the queue.
records.notes: Probabilistic-to-deterministic shape; AI confidence varies.

records.handoff_label: Conversational AI → Customer Relationship Management : intent.identified
records.description: Detected intent routes to CRM for opportunity creation or case enrichment. Failure modes: intent disambiguation when multiple intents in one conversation.
records.notes: AI-mediated routing.

records.handoff_label: Conversational AI → Contact Center as a Service : conversation.escalated_to_human
records.description: Bot-to-human handoff passes the conversation transcript and context to CCAAS. Failure modes: transcript context truncated by agent UI; customer has to repeat.
records.notes: Identity reconciliation needed across CONV-AI and CCAAS user sessions.

records.handoff_label: Field Service Management → Customer Service Management : work_order.completed
records.description: Completed field visits trigger CSM customer-satisfaction outreach and billing kickoff. Failure modes: technician sign-off lag; partial completion edge cases.
records.notes: Tight cross-cluster integration between FSM and CSM.

records.handoff_label: Field Service Management → Customer Service Management : dispatch.failed
records.description: Failed dispatch must reach CSM for customer rescheduling comm. Failure modes: failure detection lag; rescheduling SLA breached before CSM is informed.
records.notes: Going-away pattern: failure detection harder than success detection.

records.handoff_label: Customer Loyalty Management → Customer Relationship Management : tier.upgraded
records.description: Tier upgrades surface in CRM for account-tag refresh, VIP treatment, sales-rep awareness. Failure modes: tier change effective dates and CRM record sync lag.
records.notes: Identity reconciliation: LOYALTY member_id and CRM customer_id may differ.

records.handoff_label: Customer Loyalty Management → Marketing Automation : member.lapsed
records.description: Lapsed loyalty members trigger marketing-automation win-back motion. Failure modes: lapse criteria (inactivity threshold) tuning; false lapses for seasonal customers.
records.notes: Marketing automation typically same-vendor with MA platform.

records.handoff_label: Customer Service Management → Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management : customer.churn_confirmed
records.description: Confirmed churn triggers SUB-MGMT subscription cancellation and revenue-impact recognition. Failure modes: churn confirmed but contract-end-date not aligned; refund logic edge cases.
records.notes: Leaver recall: the going-away event must reliably reach finance to avoid continued billing.

records.handoff_label: Customer Service Management → Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management : subscription.expansion_requested
records.description: CSM-identified expansion needs SUB-MGMT proposal generation and CRM opportunity creation. Failure modes: duplicate opportunities when CSM and sales both file.
records.notes: Tight cross-domain coordination.

records.handoff_label: Application Portfolio Management → Software Asset Management : application.onboarded
records.description: New app triggers SAM software-title sync; identity reconciliation (app name vs software title) can lag.

records.handoff_label: Application Portfolio Management → Configuration Management Database : application.onboarded
records.description: App onboard creates CMDB CI; multi-vendor stacks need bespoke sync.

records.handoff_label: Application Portfolio Management → Configuration Management Database : application.lifecycle_state_changed
records.description: Sunset triggers CMDB CI retirement; decom timeline coordination.

records.handoff_label: Application Portfolio Management → Software Asset Management : application.lifecycle_state_changed
records.description: Sunset triggers license termination and reinstall-base cleanup.

records.handoff_label: Application Portfolio Management → IT Service Management : application_interface.broken
records.description: Integration failure escalates to incident; detection lag; true-positive rate varies.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Work Management : demand_intake.approved
records.description: SPM creates work_projects + kickoff work_items for charter and resourcing.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Strategic Workforce Planning : initiative.kickoff
records.description: SWP reserves headcount from workforce_scenarios; demand > supply requires escalation.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Strategic Workforce Planning : resource_allocation.committed
records.description: SPM books person/team; SWP syncs to workforce plan and decrements available capacity.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Product Management : roadmap_item.released
records.description: SPM closes roadmap item; PROD-MGMT marks feature shipped.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Work Management : strategic_portfolio.rebalanced
records.description: Re-prioritization cascades to project priority updates; high-touch validation.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Enterprise Performance Management : initiative.completed
records.description: Realized cost / schedule variance fed to EPM forecast and variance analysis.

records.handoff_label: Strategic Portfolio Management → Enterprise Performance Management : scenario_plan.evaluated
records.description: Evaluated scenario integrated by EPM for consolidated financial forecasting.

records.handoff_label: Governance, Risk and Compliance → Audit Management : audit_issue.created
records.description: GRC-identified compliance gap feeds AUDIT investigation workflow.

records.handoff_label: Governance, Risk and Compliance → IT Service Management : control.failed
records.description: Failed IT control → ITSM ticket; no feedback when ITSM closes ticket on GRC SLA.

records.handoff_label: Governance, Risk and Compliance → Learning Management : compliance_policy.updated
records.description: Policy version triggers LMS compliance-training requirement for scoped users.

records.handoff_label: Governance, Risk and Compliance → HR Service Delivery : compliance_policy.updated
records.description: Policy update (leave, harassment) → HRSD exception handling; no standardized machine-readable payload.

records.handoff_label: Governance, Risk and Compliance → Audit Management : obligation.overdue
records.description: Obligation past due → AUDIT escalation as non-conformance risk.

records.handoff_label: Governance, Risk and Compliance → Operational Resilience : assessment.completed
records.description: Enterprise risk assessment → OP-RES for operational-resilience planning.

records.handoff_label: Governance, Risk and Compliance → Business Continuity Management : assessment.completed
records.description: Critical risks feed BCM business-continuity-scenario planning.

records.handoff_label: Audit Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : finding.created
records.description: Audit finding flows to GRC for issue creation; canonical AUDIT→GRC separation.

records.handoff_label: Audit Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : follow_up_action.closed
records.description: AUDIT remediation closure → GRC issue closure (1:1 linkage established at finding time).

records.handoff_label: Audit Management → Enterprise Performance Management : recommendation.accepted
records.description: Accepted recommendations with budget impact → EPM scenario planning.

records.handoff_label: Audit Management → IT Service Management : audit_engagement.completed
records.description: IT audit outcomes trigger ITSM actions; requires human interpretation of scope/findings.

records.handoff_label: Audit Management → Third-Party Risk Management : finding.remediated
records.description: Third-party audit findings flow to TPRM for vendor-risk score update.

records.handoff_label: Data Integration → Data Catalog and Governance : data_asset.discovered
records.description: Schema crawler publishes new table; DCG auto-creates draft asset.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Data Loss Prevention : data_asset.classified
records.description: DCG publishes classification label; DLP must update enforcement policies.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Data Security Posture Management : data_asset.classified
records.description: DCG publishes classification; DSPM re-evaluates posture and alerts on over-privileged access.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Data Quality : data_asset.certified
records.description: Asset certified → DQ activates monitoring rules.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Identity Governance and Administration : data_access_request.approved
records.description: Access approved → IGA syncs credentials (AD group, role assignment).

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Data Loss Prevention : data_access_request.approved
records.description: Policy approved → DLP activates PII masking for named users.

records.handoff_label: Data Catalog and Governance → Knowledge Graph Platform : glossary_term.published
records.description: New glossary term published → KGP (Knowledge Graph Platform) populates concept hierarchy and links related entities.

records.handoff_label: Data Quality → IT Service Management : quality_rule.breach
records.description: Severity ≥ HIGH or breach > SLA threshold → ITSM incident. Dedup on (asset_id, rule_id).

records.handoff_label: Data Quality → IT Service Management : dq_scorecard.breached
records.description: Scorecard SLA breach → ITSM escalation ticket.

records.handoff_label: Data Quality → Data Catalog and Governance : profile_result.updated
records.description: Aggregated stats published back to DCG as asset metadata.

records.handoff_label: Master Data Management → Customer Relationship Management : customer_golden_record.created
records.description: Resolved golden ID + merged attributes; CRM links operational record.

records.handoff_label: Master Data Management → Customer Service Management : customer_golden_record.created
records.description: Resolved golden ID published to service-view.

records.handoff_label: Master Data Management → Subscription and Revenue Lifecycle Management : customer_golden_record.created
records.description: Published to billing for invoice/subscription account reconciliation.

records.handoff_label: Master Data Management → Customer Data Platform : customer_golden_record.updated
records.description: Golden record changes must propagate within SLA; identity corrections time-sensitive for marketing.

records.handoff_label: Master Data Management → Supplier Lifecycle Management : supplier_golden_record.updated
records.description: Golden-record changes flow to SUP-LIFE for risk reassessment; approval workflows add latency.

records.handoff_label: Master Data Management → Human Capital Management : employee_golden_record.created
records.description: Resolved identity → HCM links operational HR record.

records.handoff_label: ESG Management → Audit Management : emissions_record.ingested
records.description: ESG publishes immutable fact; AUDIT reads for assurance sampling.

records.handoff_label: ESG Management → Audit Management : esg_disclosure.submitted_for_assurance
records.description: Disclosure handed to AUDIT; tight Q deadline; no ack/retry on missed submissions.

records.handoff_label: ESG Management → Supplier Lifecycle Management : supplier_esg_assessment.score_updated
records.description: Updated ESG score → SUP-LIFE supplier_qualifications field; tier reassessment.

records.handoff_label: ESG Management → Third-Party Risk Management : supplier_esg_assessment.score_updated
records.description: Score → TPRM risk model; no feedback loop on TPRM action.

records.handoff_label: ESG Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : emission_target.breached
records.description: Target breach (SBTi-committed) → GRC obligation tracking.

records.handoff_label: Data Loss Prevention → Security Operations : dlp_incident.violation_detected
records.description: Violation events to SIEM for SOC enrichment / triage.

records.handoff_label: Data Loss Prevention → Identity Governance and Administration : dlp_incident.escalated
records.description: High-severity violations → IGA user-risk scoring; identity reconciliation friction.

records.handoff_label: Data Loss Prevention → Security Operations : dlp_incident.escalated
records.description: Critical violations fan-out to SOAR/ticketing; alert fatigue risk.

records.handoff_label: Data Loss Prevention → Privacy Management : dlp_incident.blocked
records.description: Nightly batch export of PII/GDPR blocks for privacy-incident tracking.

records.handoff_label: Data Loss Prevention → Security Operations : data_exfiltration_attempt.initiated
records.description: Raw attempts → SIEM for behavioral analytics; high volume requires tuning.

records.handoff_label: Data Security Posture Management → Data Catalog and Governance : data_asset.classified
records.description: DSPM propagates newly-discovered data-asset sensitivity labels to DCG.

records.handoff_label: Data Security Posture Management → Identity Governance and Administration : sensitive_data_incident.detected
records.description: Over-privilege findings → IGA role review; IGA may not have data-scoped roles.

records.handoff_label: Data Security Posture Management → Security Operations : sensitive_data_incident.detected
records.description: High-severity findings → SOC triage; bespoke schema mapping.

records.handoff_label: Data Security Posture Management → Privacy Management : data_classification.sensitivity_elevated
records.description: Elevation may trigger privacy data-subject / retention workflows.

records.handoff_label: Data Security Posture Management → Identity Governance and Administration : iam_access_policy.permission_escalation_detected
records.description: Over-privilege in cloud IAM / data-warehouse RBAC / CRM profiles; manual correction common.

records.handoff_label: Data Security Posture Management → Security Operations : sensitive_data_incident.resolved
records.description: Incident closure signal to SECOPS.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate and Workplace Management → Field Service Management : facility_work_order.created
records.description: Maintenance ticket dispatched to FSM for technician assignment.

records.handoff_label: Field Service Management → Real Estate and Workplace Management : facility_work_order.completed
records.description: Async, often delayed (technician retro logging); leaver/cancellation recall pattern on vacated spaces.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate and Workplace Management → ESG Management : utility_meter_reading.published
records.description: Utility readings → ESG activity_data calc; period/cycle-close coupling + meter_id↔facility_code identity reconciliation.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate and Workplace Management → Enterprise Asset Management : capital_project.completed
records.description: New assets installed; EAM records created at project closeout.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate and Workplace Management → Human Capital Management : property_space.allocated
records.description: Seat-assignment binding; low friction if shared employee master.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate Brokerage and Agent Operations → Residential Property Management : real_estate_transaction.closed
records.description: Closed sale of a rental property results in a new landlord-of-record; the new owner's property-management platform must be configured (often manual handoff via email; the buyer's PM and the seller's brokerage are different vendors).

records.handoff_label: Real Estate Brokerage and Agent Operations → Commercial Real Estate Operations : real_estate_transaction.closed
records.description: Closed sale of a CRE asset transfers operations to the new owner's CRE platform; rent-roll, leases, and CAM history must be carried over (typically manual).

records.handoff_label: Residential Property Management → Accounts Payable Automation : rent_payment.received
records.description: Reconciled rent payments post to property-level GL and roll up via batch into the AP-AUTO and ERP-FIN consolidated AR view; period-close timing must match.
records.notes: Period/cycle-close coupling — monthly close depends on rent-collection batch arriving on time.

records.handoff_label: Residential Property Management → Field Service Management : tenant_maintenance_request.created
records.description: Tenant maintenance request is dispatched as an FSM work order to in-house technician or third-party vendor; status updates flow back to tenant portal.
records.notes: Frequent failure mode: vendor confirms in their own system but doesn't update the tenant portal; tenant calls in.

records.handoff_label: Residential Property Management → Legal Service Delivery : property_tenant.evicted
records.description: Eviction initiation triggers a legal matter (filing, notice service, court date tracking); typical legal workflow runs in a separate matter-management system.
records.notes: Multi-shape: cross-vendor-stack (PM + legal-matter system) + alert-without-feedback (eviction status updates rarely flow back to PM). Plus jurisdiction-specific timing complexity.

records.handoff_label: Residential Property Management → Real Estate Investment Management : rent_payment.received
records.description: Realized rental income feeds multifamily-fund NOI calculations and ultimately property valuations and investor reporting.
records.notes: Batched monthly; misses on residential-PM-to-investment-mgmt timing cascade to NAV-refresh delays.

records.handoff_label: Commercial Real Estate Operations → Accounts Payable Automation : cam_charge.reconciled
records.description: Annual CAM reconciliation produces tenant true-up invoices (or refunds) that must post to AR; downstream cash collection cycle.
records.notes: Period/cycle-close coupling + cross-vendor stack (CRE platform reconciles, ERP-FIN bills). Tenant disputes drive frequent retro-adjustments.

records.handoff_label: Commercial Real Estate Operations → Real Estate Investment Management : commercial_lease.executed
records.description: New executed lease updates rent roll and NOI for the property; flows into RE-INVEST valuation models (often via a separate investment-valuation tool file refresh, since CRE-ops and the valuation tool rarely share schema).
records.notes: Multi-shape: cross-vendor-stack (CRE-ops platform on ops side, investment-valuation tool on investment side) + identifier reconciliation (suite-level rent-roll keys differ across systems). The classic 'high-friction' RE handoff.

records.handoff_label: Commercial Real Estate Operations → Field Service Management : tenant_maintenance_request.created
records.description: Commercial-tenant service request (HVAC, janitorial, building access) dispatches a work order to the property's FM/FSM platform.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate Investment Management → Cloud Financial Operations : property_valuation.refreshed
records.description: Refreshed property/portfolio valuations roll into corporate FP&A or fund-treasury for NAV reporting, debt-covenant compliance, and investor statements.
records.notes: Period/cycle-close coupling — quarterly NAV requires all property valuations to refresh within a fixed window.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate Investment Management → Core ERP Financial Management : fund_distribution.declared
records.description: Declared LP distributions flow to treasury for payment execution and to GL for fund-level posting.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate Investment Management → Core ERP Financial Management : capital_call.issued
records.description: Capital-call funding receipt records in treasury and posts to fund-accounting GL; partial-funding and late-payment scenarios trigger reminder workflows.
records.notes: Alert/escalation without feedback loop — chasing un-funded calls is largely manual.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate Brokerage and Agent Operations → Customer Relationship Management : real_estate_listing.qualified
records.description: Qualified buyer/seller leads flow into CRM-cluster contacts and the agent's CRM for nurture and conversion tracking.

records.handoff_label: Commercial Real Estate Operations → Contract Lifecycle Management : commercial_lease.executed
records.description: Executed commercial lease document flows into CLM repository for clause-level search, obligation tracking (TI completion, free-rent expiry), and renewal-window alerts.
records.notes: Bridge between CRE-ops (rent roll) and CLM (document obligations); commonly disconnected in practice.

records.handoff_label: Residential Property Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : rental_application.approved
records.description: Fair-housing-compliance evidence (denial reasons, screening criteria application, disparate-impact monitoring) feeds GRC audit.

records.handoff_label: Real Estate Brokerage and Agent Operations → Governance, Risk and Compliance : real_estate_transaction.closed
records.description: Disclosure-document completeness per closed transaction feeds brokerage-compliance audit and state-real-estate-commission requirements.

records.handoff_label: Vehicle Telematics → Fleet Maintenance Management : preventive_maintenance.due
records.description: Telematics-tracked mileage / engine hours / fault codes trigger PM-schedule firings that auto-generate vehicle work orders in the maintenance system.
records.notes: Cross-vendor stack: telematics platform on one side, fleet-maintenance platform on the other; identifier reconciliation on vehicle id is the common pain point.

records.handoff_label: Fleet Management → Fleet Maintenance Management : vehicle_inspection.failed
records.description: Failed DVIR inspection defects route to FLEET-MAINT as a new vehicle work order with the defect description and severity.
records.notes: Single-vendor stacks solve this in-platform; cross-vendor fails when DVIR app and maintenance system are different vendors.

records.handoff_label: Vehicle Telematics → Governance, Risk and Compliance : eld_log.violation_detected
records.description: Hours-of-service violations accumulate into CSA/FMCSA-scoring data feeds; aggregated patterns surface in GRC compliance dashboards.
records.notes: DOT-audit-relevant; missing violations can trigger CSA score downgrade.

records.handoff_label: Vehicle Telematics → Insurance Claims Management : dashcam_event.collision
records.description: Dashcam-detected collisions trigger insurance first-notice-of-loss; video evidence is preserved and shared with the carrier or claims platform.
records.notes: Multi-shape: cross-vendor-stack (telematics vendor vs carrier-claims system) + manual handoff (videos typically downloaded and emailed). Some telematics platforms have begun direct carrier integrations but most fleets still email clips.

records.handoff_label: Fleet Maintenance Management → Accounts Payable Automation : vehicle_work_order.completed
records.description: Completed external work orders (3rd-party shops) generate parts/labor invoices that flow into AP for matching and payment.
records.notes: Vendor-invoice matching against work-order line items is the common reconciliation step.

records.handoff_label: Fleet Management → Core Financial Management : fuel_transaction.posted
records.description: Reconciled fuel transactions post to GL by cost-center, vehicle class, or business unit; IFTA fuel-tax reporting compiled per quarter.
records.notes: Period/cycle-close coupling for IFTA quarterly filings.
