records.handoff_label: Utilities Operations → IT Service Management : utility_asset.failed
records.description: Failure of IT-dependent grid/SCADA asset raises an ITSM incident for dependent technology stack.

records.handoff_label: Utilities Operations → Core Financial Management : meter_read.captured
records.description: Captured meter reads feed ERP-FIN billing engine to materialize consumption-based invoices.

records.handoff_label: Utilities Operations → Field Service Management : meter_read.anomalous
records.description: Anomalous meter read triggers FSM inspection visit (leak/theft/meter failure).

records.handoff_label: Veterinary Practice Management → Core Financial Management : pet_owner.registered
records.description: Registered pet owner is materialized as customer/AR profile in ERP-FIN.

records.handoff_label: Veterinary Practice Management → Customer Service Management : veterinary_vaccination.due
records.description: Due-vaccination reminders feed CSM/CCAAS outreach campaigns to pet owners.

records.handoff_label: Veterinary Practice Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : veterinary_lab_result.critical
records.description: Critical lab results feed GRC for reportable-disease/adverse-event obligations to authorities.

records.handoff_label: Manufacturing Connected Operations → Enterprise Asset Management : production_downtime_event.recorded
records.description: Recorded downtime event auto-creates EAM maintenance work order for the affected asset.

records.handoff_label: Manufacturing Connected Operations → Core ERP Financial Management : production_order.completed
records.description: Completed production order triggers ERP-FIN WIP-to-finished-goods accounting entries.

records.handoff_label: Manufacturing Connected Operations → Governance, Risk and Compliance : production_quality_inspection.failed
records.description: Failed quality inspection is logged in GRC as non-conformance with corrective action requirement.

records.handoff_label: Manufacturing Connected Operations → IT Service Management : shop_floor_case.opened
records.description: Shop-floor case with IT/MES root cause is routed to ITSM for incident management.

records.handoff_label: Manufacturing Connected Operations → Enterprise Asset Management : production_schedule.published
records.description: Published production schedule allows EAM to plan PM windows around production blocks.

records.handoff_label: Manufacturing Connected Operations → Food Traceability and Provenance : produced_unit.completed
records.description: Completed produced unit feeds FOOD-TRACE as a CTE/KDE entry for the produced lot.

records.handoff_label: Dairy Herd Management → Food Traceability and Provenance : milking.completed
records.description: Each milking aggregates into bulk-tank lots that FOOD-TRACE captures as upstream traceability records.

records.handoff_label: Dairy Herd Management → Core ERP Financial Management : lactation_record.opened
records.description: Opened lactation cycle is reflected in ERP-FIN herd-KPI and cost-allocation models.

records.handoff_label: Dairy Herd Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : breeding_event.recorded
records.description: Breeding event is retained for traceability and welfare-program GRC evidence.

records.handoff_label: Dairy Herd Management → Core Financial Management : feed_ration.changed
records.description: Feed-ration change updates ERP-FIN feed-cost-per-liter and pricing inputs.

records.handoff_label: Dairy Herd Management → Food Traceability and Provenance : feed_ration.changed
records.description: Feed-ration change links ingredient lots to milk lots for downstream traceability.

records.handoff_label: Farmer-Direct Sales Platform → Core Financial Management : farmers_market_sale.recorded
records.description: Daily market sales are posted to ERP-FIN as revenue with stall/event cost-center allocation.

records.handoff_label: Farmer-Direct Sales Platform → Core Financial Management : wholesale_order.confirmed
records.description: Confirmed wholesale order materializes AR and inventory reservation in ERP-FIN.

records.handoff_label: Farmer-Direct Sales Platform → Customer Relationship Management : delivery_route.dispatched
records.description: Dispatched route triggers CRM/CCAAS ETA notifications to subscribers.

records.handoff_label: Farmer-Direct Sales Platform → Food Traceability and Provenance : butcher_order.ready
records.description: Ready butcher order finalizes lot/cut linkage in FOOD-TRACE for source-animal traceability.

records.handoff_label: Farmer-Direct Sales Platform → Customer Relationship Management : harvest_forecast.updated
records.description: Updated harvest forecast feeds CRM CSA-subscriber communication about availability changes.

records.handoff_label: Farm Management Information System → Food Traceability and Provenance : planting_record.completed
records.description: Completed planting pass instantiates the upstream traceability lot in FOOD-TRACE.

records.handoff_label: Farm Management Information System → Vehicle Telematics : variable_rate_prescription.published
records.description: Published prescription map is exported to machinery telematics systems for in-cab execution.

records.handoff_label: Farm Management Information System → Core ERP Financial Management : ag_input_inventory.low
records.description: Low-input threshold triggers ERP-FIN purchase requisition for replenishment.

records.handoff_label: Farm Management Information System → Vehicle Telematics : machinery_telemetry_record.captured
records.description: Telemetry feed is consumed by TELEMATICS for utilization/efficiency analytics.

records.handoff_label: Farm Management Information System → Food Traceability and Provenance : farm_field.boundary_updated
records.description: Field boundary update propagates lot-origin geometry to FOOD-TRACE.

records.handoff_label: Farm Management Information System → Core ERP Financial Management : crop_plan.committed
records.description: Committed crop plan feeds ERP-FIN input-cost and revenue projections.

records.handoff_label: Food Traceability and Provenance → Food Safety and Quality Management : traceability_lot.created
records.description: Created lot begins FSQM quality-surveillance window.

records.handoff_label: Food Traceability and Provenance → Governance, Risk and Compliance : critical_tracking_event.recorded
records.description: Recorded CTE feeds GRC FSMA-204 compliance evidence repository.

records.handoff_label: Food Traceability and Provenance → Audit Management : key_data_element.captured
records.description: Captured KDEs are retained as audit-evidence artefacts for FSMA traceability audits.

records.handoff_label: Food Traceability and Provenance → Audit Management : critical_tracking_event.recorded
records.description: CTE records are sampled by internal AUDIT to verify traceability program effectiveness.

records.handoff_label: Food Safety and Quality Management → Manufacturing Connected Operations : critical_control_point.deviation
records.description: CCP deviation forces MFG-OPS to quarantine the affected lot and halt the line.

records.handoff_label: Food Safety and Quality Management → Food Traceability and Provenance : critical_control_point.deviation
records.description: CCP deviation flags affected lots in FOOD-TRACE for hold and downstream tracing.

records.handoff_label: Food Safety and Quality Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : allergen_program.violation_detected
records.description: Allergen-control violation triggers GRC evaluation of FSMA reportable-food obligations.

records.handoff_label: Food Safety and Quality Management → Food Traceability and Provenance : environmental_monitoring_sample.positive
records.description: Positive environmental sample drives FOOD-TRACE evaluation of which lots to hold.

records.handoff_label: Food Safety and Quality Management → Manufacturing Connected Operations : sanitation_record.completed
records.description: Verified sanitation closure releases MFG-OPS to start the next production block.

records.handoff_label: Food Safety and Quality Management → Audit Management : haccp_plan.approved
records.description: Approved HACCP plan triggers AUDIT to schedule surveillance audit and align test scripts.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Core ERP Financial Management : inventory_location.opened
records.description: New inventory location must be created as a cost center / stock-ledger entity in ERP-FIN before postings can flow. Master-data sync gap is a common implementation pain point.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Digital Commerce : inventory_location.capacity_threshold_breached
records.description: Storefront must suppress that node from availability and ETA computations when capacity is exhausted, otherwise it will keep promising orders the node cannot fulfill.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Core ERP Financial Management : order_allocation.created
records.description: ERP-FIN posts inventory reservation accounting (move from available to committed) for each allocation.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Digital Commerce : order_allocation.created
records.description: Storefront and order-status pages reflect the allocated node and refined ETA to the customer.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Customer Service Management : order_allocation.failed
records.description: Failed allocations are a customer-facing exception; CSM must proactively engage to offer alternatives or refund. Typically high friction because OMS and CSM ticketing live in different stacks.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Digital Commerce : order_allocation.reassigned
records.description: Promised-delivery dates and source-node displayed to the shopper must be refreshed when allocations move; stale ETAs erode trust.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Customer Service Management : return_authorization.issued
records.description: Returns drive support case volume; CSM links the RMA to the customer record to track resolution.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Core ERP Financial Management : return_authorization.received
records.description: ERP-FIN releases the credit memo / refund and posts the inventory return to stock once goods are inspected.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Customer Relationship Management : return_authorization.received
records.description: CRM updates the customer's lifetime-value and returns-rate signals; high return rates may downgrade segmentation.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Digital Commerce : sourcing_decision.computed
records.description: Storefront calls OMS sourcing in-line during checkout (or asynchronously post-checkout) to display promised-delivery dates and shipping options.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Core Financial Management : sourcing_decision.computed
records.description: Cost-of-fulfillment analytics (carrier cost, split-shipment penalty, store-vs-DC margin) feeds ERP-FIN's profitability cube, usually nightly.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Customer Service Management : sourcing_decision.overridden
records.description: Manual overrides usually correlate with exception cases; CSM gets context to handle customer questions and slipped ETAs.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Digital Commerce : store_pickup_order.ready
records.description: Storefront sends the ready-for-pickup notification (push, email, SMS) to the customer with location and hours.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Customer Relationship Management : store_pickup_order.created
records.description: BOPIS visits are CRM-relevant in-store engagement signals; clienteling apps surface the upcoming visit to store associates.

records.handoff_label: Order Management → Core ERP Financial Management : store_pickup_order.expired
records.description: Expired pickups require refund posting and inventory return to sellable stock; reconciliation of in-flight orders is a known accounting pain.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Service Management : beta_program.launched
records.description: CSM activates white-glove monitoring and direct comms with beta participants while the program is live.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Data Platform : beta_program.launched
records.description: CDP creates and maintains the beta cohort segment for tailored messaging, in-product cues, and analytics.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Service Management : customer_feedback_item.linked_to_feature
records.description: Closing the listening loop: CSM surfaces 'you asked, we're building it / shipped it' on the customer record. Often manual today which is why product-feedback platforms exist.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Work Management : feature_request.upvoted_threshold
records.description: Once demand-signal crosses the prioritization threshold, an engineering work item / epic is created in WORK-MGMT. Many teams still do this by hand.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Relationship Management : feature_request.shipped
records.description: CRM uses 'requested-features-shipped' as renewal and expansion talk-track on the account record; close-the-loop comms run via CSM and DXP.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Digital Experience Platform : product_feature.released
records.description: DXP publishes marketing pages, docs, and in-product release notes for the new feature.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Relationship Management : product_feature.released
records.description: CRM entitlements and CPQ catalog need to reflect newly available features so reps can position and quote them.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Service Management : product_feature.deprecated
records.description: Deprecations require coordinated customer notification and migration plans; missed handoffs here lead to renewal-time blowups.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Data Platform : product_feature.adoption_threshold_reached
records.description: CDP refreshes feature-affinity segments used downstream by marketing, CSM playbooks, and pricing experiments.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Relationship Management : product_line.launched
records.description: Sales reps need the new line in CRM opportunity records and the CPQ catalog; product-master propagation is a recurring integration headache.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Core ERP Financial Management : product_line.launched
records.description: ERP-FIN sets up the revenue stream, GL coding, and cost-center mapping for the new line.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Service Management : product_metric.threshold_breached
records.description: Adoption / activation / churn-leading metrics dropping below threshold trigger CSM outreach plays for the affected accounts.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Work Management : product_release.planned
records.description: WORK-MGMT creates the delivery workstream / release train for the planned release, with the scope and target date hydrated from PROD-MGMT.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Digital Experience Platform : product_release.shipped
records.description: DXP publishes release notes, updates docs, and runs the launch content; the cadence has to match the actual ship date.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Customer Service Management : product_release.rolled_back
records.description: Rollbacks need synchronized customer comms; CSM must override the original release messaging. Friction is high because retraction loops are rarely automated.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Digital Experience Platform : product_roadmap.published
records.description: DXP updates the customer-facing roadmap page / portal so external messaging matches internal commitments.

records.handoff_label: Product Management → Work Management : product_roadmap.item_promoted
records.description: Promoting a roadmap item to now/next must create the corresponding delivery work in WORK-MGMT; manual handoff here is one of the most-cited PROD↔ENG pain points.

records.handoff_label: Configure-Price-Quote → Customer Relationship Management : quote_discount.applied
records.description: CRM updates opportunity amount and stage with the discounted value so forecast and quota tracking are accurate.

records.handoff_label: Configure-Price-Quote → Contract Lifecycle Management : quote_discount.approved
records.description: Approved discount terms must flow into the contract draft in CLM with the correct pricing, term length, and any concession clauses.

records.handoff_label: Configure-Price-Quote → Core ERP Financial Management : quote_discount.threshold_exceeded
records.description: Margin-floor or deal-desk escalations typically route through a manual approval queue spanning sales-ops and finance; integration-grade automation is rare and a known friction point.

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Human Capital Management : project_assignment.confirmed
records.description: Confirmed assignments decrement available capacity in HCM and link the consultant's calendar to the engagement. Friction stems from PSA and HCM frequently being separate vendors with different resource models.
records.notes: target NULL until HCM declares consumer DMDO on `project_assignments`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Work Management : project_assignment.confirmed
records.description: PSA seeds the WORK-MGMT project board with the newly-assigned resource so day-to-day task tracking can begin.
records.notes: target NULL until WORK-MGMT declares consumer DMDO on `project_assignments`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Strategic Workforce Planning : project_assignment.released
records.description: Released assignments return supply to the strategic workforce plan and are evaluated against forecast demand for re-deployment.

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Core ERP Financial Management : project_billing_milestone.reached
records.description: Reached milestones trigger invoice generation in the ERP AR module. Friction comes from milestone-to-invoice mapping rules differing per contract.
records.notes: target NULL until ERP-FIN declares consumer DMDO on `project_billing_milestones`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Contract Lifecycle Management : project_billing_milestone.reached
records.description: CLM updates contract-performance attributes when a milestone is met, supporting renewal valuation and SLA reporting.
records.notes: target NULL until CLM declares consumer DMDO on `project_billing_milestones`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Enterprise Performance Management : project_billing_milestone.slipped
records.description: Slipped milestones feed cash-flow and revenue forecasts in EPM so finance can re-baseline the quarter.
records.notes: target NULL until EPM declares consumer DMDO on `project_billing_milestones`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Human Capital Management : project_resource_allocation.committed
records.description: Committed allocations book named hours in HCM's capacity view, locking the resource against other demand.
records.notes: target NULL until HCM declares consumer DMDO on `project_resource_allocations`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : project_resource_allocation.demand_unmet
records.description: Unmet allocation demand is the seed for a hiring requisition; the manual handoff between resource manager and recruiter is the dominant pattern.

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Work Management : project_task.completed
records.description: PSA task completion mirrors into the WORK-MGMT board to keep team-level views current.
records.notes: target NULL until WORK-MGMT declares consumer DMDO on `project_tasks`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Core ERP Financial Management : project_task.completed
records.description: Completed billable tasks roll up to time-and-materials invoices in the ERP. Batch posting per billing run is the norm.
records.notes: target NULL until ERP-FIN declares consumer DMDO on `project_tasks`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Human Capital Management : resource_skill_inventory.updated
records.description: Updated skill inventory enriches the HCM talent profile so non-billable internal moves and career planning use the same skill graph.
records.notes: target NULL until HCM declares consumer DMDO on `resource_skill_inventories`

records.handoff_label: Professional Services Automation → Strategic Workforce Planning : resource_skill_inventory.gap_identified
records.description: Identified skill gaps feed the strategic workforce plan to inform hire-vs-train-vs-contract decisions for the practice.

records.handoff_label: Legal Service Delivery → Enterprise Content Management : in_house_legal_matter.opened
records.description: Opening a matter provisions a privileged ECM workspace where pleadings, correspondence, and work-product are filed under legal hold.

records.handoff_label: Legal Service Delivery → Audit Management : in_house_legal_matter.closed
records.description: Closed matters may be referenced in internal-audit work; legal counsel manually shares the relevant outcome and remediation summary.

records.handoff_label: Legal Service Delivery → Governance, Risk and Compliance : in_house_legal_matter.regulatory_disclosure_required
records.description: Disclosure-triggering matters open a GRC compliance obligation with the deadline and reporting authority pre-populated.

records.handoff_label: Legal Service Delivery → Enterprise Content Management : legal_advice_record.issued
records.description: Issued advice memos are filed in the privileged ECM repository with appropriate legal-hold and access controls.

records.handoff_label: Legal Service Delivery → Human Capital Management : legal_advice_record.employee_related
records.description: Employee-related advice is referenced from the HR case without exposing privileged content; the handoff is deliberately gated through counsel.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Human Capital Management : candidate_assessment.passed
records.description: Passing an assessment advances the candidate; on eventual hire, HCM uses the assessment result as the first data point for the new-hire skill profile.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Talent Management : candidate_assessment.passed
records.description: Completed assessment scores seed the talent-management skill profile for hired candidates and a structured talent pool for non-hires.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Human Capital Management : candidate_assessment.failed
records.description: Failed-assessment outcomes close the candidate's loop in ATS and propagate to HCM only if the candidate is an internal-mobility applicant whose profile should reflect the development gap.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Human Capital Management : pre_employee.activated
records.description: Pre-employee activation hands the canonical reconciliation to HCM-mastered `employees`. ATS owns the pre-employee lifecycle stage (paperwork, background check, pre-boarding); at start-date the pre_employee row is reconciled into the HCM employee record. Identifier mapping (pre_employee_id → employee_id) is the canonical reconciliation gap. Replaces / complements the older candidate.hired and job_offer.accepted handoffs by carrying the proper post-acceptance reconciliation milestone.

records.handoff_label: Investor Relationship and Deal Flow Management → Private Capital Fund Administration : vc_deal.closed
records.description: Closed deal triggers capital-call scheduling against the deploying fund's LP commitments. Today via custom integration between deal-flow CRM and fund-admin platform; mid-friction (timing of close vs LP-side notice deadlines).

records.handoff_label: Investor Relationship and Deal Flow Management → Portfolio Monitoring for Private Capital : vc_deal.closed
records.description: Closed deal must be added to portfolio-monitoring as a portfolio_company record with sector tag, board observer assignment, and KPI cadence. Often manual: deal lead emails portfolio team. Multi-shape pattern: identity reconciliation between INV-CRM contact record and PORT-MONIT portco entity.

records.handoff_label: Private Capital Fund Administration → Investor Relationship and Deal Flow Management : fund.final_close
records.description: Final close converts lp_prospects to lp_commitments; CRM-side prospect records need closure / archival. Today manual; the lp_prospect → lp_commitment transition is the canonical fundraising-to-fund-admin handoff.

records.handoff_label: Private Capital Fund Administration → Investor Relationship and Deal Flow Management : capital_call.issued
records.description: Capital call notification appears in LP-CRM as a touchpoint for the LP relationship — low-friction in tools that share LP master data, higher when LP CRM is separate.

records.handoff_label: Private Capital Fund Administration → Portfolio Monitoring for Private Capital : fund_distribution.executed
records.description: Executed distributions update fund-level performance metrics (DPI, RVPI, TVPI). Routine batch sync.

records.handoff_label: Portfolio Monitoring for Private Capital → Private Capital Fund Administration : portco_valuation.final
records.description: Quarter-end valuations drive PCAP statement updates; timing-coupled to the close calendar. Mid-friction when valuation and fund-admin tools are different vendors.

records.handoff_label: Cap Table Management and Equity Administration → Private Capital Fund Administration : exit_scenario.executed
records.description: Portfolio exit generates fund-side proceeds requiring distribution to LPs. Cross-vendor pattern between issuer-side cap-table tools and fund-admin; multi-shape (identity reconciliation between issuer and fund's investment vehicle + timing of post-close fund mechanics).

records.handoff_label: Cap Table Management and Equity Administration → Portfolio Monitoring for Private Capital : exit_scenario.executed
records.description: Exit event transitions portfolio_companies to `exited` state; final position return locked. Manual in most stacks because the cap-table and portfolio-monitoring tools are different vendors and the exit signal arrives via legal close, not via integrated feed.

records.handoff_label: Emerging Manager Fund Platform → Private Capital Fund Administration : fund_formation.operational
records.description: Emerging-manager fund formed; if customer migrates from EM-bundle to a full fund-admin stack later, the fund_formation record becomes the basis for FUND-ADMIN's `funds` record. Today entirely manual — customers re-key into the new platform.

records.handoff_label: Learning Management → Human Capital Management : compliance_assignment.due
records.description: Compliance assignment due-date nudges to HCM-mastered manager/employee record. HCM surfaces the impending obligation on the employee profile and routes a reminder to the line manager.

records.handoff_label: Learning Management → HR Service Delivery : compliance_assignment.due
records.description: HR Service Delivery opens (or updates) an employee-facing case/task with the impending obligation, deadline, and link to the assigned course. Failure mode: when an HRSD platform isn't deployed, the nudge falls back to direct email and the in-tool reminder.

records.handoff_label: Learning Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : compliance_assignment.due
records.description: GRC obligation tracker updates the per-employee compliance status to 'due' so the regulator-evidence dashboard reflects the impending breach risk. Drives audit-evidence reporting (e.g., Compliance Operations dashboard).

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Source-to-Pay : inv_stock_item.below_reorder_point
records.description: INV-MGMT publishes a replenishment signal; S2P is expected to raise a purchase requisition (or auto-PO if configured). Failure mode: alert without ack, no retry policy.
records.notes: Shape: alert-without-feedback-loop. INV publishes the alert; no confirmation that the PO was raised. Manual follow-up when missed.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Order Management : inv_stock_balance.on_hand_changed
records.description: High-frequency push of on_hand deltas to OMS so ATP recalculates and order allocations refresh. Volume is the dominant operational concern.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Order Management : inv_stock_balance.allocated
records.description: Reservation event when an order line locks inventory; OMS updates the order allocation record and reduces available_for_allocation.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Core ERP Financial Management : inv_cycle_count.variance_posted
records.description: Posted variance from a cycle count needs to land as an inventory adjustment journal in ERP-FIN.
records.notes: Shape: cross-vendor-stack (INV and GL frequently different vendors) plus period-cycle-close coupling (backdated entries arriving after close cascade).

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Core ERP Financial Management : inv_stock_transfer.received
records.description: Inter-location transfer receipt triggers an inter-company or inter-warehouse cost move journal.
records.notes: Shape: cross-vendor-stack.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Customer Service Management : inv_inventory_lot.expiry_warning
records.description: Pending-expiry alert for perishable lots; CSM uses this to proactively notify customers of soon-to-expire shipments.
records.notes: Shape: probabilistic signal becomes deterministic action. Threshold is subjective; false-positive volume is the failure mode.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Customer Service Management : inv_inventory_lot.recall_initiated
records.description: Recall trigger; CSM traces shipped lots to affected customers and initiates outreach.
records.notes: Shape: leaver / cancellation recall (going-away is harder than arriving). Fan-out to CSM and GRC shares one trigger_event.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Governance, Risk and Compliance : inv_inventory_lot.recall_initiated
records.description: Recall evidence for compliance: regulator filings (FDA recall classification), ISO traceability audit trail, supplier notification.
records.notes: Shape: leaver / cancellation recall. Second subscriber on same trigger_event.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Customer Service Management : inv_serialized_unit.warranty_activated
records.description: Issued serialized unit registers warranty start in CSM for future claim handling.

records.handoff_label: Inventory Management → Digital Commerce : inv_stock_item.created
records.description: New SKU sync to storefront-facing catalog; B2C-COMM creates or updates the `commerce_products` record.

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : job_application.submitted
records.notes: intra | ATS | candidate submits an application; pipeline picks it up in 'applied'

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : talent_pool.candidate_activated
records.notes: intra | ATS | pool re-engagement materializes as a new application against an open req

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : candidate_referral.submitted
records.notes: intra | ATS | referral submission creates the candidate in candidate-CRM

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : job_application.advanced
records.notes: intra | ATS | application advance to interviewing stage prompts interview creation

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : interview.completed
records.notes: intra | ATS | interview-completed signal feeds back into pipeline stage decision

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : candidate_assessment.passed
records.notes: intra | ATS | passing-assessment signal advances application in pipeline

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : candidate_assessment.failed
records.notes: intra | ATS | failing-assessment signal rejects or holds application in pipeline

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : job_application.advanced
records.notes: intra | ATS | application advance to offer_extended stage prompts offer drafting

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : job_offer.accepted
records.notes: intra | ATS | offer-accepted triggers contingent background-check workflow

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : job_offer.accepted
records.notes: intra | ATS | offer-accepted creates the pre-employee paperwork shell

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : background_check.cleared
records.notes: intra | ATS | background-check clearance unblocks pre-employee activation

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : background_check.flagged
records.notes: intra | ATS | flagged background check may force offer rescission; HR/Legal review path

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : job_offer.rescinded
records.notes: intra | ATS | rescind cancels any in-flight background check

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Applicant Tracking and Recruiting : job_offer.rescinded
records.notes: intra | ATS | rescind cancels pre-employee record; classic leaver-recall friction shape

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Employee Onboarding : job_offer.rescinded
records.notes: cross | ATS->ONBOARDING | rescind recalls the onboarding journey if already spawned

records.handoff_label: Applicant Tracking and Recruiting → Benefits Administration : job_offer.rescinded

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Farmer-Direct Sales Platform : customer.churn_confirmed
records.notes: Leaver pattern: confirmed CRM churn triggers CSA-side cancellation (cancel future shares, prorate refunds, release the pickup slot). High friction: the going-away signal often arrives via a different channel than membership signup, and refund timing is constrained by share cycles already invoiced.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Farmer-Direct Sales Platform : customer.signed_up
records.notes: New CRM customer activation flows to CSA-MGMT for membership-eligibility checks and welcome-pack composition.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Farmer-Direct Sales Platform : account.tier_changed
records.notes: Tier promotion (e.g. chef → restaurant chain → food-hub buyer) re-segments the customer in wholesale catalog/pricing tiers; FDS-WHOLESALE must re-apply contract terms and credit limits.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Farmer-Direct Sales Platform : account_health.declined
records.notes: Probabilistic signal becomes deterministic action: CRM health-score decline triggers CSA retention motion (proactive pickup-issue check, share-customization reset, satisfaction outreach). Failure mode is false-positive volume on heuristic scores.

records.handoff_label: Customer Relationship Management → Farmer-Direct Sales Platform : health_score.declined
records.notes: Probabilistic signal pattern: a customer-level (vs account-level) health drop triggers CSA-side retention; same failure-mode shape as account_health.declined. Both events shipped catalog-wide and FDS subscribes to both until the two are consolidated upstream.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : employee.created
records.description: New consultant hired. PSA resource pool adds the employee as available capacity; skill inventory record is seeded for downstream certifications.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : employee.promoted
records.description: Consultant promoted (level / job profile change). PSA reevaluates billable rate band and skill inventory; existing project_assignments may need rate revision.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : employee.terminated
records.description: Consultant terminated. PSA must release any active project_assignments, return capacity to bench and re-allocate forecast. Medium friction: leaver-event timing varies (immediate vs notice period) and active assignments may need urgent rebalancing.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : attrition_risk.high
records.description: ML attrition score crosses high threshold. PSA resource managers may proactively rebalance assignments away from at-risk consultants on critical engagements. High friction: probabilistic→deterministic pattern (score requires judgment call), false-positive volume can swamp the staffing queue.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : employee.terminated
records.description: Terminated employee may be the assignee on open project_tasks. PROJECT-DELIVERY needs to surface affected tasks for reassignment or completion handover.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : job_profile.published
records.description: New job profile published. PSA picks up the role definition (competencies, level) as a new shape for skill-based demand modeling and resource_skill_inventories matching.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : job_profile.updated
records.description: Job profile updated (competencies, level, responsibilities). PSA revalidates the resource pool's skill matches and surfaces gaps via existing resource_skill_inventory.gap_identified signal.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : job_profile.activated
records.description: Job profile activated for production. PSA makes the role assignable on new project_assignments and project_resource_allocations.

records.handoff_label: Human Capital Management → Professional Services Automation : job_profile.retired
records.description: Job profile retired. PSA blocks new assignments to the role and surfaces a migration list for any existing project_assignments still referencing it.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Employee Onboarding : onboarding_plan.activated
records.notes: Plan activation seeds a document_collection for the journey; intra-domain progression, no out-of-process message.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Employee Onboarding : onboarding_plan.activated
records.notes: Plan activation schedules the welcome cadence and pairs a buddy; intra-domain progression.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Employee Onboarding : onboarding_document_collection.completed
records.notes: Doc collection completion unblocks day-one transition on the journey.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Employee Onboarding : welcome_communication.sent
records.notes: Welcome communication sent advances the journey's pre-board stage.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Employee Experience and Engagement : onboarding_stage.completed
records.notes: Stage completion (pre-board, day-one, week-one, 30-day) fires onboarding milestone surveys via EMP-EXP continuous-listen.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Employee Onboarding : buddy_assignment.activated
records.notes: Buddy assignment active marks pre-board stage progress on the journey.

records.handoff_label: Employee Onboarding → Learning Management : onboarding_cohort.activated
records.notes: Cohort activation triggers cohort-scoped LMS compliance training enrollments for the cohort members.

records.handoff_label: Product Information Management → Digital Commerce : pim_product.published
records.description: PIM publishes a product release; B2C-COMM refreshes its storefront-runtime cache (commerce_products). Failure modes: cross-vendor cache invalidation (PIM and commerce often different vendors), partial-publish where some attributes propagate before others, CDN URL mismatch between PIM-managed assets and storefront media library.
records.notes: target NULL until B2C-COMM is modularized. Multi-shape: cross-vendor stack + alert-without-feedback-loop (rejected publishes routinely need manual remediation in PIM).

records.handoff_label: Product Information Management → Inventory Management : pim_product.published
records.description: New SKU appears in stock master so inventory tracking can begin. Routine sync; medium friction because new-SKU first-stock-receipt timing has to coordinate with vendor receiving.

records.handoff_label: Product Information Management → Configure-Price-Quote : pim_product.published
records.description: CPQ pulls the attribute schema and option dependencies for a newly-published product so the configurator UI can offer it. Medium friction: attribute-shape changes break existing CPQ rules.
records.notes: target NULL until CPQ is modularized.

records.handoff_label: Product Information Management → Digital Commerce : pim_product.discontinued
records.description: Discontinued SKU must be pulled from storefront and marketplace listings. Multi-shape high-friction: leaver pattern (going-away signal often arrives via different channel than original arrival) + cross-vendor stack.
records.notes: target NULL until B2C-COMM is modularized. Leaver-pattern handoff.

records.handoff_label: Product Information Management → Product Information Management : pim_product.approved
records.description: Approved product enters the syndication queue; one pim_syndication_jobs row is created per configured channel target. In-process; no message moves between modules.

records.handoff_label: Product Information Management → Product Information Management : pim_digital_asset.approved
records.description: Approved asset becomes available to in-flight syndication jobs that need its CDN URL. Lifecycle progression; no message moves.

records.handoff_label: Product Information Management → Product Information Management : pim_translation.approved
records.description: Approved translation becomes consumable by locale-specific syndication jobs. Lifecycle progression.

records.handoff_label: Product Lifecycle Management → Product Information Management : engineering_change_order.released
records.description: PLM engineering-change-order release rev-bumps the engineering part; PIM must refresh merchandising attributes that mirror engineering revisions (dimensions, material, compliance flags). Multi-shape high-friction: cross-vendor stack (PLM and PIM often different vendors) + period-cycle-close coupling (mid-launch-window ECOs cascade through merchandising approvals).

records.handoff_label: Product Lifecycle Management → Product Information Management : engineering_part.released
records.description: New engineering part released to market; PIM creates the merchandising shell with engineering-attribute seeds. Medium friction: engineering and merchandising vocabularies diverge, so attribute mapping is rarely 1:1.

records.handoff_label: Product Lifecycle Management → Product Information Management : product_compliance_declaration.approved
records.description: Approved product-compliance declaration updates region-specific PIM attributes (REACH / RoHS / Prop 65 / FDA). Medium friction: compliance vocabularies are jurisdiction-specific and rarely map cleanly to PIM channel-feed shapes.

Discrete and process manufacturing across industrial, automotive, electronics, chemicals, food & beverage, and consumer goods.
Brick-and-mortar and omnichannel retailers — store operations, merchandising, and customer-facing commerce.
Regulated electric, gas, and water utilities — generation, transmission, distribution, and customer billing.
Wireline, wireless, cable, and broadband network operators — OSS/BSS, network operations, and customer experience.
Universities, colleges, and post-secondary institutions. Workday's foundational vertical via Workday Student. Distinct from K-12 in regulatory environment (FERPA, IPEDS) and funding model.
Services firms billing client engagements: management consulting, IT services, engineering, accounting, law. Project-economy industry where PSA is the operational backbone.
Pharmaceutical manufacturers, biotech, medical devices, and contract research organisations. Heavy regulatory burden (FDA, EMA, GxP) and global-payroll complexity.
Sub-national government entities: states/provinces, counties, municipalities, public agencies. Distinct procurement (StateRAMP, GovCloud), labour rules, and budget cycles from federal Public Sector.
Tax-exempt organisations including charities, foundations, religious bodies, advocacy groups. Distinct grant-accounting, fund-balance, donor-restricted-fund requirements.

Outsourced IT operations firms that remotely monitor, manage, and support customer endpoints, networks, and cloud estates on recurring contracts. Multi-tenant customer estates, block-hour / per-endpoint / value-based pricing, per-customer SLAs. Distinct buyer profile and vendor stack from internal-IT — buys RMM, MSP-PSA, and BCDR as the operational core. Vendors targeting this segment: Kaseya, ConnectWise, N-able, Atera, NinjaOne, SuperOps, Halo, Datto (Kaseya).

Brokerages, property-management firms, commercial-real-estate operators, and real-estate investment vehicles. Distinct vendor stack per sub-segment (residential brokerage CRM, multifamily property mgmt, CRE leasing/asset mgmt, fund accounting). Sub-segments share property-as-asset model but diverge on revenue model (commission vs rent vs distributions). Vendors active across segments: Yardi, MRI, AppFolio, RealPage, Entrata, Lone Wolf, Inside Real Estate, VTS, CoStar, Altus, Juniper Square.

Law firms, solo practitioners, and legal-service organisations: litigation, transactional, regulatory, IP, real-estate, family, criminal defense, and in-house counsel offshoots. Buyer profile distinct from other professional services by ABA Model Rules, IOLTA trust accounting, conflict-of-interest constraints, and matter-centric workflow. Sub-segment of Professional Services in NAICS.

CPA firms, tax preparers, bookkeeping practices, and accounting outsourcers. Buyer profile distinct from generic professional services by tax-calendar-driven seasonality, AICPA professional-conduct constraints, IRS Pub 4557 + GLBA taxpayer-data safeguards, and engagement-letter-driven service delivery. Sub-segment of Professional Services in NAICS.

Veterinary clinics and hospitals serving companion animals, livestock, and equine practices. Distinct buyer profile from human-healthcare providers: no HIPAA exposure (animals aren't covered entities), DEA-controlled-substance ledger constraints only when prescribing animal narcotics, state-veterinary-board licensing, pet-owner-as-client (vs patient) relationship. Top-level industry: regulatory and operational profile diverges enough from generic Professional Services to warrant a separate row.

Independent and holding-company advertising, marketing, creative, PR, media-buying, and digital agencies. Buyers of vertical agency-management software (Workamajig, Deltek WorkBook, Advantage, FunctionPoint, Mediaocean). Distinct from in-house marketing teams of non-agency businesses.

NAICS 11. Primary-production sector: crop growing, animal husbandry, aquaculture, forestry, fishing. Distinct vendor stack from generic Manufacturing: weather / soil / satellite-imagery-driven operations, season-bound revenue cycles, USDA / EPA / FDA / state-ag-department regulation, federal crop insurance, NRCS conservation programs. Catalog scope: load crop and animal production now; defer forestry, fishing, and hunting until evidence threshold met.

NAICS 722. Full-service restaurants, quick-service restaurants (QSR), fast-casual, catering, food trucks, bars, coffee shops, and other prepared-food-for-immediate-consumption operations. Separate top-level (not under Hospitality) because the vendor stack is operationally distinct from lodging: restaurant POS (Toast, Square for Restaurants, TouchBistro), online-ordering aggregation (Olo, Otter), kitchen display systems, restaurant-specific labour scheduling (7shifts, Restaurant365), and direct delivery integrations. Driven by gig-labour and aggregator economics not present in lodging.

NAICS 111. Row crops (corn, soy, wheat, cotton), specialty crops (vineyards, orchards, market gardens), greenhouse / controlled-environment ag, and field vegetables. Vendor stack diverges sharply by farm size: smallholder FMIS (Farmbrite, AgriWebb) vs enterprise row-crop FMIS (Climate FieldView, Granular, Conservis). USDA Organic certification and state-level pesticide regulations apply. Speciality-crop-specific tooling (Vinsight, AgCode, Croptracker) is a candidate sub-industry — defer until vendor evidence justifies.

NAICS 112. Beef cattle, swine, poultry, sheep, equine, and aquaculture. Excludes dairy (separate sub-industry due to distinct vendor pool and milk-cycle workflow). USDA FSIS oversight for slaughter / processing; animal-welfare regulation; CAFO permitting. Aquaculture has thin US vendor mass — global software market is healthier (AKVA Group, eFishery) but US TAM is borderline; defer aquaculture sub-industry until US scope justifies.

NAICS 311-312. Food and beverage processing: dairy plants, meat processors, bakeries, beverage bottling, packaged-food producers. Sub-segment of Manufacturing because process / batch ERP fundamentals carry over, but vendor stack adds FSMA / HACCP / SQF / BRC-GS / kosher / halal certification, allergen control, lot traceability, and short-shelf-life inventory. Vertical-ERP vendors: Aptean Food & Beverage, SAP S/4HANA F&B, Infor M3 Food, Plex Food (under Rockwell Automation).

NAICS 445. Supermarkets, grocery, specialty food retailers, beverage retailers, butcher / fish / produce shops. Sub-segment of Retail because POS / merchandising fundamentals carry over, but distinct perishables management (short shelf life, cold-chain monitoring, dynamic markdowns), thin margins driving aggressive markdown-optimisation tooling, and AP-pay-on-receipt supplier dynamics.

NAICS 1121. Milk production from cattle, goats, and sheep. Separate sub-industry of Animal Production: vendor pool (DairyComp 305 by Valley Ag, BoviSync, AfiMilk, Lely Horizon, DeLaval DelPro, CowManager) is largely independent from beef / swine livestock vendors, and milk-cycle workflows (parlor management, milk-quality testing, somatic-cell counts, FDA Grade A milk regulation, dairy cooperative pooling) have no counterpart elsewhere in livestock. ~$700M-1.2B US software TAM.
Banking, asset management, private capital (VC/PE), insurance, and wealth management.
Early-stage and growth-stage equity investment in private companies, typically with fund lifespans of 7-10 years and LP commitments from institutional and individual investors.
Buyout, growth equity, and credit strategies in private companies, characterised by control or significant minority stakes and longer holding periods.

NAICS sector 23. Buildings (residential and non-residential), heavy and civil engineering construction, and specialty trade contractors. Distinct from Manufacturing (which produces goods) and Real Estate (which owns and operates properties).

NAICS sub-sector 238. Trade contractors performing specialized activities (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, roofing, drywall, painting, masonry) usually subcontracted to general contractors or working directly for property owners. Buyer for trade-specific service starters (HVAC, plumbing, electrical service-management bundles).

Heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration installation and service contractors. Small field-service operators running install, maintenance, and repair work orders for residential and light-commercial sites.

records.description: Global frameworks and standards with no single issuing geography — e.g. ISO standards, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, IFRS, TCFD. Used when a regulation or framework applies broadly across nations rather than being issued by a specific country or supranational body.
Supranational body covering EU member states. Issues directives and regulations (GDPR, NIS2, DORA, MiFID II, CSRD) that apply across member states either directly or via national transposition.
Federal jurisdiction of the United States of America. State-level jurisdictions (e.g. California) are modelled separately as children.
Post-Brexit UK jurisdiction. Inherits much of the EU regulatory legacy (UK GDPR, UK PSD2 equivalents) but evolves independently.
US state of California. Sets the most influential US state-level privacy regime (CCPA/CPRA) and several sectoral rules that often become de-facto national standards.
Federal jurisdiction. Workday Payroll native country. Provincial variations (Quebec especially) affect payroll, tax, and language requirements.
EU member state. Workday Payroll native country. DSN (Déclaration Sociale Nominative) is the consolidated social-security reporting; URSSAF is the principal authority.
Federal jurisdiction. Workday Payroll native country. Single Touch Payroll (STP) and SuperStream are the principal payroll reporting regimes.
EU member state. Workday Global Payroll Connect partner country. Finanzamt (tax) and DEUEV (social security) are the principal payroll-reporting endpoints. GoBD governs accounting record retention.
EU member state. Workday's EMEA headquarters jurisdiction. Revenue Online Service is the principal payroll endpoint.
Federal jurisdiction. Major Workday delivery centre; localised payroll via partner. Complex statutory deductions (PF, ESI, professional tax, TDS) and state-level variations.
Workday partner-payroll country. Complex multi-pay-period social-insurance cadence (kyousai, kenpo, koyou).
Federal jurisdiction. Workday partner-payroll country. eSocial is the consolidated statutory-reporting platform; complex 13th-month, vacation, FGTS calculations.
Federal jurisdiction. Workday partner-payroll country. CFDI de Nómina is the electronic payroll receipt standard; IMSS social-security reporting.
EU member state. Workday partner-payroll country. Belastingdienst tax authority; loonaangifte is the wage-tax declaration.
US state. NYC Local Law 144 (AEDT bias audit), NY state pay-transparency law (s.194-b), state DOL labour rules.
US state. Equal Pay for Equal Work Act (salary-disclosure leader, 2021).
US state. Pay-transparency requirements (SB 5761) and L&I labour rules.

entity.description: Junction between `processes` and `tools`. Records that a cross-domain value-stream process requires (or optionally uses) an atomic tool. A tool is atomic and lives once in `tools`; this row only references `tool_id`. A `process` skill (linked via `skills.process_id`) derives its toolset from these rows. Replaces the retired process-skill `skill_tools` grain per plans/per-domain-skill-restoration.md.

computed_fields.name: key
computed_fields.description: 2-tuple natural key for the process_id -> tool link: process_id.tool_id. Materialized by the BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger from this computed_fields JsonLogic. Mirrors the handoff_processes.key idiom.

fields.title: Process
fields.description: The value-stream process that requires this tool.

fields.title: Tool
fields.description: The atomic tool (canonical row in `tools`) this unit requires. Referenced, never copied.

fields.title: Requirement Level
fields.description: Whether the tool is irreducible for this unit's primary workflows (`required`) or covers a degraded / augmenting mode (`optional`). Carried verbatim from the migrated `skill_tools` rows; the coverage rollup counts only `required` tools in its denominator.

fields.title: Notes
fields.description: Empty by default. Populate only when there is something exceptional to call out about this pair. No vendor or product names (SKILL.md Rule #18).

fields.title: Record Status
fields.description: Standard workflow per SKILL.md Rule #1. Carried verbatim from the migrated `skill_tools` rows (all `new`).

fields.title: Key
fields.description: Computed 2-tuple natural key (process_id.tool_id). Materialized by the BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger from entities.computed_fields. unique_value=true enforces idempotency on the pair at the database layer.

entity.description: Industry-standard business processes (APQC PCF cross-industry + future industry PCFs + org-specific custom rows). Hierarchical via parent_process_id. Discovery backbone for Phase D process-skill candidates: clustered handoff subgraphs are matched against this catalog to assign an industry-standard process name. Discriminated by source_framework so PCF imports and custom rows coexist without naming collisions.

fields.title: Code
fields.description: Natural key. For PCF rows: literal PCF ID (e.g. 6.1.1, 8.4.2.1). For custom rows: CUSTOM-<CLUSTER>-<SHORT-NAME> (e.g. CUSTOM-ONBOARD-DAY-1).

fields.title: Description
fields.description: PCF rows: verbatim from the PCF Excel. Custom rows: authored description of what the process orchestrates.

fields.title: Source Framework
fields.description: Discriminator. apqc_pcf_cross_industry is the v8 cross-industry framework. Industry-specific PCFs are placeholders for future loads. custom is org-specific or discovery-derived.

fields.title: Process Key
fields.description: Authored, stable, unique snake_case key derived from process_name. Durable human-readable identifier for cross-referencing a process; complements the numeric id and the APQC external_id / process_code (which are blank for custom processes). Stable: a snapshot of process_name at authoring time, not recomputed when the name changes.

fields.title: External ID
fields.description: Framework's own identifier — the PCF ID for any apqc_pcf_* row. Empty string for custom rows.

fields.title: Hierarchy Level
fields.description: 1–5 matching APQC's level scheme for PCF rows; 1–N for custom. Lets queries filter by depth without recursive CTEs.

fields.title: External URL
fields.description: Optional pointer to source documentation. Empty string acceptable.

fields.title: Parent Process
fields.description: Hierarchical parent. Null for level-1 categories.

records.description: Establishing a direction and vision for an organization. This involves defining the business concept and long-term vision, as well as developing the business strategy and managing strategic initiatives. Processes in this category focus on creating a vision, a mission, and strategic objectives, and culminate in creating measures to ensure that the organization is moving in the desired direction.

records.process_name: Develop and Manage Products and Services
records.description: Detailing practices and procedures related to the concept of developing and managing products and services. These are reflected in the process groups Govern and manage product/service development program [19696], Generate and define new product/service ideas [19698], and Develop products and services [10062].

records.process_name: Market and Sell Products and Services
records.description: Outlining process groups related to understanding markets, customers, and capabilities; developing marketing strategies; executing marketing plans; developing sales strategies; developing and managing marketing plans; and managing sales partners and alliances.

records.process_name: Manage Supply Chain for Physical Products
records.description: Performing supply chain activities include planning supply chain, procuring materials and services, and managing logistics.

Offering services to customers. This is the act of providing service delivery as a core business practice and covers identifying strategies for performing service delivery, managing resources, and delivering services to the customer.

Managing interactions with current customers after the delivery of products and services. This includes developing and planning customer service practices with a focus on handling inquiries after sales, feedback, warranties, recalls, and other related processes.

Delivering processes traditionally defined as "human resources". Process groups include those related to developing and maintaining workforce strategy, recruiting employees, developing and counseling employees, managing employee relations, rewarding and retaining employees, redeploying and retiring employees, managing employee information, and managing employee communications.

Managing process groups relevant to the business of information technology within an organization. The process groups include "Develop and manage IT customer relationships", "Develop and manage IT business strategy", " Develop and manage IT resilience and risk", " Manage information", " Develop and manage services/solutions", "Deploy services/solutions", and " Create and manage support services/solutions".

Overseeing key back-office processes for organizations. This category includes process groups related to planning and management accounting, revenue accounting, general accounting and reporting, fixed-asset project accounting, payroll, accounts payable and expense reimbursements, treasury operations, internal controls, tax management, international funds/consolidation, and global trade services.
Relating to the design, construction, acquisition, and management of both productive and non-productive assets.

records.process_name: Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Remediation, and Resiliency
records.description: Ensuring that an organization effectively manages its risk. Process groups are aligned with traditional risk management activities.

Fostering external relationships with stakeholders of the entity, including investors, government and industry, the board of directors, and the general public. This is not related to customer management.

Performing activities by an organization that are fundamental to the successful operation of the organization, even across functions in a business. Capabilities defined in the PCF include business process management; portfolio, program, and project management; quality management; change management; benchmarking; environmental health and safety management; and knowledge management.

records.process_name: Define the business concept and long-term vision
records.description: Creating a conceptual framework of the organization's business activity and strategic vision with long-term applicability. Scout the organization's internal capabilities, as well as the customer's needs and desires, to identify a fit that can be used to advance a conceptual structure of the organization's business activity. Conduct analysis in light of relevant externalities and large-scale shifts in the market landscape.

Developing an organization's mission statement, strategy, and business design. Create a concise statement that clearly articulates the mission of the organization, outlining practicable targets to Establish a strategic vision [10020]. Delineate strategic options by matching these alternatives with the organization's internal capabilities. Create an organizational design, and identify goals by developing strategies at the functional and process levels.

Managing strategic initiatives, from development through selection, execution, and evaluation. Conduct and oversee strategic projects supporting long-term objectives. Administer programs of strategic significance by developing such initiatives, select the most appropriate projects, and formulate measures to assess their impact.

Establishing how an organization creates, delivers and captures value or makes profit. Identify the products or services that a business will sell, its target market, anticipated expenses, and other core aspects of its modus operandi. Revise the plan as required to reflect changing circumstances.

records.process_name: Govern and manage product/service development program
records.description: Supervising the complete product/service program from innovation until its commercial success. Meeting the customer demand and expectations. Conduct further development and innovation pertaining to business goals.

records.process_name: Generate and define new product/service ideas
records.description: Identifying and describing new product or service thoughts based on organizational objectives/targets.
Developing new products/services from scratch, including all activities associated with the design, prototyping, evaluation, and market testing of these planned offerings.

Making sense of the market and customers to identify the right opportunities to be capitalized, given the organization's competencies. Discern trends and shift in the market and customers. Identify the right market opportunities that fit closely with the organization's capabilities and strategy by gathering intelligence on various attributes of different market/customer segments.

Charting a strategic course for marketing products/services. This will include defining the value proposition, creating a mechanism for pricing, and determining the right mix of marketing channels. Create a specific positioning and branding for the organization's offerings. Enlist marketing head to lead, with inputs from the business development and sales functions.

Creating specific plans to market offerings to customers. This process group includes processes for making budgets, identifying and developing media, pricing products and services, managing packaging, managing marketing content and promotional activities, tracking and responding to customer insight and monitoring measures established within "develop marketing strategy". Additionally, in this process group, organizations take action on plans made in earlier processes. Here, marketing and customers are managed and measured along with any supporting materials.

Developing concrete plans for guiding and providing support to the sales function. Chart a road map for the sales function, including an analysis of historical sales data to create forecasts for anticipated sales, forming sales targets, forging partnerships with other economic agents to boost sales, devising a budget for this function, and determining metrics to measure customer management activities as well as progress in achieving sales targets.

Selling products/services. Set appropriate customer expectations. Work with customers using the same schedule that product/service development, production, and customer service functions follow. Manage sales personnel and sales partnerships/alliances.

records.process_name: Plan for and align supply chain resources
records.description: Creating strategies for production and materials. Handle the demand for the products of the organization. Develop plans for handling materials. Develop and administer the schedule for master production. Plan for distribution requirements and its constraints by reviewing and assessing distribution policies and performance and by establishing quality standards and procedures.

Creating a plan for procuring materials and services. Develop strategies for sourcing materials and services. Choose the most appropriate suppliers, and develop contracts with them. Order the materials and services as per the requirements. Manage relationships with suppliers.

Processing and delivering the finished goods manufactured by the organization. Schedule the production of products. Execute the product production activities. Perform tests to oversee and ensure quality of production. Maintain records of the production process. Track lots.

Administering and overseeing all activities related to logistics and warehousing. Outline and establish a strategy for the logistics function. Plan and administer the flow of inbound materials. Administer the operational activities of warehousing and outbound transportation. Manage reverse logistics including returns and exchanges.

records.process_name: Establish service delivery governance and strategies
records.description: Creating rules and regulations for service delivery to the customer. Establish a system to manage performance, delivery, and direction of service delivery. Engage with the customer for satisfaction feedback. Define goals, policies, processes, and workplace layout and infrastructure as a part of the service delivery strategy.
Understanding the demands on resources and creating a plan to enable the delivery of services via those resources.

records.process_name: Manage and Operate Service Delivery System
records.description: Managing and operating the systems, resources, and processes used to deliver services to customers, including planning, startup, ongoing operations, and service assurance.
Rendering service to the customer by initiating, executing, and completing tasks associated with service delivery.

Defining a plan that removes customer obstacles by gathering operational insight and competitive insight, as well as improving soft skills and forward resolution for employees. Develop customer segmentation. Define rules and regulations for customer service. Establish service levels for customers.

records.process_name: Plan and manage customer service contacts
records.description: Planning and administering workforce operations for customer service provision by taking care of customer services requests/inquiries, as well as the complaints.

Assigning post-sales policies and paying claims on purchased products.  This is a process that is an administrative function focused on creating rules (claim codes). This group ensures that claims are valid and are processed quickly.  As well as to quickly determine responsibility for claim settlement.

records.process_name: Manage product recalls and regulatory audits
records.description: Removing defective products from the distribution chain. Participate in audits from watchdog agencies.

records.process_name: Evaluate customer service operations and customer satisfaction
records.description: Calculating and assessing the operational activities of the customer service function. Evaluation is achieved through the customer requests/inquiries handling process, the customer complaint handling process, and product and services quality. Examine activities to ensure high levels of customer service.

records.process_name: Develop and manage human resources (HR) planning, policies, and strategies
records.description: Creating strategies for the HR function. Create and implement strategies for managing the work force. Supervise and enhance the strategies, plans, and policies supporting the HR function. Developing models for managing competency levels of the HR of the organization.

Determining and handling employee requirements. Recruit or source the candidates as per the requirements. Screen and select the most appropriate candidates. Take care of the newly hired and re-hired employees. Maintain records of information for all applicants.

records.process_name: Manage employee onboarding, training, and development
records.description: Assisting employees in developing their capabilities, and providing them counseling services. Handle the orientation and deployment of the employees. Administer the performance of employees. Administer the development and enhancement of the employees. Provide training and development programs for employees.

Assisting general management in developing, maintaining, and improving employee relationships. This is accomplished through communication, performance management, processing grievances, and/or dispute. Interpret and convey organizational policies.

Creating frameworks for rewarding and recognizing employees with the objective of retaining them. Create and manage programs for provision of rewards, recognition, and motivation. Manage and administer the benefits for employees. Help assist and retain employees. Administer payroll to employees.

Managing employee mobility and retirement. Manage the process of employee promotion and demotion. Administer separation, retirement, and leaves of absence. Outplace employees. Deploy personnel. Relocate employees in order to manage assignments.

Managing the employee reporting processes, employee inquiry process, employee information and data, and the HR information systems. Create and administer the employee metrics. Develop and handle the time and attendance systems. Refurbish the indicators for employee retention and motivation.
Creating an effective plan that initiates and promotes communication and engagement among the employees and between employees and management.

records.process_name: Develop and manage IT customer relationships
records.description: Creating and administering relationships with IT customers. Understanding customer needs including high-level business requirements for IT transformation. Plan for and communicate IT services along with establishing IT service levels, providing transformation guidance, and performance analysis that foster IT customer relationships.

records.process_name: Develop and manage IT business strategy
records.description: Handling the business of IT. Create a organization-wide strategy for the IT function. Define the organization's IT architecture. Manage the IT portfolio. Research and innovate in the field of IT. Assess and convey the performance and the value of the IT function.

records.process_name: Develop and manage IT resilience and risk
records.description: Develop and include the processes required to rapidly adapt and respond to any internal or external opportunity, demand, disruption, or threat to IT and cybersecurity. Build a dynamic, strategic, and integrated approach to managing IT and cyber risks, compliance obligations, and resilience, while ensuring alignment with global standards and frameworks.
Creating strategies to manage the organization's information and content. Outline the architecture for information. Administer information resources. Administer the management of data and content.
Designing and maintaining the IT services/solutions catalogue. Evaluate the performance of IT services/solutions. Communicate the results to the management.
Executing IT services/solutions by creating a strategy for deployment. Plan and execute the changes. Plan and administer the release of its IT services and solutions.

Establishing and managing services for providing support to users of IT services and solutions. Define the plethora of services by which the organization assists users of computers, software products, or other information technology products.

Determining different stages of the planning process and accounting. Classify, determine, analyze, interpret, and communicate information to make up-to-date business decisions for better management and control functions.
Comparing revenue targets to reality. Review all transactions and entries passed in final accounts in a year in order to examine profits.

Making statements about business activities and functions. Prepare financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, statement of cash flows, and statement of stockholders' equity) according to accounting concepts and principles.
Managing accounts for large funds-invested projects. Manage and account for fixed assets projects (capital projects), which required significant capital investments over many years.
Handling reporting time, managing pay, and processing taxes from salaries. Pay employees. Withhold taxes. Confirm the correct funds are paid to the correct government agency.

records.process_name: Process accounts payable and expense reimbursements
records.description: Handling bills and reimbursements to be made. Make payments for goods or services taken or used on behalf of the organization.

Managing business's investments in trading in bonds, currencies, financial derivatives, etc. Manage the financial assets and holdings of the organization. Optimize the organization's liquidity. Invest excess cash. Reduce financial risks.

Administering internal controls. This process requires the organization to manage entity's board of trustees, management, and other personnel in order to offer judicious assurance about the achievement of effectiveness, proficiency of operations, and reliability of financial reporting.
Estimating the organization's periodic tax liabilities. Ensure that appropriate taxing authorities receive tax return filings and payments when due.

Managing cash collections and disbursements made by operating units across the enterprise. When appropriate, transfer cash from the operating units to parent-level bank accounts managed by the organization's treasury team.
Making and collecting payments for transactions in products/services, and transporting them to interested markets.
Planning, acquiring, and managing facilities, workspaces, and supporting assets. Acquire, configure, and manage facilities and workspaces, to include supporting equipment and materials.

Designing and constructing assets such as machines, tools, factories, etc. Manage steps to acquire assets including managing capital, as well as planning, scheduling, and overseeing acquisition/construction.
Preserving assets through the planning, managing, and performance of preventative, routine, and critical maintenance work.

Managing the disposition of assets at their end-of-life. End-of-life for an asset may be due to obsolescence, replacement, excess capacity, or disrepair among other potential factors. Steps may include decommissioning, disassembly, recycling, etc. Tracking and reporting may also be appropriate for some or all asset types due to law, regulation, or social/environmental responsibility.

Creating requisite frameworks and coordinating all risk management activities for the entire organization and each function. Manage the enterprise risk by outlining the risk policies and procedures. Monitor and communicate all risk management activities. Encourage correspondence among the business units. Manage the risk of all business units and functions.
Managing steps to confirm enduring compliance to industry regulations and government legislation.

Administering the efforts and activities for remediation. This process element requires the organization to create plans for corrective action in collaboration with government agencies and pertinent professional services agencies which specialize in remediation efforts relevant to the organization's operations. Additionally, the organization needs to consult experts to validate the plan, determine resources allocation, resolve any legal concerns, and formulate a company-wide policy for remediation.

Including the processes required to rapidly adapt and respond to any internal or external opportunity, demand, disruption, or threat. Develop a more dynamic, strategic, and integrated approach to managing compliance obligations.

Creating a strategic management responsibility for integrating finance, communication, marketing, and securities law compliance. Allow the most effective two-way communication among the organization, the financial community, and other constituencies.
