Designing key measures that analyze and interpret how effectively the business is achieving its objectives.
Deciding on the appropriate amount of supervisions that are needed to effectively assess the performance of business plans.
Consolidating acquired metrics and trends. Provide data that can be benchmarked against historical data.
Measuring the performance of process planning. Quantify the performance, record results of the performance tests, and report them to the appropriate authority.
Recognizing the trends in performance. Carefully and strategically assess the results in order to effectively spot the trends.
Evaluating the gaps between achieved and benchmarked performance. Analyze how performance differs from the optimal or expected performance.

Creating reports that systematically record and represent the performance planning. Construct a detailed report specifying the performance, and include indicators such as the performance gaps, performance trends, and analysis.
Using performance indicators to report, analyze, and create a detailed performance improvement plan to bridge the performance gaps.

records.process_name: Evaluate environmental impact of products, services, and operations
records.description: Evaluating the impact of offerings and the auxiliary operations required to process them on the immediate ecosystem and the environment at large. Study the lifecycle of the products/services offered by the organization. Estimate any affect on the environment through metrics such as a calculation of carbon footprint.

records.process_name: Conduct health and safety and environmental audits
records.description: Conducting an inspection to verify that the organization adequately complies with the environmental, health, and safety standards. Audit procedures and records regarding responsibility for the environment, health, and safety.

Determining any protocols or standards to comply with, set by regulatory agencies or the organization's stakeholders. Closely examine all standards and matters of compliance relating to the environment, health, and safety.

Evaluating any risks and opportunities that might affect the environmental, health, and safety of products/services. Leverage techniques such as cost-benefit analysis, trend extrapolation, systems analysis, social surveys, historical surveys, historical analogy, Delphi, conferences, workshops, briefings, hearings, advisory committees, moot courts, artistic judgment, on-site field investigation, scaling techniques, and scenario creation.

Creating a plan for managing the environmental, health, and safety impact of products/services. Establish minimum requirements for the organization regarding the environment at large and the health and safety of employees. Develop policies, written procedures, and supporting tools to dictate how the organization will meet policy requirements.
Recording and managing all events and activities associated with complying with environmental, health and safety standards. Create event calendars. Assign funds. Educate employees. Conduct events.
Administering the costs and benefits of EHS management program. Evaluate program costs to ensure that the benefits of the program always outweigh its costs.

Using performance techniques and indicators. Utilize number of audits or inspections performed, safety committee meetings, the number and types of findings and observations, timely preventive maintenance tasks performed, etc.

Implementing a program for organizing, coordinating, and directing available resources to respond to the event. Conduct a risk assessment to identify potential emergency scenarios in order to create a program that ensures that resources are on hand--or quickly available--in case of emergencies.

Implementing a program that reduces or eliminates the creation of pollutants through increased efficiency in the use of raw materials, energy, water, or other resources. Implement a program to inspect facilities that store, manufacture, or use hazardous, toxic, or polluting materials.
Conducting programs such as on-the-job training sessions, group training workshops, and online training.

Supporting employees in light of the organization's environmental, health, and safety policies and standards. Provide medical insurance, maternity leave, environmental education, training over safety, etc.

Identifying, documenting, and communicating sustainability requirements. Closely examine all standards and matters of compliance relating to ESG. Determine protocols or standards to comply with, set by regulatory agencies or the organizations stakeholders.

Establishing organizational sustainability goals/objectives. Gather, align, and promote organization-wide sustainability goals that collectively address the overall sustainability requirements. Ensure the goals are measurable and have qualitative and quantitative targets.
Establishing, documenting, and communicating sustainability policies. Develop policies, written procedures, and supporting tools to dictate how the organization will meet policy requirements.
Defining sustainability measures. Provide organization-wide measures, to include data collection strategies, calculations, analytics, and reporting formats.

Creating sustainability plans. Develop and socialize sustainability plans for the organization, functional units, and support services. Ensure alignment to sustainability requirements, goals, and governance.
Providing sustainability training and awareness. Plan, prepare, and oversee delivery of sustainability education and enablement activities.
Providing support for sustainability activities. Augment functional units and support teams with coaching, mentoring, and SME capacity to perform sustainability projects and activities.
Conducting and supporting sustainability reporting. Collect, analyze, and report sustainability performance to requirements. Align reporting across functional units and support teams.

Appraising entities identified as being suitable for acquisition, taking into account the restructuring opportunities in the internal and external context. Verify the appropriateness and viability of the short-listed options. Ensure these entities pertain to the state-of-affairs in the market, as well as fit with the resources and capabilities of the organization.

Appraising entities identified as being suitable for a merger, taking stock of the restructuring opportunities within the firm and the market. Verify the appropriateness and viability of such options. Assess these entities to ensure their pertinence to the contextual state-of-affairs in the market, as well as a fit with the resources and capabilities of the organization itself. (This process can be carried out, in its entirety, by qualified in-house personnel or may be designated to specialist professional services providers.)

Evaluating departments and subsidiaries within the organization, and/or previously merged entities, to assess the appropriateness of a de-merger, taking account of the fit between these entities as well as any relevant externalities. Examine the pertinence and soundness of a formalized dissociation.

Evaluating departments and/or subsidiaries within the organization to assess the appropriateness of a divestment, taking account of all market externalities. Examine any internal entities that have been identified to be suitable for dismemberment from the organization. Ensure the pertinence and soundness of such a move.

records.process_name: Select partnerships and relationships to support the extended enterprise
records.description: Supporting the design, manufacture and distribution of product and services through the extended enterprise model.  This is concerned with the strategic decisions on make vs buy, in house or out sourced.  Senior Executives map out how they want to run their business.  Make strategic choices as to whether to buy in components / sub-assemblies, run their own distribution fleet or contract out, own their dealerships or franchise out, etc.  Strategize with partnerships. Collaborate design consideration at strategy level for automotive and procurement act within the Target Operating Model set at strategy level.

records.process_name: Identify implications for key operating model business elements that require change
records.description: Determine impacts of elements such as staffing, skills, training, new markets, technology, or policies within operating model which needs change.

records.process_name: Identify implications for key technology aspects
records.description: Determining key factors for technology ROI, benefits, architecture, etc.

Creating methods to gauge customer experiences, expectations, and suggestions. Review both liked and disliked areas of product/services to be delivered. Evaluate touchpoints based on the nature of product/service in the market e.g., billboards, web sites, direct mail, service calls, etc.

Evaluating customer experiences, expectations, and suggestions in both liked and disliked areas of the product or services. Analyze all modes of communication, human and physical interactions, or customers experience during the relationship lifecycle with your organization. Evaluate the gaps/further development/alterations to the existing product/service to attain better customer response.

records.process_name: Perform root cause analysis of problematic customer experiences
records.description: Analyzing the core reason for the customer experience/feedback/response about the product/service to take considerable action for better customer experience.

Identifying a set of characteristics that define the demographic and behavioral patterns of the customer. Further, use persona scoring to design your marketing strategies around personas, and measure and optimize your interactions with the contacts classified by a certain persona.
Creating a story of the customer's experience: from initial contact, through the process of engagement and into a long-term relationship. The goal is to teach organization about the customer.

records.process_name: Define single view of the customer for the organization
records.description: Defining parameters to show aggregated, consistent, and holistic representation of known data about customers. Define key parameters which enable the tracking of customers and communications across every channel.

records.process_name: Define a vision for the customer experience
records.description: Establishing a direction and vision on how the organization behaves towards customers in a consistent, effective way. The key attributes for customer experience vision consists of emotional connection, commitments and expectations, compelling value proposition, and ease of understanding the organization's behavior.

Creating a process to validate the sales process and the assumptions that underpin the business model. Understand if the products/services have a repeatable, scalable business model around that product.

records.process_name: Align experience with brand values and business strategies
records.description: Aligning and defining a relevant, differentiated, and credible value proposition for the brand. Align experience to ensure that the product and service quality is consistent with brand promise and business strategies.

Planning, development, and management of content-written or in other media. Getting the right content to the right user at the right time through strategic planning of content creation, delivery, and governance.
Determining the necessary skills and competencies required to efficiently collect customer experiences through the support structure.
Identifying the affect of customer experience through customer experience support structure on other functions of customer services related to customer.

records.process_name: Carry out post launch analytics to test the acceptability in the market
records.description: Measuring the performance of marketing once the product/services are launched. This broadly covers measuring user engagement and product's/service's performance in the market.

Conducting customer and market analysis to review progress and identify opportunities for increasing market position. Track and review product/service response through sales reports, website statistics, direct response from customers, and survey reports.

records.process_name: Review effectiveness of supply chain and distribution network
records.description: Determining the performance of supply chain to all departments and logistics from input to shop floor. Seeking performance reviews at each intersection and communication channels. Review effectiveness of supply chain and distribution to check if it is meeting the demands of the various groups and organizations that are concerned with its activities (groups might include customers, partners, suppliers, and vendors).

records.process_name: Apply data and analytics to review supply chain methodologies
records.description: Collecting and examining raw data with the purpose of drawing conclusions about that information and correlate gaps and efficiencies to the existing supply chain channels. Apply the information to make better business decisions to the related supply chain methodologies to meet efficiency.

records.process_name: Review quality and performance of the product/service
records.description: Identifying the quality and performance of the product/service delivered to customers. Analyze data from the customer feedback, audits, measures of customer satisfaction (such as product quality complaints and recalls), and organizational policies on delivery.
Evaluating organization's financial reports and financial reporting processes. Review and document the ROI catered by the product/service delivery to the customer in the market.

records.process_name: Conduct new product development process assessment
records.description: Analyzing the steps involved in the development of new product, its effect on existing product, resources, and functions related to the development of the new product until its sale in the competitive market place.

records.process_name: Train employees on appropriate regulatory requirements
records.description: Conducting training and impart learning to existing and new employees. Training will relate to the most recent/enforced regulations of the business to meet Manage regulatory requirements [12771].

Identifying steps and procedures to manage and regularly update the records for regulatory agencies. Updates will be made to safety procedures, identity and access management, software tools and applications, internal accessibility policies, internal quality parameters, etc.
Determine and follow the timely input and update of regulatory information by assessing reforms, regulatory policies, and guidelines.
Determining the operations of functions related to the product/service in the marketing environment.

records.process_name: Derive interoperability requirements for products and services
records.description: Determining the ability of products and services to work together, exchange and use information in a multi-vendor, multi-network, and multi-service environment.

records.process_name: Derive safety requirements for products and services
records.description: Developing safety requirements in line with environmental safety, occupational health and safety, and community health and safety guidelines.

records.process_name: Derive security requirements for products and services
records.description: Implementing security requirements through authentication and encryption of CE device data stream.  Utilize security measures such as cryptographic protocols and hardware security (smart cards).
Meeting regulatory requirements set forth by such directives as RoHS, WEEE, ELV, and REACH.
Complying with consumer electronic industry standards developed by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA).
Identifying and creating steps and tools to develop the user experience.
Productizing the service by defining the scope of the service/cost.  Target market for the service and make the service more tangible.

records.process_name: Identify requirements for product/service design/development partners
records.description: Determining essential elements for collaborators involved in blueprint/development of product/service.
Carrying out the steps necessary to appropriately manufacture correct parts.  This includes designing application, product hardware, mold, casting, mechanical, and electrical aspects of the product.
Creating product application service view to allow for product servicing and refurbishing.
Replacing core components and republishing.
Reviewing the design and approach for troubleshooting the product.

records.process_name: Design and manage product data, design, and bill of materials
records.description: Designing the BOM-Bill of material, manufacturing BOM and Service BOMA bill of materials list for all the raw materials and components/parts used in the producing end product.
Designing hardware and software upgrade techniques.
Regularly monitoring production runs of the production and/or delivery operations.

records.process_name: Understand consumer needs and historical behaviors
records.description: Identifying the factors that drive the targeted market segment. Model customer purchasing patterns, and forecast their future purchasing behavior.
Using customer segmentation tools to examine past customer behavior to predict future purchasing patterns.

Determining the increase or decrease of the company's sales volume in the targeted markets. Conduct an analysis to determine the factors and underlying causes that affect the changes in the demand for products or services offered. Consider changes in offerings or in the business strategy to regain or increase the market share.

records.process_name: Identify under-served and saturated market segments
records.description: Determining which groups of potential customers do not yet, or already do have access to the product or a service that the company produces or markets. Use those findings to create specialized product offerings and differentiated marketing campaigns.

Validating identified market opportunities by testing company's offerings on limited-size samples of the consumer population that are hypothesized to be representative of the target market at large and to have similar purchasing behavior. The feedback gained through consumer testing can be used to modify or reject product offerings before their full scale launch, saving the company valuable resources, should the initial offering not be successful.

Verifying that the company has sufficient infrastructure and resources to deliver their offerings in a timely and cost-effective manner, and that it is able to scale up from the small-scale market samples, used for consumer testing, to the entire identified market segment.

Devising a strategy to market company's products or services seamlessly through all or most channels that are in widespread use among the target market. This may mean cross-channel access to customer preferences and purchasing history to accept returned merchandise, provide refunds, resolve payment issues or to provide technical support.

Identifying necessary preconditions that a channel should fulfill in order to be included as one of the adopted channels, such as required throughput capacities, service capabilities, competitive pricing, and alignment with organizational marketing strategies.

Determining the detailed policies and procedures that each of the channels needs to follow in order to conform to the organizational marketing strategy and to provide seamless customer service experience.

Communicating with customers and prospects with the intent of creating sales opportunities. Reach out to existing and prospective customers through alternate media and networking channels, apart from cold calling/emailing.
Capitalizing on sales calls by pitching on bids and closing deals. Outline the nature and scope of the work, draft agreement terms, prepare proposals and agreements, and propose timelines and prices.

Arranging and leading meetings, seminars, workshops and training events with customers to educate them about current offerings, best practices and technological advances to provide more value to customers and to increase their attrition and loyalty.
Formalizing a sale by reaching an agreement on terms of the deal. Negotiate on the price, and reach a consensus on the terms and conditions.

Completing all the paper-work associated with the sale of its products/services. Exchange any pertinent legal/financial information required for completing the sale, signing of a contract/work-order, and issuing copies of bills/invoices.

records.process_name: Collect and merge internal and third-party customer information
records.description: Gathering the data about customers. Combine the information available locally with the data obtained from external sources.
Eliminating redundant information in customer data.
Managing essential information of customer accounts.
Obtaining detailed information about customers.
Altering information about involved parties.
Documenting address information.
Documenting contact information.

records.process_name: Record key customer communication profile details
records.description: Providing information about important business rules regarding communicating with customers.
Revising information about involved parties.
Dismissing information about involved parties.
Provide training and certification to develop strategies for marketing-driven sales.
Reviewing, processing and issuing certifications and accrediting skills and competencies.
Backing sales partners and strategic alliances.
Creating and applying technology to monitor and control the production and delivery of products and services. Automation involves a broad range of technologies.

Including a broad range of techniques and technologies implemented within industrial process control systems that are routinely reviewed, audited, and improved, advanced process controls typically address particular performance or economic improvement opportunities. An advanced set of process control measures can be used to reduce variation and identify primary improvement options. Results of analysis are fed back into process design for incorporation into production.

Helping organizations increase performance and efficiency, real-time optimization is a category of closed-loop process control that aims at optimizing process performance in real time for systems. It is normally built upon model-based optimization systems and is usually large scale. Real-time optimization automatically detects errors, and can modify and eliminate both random and non-random errors, as well as analyze and monitor all systems involved.

Applying human factors and instrumentation engineering and systems thinking to manage the design of an alarm or alert system to increase its usability. Typical challenges include having too many alarms in a plant, poorly designed alarms/alerts, improperly set alarm/alert points, unclear alarm/alert messages, etc. Poor alarm management is one of the leading causes of unplanned downtime.
Implement a checks and balances system to verify that returned parts meet acceptable quality standards to determine appropriate disposition activity.

Executing activities for reinstating the returned products. Present the customer with additional incentives of compensation in case of any defective products delivery or any discrepancy in the product specifications in order to save the order from being permanently returned.

Administering the reinstatement of the returned product in order to return them back to customers. Repair or remanufacture the defective or ineffective products returned by the customer. Process the delivery of the repaired or remanufactured products back to the customer.

Moving a returned product back to inventory or stock. Whether a product is sufficient as returned, repaired, or refurbished, moving that product back to inventory for resale or returning to customer is the fnal step in Manage disposition of returned products.

Soliciting or acquiring information using various sources such as databases, customer interactions, and customer request forms. Hand them further up the hierarchy to deal with them. Categorize the user's request, determining if the request is supportable and prioritizing the request.
Documenting the individual customer service requirements solicited, along with personal information of the customers, in order to generate customized profiles that hasten the delivery process.

Designing a short-term agreement between the service provider and customer. One-time services are ordered by the service recipient and resource-related billing is performed upon completion. Use the service order to document service and customer service work.

Developing a plan for sourcing and deploying the resources required to fulfill customer service needs. Document a detailed summary of all types of resources (equipment, finance, personnel, time, etc.) required to complete customer service requests and procure these resources. Identify and assess various sources in order to effectively create a resourcing plan.

records.process_name: Create last mile delivery service order fulfillment schedule
records.description: Designing a detailed summary of customer service order requirements, along with information concerning the timing and duration for these services. Categorize the customer needs. Monitor the services delivered.

records.process_name: Organize daily last mile delivery order fulfillment schedule
records.description: Laying out a daily plan of specific service orders that need to be fulfilled. Document and systematically order these activities to ensure high effectiveness and efficiency.
Dispatching and delivering the resources needed for the specific service requirements from the source/warehouse. Manage the dispatch, transportation, and delivery of the services.

records.process_name: Manage last mile delivery order fulfillment
records.description: Handling and managing orders fulfilled, along with the orders are not or partially fulfilled to track the order fulfillment progress. Use electronic devices such as trackers and GPS in order track and ensure delivery of the orders.

records.process_name: Identify completed last mile delivery orders for feedback
records.description: Determining the service orders that have been successfully delivered. Identify the service orders completed and delivered to the customer. Leverage communication systems to ensure coordination with the customers in order to avoid mishaps.

records.process_name: Identify incomplete last mile delivery orders and last mile delivery service failures
records.description: Determining orders which have not been completed or delivered. Identify the service orders that are partially or entirely incomplete, as well as the orders that have not been delivered to the customer. Use techniques such as project trackers to recognize the progress of the service orders.

records.process_name: Solicit customer feedback on last mile services delivered
records.description: Obtaining and procuring customer reviews or feedback on the services delivered. Design a customer feedback form, or communicate with the customer through the phone or online.

records.process_name: Process customer feedback on last mile services delivered
records.description: Assessing and incorporating customer reviews/feedback into the service plan to ensure high quality of service.
Providing the workforce with a plan of action and goals necessary to provide a service. Make sure that those objectives are met.

Establishing guidelines for how resources engage with the customer. For example, set rules of accountability, interaction, and accommodation when engaging the customer. Resources should be polite, empathetic, and attentive.

Defining the issue of the claim. The warranty team will look into the issue and understand whether it is covered by the claim code or if more detail is required. Field service will be scheduled to further qualify the definition of the issue and to collect more evidence.

Scheduling additional investigative field service. This is performed for high priority claims or claims that require additional investigation. Field service engineers will gather additional information, perform further investigation, and qualify the definition of the issue.
Requesting receipt of a defective part for further investigation.

Investigating claims by an appropriate functional representative. Once the issue has been clearly defined and diagnosed and a recommendation for corrective action is determined, it will be provided to the warranty management team.

records.process_name: Receive investigation result/recommendation for corrective action
records.description: Receiving investigative results to assess claim approval or denial. The warranty team will assess the results of the investigation and the recommendations for corrective action.

records.description: Determining orders which have not been completed or delivered. Use techniques such as project trackers to recognize the progress of the service orders.

records.process_name: Solicit customer feedback on services delivered
records.description: Obtaining and procuring customer reviews or feedback on the services delivered. Design a customer feedback form, or communicate with the customer through the phone or online.

records.process_name: Process customer feedback on services delivered
records.description: Assessing and incorporating customer reviews/feedback into the service plan to ensure high quality of service.

records.process_name: Develop and manage strategic workforce planning framework
records.description: Defining and maintaining the structure, principles, and approaches used to assess workforce supply and demand, capabilities, and gaps over the strategic planning horizon.

Determining the requirements for employees and the need for employee resourcing for each unit/function. Lay out a plan detailing employee resourcing requirements of individual functions and the organization as a whole.

records.process_name: Advise business in implementing strategic workforce planning
records.description: Providing guidance and expertise to business leaders on applying the strategic workforce planning framework to inform workforce decisions, plans, and initiatives.

records.process_name: Partner with the business to execute workforce plan
records.description: Collaborating with business leaders to translate workforce plans into actionable initiatives and to support execution of agreed workforce actions.

records.process_name: Monitor and adjust strategic workforce plan
records.description: Tracking workforce outcomes and changes in business needs to update workforce plans and address emerging gaps, risks, or opportunities.

records.process_name: Establish wages, salaries, and benefits strategy
records.description: Defining the strategic approach for wages, salaries, and benefits to support workforce attraction, retention, performance, and alignment with organizational objectives and market conditions.

Creating a scheme of rewards and recognition for employees to promote a results-based culture. Create specific incentives to reach desired outcomes, such as landing key clients, growing the customer base, providing exceptional servicing, and increasing profit margins.
Defining the approach to severance pay, including principles and guidelines, to support workforce transitions while managing financial, legal, and reputational considerations.

records.process_name: Complete position classification and level of experience
records.description: Identifying the requirements for the position to be filled. Determine the experience and skills necessary to perform the tasks outlined.
Determining roles that are essential to organizational performance or continuity and that require succession planning.
Identifying and selecting employees with the potential to assume critical roles based on defined criteria and future capability requirements.

records.process_name: Develop and implement individual succession plans
records.description: Creating and executing development plans for identified successors to prepare them for future roles through targeted learning and experience opportunities.
Reviewing succession plans on a regular basis and updating them to reflect changes in roles, talent, organizational priorities, and performance outcomes.
Coordinating with third party certification authorities to provide training and certifications for necessary skills.
Providing tests to the workforce that will satisfy completion of certifications.
Ascertaining the experience level needed to qualify for a specific job or certification within the organization. Some certificates require practical experience as well as training programs.
Administering certificates to all candidates that have successfully met experience qualifications, and passed all tests necessary to obtain the certificate.
Creation and execution of a plan that might allow for work from home days, or alternate hours.
Managing transportation-related programs and services provided to employees to support commuting, mobility, and work/life balance objectives.

records.process_name: Align IT risk management with cybersecurity frameworks
records.description: Include alignment with established cybersecurity frameworks like NIST CSF, ISO 27001, and ENISA risk management guidelines.

records.process_name: Integrate IT and OT risk management strategies
records.description: Ensure risk management processes are extended to cover OT systems and environments.
Adopting MFA to ensure secure user authentication across all systems.

records.process_name: Implement identity federation and single sign-on (SSO)
records.description: Integrating identity federation and SSO solutions to enhance user experience and security.

records.process_name: Assess and validate IT service/solution requirements
records.description: Evaluating and validating the requirements and needs of IT service/solution.
Formulating a design for service/solution that helps an organization to meet its objectives. Develop a new framework for molding the service/solution processes into a coherent and structured form.

records.process_name: Build and test IT service/solution components
records.description: Building and testing new components required for the development of IT services and solutions.
Combining the newly built IT component along with IT services in order to gain optimum output.
Validating that the proposed IT service/solution is feasible and provides the needed services for the customer.

Creating and implementing a strategy for the deployment of IT service/solution by defining all of the activities that make the IT function available for use. Define the deployment process, procedures, and tools. Select the most feasible and practical methodologies for the deployment process.
Identifying and resolving internal needs/inquiries for service/solution that cannot be resolved immediately. Research inquiries that require the need of exceptional solutions.
Evaluate plans to address information technology environmental adulteration for rectification efforts.
Redesign the roadmap to seek solution or service with an overall process flow and impact timeframe.

Administering the efforts and activities for IT service/solution remediation. This process element requires the organization to create plans for corrective action in collaboration with government agencies and pertinent professional services agencies which specialize in remediation efforts relevant to the organization's service/solution. Additionally, the organization needs to consult experts to validate the plan, determine resources allocation, resolve any legal concerns, and formulate a company-wide policy for IT service/solution remediation.

Understanding customer requirements. Managing services/solutions based on the requirements. Develop components for providing the requirements. Train resources to provide support. Confirm the customer experience post-sale. Evaluate the performance of service/solution. Communicate the results to the management.
Developing packaging for fixed/enhanced service/solution based on the standalone or bundled offerings to be used by the organization.
Scheduling resources to provide service delivery to IT users. Ensure design, development, deployment, and operations are aligned with the business objectives.
Maintaining and scheduling batch jobs to run in the background at a certain date and time.
Determine the timely change or release of IT services or support. Assign periodic release/change to IT systems or services.
Schedule or optimize backup and archive activities for IT services and solutions. Use a backup system or application and archive operations data for future retrieval.

records.process_name: Balance operational workloads across available infrastructure components
records.description: Balancing workloads of all the processes and services that are provisioned to their internal or external clients, across available components of IT infrastructure. No component should be over or under utilized with the workflow of the IT operations.
Determining process and procedure to provide support for specific IT service problems.
Collecting and storing data that pertains to interest rate markets.

records.process_name: Determine interest rate exposure for all markets
records.description: Identifying potential interest rate risks for all markets.

records.process_name: Determine interest rate hedge requirements in accordance with risk policy
records.description: Deciding the requirements on interest rate investments that are made by trading in futures or options market, on the basis of the accepted risk policy.
Performing trading on interest rates.
Handling and processing information about changes in foreign exchange rates.

records.process_name: Determine foreign exchange exposure for all currencies
records.description: Establishing potential foreign exchange risks for all currencies.

records.process_name: Determine foreign exchange hedge requirements in accordance with risk policy
records.description: Deciding the requirements on investments in foreign exchange made by trading in futures or options market, on the basis of current risk policy.
Executing all aspects for foreign exchange trade within foreign exchange market. This includes buying, selling, and exchanging currencies at the current or expressed price point.

records.process_name: Manage foreign exchange balance sheet risk
records.description: Overseeing the foreign exchange balance sheet with an eye towards potential risk. Risks include changes in conversion rates between the time the transaction occurred and when it is completed, or when transactions are made in a denomination other than that of the organization's base currency.

records.process_name: Determine current customer exposures and limit exceptions
records.description: Establishing ongoing risks that the customers face, and the exceptions to exceeded limits.
Settling cases that involve violations of customer exposure limit.
Handling customer securities to recover loans that are not paid back.
Conducting reviews to assess customer credit on a yearly basis. Introduce changes or make recommendations, if needed.
Evaluating investments made in some market to offset the risks of investing in a contrary or opposing market.
Determining which hedge options to execute.
Closing out a position or cashing in derivatives early.
Examining options in the market for hedging investments. Select an option.
Revising credit reports periodically for accurateness and changes that could be suggestive of duplicitous activity.
Evaluating the changing needs for insurance coverage. Research available insurance providers and offerings.
Realizing those practices and procedures that are the most effective to the success of the business and making that information available.
Determining the need for additional performance indicators that would be necessary to successfully achieve the business goal.
Recognizing and defining what the project is ultimately supposed to do. Specify the capabilities, features, or attributes of the project's deliverables, as well as any kind of formal documentation.

Identifying the prerequisites of business projects. Identify the people with appropriate and applicable skills and competencies. Locate resources such as capital, facilities, equipment, material, and information required to accomplish the objectives of a specific project.

records.process_name: Assess culture and readiness for project management approach
records.description: Evaluating the culture and readiness of the organizational environment is order to implement the project management approach.
Creating a document that includes the current situation, proposed solution, financial analysis, conclusion, etc. Convince a decision maker and investors to approve the project. Obtain funding.

Developing procedures and indictors to assess performance of business projects. Design and develop metrics and indicators--such as cost, schedule, resources, risk, and quality--that exhibit the performance of the business projects.

records.process_name: Prioritize and select projects for the portfolio
records.description: Stack ranking of projects in the portfolio based upon preestablished criteria.
Outlining the resources and their roles in the business projects.
Procuring the necessary resources outlined in Define roles and resources [11123]

Determining the IT requirements for specific business projects. Identify the requirements of computers and telecommunications equipment to store, retrieve, transmit, and manipulate data related to the project. Consider factors such as functional requirements, design requirements, project phases, and project schedule.

Designing a plan for equipping the project team with the necessary skills and abilities to fulfill their roles and responsibilities in the project effectively and efficiently. Offer formal training, mentoring, or coaching. Initiate informal conversations. Communicate messages during the project.
Creating a plan for recognizing and rewarding extraordinary performances within the business projects. Use incentives, bonuses, and certificates for recognition and rewarding purposes.

records.process_name: Design and plan launch of project
records.description: Creating a plan specifying when to initiate the project, and introducing it to the target audience. Clearly define the project team, objectives, timelines, and milestone.
Putting the project into position by effectively bringing it into action.

records.process_name: Evaluate impact of project management (strategy and projects) on measures and outcomes
records.description: Assessing the impact of business project management on the measures and outcomes of the projects. Gauge non-financial measures, frequency of measurement, action plan, etc.
Recording and documenting the current status and position of the project. Record and report items such as completed tasks, incomplete tasks, planned tasks, and problems faced.

Determining and documenting a list of specific project goals, deliverables, tasks, costs, and deadlines. Use the scope statement to explain the boundaries of the project. Assign responsibilities for team members. Set up procedures for verifying and approving the completed tasks.

records.process_name: Promote and sustain activity and involvement
records.description: Encouraging and sustaining the activities and involvement while executing projects. Promote the execution activities of the projects. Encourage employee involvement in project implementation.

records.process_name: Conduct Project Reviews with Program Managers and other stakeholders
records.description: Hold post project reviews, lessons learned, or After Action Reviews (AARs) at the end of each project to understand what could be improved during future projects.

records.process_name: Realign and refresh project management strategy and approaches
records.description: Reorganizing and stimulating the approach and strategy for managing business projects. Make improvements based on the project scope and on findings from Evaluate the impact of project management (strategy and projects) on measures and outcomes [11131].
Changes to project plans based upon internal and or external influences on the project.  This would include the update to the project plan file, as well as the communication to the team.

records.process_name: Define process steps for controls (or integration points)
records.description: Establishing the steps for developing quality controls. Conduct Alpha testing. Have the product team conduct rework. Send the product/service for Beta testing, and carry on rework as needed.

Establishing a detailed summary including measures, on which material, in what manner, and by whom. Identify the parameters to be measured, the range of possible values, and the required resolution. Provide a sampling scheme that details how and when samples will be taken. Select sample sizes. Assign roles and responsibilities.

Using tools to measure quality. Use tools such as quality improvement oversight system tool, performance measurement tools, consumer information models/guides, and validation tools to effectively determine the quality levels.
Defining the competencies required for developing quality controls. Define the required competencies including compliance management, audit management, and document control and document management.

Evaluating quality performance through periodic or episodic testing against the established standards for quality characteristics. For periodic testing, design a schedule with sufficient time to make any required adjustments to the process or system to maintain the desired level of quality. For episodic testing, conduct a test whenever a known non-conformance or fault occurs, which results in outputs or outcomes known to be unsatisfactory to performance requirements.
Maintaining and recording the results of Test against the quality plan [17483] electronically and in standard formats. Assign ownership to a designated function or role.

Deciding whether to take any additional actions based on the results of quality tests. Initiate a quarantine disposition and relocated inventory, scrap workflow item and scrap transaction, rework operation, net-able and nonnet-able items, and the activity list.

Assessing the significance of the sample chosen for the test in order to determine whether or not the sample is representative of the larger output or outcome. Determine if the sample meets or does not meet the requirements. Identify the conditions for acceptance, rejection, remediation, and prevention.

Outlining the major facts and figures of the quality test results in order to provide insights and information. Use charts, tables, statistical test results, and written findings and conclusions in a summary of results.

Recommending measures for improvement. Assess the summarized results to identify areas which can be improved. Suggest actions to management for improving the quality plan basis on the results of the tests.
Selecting the subsequent actions that the organization can adopt for improving the enterprise quality. Select measures and recommended actions for managing the enterprise quality.

Provisioning rewards for achieving quality excellence. Provide monetary and nonmonetary rewards such as compensation, vacations, gift cards, and reimbursements to employees in in recognition of their services, efforts, and achievements in quality excellence.

Establishing and maintaining partnerships with third-party sources to achieve quality excellence. Source and evaluate third-party sources both public and private to ensure that the most effective and efficient partnerships are formed.

Maintaining a common denominator for the competency level within the organization's talent circle. Conduct training sessions, skill development activities, and quality excellence activities to ensure that the resources of the organization are competent enough and have the capabilities to achieve the required level of quality.

records.process_name: Incorporate EQMS messaging into communication channels
records.description: Assimilating all the communication related to the EQMS into the organization's already established communication channels.

records.process_name: Assure independent EQMS management access to appropriate authority in the organization
records.description: Ensuring EQMS access to the person in charge of the quality management process. Establish who has the authority to manage the EQMS. Ensure access of EQMS to only the person(s) in authority.

Recording and transferring the best practices and proven methods associated with enterprise quality management systems (EQMS) that can be leveraged in improving the organization's framework. Record proven methodologies and approaches with the objective of communicating them for upgrading, refining, and enhancing the organization's systems.

Defining and communicating sustainability disclosure requirements. Clarify and align disclosure requirements to other organizational reporting requirements and needs. Integrate preparation and reporting activities.
Defining governance requirements for sustainability. Include structure, roles, alignment to organization models, processes and standards to be applied.

records.process_name: Define sustainability functional and performance requirements
records.description: Defining functional and performance requirements for sustainability. Align with ESG strategies, goals, and the implementation of sustainability efforts across the organization, provide a roadmap and visibility to shared and collective requirements.

Measuring sustainability performance. Setup, collect, and validate sustainability data. Conduct audits and inspections. Evaluate results to requirements and targets. Identify and track resolution of gaps and variances.

Preparing sustainability statements. Given the multitude of potential audiences for reporting, alignment and consistency of sustainability statements provides clarity and reusability for those audiences.
Coach sales reps on recorded calls: anchor a 1-on-1 session to a call, score it against a rubric, and track improvement. Cross-industry PCF has no matching activity.

Cross-domain employee lifecycle value stream: the joiner, mover, and leaver journey that spans recruiting, hire and onboarding, identity and access provisioning, payroll and benefits enrollment, role and org changes, and offboarding. Coordinates the agent workflows that no single domain owns end to end.

Cross-domain lead-to-cash value stream: the opportunity journey from demand generation and lead qualification through pipeline, quoting and configuration, order capture, fulfillment, invoicing, and revenue recognition. Coordinates the agent workflows that span the marketing, sales, and finance domains.

Cross-domain case and service value stream: the customer issue journey from intake and triage through case management, field or remote service execution, knowledge capture, and resolution and follow-up. Coordinates the agent workflows that span the support, service, and operations domains.
Periodic recertification of intranet content: owners attest that content is current, or flag it stale for remediation or archival, keeping the intranet free of ghost-town content.

entity.description: Compliance frameworks, country localizations, and industry standards that constrain how domains are run. Examples: HIPAA (data privacy in US healthcare), GDPR (data privacy in the EU), SOX (financial reporting for US-listed companies), PCI-DSS (security for card-handling), IFRS (accounting standard), ISO 27001 (security, globally applicable), Payroll-DE (German payroll localization). Each regulation may be scoped to a jurisdiction (null means globally applicable); each regulation binds to the domains it constrains through the domain-regulations junction.

fields.title: Code
fields.description: Short identifier (HIPAA, GDPR, SOX, ISO-27001, PCI-DSS-4)

fields.title: Type
fields.description: Family of constraint the regulation belongs to

fields.title: Jurisdiction
fields.description: Null marks a globally applicable regulation (e.g. ISO 27001); set for jurisdiction-scoped regulations (HIPAA in USA, GDPR in EU, Payroll-DE in Germany)

fields.title: Issuing Body
fields.description: Authoring authority (US Department of Health and Human Services, European Commission, PCI Security Standards Council)

fields.title: Effective Date
fields.description: Date the regulation took effect (historical dates valid for established regulations; future dates valid for upcoming ones)

fields.title: Certification Required
fields.description: TRUE when this regulation acts as a certification gate — a vendor cannot legally sell or operate without obtaining the relevant certification (e.g. FedRAMP authorization, FDA 510(k) clearance, CE marking under EU MDR or EU AI Act, CMMC level, StateRAMP).

fields.title: Reference URL
fields.description: Primary citation, typically the issuing body's canonical page

records.description: Lawful basis, data-subject rights, processor obligations, breach notification, DPIAs, DPO. Applies extraterritorially to any processing of EU residents' personal data.
Post-Brexit UK adaptation of GDPR. Substantially aligned with EU GDPR but diverges on transfers and ICO enforcement guidance.
Consumer rights to know, delete, correct, opt out of sale/share, and limit use of sensitive personal information. Applies to businesses meeting CA revenue/data thresholds.

records.regulation_name: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
records.issuing_body: US Department of Health & Human Services
records.description: Privacy Rule, Security Rule, and Breach Notification Rule for protected health information (PHI). Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) gate vendor relationships.

Sections 302, 404, and 906: management certification of financial reports, internal control over financial reporting (ICFR), and auditor attestation. Drives segregation of duties and access controls across financially relevant systems.
Principle-based global accounting standards adopted by 140+ jurisdictions for listed company financial statements.
Rule-based US accounting standards for public and private entity financial reporting.
Capital adequacy, leverage, and liquidity standards for internationally active banks. Implemented via national regulators (CRD/CRR in EU, US rules at Fed/OCC/FDIC).

records.regulation_name: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive II
records.description: Investor protection, transaction reporting, best execution, product governance for investment firms operating in the EU.
Open banking access via APIs, strong customer authentication (SCA), and licensed Account Information / Payment Initiation Service Providers.
AML/CTF predicate offences, ultimate-beneficial-owner registers, enhanced due diligence, and sanctions screening obligations for obliged entities.
Risk-based capital requirements for EU insurance and reinsurance undertakings, plus governance and disclosure (ORSA, SFCR).
Accounting standard for insurance contract liabilities. Drives major actuarial and IT change across insurers' financial reporting platforms.
International standard for ISMS. Independent certification by accredited bodies is the de-facto enterprise procurement gate worldwide.
Auditor attestation report (Type I / Type II) over controls aligned to Trust Services Criteria. Standard procurement gate for SaaS in North America.

records.regulation_name: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
records.description: Mandatory technical and operational requirements for any entity that stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data. Certified via QSA or self-assessment depending on level.
Voluntary risk-based framework (Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover). Heavily referenced by US regulators and contract clauses.
EU-wide cybersecurity obligations for essential and important entities across critical sectors, with management-board accountability and incident reporting.
ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing (incl. TLPT), and third-party ICT risk for EU financial entities and their critical ICT providers. Critical TPPs supervised at EU level.

records.regulation_name: Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act
records.description: Expanded HIPAA enforcement, breach-notification rules, and incentivised EHR adoption. Aligns ePHI safeguards with HIPAA Security Rule.
Classification, conformity assessment, UDI, EUDAMED registration, post-market surveillance, and CE marking for medical devices placed on the EU market.

records.regulation_name: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic Records and Signatures
records.description: Requirements for electronic records and signatures in FDA-regulated industries (pharma, medical devices, biotech): validation, audit trails, access controls, e-sig binding.
Mandatory sustainability reporting under ESRS standards with double-materiality and external assurance for in-scope companies operating in the EU.
Disclosure obligations for financial market participants on integration of sustainability risks and adverse impacts (PAI) at entity and product level.
Mandatory climate-related disclosures for SEC registrants (governance, strategy, risk management, GHG metrics — final scope evolving).

records.regulation_name: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
records.description: Voluntary framework for climate-related financial disclosure across governance, strategy, risk management, and metrics — increasingly embedded in mandatory regimes (ISSB, CSRD).
Federal minimum wage, overtime, recordkeeping, and child-labor standards. Drives time-and-attendance and payroll calculation rules.
Employer-mandate offer-of-coverage tracking, 1094/1095 reporting, and affordability calculations for US benefits administration.
Fiduciary, reporting (Form 5500), and disclosure standards for private-sector employee benefit plans, including 401(k) and health & welfare.
Pay transparency obligations including salary-range disclosure in job adverts and gender pay-gap reporting for EU employers above thresholds.

records.regulation_name: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program
records.description: Standardised security assessment, authorization (ATO), and continuous monitoring for cloud products sold to US federal agencies. Levels: Low / Moderate / High / Tailored.
Mandatory standards for bulk electric system cybersecurity across asset identification, access, system security management, incident response, and supply chain.
Risk-tiered obligations for AI systems. High-risk systems require conformity assessment, CE marking, post-market monitoring, and registration in the EU database before market placement.
Framework for electronic identification, trust services (qualified e-signatures, e-seals, timestamps). Qualified Trust Service Providers undergo conformity assessment and supervisory designation.
OTC derivatives reporting, central clearing obligations, and risk-mitigation techniques for non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
Cybersecurity essential requirements for products with digital elements placed on the EU market, including CE marking, vulnerability handling, and SBOM-style obligations.
User access to data generated by connected products and related services, B2B data sharing, cloud-switching, and government access in exceptional need.
Mandatory internal reporting channels and protection from retaliation for whistleblowers in employers with 50+ employees and public-sector entities.
Common VAT system across EU member states: rates, place-of-supply, e-invoicing rules (ViDA), and One Stop Shop (OSS) for cross-border B2C.
Conduct-of-business, demands-and-needs test, product oversight and governance (POG), and disclosure rules for insurance intermediaries and undertakings.
Authorisation, capital, depositary, valuation, and reporting requirements for managers of alternative investment funds in the EU.

records.regulation_name: Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities
records.description: Pan-EU framework for retail-oriented collective investment funds, with eligible-asset, diversification, and disclosure rules.
Eco-design requirements, digital product passport (DPP), and unsold-goods destruction restrictions for products placed on the EU market.
Carbon footprint, recycled content, due diligence, and digital battery passport requirements for batteries placed on the EU market.
Embedded-emissions reporting and (from 2026) charges on imports of cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, and hydrogen.
Content moderation, transparency reporting, notice-and-action, and systemic-risk obligations for online platforms operating in the EU; tighter obligations for VLOPs/VLOSEs.
Financial Privacy Rule and Safeguards Rule for US financial institutions: customer notice, opt-out, and information-security program requirements.
Post-2008 reform: derivatives clearing/reporting, Volcker Rule, CFPB, stress testing, whistleblower programs, and resolution planning for US financial institutions.
US AML foundation: CTRs, SARs, KYC/CIP, OFAC sanctions screening obligations for US financial institutions.
Reporting of US persons' foreign financial accounts and FFI withholding obligations under intergovernmental agreements.
Tiered cybersecurity certification (Levels 1–3) for the Defense Industrial Base. Required to bid on US DoD contracts handling FCI or CUI.
State and local government equivalent to FedRAMP, with shared assessments and an authorized-products marketplace for SLED procurement.
Premarket submission to demonstrate substantial equivalence to a legally marketed device. Standard route to clear most Class II medical devices in the US.

records.regulation_name: FDA Quality System Regulation (21 CFR Part 820)
records.description: Quality system requirements for medical device manufacturers: design controls, CAPA, document control, supplier controls — audited via FDA inspections.
Verifiable parental consent and data-handling requirements for online services directed at or knowingly collecting data from US children under 13.

records.regulation_name: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act
records.description: Student education record privacy. Gates US K-12 and higher-ed SaaS with consent, disclosure, and access-control requirements.
Five-step revenue recognition model under US GAAP. Drives subscription, multi-element, and variable-consideration accounting in billing/revrec engines.
Restrictions on autodialed calls/texts, prerecorded messages, fax marketing, and DNC. Drives consent management in marketing-automation and contact-center SaaS.
Commercial email rules: header/subject accuracy, opt-out, identification of advertising, physical address. Drives email-marketing compliance logic.
Caller location obligations for VoIP and multi-line telephone systems; supports US emergency-response routing.
Title III accessibility for places of public accommodation, increasingly applied to websites and mobile apps via WCAG-aligned settlements.
Mandatory ICT accessibility for US federal procurement, aligned to WCAG 2.0 AA. VPAT/ACR documentation is the de-facto gate for federal sale.

records.regulation_name: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
records.description: Federal prohibition on employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. Foundation of US employment law; drives EEO-1 reporting, applicant-tracking record-keeping, and AI-fairness scrutiny in screening systems.
Federal prohibition on age-based employment discrimination against workers 40 and older. Drives age-anonymised candidate review and disparate-impact testing in workforce-analytics tooling.

Annual demographic data filing by US employers with 100+ employees and federal contractors with 50+ employees. Component 1 covers race/ethnicity, sex, and job category counts. Drives EEO-category mapping in HRIS.

Federal continuation of employer-sponsored health coverage after qualifying events (termination, hours reduction, divorce). Drives leaver-event triggers in benefits administration and carrier_feed flagging.
Federal prohibition on use of genetic information in employment decisions and health insurance underwriting. Drives benefits-enrolment data minimisation and wellness-program design.
Federal employment-eligibility verification requirement for every new hire. Form I-9 must be completed within three days of hire; supporting documentation retained. Drives onboarding workflow gates.
Internet-based work-authorisation verification system. Mandatory for federal contractors and in several US states; voluntary elsewhere. Integrates with I-9 onboarding flow.

UK tax legislation determining whether a contractor working through an intermediary is a disguised employee. Drives VMS worker-classification flagging, status determination statements, and PAYE deduction at source.
Codifies the ABC test for distinguishing employees from independent contractors. Drives VMS classification screening for California-based contingent workers.
Directive (2024/2831) establishing rebuttable employment presumption for platform workers, algorithmic-management transparency, and data-subject rights for workforce-management algorithms.
Directive 2003/88/EC: minimum daily rest, weekly working-time cap, paid annual leave, night-work limits. Drives WFM scheduling-compliance rules across EU member states.

Aggregated category covering NYC, Seattle, Oregon, San Francisco, Chicago, Philadelphia predictive-scheduling laws: advance posting (7–14 days), premium pay for clopen/last-minute shifts, right-to-rest. Drives WFM scheduling rules for frontline workers.

records.regulation_name: Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act
records.description: Federal advance-notice requirement for mass layoffs and plant closings (typically 60 days). Several states have stricter Mini-WARN variants. Drives HCM termination workflow gates.

Illinois statute requiring informed written consent before collecting biometric identifiers (fingerprint, retina, hand geometry). Major exposure for WFM clock-in / time-and-attendance vendors with substantial settlement history.

records.issuing_body: American Bar Association (adopted by state bars)
records.description: ABA Model Rule 1.6 requires lawyers to keep client information confidential and to make reasonable efforts to prevent inadvertent or unauthorized disclosure. Adopted (with variations) by every US state bar. Regulates the attorney, not the software vendor — vendor must enable confidentiality features, but the lawyer carries liability.

records.issuing_body: American Bar Association + state IOLTA programs
records.description: ABA Model Rule 1.15 and state IOLTA (Interest on Lawyers Trust Accounts) programs require lawyers to hold client funds in separate trust accounts, maintain detailed ledgers, perform three-way reconciliation, and remit interest to state-administered legal-aid programs. Practice-management vendors typically advertise 'IOLTA-compliant' features but the lawyer is the account holder and bears the regulatory burden.

records.regulation_name: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure — eDiscovery (Rules 26-37)
records.description: FRCP Rules 26-37 govern discovery of electronically stored information (ESI) in federal civil litigation: preservation duties, production format, proportionality, sanctions for spoliation. Constrains how law firms manage matter-scoped documents and preservation holds. State-court eDiscovery rules largely mirror.

IRS Pub 4557 provides safeguarding requirements for tax preparers handling taxpayer data: written information-security plan (WISP), data encryption, access controls, breach response, and reporting. Required for any preparer with a PTIN. Enforced under GLBA Safeguards Rule (FTC) for tax preparers, who are classified as financial institutions for GLBA purposes (per IRS Pub 5293).

records.issuing_body: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants
records.description: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct governs CPAs in public practice: confidential client information (Section 1.700), independence (Section 1.200), integrity and objectivity (Section 1.100), client communications, contingent fees, commissions. State CPA boards adopt with state-specific variations. Regulates the CPA, not the vendor.

Controlled Substances Act requires registrants (including veterinarians) to maintain perpetual inventory of Schedule II-V controlled substances, conduct biennial reconciliations, and use DEA-certified e-prescribing platforms (EPCS). Veterinary clinics must maintain controlled-substance ledgers separately from general inventory. For e-prescribing, the vendor's EPCS module must pass third-party security audit per 21 CFR Part 1311.

Each US state's Veterinary Practice Act governs licensure, supervision of veterinary technicians, recordkeeping (retention of patient records 3-7 years typically), informed consent for treatment, and unauthorized practice of veterinary medicine. Practice-management vendors must accommodate state-specific record-retention and signature workflows.

US federal statute (15 U.S.C. §1681 et seq.) governing collection, dissemination, and use of consumer credit information including pre-employment background checks. Mandates pre-adverse-action and adverse-action notices, candidate disclosure of report sources, and a Summary of Rights acknowledgement.

US federal regulations (41 CFR Parts 60-1 through 60-741) administered by OFCCP requiring federal contractors and subcontractors to maintain applicant-flow records, voluntary self-identification of veteran and disability status, and equal-opportunity audit trails. Triggers Internet Applicant Rule applicant-tracking obligations.

Process framework for IT asset management. Sets the management-system requirements an organization uses to govern its hardware and software assets, with the configuration record acting as the substrate that asset and license management build on.
Governs fair-market-value determination for deferred compensation, including the 409A valuation that sets option strike prices for private-company equity.
US GAAP standard for measuring and recognizing the expense of stock-based compensation awards over the vesting period.
Exemption allowing private companies to issue equity compensation to employees and service providers without full securities registration, subject to disclosure thresholds.
Private-placement exemption framework; Form D is the notice filing required after selling securities in an exempt offering.
Annual information return reporting the exercise of incentive stock options to the IRS and the optionee.
Annual information return reporting the transfer of stock acquired through an employee stock purchase plan.
Rule 206(4)-1 under the Investment Advisers Act governing adviser advertising and LP-facing performance presentation, including net-performance and book-of-record substantiation requirements.
Institutional Limited Partners Association templates and conventions for capital-call notices, distribution notices, and quarterly fee-and-expense reporting to LPs.
OECD automatic-exchange-of-information standard requiring collection and reporting of LP tax residency and financial-account information across participating jurisdictions.
Cayman Islands Monetary Authority registration, audit, and reporting requirements applicable to Cayman-domiciled investment funds.

State-level pay-range disclosure and pay-data reporting requirements enacted by individual US states, including California, Colorado, New York, Washington, and Illinois. Requires salary-range publication on job postings and, in some states, pay-data reporting drawn from worker and compensation records.

records.issuing_body: US General Services Administration, Department of Defense, and NASA
records.description: Primary regulation governing acquisition of goods and services by US federal executive agencies; sets mandatory contract clauses for federal contracts.
Department of Defense supplement to the Federal Acquisition Regulation; adds defense-specific contract clauses including cybersecurity and supply-chain requirements.
US occupational safety and health law governing workplace safety standards, injury and illness recordkeeping (Forms 300, 300A, 301), hazard communication, and exposure limits.

records.regulation_name: ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems
records.description: International standard for occupational health and safety management systems, certifiable by accredited bodies and used to demonstrate a conformant safety management system.
International standard for environmental management systems, certifiable by accredited bodies and used to govern environmental aspects, impacts, and continual improvement.
EU regulation on the registration, evaluation, authorization, and restriction of chemicals, driving safety data sheet and hazardous-substance recordkeeping.

records.regulation_name: EPCRA Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act
records.description: US environmental law requiring chemical inventory (Tier II) and toxic release reporting, underpinning emissions and chemical-release recordkeeping.

US GAAP lease accounting standard requiring lessees to recognize right-of-use assets and lease liabilities for operating and finance leases on the balance sheet, with a dual classification model and prescribed quantitative and qualitative disclosures.

IFRS lease accounting standard applying a single lessee model under which all leases are recognized on the balance sheet as right-of-use assets and lease liabilities (treated like finance leases), with low-value and short-term exemptions and an IFRS-specific disclosure schedule.

Federal grant program funding sewage pump-out and dump-station facilities for recreational boats. Marinas receiving CVA grants must log pump-out usage and report it; many states add their own pump-out mandates.

Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure rule requiring facilities storing over 1,320 gallons of aboveground oil (including marina fuel docks) to maintain a written SPCC plan, fuel-inventory and inspection records, and periodic review.

entity.description: Junction: which modules does this role touch, and how heavily. `interaction_level` is two-value (`primary` / `secondary`) — read-only-ness is captured by the role's permission bundle holding only `:read` for that module, not a separate axis. Per plan-roles.md §7 Q1 resolution. The 2-module floor (§7 Q5) is enforced by the loader, not at the DB level.

fields.title: Role
fields.description: The role that touches this module.

fields.title: Module
fields.description: The catalog module this role interacts with.

fields.title: Interaction Level
fields.description: How heavily this role touches this module. `primary` = the role can't function without this module (drives the role-union on-ramp per plan-roles.md §5.1). `secondary` = the role uses this module supportively or read-only.

fields.title: Notes
fields.description: Optional. Why this role touches this module at this interaction level.

entity.description: An agent skill (system, process, or role) that bundles a coherent capability and depends on a set of tools to operate. System skills correspond one-to-one to a domain in the Domain Map; process skills orchestrate a cluster of cross-domain handoffs; role skills wrap a particular user role.

validation_rules.message: A domain_id is required when skill_type is domain.
validation_rules.description: Domain skills mirror one Domain Map domain by definition; the FK is the only thing that ties the skill to its home market. Process and role skills may legitimately leave the FK null.

fields.title: Domain
fields.description: Optional; set for system skills that mirror a specific Domain Map domain. Null for process and role skills.

fields.title: Skill Type
fields.description: `system` skills mirror a Domain Map domain; `process` skills orchestrate cross-domain handoff clusters; `role` skills wrap a specific user role's day-to-day work.

fields.title: Role
fields.description: For `skill_type='role'` skills, the role this skill wraps. NULL on `system` and `process` skills. Role skills themselves are deferred to plan-roles.md Phase 2 (§4.4); the column lands now so the FK shape is stable.

fields.title: Process
fields.description: A `process` skill formally references the APQC PCF row it implements (`processes.source_framework='apqc_pcf_*'`) or the custom-process row (`source_framework='custom'`). NULL on `system` and `role` skills.

fields.title: Trigger Keywords
fields.description: Comma-separated trigger terms appended to the generated SKILL.md routing description (as 'Use for: ...'). Curated synonyms and industry terms a user would type to trigger this domain skill, deduped against the prose at generation time. Author the complement of skills.description: do not repeat words already in the prose.

records.description: Run third-party and vendor risk end to end. records.description: Procure outsourced services under a statement of work end to end. fields.title: Solution Type

fields.title: Active in Market

fields.title: Min Org Size
fields.description: Smallest organisation-size tier the solution targets. Values: 10 xs <50 / 20 s <500 / 30 m <2500 / 40 l <10000 / 50 xl 10000+. Leading number sorts; t-shirt letter is for human conversation; upper bound is the memory aid.

fields.title: Max Org Size
fields.description: Largest organisation-size tier the solution targets. Values: 10 xs <50 / 20 s <500 / 30 m <2500 / 40 l <10000 / 50 xl 10000+.

fields.title: Cost Band
fields.description: Typical annual subscription tier for an enterprise deployment. $ <$50K, $$ $50K-$250K, $$$ $250K-$1M, $$$$ $1M-$5M, $$$$$ $5M+.

fields.title: Solution Kind
fields.description: Classification used by the Semantius coverage rollups. `external_connector` is a system of record providing query/mutate tools (SAP, NetSuite, Salesforce CRM). `action` is a side-effect service (Microsoft Graph Mail, Twilio, DocuSign, Stripe). `compute_service` is a compute / AI / web-automation service (OpenAI Platform, Anthropic API, Playwright). `standard_solution` is the default for solutions not yet integrated as a tool source. Semantius itself is NOT classified here; Semantius coverage is intrinsic to the tool's operation_kind (see tools.operation_kind).

records.notes: Strong fit for existing Zoho customers (CRM, Desk, Campaigns) at SMB/mid-market scale.

records.description: Category-defining headless CMS with content modeling, REST and GraphQL delivery APIs, authoring UI, and a composable content platform around it (Studio Experiences, Compose, Launch).
Structured-content platform with a real-time content lake, GROQ/GraphQL APIs, the customizable Sanity Studio, and the Presentation tool for visual editing of composable frontends.

GraphQL-native headless CMS (formerly GraphCMS) with federation/Content Federation for stitching multiple content sources behind a single API.
Enterprise headless CMS (formerly Kentico Kontent) with structured content, multi-language and workflow capabilities, and the Web Spotlight in-context editor.
